2-0006-0000.sourceText:
Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgt die Aussprache über die Erklärung der Kommission zu den dringenden Maßnahmen zur Stärkung der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und zur Sicherung hochwertiger Arbeitsplätze im Automobilsektor der EU (2026/2806(RSP)).

Ich möchte die Rednerinnen und Redner daran erinnern, dass angesichts der derzeit durchgeführten Testmaßnahmen und des festgesetzten Zeitpunkts für den Abschluss der Aussprache die Redezeit bitte strikt eingehalten wird. Die Regeln zu Blue Cards und Catch-the-Eye sind Ihnen, glaube ich, mittlerweile ausreichend bekannt.
2-0006-0000.englishText:
The next item on the agenda is the debate on the Commission statement on urgent measures to strengthen competitiveness and secure high-quality jobs in the EU automotive sector (2026/2806(RSP)).

I would like to remind the speakers that, given the test measures currently being carried out and the set time for the conclusion of the debate, please strictly adhere to the speaking time. I believe you are now sufficiently familiar with the rules on blue cards and catch-the-eye.

2-0007-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Mesdames et Messieurs les députés, le secteur automobile européen est en danger de mort. J’avertissais de ce constat il y a plus d’un an et aujourd’hui, constructeurs, équipementiers, c’est l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur qui est sous tension, et l’avenir de millions d’emplois en jeu – soyons lucides, derrière ces emplois, c’est la prospérité, c’est la cohésion sociale de beaucoup de nos territoires, en particulier des territoires ruraux…

Ces secteurs affrontent en même temps un retard technologique, des chaînes d’approvisionnement fragilisées par l’instabilité géopolitique, des bilans financiers plombés par les droits de douane, des restrictions d’accès aux marchés étrangers, une stratégie prédatrice de la Chine pour déverser des surcapacités en Europe.

Le résultat est sans appel: des pertes de parts de marché pour nos constructeurs, l’importation massive de modèles chinois, qui représentent aujourd’hui plus de 15 % des segments électrifiés en Europe, des usines européennes qui tournent au ralenti et le spectre, évidemment, des licenciements collectifs. La Commission européenne mesure pleinement l’urgence de la situation.

Depuis le début de ce mandat, nous nous employons à bâtir, autour du dialogue stratégique avec l’ensemble de la filière, une véritable politique industrielle sur le secteur. Avec le paquet automobile de décembre, complété par la proposition d’accélération industrielle en mars, nous déployons pour la première fois une stratégie sur l’entièreté de la chaîne de valeur du secteur de l’automobile. Avec les règles de contrôle des émissions de CO2, nous introduisons des flexibilités tout en gardant notre cohérence sur nos objectifs. Avec le règlement sur la décarbonation des flottes, nous protégeons un segment essentiel pour nos constructeurs, garantissant la disponibilité de véhicules électriques de seconde main pour les foyers européens. Avec les efforts de simplification, nous accélérons le déploiement des petits véhicules électriques abordables. Avec le «Battery Booster», nous finançons la montée en puissance de notre propre industrie européenne de la batterie. Avec l’accélérateur industriel, nous protégeons les emplois en Europe, nous stoppons l’hémorragie chez les équipementiers et renforçons leur place dans la chaîne de valeur électrifiée.

Alors, vous comprenez, Mesdames et Messieurs les députés, l’urgence qu’il y a à envoyer aujourd’hui des signaux clairs à la filière, et donc la responsabilité collective de l’ensemble des institutions européennes pour ce qui est d’adopter le plus rapidement possible ces textes, qui sont sur la table. L’objectif est clair: casser le cycle mortifère du triple déclin européen – baisse de la production, baisse des parts de marché pour nos constructeurs, baisse de la valeur ajoutée en Europe. Nous le devons à notre industrie. Nous le devons à ses salariés. Nous le devons à nos régions, qui sont sur ce segment automobile.

Vous pouvez compter en tout cas sur moi pour déployer cette stratégie industrielle, tout comme les commissaires Tzitzikóstas et Hoekstra et l’ensemble de la Commission européenne.
2-0007-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable Members, the European automotive sector is facing mortal danger. I warned of this observation more than a year ago, and today, manufacturers, equipment suppliers, the entire value chain is under strain, and the future of millions of jobs is at stake – let us be clear, behind these jobs lies prosperity, the social cohesion of many of our regions, in particular rural areas...

These sectors are simultaneously facing a technological lag, supply chains weakened by geopolitical instability, financial balances burdened by customs duties, restrictions on access to foreign markets, and a predatory strategy by China to dump excess capacity in Europe.

The result is unequivocal: losses in market share for our manufacturers, the massive importation of Chinese models, which today account for more than 15% of electrified segments in Europe, European factories operating below capacity and the spectre, obviously, of mass redundancies. The European Commission fully appreciates the urgency of the situation.

Since the beginning of this term, we have been working to build, around strategic dialogue with the entire sector, a genuine industrial policy for the sector. With the automotive package in December, supplemented by the industrial acceleration proposal in March, we are deploying for the first time a strategy across the entire value chain of the automotive sector. With the CO2 emission control rules, we are introducing flexibilities while maintaining our consistency on our objectives. With the regulation on the decarbonisation of fleets, we are protecting an essential segment for our manufacturers, guaranteeing the availability of second-hand electric vehicles for European households. With simplification efforts, we are accelerating the deployment of small, affordable electric vehicles. With the "Battery Booster", we are funding the ramp-up of our own European battery industry. With the industrial accelerator, we are protecting jobs in Europe, stopping the bleeding among equipment suppliers and strengthening their place in the electrified value chain.

You can therefore understand, honourable Members, the urgency of sending clear signals to the sector today, and therefore the collective responsibility of all European institutions to adopt as quickly as possible these texts which are on the table. The objective is clear: to break the death spiral of Europe's triple decline – falling production, falling market share for our manufacturers, falling value added in Europe. We owe it to our industry. We owe it to its workers. We owe it to our regions that are in this automotive segment.

You can in any case count on me to deploy this industrial strategy, just as you can count on Commissioners Tzitzikostas and Hoekstra and the entire European Commission.

2-0008-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dobbiamo riconoscere che quello che sta accadendo nell'assetto dell'industria europea vede nel pacchetto automotive uno dei punti centrali, decisivi per garantire un futuro all'intera manifattura europea.

Quindi, è assolutamente benvenuta la proposta di revisione della Commissione europea sul regolamento per le emissioni di CO2 in atmosfera per veicoli leggeri.

L'industria europea nel settore automobilistico ha investito miliardi di euro per accettare tutte le nuove sfide, in primis la sfida dell'elettrificazione, oggi le nostre case automobilistiche possono produrre motori elettrici e motori endotermici.

Il mercato, però, segnala che il ritmo previsto dall'ambizioso regolamento non viene rispettato: abbiamo un 20 % di penetrazione dell'elettrico a maggio 2026, ma le previsioni sono per un 38 al 2030 e un 64 al 2035, quindi è necessario un intervento.

Cosa serve? Servono condizioni abilitanti. Quindi, innanzitutto ci vuole un'accessibilità economica per i consumatori, ci vuole una diffusione dei sistemi di ricarica capillare e un sistema energetico europeo adeguato. Questo consentirà di avere investimenti europei completi, che tengano conto delle dinamiche di mercato e che tengano conto delle esigenze dei cittadini.

L'alternativa sarebbe quella di ridurre la produzione europea e acquistare crediti, magari da case automobilistiche non europee, una prospettiva che non possiamo accettare. Abbiamo la modifica del regolamento sulle emissioni di CO2, che è lo strumento più veloce per ottenere i risultati attesi e per adeguarci al mercato attraverso due grandi asset tecnici, giuridici e industriali: la flessibilità e la neutralità tecnologica. Lavoreremo in questa direzione.
2-0008-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, we must recognise that what is happening in the structure of European industry sees the automotive package as one of the central, decisive points for guaranteeing a future for the whole of European manufacturing.

Therefore, the European Commission's proposal to revise the regulation on CO2 emissions into the atmosphere for light vehicles is absolutely welcome.

The European automotive industry has invested billions of euros to accept all new challenges, first and foremost the challenge of electrification. Today our car manufacturers can produce electric engines and internal combustion engines.

The market, however, indicates that the pace foreseen by the ambitious regulation is not being met: we have 20% electric penetration in May 2026, but the forecasts are 38% by 2030 and 64% by 2035, so intervention is necessary.

What is needed? Enabling conditions are needed. Therefore, first of all, economic accessibility for consumers is required, along with a widespread rollout of charging systems and an adequate European energy system. This will make it possible to have comprehensive European investments that take into account market dynamics and citizens' needs.

The alternative would be to reduce European production and purchase credits, perhaps from non-European car manufacturers, a prospect we cannot accept. We have the amendment of the CO2 emissions regulation, which is the fastest tool to obtain the expected results and to adapt to the market through two major technical, legal and industrial assets: flexibility and technological neutrality. We will work in this direction.

2-0009-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, ik ben bang dat we elk half jaar — ik hoop het niet — in debat gaan over de toekomst van de auto-industrie, dat er weer een fabriek gaat sluiten en de producent van die autotechniek waarschijnlijk ergens buiten Europa een fabriek gaat opzetten.

We hebben te lang lacherig gedaan over elektrisch rijden. In Brabant hebben wij een autodealer die trots een heel groot bord voor zijn showroom heeft staan dat elektrisch rijden iets is voor de kermis. Maar ik denk dat er heel veel automobilisten de afgelopen maanden van een koude kermis thuis zijn gekomen, in de rij hebben gestaan bij Turnhout, Brecht of Poppel om goedkoop te tanken in België.

Wij hebben last van cognitieve dissonantie. We houden vast aan een technologie waarvan we zien dat de wereldwijde vraag daalt: de verbrandingsmotor. Tegelijkertijd wint de elektrische auto aan terrein. De vraag naar nieuwe elektrische auto's en tweedehands elektrische auto's stijgt.

Achter die ontwikkeling schuilt een veel grotere trend. Terwijl partijen hier koste wat kost vasthouden aan die technologie, focust de rest van de wereld op elektrisch vervoer. Ethiopië heeft de import van auto's met een verbrandingsmotor verboden. Laos gaat hetzelfde doen. Landen in Azië en Zuid-Amerika schakelen in hoog tempo over op elektrisch vervoer.

Naar verwachting zal in 2035 de helft van alle wereldwijd verkochte auto's elektrisch zijn. De vraag is dus niet wanneer die omslag gaat komen, maar waar we die auto's gaan bouwen en waar de banen straks liggen: in Europa of in China?
2-0009-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I am afraid that every six months — I hope not — we will be debating the future of the automotive industry, that another factory will close and that the producer of that automotive technology will probably set up a plant somewhere outside Europe.

For too long, we have scoffed at electric driving. In Brabant, we have a car dealer who proudly displays a very large sign in front of his showroom stating that electric driving is something for the funfair. But I think many motorists have had a rude awakening in recent months, having queued in Turnhout, Brecht or Poppel to refuel cheaply in Belgium.

We are suffering from cognitive dissonance. We are clinging to a technology for which we see global demand falling: the internal combustion engine. At the same time, the electric car is gaining ground. Demand for new electric cars and second-hand electric cars is rising.

Behind that development lies a much larger trend. While parties here stubbornly cling to that technology, the rest of the world is focusing on electric transport. Ethiopia has banned the import of cars with an internal combustion engine. Laos is going to do the same. Countries in Asia and South America are rapidly switching to electric transport.

It is expected that by 2035, half of all cars sold worldwide will be electric. The question is therefore not when that transition will come, but where we are going to build those cars and where the jobs will be in the future: in Europe or in China?

2-0010-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, vážení kolegové, je moc fajn, že Evropská komise ve svém akčním plánu konečně přiznává to, na co automobilový průmysl upozorňuje už několik let. Vysoké ceny energií, rostoucí náklady na výrobu, narušené dodavatelské řetězce i sílící konkurence ze třetích zemí ohrožují jedno z nejdůležitějších evropských průmyslových odvětví. Bohužel správná diagnóza ještě neznamená správnou léčbu. Komise mluví o konkurenceschopnosti, ale zároveň zachovává regulační rámec, který naši konkurenceschopnost systematicky oslabuje. Mluví o zjednodušení, ale přidává další administrativní náklady. Mluví o inovacích, ale stále více předepisuje, jaké technologie mají být používány, místo toho, aby nechala inovace vznikat přirozenou soutěží. Evropské automobilky nepotřebují další strategické dokumenty. Potřebují levnější energie, předvídatelná pravidla, méně byrokracie a skutečně technologicky neutrální prostředí. Jestliže budou evropské podniky vyrábět za výrazně vyšší náklady než jejich konkurenti v Číně nebo ve Spojených státech, nebude rozhodující kvalita našich inženýrů ani zkušenosti našich pracovníků. Rozhodující budou náklady. Milá Komise, neztrácejte čas dalšími plány. Začněte odstraňovat překážky, které jste evropskému průmyslu sami vytvořili.
2-0010-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear colleagues, it is great that the European Commission finally admits in its action plan what the automotive industry has been pointing out for several years. High energy prices, growing production costs, disrupted supply chains, and strengthening competition from third countries are threatening one of the most important European industrial sectors. Unfortunately, a correct diagnosis does not yet mean the right treatment. The Commission talks about competitiveness, but at the same time maintains a regulatory framework that systematically weakens our competitiveness. It talks about simplification, but adds further administrative costs. It talks about innovation, but increasingly prescribes which technologies are to be used, instead of letting innovation emerge through natural competition. European car manufacturers do not need more strategic documents. They need cheaper energy, predictable rules, less bureaucracy, and a truly technologically neutral environment. If European businesses are to produce at significantly higher costs than their competitors in China or the United States, the quality of our engineers or the experience of our workers will not be decisive. Costs will be decisive. Dear Commission, do not waste time with further plans. Start removing the obstacles that you yourselves have created for European industry.

2-0011-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, grazie per la Sua chiarezza, la Sua durezza e l'analisi.

È sulla ricetta che abbiamo delle differenze, perché, come ricordava Lei, ma io ricordo, addirittura, due anni fa, luglio 2024, qui si faceva un dibattito sull'automotive. Cos'è cambiato? Niente rispetto all'indirizzo della Commissione – poco, direi – mentre il mercato è decisamente peggiorato: la Cina ha invaso il nostro mercato delle auto e assistiamo alla perdita di posti di lavoro. Lei stesso, in Commissione, ha ricordato che abbiamo già perduto 200 000 posti di lavoro. Una delle più grandi aziende europee, Volkswagen, dichiara la riduzione di ulteriori 100 000 posti di lavoro, di solito uomini con famiglia.

Questo è un impoverimento dell'Europa. E, dall'altro lato, chiusura di fabbriche e l'impoverimento dell'intera filiera – come Lei ha ben ricordato – della supply chain. Una filiera che è una filiera ricca, che ha investito, che ha investito anche in contenimento dei danni ambientali, che si suppongono da un'industria.

Ma è sulla ricetta che non ci siamo. Noi chiediamo fortemente neutralità tecnologica. Il mercato non sta chiedendo auto elettriche, il mercato vuole essere libero, i consumatori sono liberi, siamo in un'Europa libera. Abbiamo necessità di fare in modo che tutta la neutralità tecnologica riguardi anche i carburanti e abbiamo la necessità di non penalizzare un settore, come quello dei camion, del trasporto pesante, che noi ci illudiamo possa andare con una batteria elettrica fatta in Cina.
2-0011-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable members, Commissioner, thank you for your clarity, your firmness and your analysis.

It is on the prescription that we have differences, because, as you recalled, but I recall, even two years ago, July 2024, a debate on the automotive sector took place here. What has changed? Nothing with regard to the Commission's direction – little, I would say – whereas the market has decidedly worsened: China has invaded our car market and we are witnessing the loss of jobs. You yourself, in committee, recalled that we have already lost 200,000 jobs. One of the largest European companies, Volkswagen, is announcing the reduction of a further 100,000 jobs, usually men with families.

This is an impoverishment of Europe. And, on the other hand, the closure of factories and the impoverishment of the entire supply chain – as you rightly recalled. A supply chain that is a wealthy one, which has invested, which has also invested in containing the environmental damage expected of an industry.

But it is on the prescription that we do not agree. We strongly demand technological neutrality. The market is not demanding electric cars, the market wants to be free, consumers are free, we are in a free Europe. We need to ensure that all technological neutrality also applies to fuels, and we need not to penalize a sector, such as that of trucks and heavy transport, which we delude ourselves can run on an electric battery made in China.

2-0012-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, morning. Let's start with some good news.

June was an all-time high for electric car sales in the EU. We are setting records as we speak. Across Europe, more and more people are choosing electric cars. They are getting better, cheaper and more accessible. At the same time, let's be honest, high fossil fuel prices make the shift even more attractive.

If we don't prioritise producing electric vehicles for European citizens, China seems more than ready to. Our European competitiveness, industrial strength and jobs depend on accelerating that European transition, not hitting the brakes to slow it down.

Yet, some in this House want to reopen old debates or weaken the regulatory framework – the certainty that Europe and our European industry needs. They claim it will protect the European car industry, but in reality it will do the opposite. It will mean less innovation, fewer investments and an industry that falls even further behind China.

We cannot secure the jobs of tomorrow with the industrial policy of the past. Europe will not help its workers by pretending the global market is standing still. We need to support you. We need to be brave, give our companies a clear, stable, ambitious framework.

2-0013-0000.sourceText:
Collega's, kunnen jullie de mensen van Volkswagen vandaag recht in de ogen kijken en beweren dat de toekomst van hun job in diesel- en benzinemotoren ligt?

Wat er vandaag gebeurt bij Volkswagen is verschrikkelijk. Honderdduizend arbeiders vrezen voor hun job. Dat zijn mensen die vaak al heel hun leven voor het bedrijf werken; het is hun familie geworden; het zijn vrienden geworden.

Dit doet mij denken aan de ontslagronde die we bij Audi in Brussel hebben gezien. Ook daar hebben mensen erg geleden onder de ontslagronde. Een koppel dat er al 33 jaar werkte, getuigde hoe koud ze afscheid moesten nemen, via een brief, een veiligheidsagent die hen begeleidde om hun spullen op te halen. Zij kregen niet eens de mogelijkheid om afscheid te nemen.

Hadden de CEO's van Volkswagen meer tijd gestoken in de concurrentie met China op de markt van de elektrische voertuigen in plaats van sjoemelsoftware te installeren, dan hadden die mensen vandaag nog een job. Laat ons diezelfde fout niet opnieuw maken.
2-0013-0000.englishText:
Colleagues, can you look the people at Volkswagen straight in the eye today and claim that the future of their job lies in diesel and petrol engines?

What is happening at Volkswagen today is terrible. One hundred thousand workers fear for their job. These are people who have often worked for the company all their lives; it has become their family; they have become friends.

This reminds me of the layoff round we saw at Audi in Brussels. There, too, people suffered greatly from the layoff round. A couple that had been working there for 33 years testified how coldly they had to say goodbye, via a letter, a security guard escorting them to collect their belongings. They were not even given the opportunity to say goodbye.

Had Volkswagen's CEOs put more time into competing with China in the electric vehicle market instead of installing defeat devices, those people would still have a job today. Let us not make that same mistake again.

2-0014-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar! Die Beschäftigten von Mercedes-Benz wehren sich dagegen, ohne Lohnausgleich länger zu schuften, während überhohe Dividenden an die Großaktionäre ausgeschüttet werden. Das Management von Volkswagen hat einen drastischen Stellenabbau angekündigt; vier Standorte sollen allein in Deutschland geschlossen werden. Und Konzernchef Blume ist so unverschämt, jedes Jahr über 10 Millionen Euro einzusacken, die von diesen Beschäftigten erwirtschaftet worden sind.

Die Automobilindustrie steht vor großen Herausforderungen: internationale Konkurrenz, die Umstellung auf E-Autos, die Digitalisierung. Aber das anhaltende Versagen des Managements verschärft diese Krise nur. Werke sollen jetzt sogar zur Aufrüstung genutzt werden: Raketenabwehrsysteme statt Volkswagen und Panzer mit Mercedesstern, wenn es nach Herrn Blume und Mercedes-Boss Källenius geht.

Nicht mit uns! Schluss mit dem Kürzungskurs auf dem Rücken der Beschäftigten! Wir fordern Zukunftsinvestitionen, um Standorte langfristig zu sichern, mit Beschäftigungsgarantien. Schluss mit den Angriffen auf Arbeitszeit und Tarifverträge!
2-0014-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner! Mercedes-Benz employees are resisting working longer hours without wage compensation while excessively high dividends are distributed to major shareholders. The management of Volkswagen has announced drastic job cuts; four plants are to be closed in Germany alone. And CEO Blume has the audacity to pocket over 10 million euros every year that were generated by these employees.

The automotive industry is facing major challenges: international competition, the transition to electric cars, digitalization. But the management's ongoing failure only exacerbates this crisis. Factories are now even supposed to be used for rearmament: missile defense systems instead of Volkswagen and tanks with a Mercedes star, if it is up to Mr. Blume and Mercedes boss Källenius.

Not with us! Put an end to the course of cuts at the expense of the employees! We demand future investments to secure locations in the long term, with employment guarantees. Put an end to the attacks on working hours and collective bargaining agreements!

2-0015-0000.sourceText: Vážená pani predsedajúca, kolegovia. Je mi jasné, že zelení fanatici v Bruseli, ako je pán Hojsík, by najradšej všetky normálne autá zakázali a v podstate nenávidia šoférov. Ale realita je taká, že dnes, v dnešnom svete, bežná rodina bez auta proste nemá šancu. A kvôli vašim opatreniam sú tie autá čoraz drahšie a nedostupnejšie. Teraz Volkswagen oznámil, že plánuje prepustiť 100 tisíc ľudí a plánuje sa preorientovať na výrobu zbraní, pretože Green deal pre zbrane jednoducho neplatí. Tak prosím vás, vy tu neobviňujte teraz nejakých Číňanov, že nás v automobiloch predbehli. Obviňujte v prvom rade samých seba, že ste to dopustili, pretože to je realita a to je výsledok vašej práce. Pozrite sa za posledné roky, čo sa tu udialo. Najprv ste prišli so zákazom spaľovacích motorov, ktorý doteraz nebol zrušený. Potom ste presadzovali normu Euro 7, ktorú aj inžinieri označovali za technicky nerealizovateľnú. Teraz najnovšie pretláčate povinné tachografy už aj pre malé dodávky. Pre ľudí, pre obyčajných ľudí chcete zdražieť palivá, benzín, naftu cez emisné povolenky ETS 2. Firmy nútite do nakupovania povinného podielu elektromobilov, ktoré stoja na európskych skladoch. A dokonca do vedenia firiem cez genderové kvóty tlačíte polovicu žien, pričom ja absolútne nerozumiem, čo má nejaké pohlavie spojené s nejakými riadiacimi schopnosťami. Prosím vás, kedy ste naposledy niečo zjednodušili alebo uvoľnili? Všetko len komplikujete a zdražujete. A to je to, čo chceme zastaviť, a to je to, čo chceme napraviť.
2-0015-0000.englishText:
Madam President, colleagues. It is clear to me that the green fanatics in Brussels, such as Mr Hojsík, would ideally ban all normal cars and basically hate drivers. But the reality is that today, in today's world, an ordinary family simply has no chance without a car. And because of your measures, those cars are becoming increasingly expensive and out of reach.
Now Volkswagen has announced that it plans to lay off 100 thousand people and plans to reorient itself towards arms production, because the Green Deal simply does not apply to weapons. So please, do not blame some Chinese here for overtaking us in automobiles. Blame first of all yourselves for allowing this, because that is the reality and that is the result of your work.
Look at what has happened here over the last few years. First you came up with the ban on internal combustion engines, which has not been repealed to this day. Then you pushed for the Euro 7 standard, which even engineers described as technically unfeasible. Most recently, you are pushing through mandatory tachographs even for small vans. For people, for ordinary people, you want to make fuels, petrol, diesel more expensive through ETS 2 emission allowances. You are forcing companies to buy a mandatory share of electric vehicles that are sitting in European warehouses. And you are even pushing half of women into company management via gender quotas, while I completely do not understand what gender has to do with any management skills.
Please, when was the last time you simplified or deregulated anything? You only complicate and make everything more expensive. And that is what we want to stop, and that is what we want to fix.

2-0016-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, revenons d’abord peut-être sur les facteurs de compétitivité que vous avez chacun mentionnés dans vos interventions.

Retards technologiques, je l’évoquais en introduction, ce sont d’une part des choix industriels – et il y a eu, en toute honnêteté, des mauvais choix industriels de la part de nos constructeurs sur des stratégies industrielles, et il y a eu également des choix dans notre capacité à pouvoir aller conquérir un certain nombre de marchés. Nous sommes exposés à la concurrence internationale, avec le choix des autres pays de se concentrer sur leur marché domestique. Je pense notamment à la Chine, où un certain nombre de constructeurs chinois viennent aujourd’hui remplacer les constructeurs européens. Ce sont, d’autre part, des choix politiques de nos concurrents à l’international sur des marchés, d’où l’ouverture d’autres marchés à l’étranger, la constitution et l’organisation de nouveaux accords commerciaux pour pouvoir trouver des débouchés. Et puis, de notre côté, un travail sur notre compétitivité interne au niveau européen qu’il faut poursuivre.

Chaînes de valeur et d’approvisionnement fragilisées liées à la géopolitique, bilan financier plombé par les droits de douane, avec des constructeurs qui avaient un concept de production global pour le local, avec des chaînes de valeur morcelées à travers le monde, qui aujourd’hui se retrouvent dans une difficulté où le retour du protectionnisme, le retour des droits de douane viennent fragiliser les modèles économiques de nos constructeurs.

Perte également de compétitivité domestique au niveau européen. Le prix de l’énergie fera l’objet probablement de nombreux débats ici pendant cette session. Règles européennes complexes et un travail sur la simplification d’un certain nombre de dispositifs pour pouvoir faciliter la commercialisation de nouveaux types de véhicules. Bref, la Commission s’est attaquée à l’ensemble des facteurs de la compétitivité.

Un dernier mot sur quelques chiffres que vous évoquez. En Europe, nous avons atteint 25 % de parts de marché pour le véhicule électrique et plus de 35 % si on ajoute les hybrides rechargeables. Dans le monde, nous dépassons aujourd’hui les 13 millions de véhicules électriques produits et, aujourd’hui, nous atteignons à peu près 20 % des véhicules vendus dans le monde qui sont électriques. Cette tendance est en augmentation très forte, et, au dernier trimestre, c’est plus de 40 % des ventes supplémentaires de véhicules électriques en Europe. Pourquoi? Tout simplement parce que le marché permet la vente de ce genre de véhicules. Tout simplement parce que, pour rouler en électrique, ce sont aujourd’hui 80 euros économisés pour un mois de carburant pour un certain nombre de travailleurs. Ce sont 1 000 euros économisés pour un mois de travail pour un taxi dans une capitale européenne du fait d’avoir aujourd’hui un véhicule électrique.

Donc nous avons la capacité de pouvoir convaincre aussi avec des véhicules qui vont arriver sur le marché, plus de 200 nouvelles séries de véhicules qui vont arriver sur le marché cette année, des véhicules qui seront beaucoup moins chers et qui bénéficieront également des réformes européennes sur la simplification, sur la capacité à pouvoir justement proposer aux classes moyennes et aux classes populaires un véhicule à moins de 20 000 euros. C’était l’objectif que nous nous étions fixés avec le petit véhicule électrique européen.

Voilà: pour vous dire que la Commission, à travers ces trois textes que nous vous avons présentés, touche l’ensemble des points de compétitivité que nous voulons aujourd’hui débattre. Le message est clair: aller rapidement sur l’adoption de ces textes – pour adopter ces textes, pour qu’ils puissent entrer en vigueur et pour qu’ils puissent avoir aussi un impact sur notre industrie et sur nos emplois.
2-0016-0000.englishText:
Madam President, let us perhaps first return to the competitiveness factors that each of you mentioned in your speeches.

Technological lags, as I mentioned in my introduction, are on the one hand industrial choices—and there have been, in all honesty, poor industrial choices on the part of our manufacturers regarding industrial strategies, and there have also been choices in our ability to go out and conquer a certain number of markets. We are exposed to international competition, with other countries choosing to focus on their domestic market. I am thinking in particular of China, where a number of Chinese manufacturers are today replacing European manufacturers. On the other hand, these are political choices made by our international competitors in markets, hence the opening of other markets abroad, the formation and organization of new trade agreements to find outlets. And then, on our side, work on our internal competitiveness at the European level that must be continued.

Fragilized value and supply chains linked to geopolitics, financial performance weighed down by customs duties, with manufacturers who had a global-for-local production concept, with fragmented value chains across the world, who today find themselves in a difficulty where the return of protectionism and the return of customs duties are weakening our manufacturers' economic models.

Also, loss of domestic competitiveness at the European level. The price of energy will likely be the subject of much debate here during this session. Complex European rules and work on the simplification of a number of mechanisms to facilitate the marketing of new types of vehicles. In short, the Commission has tackled all the factors of competitiveness.

A final word on some figures you mentioned. In Europe, we have reached a 25% market share for electric vehicles and more than 35% if plug-in hybrids are added. Worldwide, we now exceed 13 million electric vehicles produced and today, we reach about 20% of vehicles sold worldwide that are electric. This trend is increasing very sharply, and in the last quarter, it is more than 40% of additional sales of electric vehicles in Europe. Why? Simply because the market allows the sale of this kind of vehicle. Simply because, to drive electric, that is nowadays 80 euros saved for a month of fuel for a certain number of workers. That is 1,000 euros saved for a month of work for a taxi driver in a European capital thanks to having an electric vehicle today.

So we also have the capacity to convince with vehicles that will arrive on the market, more than 200 new series of vehicles that will arrive on the market this year, vehicles that will be much cheaper and will also benefit from European reforms on simplification, on the ability to precisely offer the middle classes and working classes a vehicle at less than 20,000 euros. That was the objective we had set ourselves with the small European electric vehicle.

There you have it: to tell you that the Commission, through these three texts that we have presented to you, touches upon all the competitiveness points that we want to debate today. The message is clear: move quickly on the adoption of these texts—to adopt these texts, so that they can enter into force and so that they can also have an impact on our industry and our jobs.

2-0017-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wenn Europas größter Automobilhersteller 100 000 Stellen abbauen will, dann ist das mehr als eine Unternehmensentscheidung, dann ist das ein verzweifelter Hilfeschrei. Die Automobilindustrie ist eine der Schlüsselindustrien Europas; wenn sie an Wettbewerbsfähigkeit verliert, verliert Europa – und genau das erleben wir seit Jahren.

Während China und die USA ihre Industrie massiv unterstützen, hat Europa seine Industrie mit Verboten und Bürokratie überfordert. Das zeigt, es braucht einen echten Kurswechsel. Nur eine wirtschaftlich starke Industrie kann die Transformation meistern und Jobs in unseren Regionen erhalten. Deshalb müssen wir Bürokratie abbauen, Verfahren beschleunigen und Lade- und Wasserstoffinfrastruktur ausbauen. Und wir brauchen CO2-Flottengrenzwerte, die praxistauglich sind und die Technologieoffenheit gewährleisten. Wer Innovation fördern will, darf Unternehmen nicht mit immer neuen Belastungen die Luft zum Atmen nehmen.

Die Beschäftigten in der Industrie erwarten zu Recht, dass wir nicht nur über Arbeitsplätze reden, sondern diese sichern. Dafür braucht es eine Industriepolitik, die Vertrauen schafft, Investitionen ermöglicht und Europa als Produktionsstandort stärkt. Unser Ziel ist klar: klimaneutrale Mobilität – aber mit europäischen Fahrzeugen, europäischen Innovationen und europäischen Arbeitsplätzen. Deshalb möchte ich heute einen Appell an alle demokratischen und verantwortungsbewussten Kräfte dieses Hauses richten: Lassen Sie uns gemeinsam Europas Automobilindustrie zurück an die Weltspitze führen – für Beschäftigte, Unternehmen und unseren Wohlstand.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0017-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! When Europe's largest car manufacturer wants to cut 100,000 jobs, that is more than a corporate decision; it is a desperate cry for help. The automotive industry is one of Europe's key industries; when it loses competitiveness, Europe loses – and that is exactly what we have been experiencing for years.

While China and the USA are massively supporting their industries, Europe has overburdened its industry with bans and bureaucracy. This shows that a real course correction is needed. Only an economically strong industry can master the transformation and preserve jobs in our regions. Therefore, we must cut bureaucracy, accelerate procedures, and expand charging and hydrogen infrastructure. And we need CO2 fleet limits that are practicable and ensure technological openness. Anyone who wants to promote innovation must not suffocate companies with ever-new burdens.

Industrial workers rightly expect us not just to talk about jobs, but to secure them. This requires an industrial policy that creates trust, enables investment, and strengthens Europe as a production location. Our goal is clear: climate-neutral mobility – but with European vehicles, European innovations, and European jobs. Therefore, I would like to make an appeal today to all democratic and responsible forces in this House: Let us lead Europe's automotive industry back to the top of the world together – for workers, companies, and our prosperity.

(The speaker agreed to answer a "blue card" question.)

2-0018-0000.sourceText: Szanowny Panie Pośle, Pan mówi tutaj, że przemysł motoryzacyjny jest w trudnej sytuacji. Ja się zgadzam z Panem absolutnie. Natomiast jednocześnie Pan mówił tutaj o przyspieszeniu celów klimatycznych. Ja chciałbym zrozumieć Pana wypowiedź. Czy Pan uważa, że przyspieszenie celów klimatycznych w Europie ma pomóc przemysłowi motoryzacyjnemu? Czy ja dobrze Pana rozumiem? Czy jednak właśnie my powinniśmy podejść do tego w sposób bardziej pragmatyczny i cele, które Państwo wyznaczyli jeszcze niedawno na tej sali, są de facto powodem, dla którego przemysł motoryzacyjny ma takie kłopoty w Europie (między innymi zakaz rejestracji samochodów spalinowych od 2035 roku).
2-0018-0000.englishText: Dear Mr. Member, you are saying here that the automotive industry is in a difficult situation. I agree with you absolutely. However, at the same time, you were talking here about accelerating climate goals. I would like to understand your statement. Do you think that accelerating climate goals in Europe is supposed to help the automotive industry? Did I understand you correctly? Or rather, should we approach this in a more pragmatic way, and the goals that you set not long ago in this chamber are de facto the reason why the automotive industry is in such trouble in Europe (among other things, the ban on the registration of combustion engine cars from 2035)?

2-0019-0000.sourceText: (PPE), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ich glaube, offensichtlich haben Sie mich da missverstanden. Ich habe nicht gesagt, dass wir die Klimaziele beschleunigen müssen, sondern ich habe gesagt, dass wir technologieoffen sein müssen und praxisgerechte Möglichkeiten finden müssen, die Transformation zu gewährleisten. Das heißt, keine Beschleunigung, sondern an den Zielen festhalten, aber einen Mix an Möglichkeiten und einen Wettbewerb der Technologien zulassen. Insofern ist das, glaube ich, ein Ansatz, den wir gemeinsam vertreten können.
2-0019-0000.englishText: (PPE), answering a question under the "blue card" procedure. – I believe you obviously misunderstood me there. I did not say that we must accelerate the climate targets, but rather that we must be open to technology and find practical ways to ensure the transformation. That means no acceleration, but sticking to the targets while allowing a mix of options and a competition of technologies. In that respect, I believe this is an approach that we can jointly support.

2-0020-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Es ist doch auf jeden Fall klar, dass die Beschäftigten diese Krise nicht verursacht haben. Kommissar Séjourné hat das gesagt – wir haben es hier auch mit massiven Managementfehlern zu tun, die wir hier nicht verschweigen können, und gleichzeitig auch mit einem Mangel an Innovationsfähigkeit. Und wenn wir da ran wollen, müssen wir mit dem Industriebeschleuniger beschleunigen.

Wir brauchen ein made in Europe, und das brauchen wir relativ schnell. Und noch mal: Wenn man jetzt aufgrund der Fehler, die im Management begangen wurden, die Arbeitnehmer und Arbeitnehmerinnen die Zeche zahlen lässt, dann ist das doch schändlich.

Wir haben bislang auch als EU nicht geliefert mit dem Versprechen der fairen Übergänge. Hier muss nachgerüstet werden; alle Maßnahmen zur Unterstützung der Beschäftigten. Wir haben SURE; wir haben die Erfahrung, dass es funktioniert. Sind wir ready hier, um das einzusetzen? Auch wenn wir öffentliche Gelder geben, dann nicht ohne Konditionen. Gute Arbeit, tarifvertragliche Lösungen finden für diese Krise – das ist das Gebot der Stunde.
2-0020-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is in any case clear that the employees did not cause this crisis. Commissioner Séjourné said so – we are also dealing here with massive management errors that we cannot conceal, and at the same time with a lack of capacity for innovation. And if we want to tackle that, we must accelerate with the industrial accelerator.

We need a "made in Europe", and we need it relatively quickly. And again: if workers are now made to pay the price because of the mistakes made by management, then that is shameful.

So far, the EU has also failed to deliver on the promise of fair transitions. Remedial action is needed here; all measures to support employees. We have SURE; we have the experience that it works. Are we ready here to use that? Even when we provide public funds, then not without conditions. Good work, finding collective bargaining solutions for this crisis – that is the imperative of the hour.

2-0021-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, sono allibito dal fatto che in quest'Aula nessuno si ponga la domanda se l'elettrico a tutti i costi possa essere compatibile con quelli che sono i limiti in termini di generazione elettrica.

Se noi analizziamo il contesto, abbiamo un mercato americano chiuso alla Cina, una domanda interna cinese in stagnazione e, dall'altra parte, l'Europa che è diventata valvola di sfogo, terreno di conquista, per la sovraccapacità industriale di Pechino.

Per cui, il titolo di questo dibattito mi sembra suoni un po' come se fosse una beffa: si parla di posti di lavoro di qualità, ma qua è già tanto se di posti di lavoro ne rimarrà qualcuno. Ricordo che tra qualche giorno Volkswagen valuterà un piano industriale che prevede il taglio di 100 000 posti di lavoro e la chiusura di quattro stabilimenti.

Allora, a questo punto, io mi chiedo se qui ci sia nessuno che pensa che un prezzo vada pagato, ma, soprattutto: vi sentite tutti sereni? C'è nessuno che si sente responsabile?
2-0021-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, I am appalled by the fact that in this House no one is asking whether all-out electric vehicles can be compatible with the limits in terms of electricity generation.

If we analyse the context, we have an American market closed to China, stagnant Chinese domestic demand and, on the other hand, Europe which has become a safety valve, a conquest ground, for Beijing's industrial overcapacity.

Therefore, the title of this debate sounds a bit like a mockery to me: we talk about quality jobs, but here we are lucky if any jobs are left at all. I recall that in a few days Volkswagen will evaluate an industrial plan that involves cutting 100 000 jobs and closing four plants.

So, at this point, I wonder if anyone here thinks that a price must be paid, but above all: do you all feel at ease? Is there anyone who feels responsible?

2-0022-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Sektor motoryzacyjny jest niezwykle ważny dla całej Europy. Wiemy doskonale, jak wyglądają łańcuchy dostaw, jak wiele państw członkowskich jest zaangażowanych w ten przemysł, jeżeli chodzi o możliwości zarobkowania właśnie na nim. Dziwię się więc dzisiaj na tej sali, gdy słucham tej dyskusji, ponieważ mam wrażenie, że właściwie nic nie da się zrobić. To znaczy wy uważacie, że na przykład cele klimatyczne do 2040 roku – 90% – mają pomóc przemysłowi motoryzacyjnemu, że zakaz rejestracji samochodów spalinowych od 2035 roku ma pomóc naszemu przemysłowi. Czy to, że ceny energii w Europie mamy dwa, trzy razy wyższe niż w Stanach Zjednoczonych czy Chinach, to ma pomóc temu sektorowi?

Dzisiaj na tej sali mam wrażenie, że wiele osób uważa, że wszystko jest w porządku. I będziecie mówić o pomocy publicznej dla zakładów, a ja wolałbym, żebyście dzisiaj powiedzieli o rezygnacji z celów klimatycznych tych wysokich, które w tej chwili są, o likwidacji ETSu, o likwidacji zakazu rejestracji samochodów spalinowych po 2035 roku. To trzeba zrobić, bo inaczej europejski przemysł samochodowy po prostu upadnie.
2-0022-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The automotive sector is extremely important for the whole of Europe. We know very well what supply chains look like, how many Member States are involved in this industry when it comes to the earning opportunities it provides. I am therefore surprised today in this hall when I listen to this discussion, because I have the impression that actually nothing can be done. That is to say, you believe that, for example, the climate targets for 2040 – 90% – are supposed to help the automotive industry, that the ban on the registration of combustion engine cars from 2035 is supposed to help our industry. Does the fact that energy prices in Europe are two or three times higher than in the United States or China help this sector?

Today in this hall I have the impression that many people think everything is fine. And you will talk about state aid for plants, but I would prefer it if today you spoke about abandoning the high climate targets that currently exist, about abolishing the ETS, about abolishing the ban on the registration of combustion engine cars after 2035. That needs to be done, because otherwise the European automotive industry will simply collapse.

2-0023-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Hunderttausende Jobs bei Autobauern und Zulieferern sind in Gefahr, weil wir derzeit in Europa nicht wettbewerbsfähig sind. Und, liebe Freundinnen und Freunde, die bisherigen Regeln, die wir haben, nämlich das Verbrenner-Aus in 2035, verschärfen die Krise bei den Autobauern. Die Zukunft ist elektrisch – ja, aber sie kommt nicht so schnell, wie sich das hier einige gedacht haben, und sie wird auch nicht zu 100 Prozent elektrisch sein.

Unsere Regeln, die wir uns gegeben haben, sind nicht flexibel genug; sie strangulieren heute unsere Automobilindustrie. Deshalb brauchen wir mehr Flexibilität. Nicht alle Vorschläge, die die Kommission vorgelegt hat, sind diesem Ziel gewidmet, aber ich glaube, dass wir im Rahmen des parlamentarischen Verfahrens daran arbeiten können, diese Flexibilität, die vorgeschlagen wurde von der Kommission, noch zu erweitern.

Wir brauchen Technologieoffenheit, damit wir alternative Kraftstoffe zur CO2‑Reduktion in Europa nutzen können.
2-0023-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues! Hundreds of thousands of jobs at car manufacturers and suppliers are at risk because we are currently not competitive in Europe. And, dear friends, the rules we have had up to now, namely the phase-out of the internal combustion engine in 2035, are exacerbating the crisis for car manufacturers. The future is electric – yes, but it is not coming as fast as some people here thought it would, and it will not be 100 percent electric either.

Our rules that we have set for ourselves are not flexible enough; today they are strangulating our automotive industry. That is why we need more flexibility. Not all the proposals presented by the Commission are dedicated to this goal, but I believe that within the framework of the parliamentary procedure we can work on expanding this flexibility proposed by the Commission.

We need technological openness so that we can use alternative fuels for CO2 reduction in Europe.

2-0024-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar! Der Verbrennermotor – das war große und gute Ingenieurskunst, und darauf können die Beschäftigten in der Automobilindustrie stolz sein. Aber ganz ehrlich – der Verbrennermotor, das war einmal. Dass Volkswagen und Bosch und viele Arbeitsplätze streichen, liegt daran, dass wir bei der Umstellung auf die E‑Mobilität nicht schnell genug sind, dass die anderen uns die Butter vom Brot nehmen.

Seit 2017 sinken die Absatzzahlen von Verbrennermotoren – seit 2017 um 30 %. Und selbst in Deutschland werden heute mehr Elektroautos verkauft als Benziner. Ihr nostalgisches Festhalten am Verbrennermotor zerstört letztlich Arbeitsplätze, denn die Autos der Zukunft, die sind elektrisch, die sind digital, die sind bezahlbar; und entweder wir bauen sie, oder sie werden in China gebaut und bei uns schließen die Fabriken.

Wir können Weltklasseautos bauen – das haben wir 100 Jahre lang gezeigt; aber für Weltklasse muss man zehn Jahre in die Zukunft schauen und nicht 50 Jahre in den Rückspiegel.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0024-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner! The internal combustion engine – that was great and good engineering, and the workers in the automotive industry can be proud of that. But quite honestly – the internal combustion engine is a thing of the past. The fact that Volkswagen and Bosch and many others are cutting jobs is because we are not fast enough in switching to e-mobility, because others are taking the bread out of our mouths.

Since 2017, sales figures for internal combustion engines have been falling – down 30% since 2017. And even in Germany today, more electric cars are sold than petrol cars. Your nostalgic clinging to the internal combustion engine is ultimately destroying jobs, because the cars of the future are electric, they are digital, they are affordable; and either we build them, or they are built in China and our factories close.

We can build world-class cars – we have proven that for 100 years; but for world-class, you have to look ten years into the future and not 50 years into the rearview mirror.

(The speaker agreed to answer a "blue card" procedure question.)

2-0025-0000.sourceText:
Quería compartir con usted si considera que lo que necesitamos, teniendo en cuenta la normativa que tenemos en tramitación, es realmente un acompañamiento mayor a nuestras empresas, una definición clara del «Made in Europe», única y armonizada, fácil de aplicar y, sobre todo, fácil de auditar, y, sobre todo, que cualquier definición de origen deba ser clara, estable y fácilmente verificable.

Asimismo, creo que necesitamos unas condiciones marco que favorezcan la inversión industrial en Europa, promoviendo así empleos de calidad. Y también si considera usted que debemos reforzar el desarrollo de cadenas de valor estratégicas europeas, especialmente en el ámbito de las baterías, como manera de conseguir blindar el coche eléctrico.
2-0025-0000.englishText:
I wanted to share with you whether you consider that what we need, taking into account the regulations we have in the pipeline, is truly greater support for our businesses, a clear definition of "Made in Europe" that is unique and harmonized, easy to apply and, above all, easy to audit, and, above all, that any origin definition must be clear, stable and easily verifiable.

Likewise, I believe we need framework conditions that favor industrial investment in Europe, thereby promoting quality jobs. And also whether you consider that we must strengthen the development of European strategic value chains, especially in the field of batteries, as a way to manage to shield the electric car.

2-0026-0000.sourceText:
Thank you very much. What I think is that we see an amazing rise of the sales of electric cars in Europe, much better than expected: 40 % growth rates.

And in this very moment, to cut down on our legislation, it just doesn't make sense. I mean, the market is much further than the right part of this House. So, there's the first mistake: we are acting against the market.

The second is we want to be naive and stay in the old world. China is doing a lot of industrial policy to strengthen its electromobility and its battery sector. Europe should do the same. If we don't do it, we will lose our industry.

2-0027-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, 50 000, c’est le nombre d’emplois détruits dans l’automobile en France depuis 2017. Si nous ne faisons rien, ce sont des milliers d’autres qui vont être sacrifiés demain. Voilà la réalité du séisme qui frappe notre industrie, et plus nous tardons à réagir, plus la facture sera lourde à payer pour toute notre société. Je parle ici de toute notre société, car, n’en déplaise à la droite et à l’extrême droite de cet hémicycle, face au dérèglement climatique, aux canicules qui s’enchaînent, la transition électrique n’est plus négociable. C’est une urgence vitale, alors que 30 % de nos émissions dépendent directement du secteur du transport.

Donc oui, il faut investir massivement, mais évidemment pas pour alimenter la spéculation, comme nous avons pu le voir: l’argent public doit servir vraiment à protéger les salariés, à transformer notre industrie et pas à enrichir des actionnaires. Pour réussir, il faut évidemment un bouclier, un véritable «made in Europe» dans l’automobile, afin de maîtriser nos batteries et nos technologies. En ce sens, les plans actuels ne vont pas assez loin sur la préférence locale et sur l’aide à l’acquisition de véhicules abordables électriques pour tous les citoyens. Donc, il faut sortir de ces logiques mortifères du libre-échange et vraiment protéger notre marché et notre industrie.
2-0027-0000.englishText:
Madam President, 50,000 is the number of jobs destroyed in the automotive sector in France since 2017. If we do nothing, thousands more will be sacrificed tomorrow. This is the reality of the earthquake hitting our industry, and the longer we delay in reacting, the heavier the bill will be for our entire society. I am speaking here of our entire society, because, with all due respect to the right and the far right in this hemicycle, in the face of climate change and successive heatwaves, the electric transition is no longer negotiable. It is a vital urgency, given that 30% of our emissions depend directly on the transport sector.

So yes, we must invest massively, but obviously not to fuel speculation, as we have been able to see: public money must truly serve to protect workers, to transform our industry, and not to enrich shareholders. To succeed, we obviously need a shield, a true "made in Europe" in the automotive sector, in order to master our batteries and our technologies. In this sense, current plans do not go far enough regarding local preference and aid for the acquisition of affordable electric vehicles for all citizens. Therefore, we must break away from these lethal logics of free trade and truly protect our market and our industry.

2-0028-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, peut-être un mot pour vous dire que l’objectif est bien de stopper l’hémorragie et de repositionner notre industrie sur un secteur de l’avenir, de l’innovation, avec des conditions de compétitivité, y compris à l’international, qui sont améliorées.

Quelques messages sur les propositions de la Commission: nous avons proposé d’avoir une définition d’une voiture européenne pour pouvoir discriminer positivement, quand il y a engagement de l’argent public européen, dans le cadre des marchés publics, dans le cadre des subventions à l’achat, pour qu’il y ait une préférence d’achat européenne à partir du moment où le consommateur souhaite bénéficier de cette fiscalité particulière.

Je trouve normal aujourd’hui, au vu du constat que vous faites toutes et tous ici, dans cet hémicycle, que l’argent public qui est prélevé par l’impôt puisse profiter avant tout à la création de la demande, en Europe, sur des segments particuliers, notamment sur les segments des véhicules électriques. C’est la proposition que nous avons faite, avec 70 % de composants européens dans une voiture électrique (hors batterie), avec 50 % de composants européens pour la chaîne de propulsion électrique et 50 % de composants européens pour l’électronique.

Voilà la proposition qui est sur la table, sur laquelle vous devez débattre, mais qui est une partie de la solution que nous vous proposons – pas toute la solution, mais une partie de la solution qu’on vous propose dans le cadre de ce texte.

Encore un dernier message: il faut absolument que ce texte puisse arriver à destination le plus rapidement possible – et l’urgence de la situation démontre que le vote de l’accélérateur industriel est aussi une question d’urgence pour le secteur de l’automobile.
2-0028-0000.englishText:
Madam President, perhaps a word to tell you that the objective is indeed to stop the bleeding and reposition our industry in a sector of the future, of innovation, with improved competitiveness conditions, including internationally.

A few messages regarding the Commission's proposals: we have proposed having a definition of a European car in order to be able to positively discriminate, when European public money is committed, within the framework of public procurement, within the framework of purchase subsidies, so that there is a European purchase preference from the moment the consumer wishes to benefit from this particular taxation.

I find it normal today, given the observation that all of you are making here, in this hemicycle, that the public money collected through taxes can benefit above all the creation of demand, in Europe, on particular segments, notably on electric vehicle segments. This is the proposal we have made, with 70% European components in an electric car (excluding the battery), with 50% European components for the electric propulsion chain and 50% European components for electronics.

Here is the proposal on the table, which you must debate, but which is part of the solution we are proposing to you – not the whole solution, but a part of the solution we are proposing to you within the framework of this text.

One last message: this text absolutely must reach its destination as quickly as possible – and the urgency of the situation demonstrates that the vote on the industrial accelerator is also a matter of urgency for the automotive sector.

2-0029-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, meine Damen und Herren! Die Kommission sorgt sich um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit unserer Autoindustrie, um die Sicherung von Arbeitsplätzen. Im Ernst? Wer hat denn diese großartige Industrie an die Wand gefahren? Warum stecken unsere Betriebe in der tiefsten Krise ihrer Geschichte? Warum werden Zigtausende von Arbeitnehmern entlassen? Das ist doch das Ergebnis auch Ihrer Politik. Sie haben sich angemaßt, in einen Markt einzugreifen, der funktioniert hat: Es gab Autos für jeden Geldbeutel, für jeden Zweck, für jeden Geschmack. Aber jetzt stellt sich Frau von der Leyen hin und verlangt, dass kleine Batterieautos gebaut werden.

Politiker haben unseren Unternehmern nicht vorzuschreiben, welche Autos sie bauen sollen. Politiker haben einen Rahmen für den Markt zu schaffen, mehr aber auch nicht. Jetzt werden in Deutschland Werke geschlossen, Arbeitsplätze abgebaut, die Produktion nach China und in die USA verlagert. Sieht so das Erfolgsmodell in Europa aus? Nein! Diese Kommission setzt auf Weltrettung statt auf Marktwirtschaft. Sie setzt auf Verbote statt auf Technologieoffenheit. Sie setzt auf faule Kompromisse statt auf faire Rahmenbedingungen und treibt die Energiepreise in Höhen, die jeden Wettbewerb abwürgen.

Noch ist es nicht zu spät. Noch können allein in Deutschland 50 000 Arbeitsplätze gerettet werden, wenn Sie sich vom Verbrenner-Aus verabschieden. Verabschieden Sie sich von grünen Träumereien, denn mit dem Kampf gegen unsere Industrie ändern Sie nicht das Weltklima, Sie verschlechtern nur das Investitionsklima. Europa ist zur No-go-Area für Innovation geworden, und das ist leider auch Ihre Schuld.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0029-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! The Commission is concerned about the competitiveness of our automotive industry, about securing jobs. Seriously? Who drove this great industry into the ground? Why are our businesses in the deepest crisis in their history? Why are tens of thousands of employees being laid off? That is also the result of your policy. You presumed to intervene in a market that was functioning: there were cars for every budget, for every purpose, for every taste. But now Ms von der Leyen stands up and demands that small battery cars be built.

Politicians have no business dictating to our entrepreneurs which cars they should build. Politicians are supposed to create a framework for the market, nothing more. Now plants are being closed in Germany, jobs are being cut, production is being relocated to China and the USA. Does this look like a success model in Europe? No! This Commission relies on saving the world instead of a market economy. It relies on bans instead of technological openness. It relies on rotten compromises instead of fair framework conditions and drives energy prices to heights that stifle any competition.

It is not too late yet. 50,000 jobs in Germany alone can still be saved if you abandon the ban on the internal combustion engine. Abandon green daydreams, because by fighting our industry you are not changing the global climate, you are only worsening the investment climate. Europe has become a no-go area for innovation, and unfortunately that is also your fault.

(The speaker agreed to answer a blue-card question.)

2-0030-0000.sourceText:
Cher Monsieur, vous nous parlez d’économie de marché, mais n’avez-vous pas l’impression que l’économie de marché, justement, elle donne la victoire aux véhicules électriques, aujourd’hui? Vous parlez d’économie de marché, mais en fait vous niez la réalité même du marché.

Vous parlez par ailleurs d’énergie, d’énergie de plus en plus chère, et vous défendez le fait qu’on continue à acheter cette énergie cher plutôt que de passer à une énergie qui nous permet d’avoir notre souveraineté et un prix moins cher – et qui est l’électricité.

Il y a là deux paradoxes qu’il me semble simplement impossible de justifier.
2-0030-0000.englishText:
Dear Sir, you talk to us about a market economy, but do you not have the impression that the market economy precisely gives the victory to electric vehicles today? You talk about a market economy, but in fact you deny the very reality of the market.

You also talk about energy, energy that is increasingly expensive, and you defend the fact that we continue to buy this energy at a high price rather than switching to an energy that allows us to have our sovereignty and a cheaper price -- which is electricity.

There are two paradoxes here that it seems simply impossible to justify.

2-0031-0000.sourceText:
(ESN), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank für die Frage. Sie gestatten mir, dass ich wieder auf Deutsch antworte.

Natürlich gibt der Markt auch einen Markt für Elektroautos her; das ist überhaupt gar keine Frage. Wir haben auch nie abgelehnt, dass es Elektroautos geben soll, aber wir haben immer gesagt, es muss beide oder mehrere Antriebsformen geben. Denn Elektroautos eignen sich für viele Zwecke – der Herr Kommissar hat es ja auch gesagt, für Taxen, zum Beispiel, für Kurierdienste, für die Post – sehr, sehr gut, aber sie eignen sich eben nicht für alle. Und der Erfolg, der angebliche Erfolg, liegt ja auch an den Subventionen, an hohen Subventionen, mit denen der Staat in den Markt eingegriffen hat. Und das ist keine Marktwirtschaft, das ist Planwirtschaft, und die lehnen wir ab.
2-0031-0000.englishText:
(ESN), Answer to a question under the "blue card" procedure. – Thank you very much for the question. You will allow me to answer in German again.

OfQtCore, the market also produces a market for electric cars; there is absolutely no question about that. We have also never rejected the idea that there should be electric cars, but we have always said that there must be both or multiple forms of propulsion. Because electric cars are very, very well suited for many purposes – the Commissioner also said so, for taxis, for example, for courier services, for the postal service – but they are simply not suited for all of them. And the success, the alleged success, is also due to subsidies, high subsidies with which the state has intervened in the market. And that is not a market economy, that is a planned economy, and we reject that.

2-0032-0000.sourceText: Vážená pani predsedajúca. Už hodinu tu rečníme o urgentných opatreniach na záchranu pracovných miest v automobilovom priemysle, ktorý vždy patril k pilierom európskej ekonomiky. No za posledné roky musel Stellantis pozastaviť linky v Poissy, Eisenachu či ďalších miestach. Audi kompletne zatvorilo závod v Bruseli. Mercedes prerušuje výrobu svojho elektronického GLC v Bremene. A Volkswagen po prvýkrát v histórii zvažuje zatvorenie až štyroch nemeckých výrobní, čo by znamenalo prepustenie 100 tisíc ľudí. Toto nie sú náhodné problémy ani dočasné ťažkosti prechodu na elektromobilitu. Je to dôsledok toho, že európska výroba už nie je konkurencieschopná, a kľúčovou príčinou, o ktorej tu dnes takmer vôbec nepočuť, je drahá elektrická energia – dvakrát drahšia ako v Spojených štátoch a o viac ako polovicu drahšia oproti Číne. Prečo je taká drahá? Pretože politika Európskej komisie, ideologický tlak na zelenú transformáciu bez ohľadu na cenu a spoľahlivosť, nás pripravila o lacnú a stabilnú energiu. A namiesto toho, aby sme to tu dnes riešili – túto prapríčinu – tak si tu tlieskame, ako míňame miliardy, ktoré nemáme na rekvalifikáciu prepustených observatória či dotácie na batérie. Prosím vás, prestaňme už donekonečna riešiť symptómy a začnime riešiť príčiny. Ďakujem.
2-0032-0000.englishText: Madam President. For an hour now we have been speaking here about urgent measures to save jobs in the automotive industry, which has always been one of the pillars of the European economy. But in recent years, Stellantis has had to suspend lines in Poissy, Eisenach and other places. Audi has completely closed its plant in Brussels. Mercedes is interrupting the production of its electronic GLC in Bremen. And Volkswagen, for the first time in history, is considering closing as many as four German manufacturing plants, which would mean laying off 100 thousand people. These are not accidental problems or temporary difficulties of the transition to electromobility. It is a consequence of the fact that European production is no longer competitive, and the key cause, which is hardly heard about here today at all, is expensive electricity - twice as expensive as in the United States and more than half as expensive compared to China. Why is it so expensive? Because the policy of the European Commission, the ideological pressure for the green transformation regardless of price and reliability, has deprived us of cheap and stable energy. And instead of solving this here today - this root cause - we are applauding ourselves here for how we are spending billions that we do not have on the retraining of laid-off observers or subsidies for batteries. Please, let's stop endlessly addressing the symptoms and let's start addressing the causes. Thank you.

2-0033-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, ¿hasta cuándo vamos a asistir, resignados, al declive del emblema de la industria europea?

La situación que vive hoy el sector de la automoción en Europa es la consecuencia de años de muchos errores; también años de errores políticos, años de obligaciones imposibles, objetivos inalcanzables, costes energéticos inasumibles y también trabas administrativas inaceptables. Frente a eso, una consecuencia —un resultado—: la incertidumbre que vive hoy el sector y los cierres y despidos que estamos conociendo.

Sin embargo, la Comisión ha presentado —y están en tramitación parlamentaria— dos iniciativas que nos pueden ayudar a revertir esta situación. La primera de ellas es el paquete de la automoción, una iniciativa que va en la buena dirección, pero que, para ser realmente útil y eficaz, debe colocar los principios de flexibilidad y neutralidad tecnológica como eje fundamental en su planificación y desarrollo, sin subordinación, por cierto, a otros principios climáticos. La segunda de ellas es el acelerador industrial, una herramienta que nos va a servir para acelerar inversiones estratégicas, para reducir trabas administrativas, pero, sobre todo, para hacer posible que invertir, que producir, en Europa sea una ventaja competitiva, sea un valor añadido y nunca un lastre para nuestras empresas.

Europa necesita hoy más que nunca una industria fuerte, innovadora, capaz de crecer, de crear empleo, respaldada por las instituciones públicas. Si no, es imposible que podamos hablar ni de autonomía estratégica ni de Estado de bienestar, ni tampoco de generación de empleo.
2-0033-0000.englishText:
Madam President, how much longer are we going to passively witness the decline of the emblem of European industry?

The situation facing the automotive sector in Europe today is the consequence of years of many mistakes; also years of political errors, years of impossible obligations, unattainable targets, unaffordable energy costs, and also unacceptable administrative hurdles. Faced with this, a consequence — a result —: the uncertainty the sector is experiencing today and the closures and layoffs we are witnessing.

However, the Commission has presented — and they are undergoing parliamentary procedure — two initiatives that can help us reverse this situation. The first of these is the automotive package, an initiative that goes in the right direction, but which, to be truly useful and effective, must place the principles of flexibility and technological neutrality as a fundamental axis in its planning and development, without subordination, incidentally, to other climate principles. The second of these is the industrial accelerator, a tool that will serve us to accelerate strategic investments, to reduce administrative hurdles, but, above all, to make it possible for investing, for producing, in Europe to be a competitive advantage, to be an added value and never a burden for our companies.

Europe needs today more than ever a strong, innovative industry, capable of growing, of creating jobs, backed by public institutions. If not, it is impossible for us to speak either of strategic autonomy or of the welfare state, nor of job creation either.

2-0034-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule Séjourné, sunteți vicepreședintele Comisiei Europene și astăzi sunteți prezent la o dezbatere extrem de importantă despre industria producătoare de automobile din Uniunea Europeană. Astăzi, când vorbim, în România, Dacia a anunțat primele concedieri colective din ultimii 22 de ani. Este un simptom care arată cât de gravă este situația industriei producătoare de automobile și părți pentru coindustria de automobile în România și în Uniunea Europeană, aceeași situație. De ce este asta și ce așteaptă de la noi cei care se uită cu mare îngrijorare? Pentru că dacă această coloană vertebrală este bolnavă - industria producătoare de automobile - economia Uniunii Europene este într-o situație foarte proastă.

Certificate de dioxid de carbon: în România plătim 80 de euro tona de certificate de dioxid de carbon, în China de șapte ori mai puțin. Nu este, evident, o lipsă de competitivitate? Și eu cred că primele măsuri care ar trebui să fie luate, luați în vedere, nu știu, alocări de certificate gratuite de dioxid de carbon, pentru a aduce la același nivel competitivitatea.

Poate ca toți cei care nu plătesc niciun fel de taxe la importul de mașini în Uniunea Europeană să fie supus reglementării CBAM și eu cred că toate aceste lucruri trebuie făcute acum, când nu este prea târziu.
2-0034-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Séjourné, you are Vice-President of the European Commission and today you are present at an extremely important debate on the automotive manufacturing industry in the European Union.

Today, as we speak, in Romania, Dacia has announced its first collective layoffs in the last 22 years. This is a symptom showing how serious the situation of the automotive manufacturing industry and parts for the automotive co-industry is in Romania and in the European Union—the same situation. Why is this and what are those who are watching with great concern expecting from us? Because if this backbone is sick—the automotive manufacturing industry—the European Union's economy is in a very bad situation.

Carbon dioxide certificates: in Romania we pay 80 euros per tonne of carbon dioxide certificates, in China seven times less. Is this obviously not a lack of competitiveness? And I believe that the first measures that should be taken, taken into consideration, I don't know, allocations of free carbon dioxide certificates, to bring competitiveness to the same level.

Maybe all those who do not pay any kind of taxes on the import of cars into the European Union should be subject to the CBAM regulation and I believe that all these things must be done now, when it is not too late.

2-0035-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, llevo siete años hablando con dureza, pero con respeto, de las políticas ruinosas de Europa en materia de automóvil.

Estamos hartos, hartos de la Comisión, hartos hasta las narices de ese discursito de descarbonización, transición, resiliencia y objetivos climáticos. Cada mes, en Estrasburgo, hay un debate sobre el sector del automóvil y cada mes los datos de producción caen en toda Europa.

Europa hizo la revolución industrial, cambió el mundo, cambiamos la producción y la vida de millones de personas. La historia de nuestra industria es una historia de innovación, de adaptación y crecimiento. Y ustedes, la pasada legislatura, lo destruyeron todo. Nuestros coches —los mejores del planeta— dominaban los mercados mundiales. Era empleo, riqueza, clases medias, democratización del movimiento. Ahora China produce más del 90 % de las baterías eléctricas y traslada su producción a Marruecos y Turquía para utilizar las operaciones triangulares y entrar en nuestro mercado con mejores condiciones.

Esta es la realidad y ustedes son culpables del cierre de empresas, son culpables de 104 000 despidos en los dos últimos años. Yo sueño con el día en que todos ustedes algún día sean responsables y así se declare.
2-0035-0000.englishText:
Madam President, for seven years I have been speaking harshly, but respectfully, about Europe's disastrous automotive policies.

We are fed up, fed up with the Commission, sick to death of that little speech about decarbonisation, transition, resilience and climate targets. Every month in Strasbourg there is a debate on the automotive sector and every month production figures fall across Europe.

Europe made the industrial revolution, changed the world, we changed the production and lives of millions of people. The history of our industry is a history of innovation, adaptation and growth. And you, in the last legislative term, destroyed it all. Our cars—the best on the planet—dominated world markets. It meant employment, wealth, the middle classes, the democratisation of movement. Now China produces more than 90% of electric batteries and is moving its production to Morocco and Turkey to use triangular operations and enter our market under better conditions.

This is the reality and you are to blame for the closure of companies, you are to blame for 104,000 layoffs in the last two years. I dream of the day when all of you will one day be held accountable and declared so.

2-0036-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, nous pouvons dire bravo et merci au groupe politique de M. le commissaire Stéphane Séjourné, ainsi qu’aux différents gouvernements d’Édouard Philippe, puisque, du prix de l’énergie au coût du travail et de l’interdiction des moteurs thermiques en 2035 à la concurrence déloyale chinoise, ses responsables politiques de gauche et du centre ont tout fait méthodiquement pour mettre cette industrie européenne automobile à genoux, avec comme dernière victime en date l’emblématique site de Stellantis à Poissy, qui ne produira plus de voitures neuves à compter de 2028.

Parce que votre pacte vert a abouti à un véritable «Buy China Act»: alors que la Chine avait vingt ans d’avance dans le domaine des véhicules électriques, vous n’avez rien trouvé de mieux que de lui dérouler le tapis rouge en imposant dogmatiquement la fin des moteurs thermiques. Pis, vous persévérez dans l’erreur en refusant de remettre vraiment à plat les objectifs dogmatiques de ce pacte vert. Vous aggravez par là, d’ailleurs, une dépendance étrangère aux hydrocarbures, à une dépendance encore plus concentrée, encore plus critique: celle aux batteries et aux terres rares.

Nous avions en 2019 un excédent commercial automobile de 23 milliards d’euros avec la Chine. Il s’agit aujourd’hui d’un déficit de 6 milliards d’euros, et il y a encore des gens dans cet hémicycle pour se féliciter de cette situation.

(L'oratrice accepte une question carton bleu)
2-0036-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, we can say well done and thank you to the political group of Commissioner Stéphane Séjourné, as well as to the various governments of Édouard Philippe, because, from the price of energy to the cost of labor and the ban on internal combustion engines in 2035 to unfair Chinese competition, its left-wing and center-wing political leaders have methodically done everything to bring this European automotive industry to its knees, with the latest victim to date being the emblematic Stellantis site in Poissy, which will no longer produce new cars as of 2028.

Because your Green Deal has resulted in a genuine "Buy China Act": while China had a twenty-year lead in the field of electric vehicles, you found nothing better than to roll out the red carpet for it by dogmatically imposing the end of internal combustion engines.
