Worse still, you are persisting in your mistake by refusing to truly overhaul the dogmatic objectives of this Green Deal. You are thereby worsening a foreign dependency on hydrocarbons into an even more concentrated, even more critical dependency: that on batteries and rare earths.

In 2019, we had a automotive trade surplus of 23 billion euros with China. Today, this is a deficit of 6 billion euros, and there are still people in this hemicycle to congratulate themselves on this situation.

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

2-0037-0000.sourceText: Madame Marion Maréchal, vous nous parlez de souveraineté. Est-ce que vous pouvez juste me dire quelle est la part du pétrole qu’on produit en France et quelle est la part de l’électricité qu’on produit en France? Ça me semble un sujet important, qu’on veuille passer à l’électrification, ou qu’on veuille, comme vous, rester dépendants du pétrole et refuser l’électrification.
2-0037-0000.englishText: Mrs Marion Maréchal, you speak to us about sovereignty. Could you just tell me what share of the oil we produce in France is and what share of the electricity we produce in France is? That seems to me to be an important subject, whether we want to move to electrification, or whether we want, like you, to remain dependent on oil and refuse electrification.

2-0038-0000.sourceText:
C’est un sujet tout à fait central. Vous avez raison puisque, en effet, des responsables politiques tels que vous ont milité pendant des années pour la loi Hulot, qui interdit toute nouvelle exploration et exploitation des hydrocarbures potentiellement présents sur le sol français, nous privant ainsi d’ailleurs d’une nouvelle part de souveraineté – puisque nous savons que, notamment au large de la Guyane, il y aurait potentiellement des gisements d’hydrocarbures extrêmement importants – et, de ce fait, nous voilà en effet largement dépendants des hydrocarbures étrangers.

Mais, comme je viens de le préciser, le drame avec le «tout électrique» tel que vous l’avez construit, c’est que nous remplaçons une dépendance par une autre, une dépendance encore plus critique, encore plus concentrée, qui est celle aux batteries, qui est celle aux terres rares. D’où le fait, évidemment, que je parle de dogmatisme et que je parle d’idéologie, que paient au premier chef, bien sûr, les employés du secteur automobile.
2-0038-0000.englishText:
This is a completely central subject. You are right, because indeed, political figures such as yourselves campaigned for years for the Hulot law, which bans any new exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbons potentially present on French soil, thereby depriving us of another share of sovereignty—since we know that, particularly off the coast of French Guiana, there are potentially extremely large hydrocarbon deposits—and, as a result, here we are indeed largely dependent on foreign hydrocarbons.

But, as I have just specified, the tragedy with "all-electric" as you have constructed it is that we are replacing one dependency with another, an even more critical, even more concentrated dependency, which is that on batteries, which is that on rare earths. Hence the fact, obviously, that I speak of dogmatism and that I speak of ideology, which are paid for first and foremost, of course, by the employees of the automotive sector.

2-0039-0000.sourceText:
Visiblement, Mme Marion Maréchal ne connaît pas les chiffres, donc je vais les lui expliquer: la part du pétrole qu’on produit en France, c’est 1 %. C’est pas pour des questions de loi Hulot, etc. C’est simplement pour un truc qui s’appelle la géologie: on n’a pas de pétrole en France, et les Français le savent, contrairement à vous.

Par contre, en France, on a l’électricité: on produit plus de 100 % de l’électricité grâce aux renouvelables et grâce au nucléaire. Refuser l’électrification des voitures, c’est refuser de bâtir un système énergétique français, et je suis très, très surpris que vous disiez oui au nucléaire dans vos mots, mais que, quand il s’agit de voter ici, vous alliez contre l’électrification, qui est essentielle pour l’avenir de notre filière nucléaire.
2-0039-0000.englishText:
Clearly, Ms Marion Maréchal does not know the figures, so I am going to explain them to her: the share of oil we produce in France is 1%. It is not because of issues regarding the Hulot law, etc. It is simply because of something called geology: we have no oil in France, and the French people know it, unlike you.

On the other hand, in France, we have electricity: we produce more than 100% of our electricity thanks to renewables and thanks to nuclear power. Refusing the electrification of cars means refusing to build a French energy system, and I am very, very surprised that you say yes to nuclear power in your words, but that, when it comes to voting here, you go against electrification, which is essential for the future of our nuclear industry.

2-0040-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur, je connais parfaitement les chiffres. La seule chose, c’est que j’étais en train de vous expliquer que nous pourrions avoir, contrairement à ce que vous dites, une production d’hydrocarbures français plus importante, mais que nous nous sommes interdit, pour des raisons idéologiques – du fait des Verts, avec le soutien, d’ailleurs, des centristes et de la Macronie –, d’en bénéficier, puisque nous nous sommes même interdit d’explorer la potentialité de ces gisements, dont nous savons d’ailleurs, sur le plan géologique, qu’ils pourraient exister, pas seulement d’ailleurs pour les hydrocarbures, mais également pour le gaz, par exemple, au large de Mayotte. Donc oui, je regrette cela.

Vous avez raison de dire qu’heureusement il y a eu des gens tels que nous, pendant des années, pour défendre le nucléaire, parce que s’il avait fallu compter sur le centre ou sur la gauche, nous aurions mis fin à l’énergie nucléaire française.

Je ne suis pas contre l’industrie automobile électrique, je considère que, en revanche, quand on a une avance technologique telle que la nôtre, avec l’industrie à moteur thermique, c’est évidemment dramatique de la s…

(La Présidente retire la parole à l'oratrice)
2-0040-0000.englishText:
Sir, I know the figures perfectly well. The only thing is that I was explaining to you that we could have, contrary to what you are saying, a larger French hydrocarbon production, but that we banned ourselves, for ideological reasons—because of the Greens, with the support, moreover, of the centrists and the Macron movement—from benefiting from it, since we even banned ourselves from exploring the potential of these deposits, which we know moreover, from a geological standpoint, could exist, not only moreover for hydrocarbons, but also for gas, for example, off Mayotte. So yes, I regret that.

You are right to say that fortunately there were people like us, for years, to defend nuclear power, because if we had had to rely on the center or the left, we would have put an end to French nuclear energy.

I am not against the electric car industry, I consider that, on the other hand, when you have a technological lead like ours, with the internal combustion engine industry, it is obviously dramatic to s…

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone)

2-0041-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je ne rentrerai pas dans le débat, et je crois qu’il ne me reste que très peu de temps de parole. D’abord, peut-être, quelques éléments pour étayer l’impact, notamment de la Chine, sur le marché de l’automobile. Les conséquences pour notre industrie automobile sont catastrophiques et présentes un peu partout en Europe. Ce n’est pas qu’un débat allemand, c’est un débat pour l’ensemble des Européens sur l’ensemble des chaînes de valeur. Et vous avez une industrie allemande très forte, mais vous avez aussi une industrie, des équipementiers, des sous-traitants, très présents, partout en Europe, qui alimentent l’industrie automobile.

En Europe – que ce soit en Italie, par exemple, où plus de la moitié du marché hybride rechargeable est dominé par des modèles chinois, ou en Allemagne aussi, où le premier bénéficiaire des aides publiques nationales est aujourd’hui BYD –, nous avons construit un modèle qui finance des constructeurs chinois. Ce que nous vous proposons, avec la loi d’accélération de l’industrie, c’est de revenir là-dessus et de privilégier justement la préférence européenne, le made in Europe, quand il s’agit d’argent public européen.
2-0041-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I will not enter into the debate, and I believe I have very little speaking time left. First, perhaps, a few elements to substantiate the impact, notably of China, on the automotive market. The consequences for our automotive industry are catastrophic and present almost everywhere in Europe. This is not just a German debate, it is a debate for all Europeans across all value chains. And you have a very strong German industry, but you also have an industry, equipment manufacturers, subcontractors, very present everywhere in Europe, that supply the automotive industry.

In Europe – whether in Italy, for example, where more than half of the plug-in hybrid market is dominated by Chinese models, or in Germany too, where the primary beneficiary of national public aid today is BYD – we have built a model that finances Chinese manufacturers. What we are proposing to you, with the industrial acceleration law, is to go back on this and precisely prioritize European preference, "made in Europe", when it comes to European public money.

2-0042-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, werte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wer immer und immer und immer wieder die falsche Ausfahrt nimmt, kommt nicht ans Ziel. Über 100 000 Arbeitsplätze sind bereits in der Automobilindustrie verloren gegangen; und das war erst der Anfang. Übrigens, das ist nicht nur in Deutschland, sondern in ganz Europa eine riesige Herausforderung. Das ist eine direkte Folge des Verbrennerverbots, das hier von einer Mehrheit beschlossen wurde. Nun besteht die Chance, diesen Fehler zu überarbeiten.

Wir brauchen die besten Lösungen, nicht politische Besserwisserei, keine Verbote. Unsere Aufgabe ist es, Klimaziele vorzugeben, nicht Antriebsstränge. Arbeitgeber und Gewerkschaften fordern gemeinsam genau diesen Kurs, und trotzdem legen es Grüne und Sozialdemokraten immer nur darauf an, Recht behalten zu wollen. Wenn sich nun die Realität ändert, muss Politik bereit sein, ihre Entscheidungen zu überprüfen. Wer einen Fehler begeht und ihn nicht berichtigt, begeht einen zweiten. Deshalb: Geben wir endlich unseren Ingenieurinnen und Ingenieuren wieder die Chance, die besten Technologien entwickeln zu können.
2-0042-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! Whoever takes the wrong exit over and over and over again will never reach their destination. Over 100,000 jobs have already been lost in the automotive industry, and that was only the beginning. By the way, this is a huge challenge not only in Germany, but across Europe. This is a direct consequence of the combustion engine ban that was decided here by a majority. Now there is the opportunity to revise this mistake.

We need the best solutions, not political know-it-all attitudes, no bans. Our job is to set climate targets, not drive systems. Employers and trade unions are jointly demanding precisely this course, and yet Greens and Social Democrats always just aim to be proven right. When reality changes, politicians must be willing to review their decisions. Anyone who makes a mistake and does not correct it is making a second one. Therefore: Let us finally give our engineers the chance once again to develop the best technologies.

2-0043-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Fiat, FCA, ha perso quasi 50 000 lavoratori tra il 2000 e il 2020, ben prima del Green Deal.

Quindi, l'assenza di politiche industriali europee era già un problema. E cosa abbiamo fatto? Niente.

I nostri competitor investivano in nuove tecnologie? Noi davamo i dividendi agli azionisti, invece di reinvestirli.

Gli stipendi perdevano potere d'acquisto? Si producevano sempre più auto di lusso, perché fanno più profitti.

Aumentava la cassa integrazione? Si delocalizzavano le produzioni per pagare meno.

Quindi, colleghi, fatemi capire: noi siamo qui perché non abbiamo investito, non abbiamo pianificato, non abbiamo capito qual era la direzione del futuro e la vostra soluzione è tornare indietro e fare tutti gli errori del passato?

Dobbiamo investire nelle tecnologie del futuro, diventare esperti nella produzione di batterie e motori elettrici. Dobbiamo supportare la domanda e creare più infrastrutture per la mobilità elettrica, creare un mercato per il made in Europe – però quello vero, quello che riguarda l'Europa, Commissario – dobbiamo investire sulle competenze, formando lavoratori e lavoratrici per la transizione.

Parlate tanto di competitività nell'automotive, ma non volete metterci un euro: se volete aiutare lavoratrici e lavoratori, investite su di loro.
2-0043-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, Fiat, FCA, lost almost 50,000 workers between 2000 and 2020, well before the Green Deal.

So the absence of European industrial policies was already a problem. And what did we do? Nothing.

Were our competitors investing in new technologies? We were giving dividends to shareholders, instead of reinvesting them.

Were salaries losing purchasing power? More and more luxury cars were being produced, because they make more profits.

Was the redundancy fund increasing? Production was being relocated to pay less.

So, colleagues, let me get this straight: we are here because we haven't invested, we haven't planned, we haven't understood what the direction of the future was, and your solution is to go back and make all the mistakes of the past?

We must invest in the technologies of the future, become experts in the production of batteries and electric motors. We must support demand and create more infrastructure for electric mobility, create a market for "made in Europe" - but the real one, the one that concerns Europe, Commissioner - we must invest in skills, training male and female workers for the transition.

You talk so much about competitiveness in the automotive sector, but you don't want to put a euro into it: if you want to help workers, invest in them.

2-0044-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, non voglio ripetere qui cose già dette dai colleghi.

Le sfide che abbiamo davanti sono enormi e serviranno anni, decenni, per recuperare il tempo sprecato, aumentare il potere di acquisto delle persone, rafforzare la competitività dell'auto europea e proteggere i lavoratori.

Possiamo, tuttavia, adottare da subito piccole misure, con grandi effetti: una norma tecnicamente semplice e a costo marginale, prossima allo zero, è lo State of Health – lo stato di salute della batteria – l'indicatore dello stato delle prestazioni che conserva la batteria rispetto a quando era nuova.

Per un veicolo elettrico usato è uno dei principali indicatori del suo valore reale, perché il valore residuo della batteria è più importante dei chilometri percorsi, incide direttamente sul valore dell'auto usata ed è decisivo per le flotte aziendali che, dopo pochi anni, alimentano il mercato dell'usato.

Rendiamo lo State of Health armonizzato, gratuitamente visibile sul display di bordo dell'auto e obbligatorio negli annunci dell'usato. Più trasparenza significa più fiducia, più domanda e quindi più lavoro e industria in Europa.
2-0044-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, I do not want to repeat here things already said by my colleagues.

The challenges we face are enormous and it will take years, decades, to make up for wasted time, increase people's purchasing power, strengthen the competitiveness of the European automotive industry and protect workers.

We can, however, adopt small measures immediately, with great effects: a technically simple rule with marginal cost, close to zero, is the State of Health - the health status of the battery - the indicator of the performance status that the battery retains compared to when it was new.

For a used electric vehicle it is one of the main indicators of its real value, because the residual value of the battery is more important than the kilometres travelled, directly affects the value of the used car and is decisive for company fleets which, after a few years, feed the used market.

Let us make the State of Health harmonized, freely visible on the car's on-board display and mandatory in used car advertisements. More transparency means more trust, more demand and therefore more work and industry in Europe.

2-0045-0000.sourceText:
Szanowna Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Albo uratujemy europejski przemysł motoryzacyjny, albo 14 milionów Europejczyków będzie bezrobotnych, a nasz kontynent stanie się gospodarczą marginalizacją. I wszyscy na tej sali wiemy, doskonale wiemy, że to Europa stworzyła marki samochodów, które od dziesięcioleci, dokładnie od dziesięcioleci, wyznaczają światowe standardy. I dziś nie możemy sobie w żaden sposób pozwolić, aby ten nasz kontynent, nasza Europa, stała się jedynie miejscem zbytu dla pojazdów z Chin i Stanów Zjednoczonych.

Oczywiście musimy inwestować, inwestować w nowoczesne technologie i innowacje, ale też musimy pamiętać o zwykłych obywatelach. To, że kupują chińskie samochody, to tylko dlatego, że są dużo tańsze. Po prostu europejskie samochody dla Europejczyków są zbyt drogie i musimy sobie to też powiedzieć. A skoro jesteśmy przy konkurencyjności, to musimy postawić na niezależność. Nie zamieniajmy dawnego uzależnienia od rosyjskiej ropy na uzależnienie od chińskich baterii i surowców.

I w tym całym zalewie niepokojących informacji mam też dobrą wiadomość. Otóż w Polsce podjęliśmy decyzję – w tym chyba dość trudnym momencie dla całej motoryzacji europejskiej – o budowie pierwszej fabryki pojazdów elektrycznych. W tym roku wbijamy szpadel, rozpoczynamy budowę fabryki, a pierwsze pojazdy zjadą w 2029 roku. Pierwsze 400 tysięcy sztuk. Dlaczego? Dlatego że nie możemy rezygnować z własnych ambicji. Dlatego to robimy. Ale chodzi też o miejsca pracy, o naszą gospodarkę europejską i polską. I udowodnijmy całemu światu, że najlepsza przyszłość motoryzacji wciąż nosi dumną markę Made in Europe.

(Mówca zgodził się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki)
2-0045-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Commissioner! Either we save the European automotive industry, or 14 million Europeans will be unemployed, and our continent will become an economic marginalisation. And all of us in this room know, we know perfectly well, that it was Europe that created car brands which for decades, precisely for decades, have set global standards.
And today we cannot in any way afford for our continent, our Europe, to become merely a sales market for vehicles from China and the United States.

Of course we must invest, invest in modern technologies and innovations, but we must also remember ordinary citizens. The fact that they buy Chinese cars is only because they are much cheaper. Simply put, European cars are too expensive for Europeans, and we must also admit this to ourselves. And while we are on the subject of competitiveness, we must focus on independence. Let us not replace our former dependence on Russian oil with dependence on Chinese batteries and raw materials.

And in this whole flood of disturbing information, I also have good news. Well, in Poland we have made the decision – at this rather difficult time for the entire European automotive sector – to build the first electric vehicle factory. This year we are breaking ground, we are starting the construction of the factory, and the first vehicles will roll off the production line in 2029. The first 400 thousand units. Why? Because we cannot give up our own ambitions. That is why we are doing this. But it is also about jobs, about our European and Polish economy. And let us prove to the whole world that the best future of the automotive industry still bears the proud brand Made in Europe.

(The speaker agreed to a question indicated by the raising of a blue card)

2-0046-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Pośle, to jest ten moment. Ja nawet zgodziłbym się z pańskim wystąpieniem, gdyby nie fakt – co prawda nie pańskiego – ale głosowania w zeszłej kadencji nad sprawami unijnymi, które właśnie blokują i niszczą europejski przemysł.

Więc teraz proste pytanie: czy rekomendowałby Pan Europejskiej Partii Ludowej to samo głosowanie, w taki sam sposób w sprawie ETS2? Czy dzisiaj powiedziałby Pan, że ETS2 należy wyrzucić do kosza?
2-0046-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Mr Member, this is the moment. I would even agree with your speech, were it not for the fact—though not yours, to be fair—of the voting in the last term on EU matters that are precisely blocking and destroying European industry.

So now a simple question: would you recommend the same voting to the European People's Party, in the same way regarding ETS2? Would you say today that ETS2 should be thrown in the trash?

2-0047-0000.sourceText: Rozmawiamy o przemyśle samochodowym. Wydaje mi się, że wszyscy tutaj, jeśli chodzi o polską delegację, byliśmy jednomyślni w tej sprawie. Natomiast, Panie Pośle Ozdoba, Państwo rządziliście 8 lat. Szkoda, że nic nie zrobiliście, chociaż obiecywaliście, że zbudujecie tę fabrykę samochodów, a nawet nie wbiliście przysłowiowego szpadla. Więc dzisiaj, akurat w tym momencie, mógłby Pan nie zabierać głosu na tej sali.
2-0047-0000.englishText: We are talking about the automotive industry. It seems to me that everyone here, as far as the Polish delegation is concerned, was unanimous on this matter. However, Mr Ozdoba, you governed for 8 years. It is a pity that you did nothing, although you promised that you would build this car factory, and you did not even drive the proverbial spade into the ground. So today, at this very moment, you might choose not to speak in this room.

2-0048-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, à 53 ans, mon père, handicapé, s’est retrouvé au chômage. L’usine de composants automobiles où il travaillait avait fermé. L’adolescent que j’étais a connu l’angoisse, les discussions sur l’hypothèque de la maison, la peur de l’avenir. C’est de là que je viens, de cette terre industrielle où nous avons vécu dans notre chair ce que ces licenciements font à nos familles. MPI Lisieux a disparu, mais l’usine Renault Cléon fait encore aujourd’hui travailler plus de 2 500 Normands. Ces emplois, nous pouvons les préserver. Ce qui les sauvera, ce n’est pas la nostalgie de l’extrême droite pour le moteur thermique, car, à Cléon, ce sont les moteurs électriques de la R5 et d’autres modèles électriques de Renault que nos ouvriers fabriquent.

Il est vrai que la Chine les menace. C’est pour ça qu’il faut adopter la préférence européenne, pour que les voitures achetées en Europe soient fabriquées en Europe, construites par des travailleurs européens. L’usine où travaillait mon père a fermé; celle de Cléon, nous pouvons la sauver.
2-0048-0000.englishText:
Madam President, at 53 years old, my disabled father found himself unemployed. The auto parts factory where he worked had closed. The teenager I was experienced the anxiety, the discussions about the house mortgage, the fear of the future. That is where I come from, from this industrial land where we have lived in our flesh what these layoffs do to our families. MPI Lisieux has disappeared, but the Renault Cléon factory still employs more than 2,500 Normands today. These jobs, we can preserve them. What will save them is not the far right's nostalgia for the internal combustion engine, because in Cléon, it is the electric engines of the R5 and other electric models from Renault that our workers are manufacturing.

It is true that China threatens them. That is why we must adopt European preference, so that cars bought in Europe are manufactured in Europe, built by European workers. The factory where my father worked closed; the one in Cléon, we can save it.

2-0049-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, la Commission, en bon pompier pyromane, a allumé l’incendie – avec l’interdiction des moteurs thermiques en 2035 au profit de la Chine –, et la voilà qui prétend l’éteindre avec une petite cuillère. Alors, pour vous donner bonne conscience, vous organisez ici même un énième débat sur la manière de sauver la compétitivité de notre industrie automobile. Mais quel cynisme! Car derrière vos objectifs climatiques, il y a des emplois en jeu. Il y a les salariés de l’usine Stellantis de Poissy et tant d’autres – les sous-traitants, les concessionnaires, les garagistes… –, les familles qui vivent de cette industrie, et qui voient leur avenir partir en fumée à cause de votre obstination. Ils sont en plus obligés d’entendre vos mensonges sur les créations d’emplois liées à l’électrification du parc automobile, mais au prix de combien d’emplois supprimés ailleurs?

Alors, si vous voulez réellement sauver la filière automobile, soyez plus ambitieux dans vos propositions sur la préférence européenne et pour la reconquête de la souveraineté de notre industrie. Car tous ceux qui connaissent bien mieux que vous le secteur l’affirment: il est minuit moins une avant la mort de cette industrie.
2-0049-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the Commission, acting like an arsonist firefighter, started the fire—with the ban on internal combustion engines by 2035 in favor of China—and now claims to put it out with a teaspoon. So, to ease your conscience, you are organizing yet another debate right here on how to save the competitiveness of our automotive industry. But what cynicism! Because behind your climate targets, jobs are at stake. There are the workers of the Stellantis plant in Poissy and so many others—the subcontractors, the dealerships, the mechanics...—the families who live off this industry, and who see their future go up in smoke because of your obstinacy. What is more, they are forced to listen to your lies about job creation linked to the electrification of the vehicle fleet, but at the cost of how many jobs destroyed elsewhere?

So, if you truly want to save the automotive sector, be more ambitious in your proposals on European preference and for the reconquest of our industry's sovereignty. Because all those who know the sector much better than you do state it: it is five to midnight before the death of this industry.

2-0050-0000.sourceText:
Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, k otázce automotive se na tomto fóru vracíme opakovaně. Rád bych připomněl, že to byla právě skupina ECR, kdo jako první tlačil na přijetí rezoluce v době, kdy hrozily evropským automobilkám nesmyslné pokuty. Tlačili jsme i na urychlení změny legislativy směrem ke zrušení zákazu spalovacích motorů po roce 2035 a k nastavení skutečné technologické neutrality. Ne kvůli spalovacím motorům samotným, ale hlavně kvůli tomu, abychom s automobilkami mohli sladit evropská pravidla, a hlavně, aby automobilky mohly dodat zákazníkům to, co od nich chtějí. To znamená kvalitní auta s různými pohony za férové ceny.

Teď se snažíme opravit poslední návrhy Komise a problematická je i automotive část průmyslového akcelerátoru. A o to přesně jde. Buď chceme zachovat vlastní tradiční výrobu a tradiční partnerství se spolehlivými partnery, anebo pod vlajkou klimatické politiky plně otevřeme brány invazi čínských elektromobilů. Já si přeji to první.
2-0050-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear Commissioner, we return to the automotive issue repeatedly in this forum. I would like to recall that it was precisely the ECR group that was the first to push for the adoption of a resolution at a time when European car manufacturers were facing senseless fines. We also pushed for the acceleration of legislative changes towards the cancellation of the ban on combustion engines after 2035 and the establishment of true technological neutrality. Not because of combustion engines themselves, but mainly so that we could align European rules with car manufacturers, and above all, so that car manufacturers could deliver to customers what they want from them. That means quality cars with various propulsion systems at fair prices.

Now we are trying to fix the latest Commission proposals, and the automotive part of the industrial accelerator is also problematic. And that is exactly what it is about. Either we want to preserve our own traditional production and traditional partnership with reliable partners, or under the flag of climate policy we will fully open the gates to the invasion of Chinese electric vehicles. I wish for the former.

2-0051-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, I wrote my PhD dissertation in Wolfsburg in the mid-1990s, on the introduction of flexibility and the four-day workweek at Volkswagen. It was a cyclical crisis that eventually seemed to be overcome.

Today we are talking of a genuine collapse, and the alarm is broader in scope because we are talking of the breakdown of the German social and economic model, the one based on co-determination, high wages, cooperation between capital and labour, and collaborative innovation.

'People's cars' are no longer selling for a variety of reasons. An obsessive push towards electrification without having the necessary infrastructure – how can you fix a goal without the means to reach it? – and the shift in lifestyles and so on and so forth.

So we have the paradox that Germany invested in China hoping to compete with China, but now it will be China that will eventually save Germany buying German enterprises.

So what now? The crisis cannot fall on the shoulders of the workers. It is up to Europe to find a strategy.

2-0052-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues. Europe's automotive sector means more than 13 million jobs. And of course, it's one of our industrial engines. But clearly, that engine cannot run on nostalgia.

The market is changing fast, and one in five cars that has been sold in the EU this year is already battery electric. So our task is clear: to make sure that this transition happens first of all within European factories, with European workers and, of course, with leading European technology. And that means, first of all, cheaper clean energy, charging infrastructure, European batteries, stronger software capacity and real support to European suppliers – because the automotive sector is not only Germany, the automotive sector is Europe as a whole.

Weakening targets is not going to bring competitiveness; it will only create more uncertainty and delay investment. So our answer should be industrial confidence and not industrial fear.

2-0053-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, CEO's zijn in paniek omdat de Europese automobielindustrie aan het verdwijnen is. Maar waar was die paniek toen miljoenen werknemers werden ontslagen? Ik ben er één van. In 2010 raakten duizenden collega's en ikzelf mijn job kwijt nadat Opel Antwerpen sloot. Nadien is het enkel maar verslechterd. Audi Brussel, Van Hool in Lier en nu Volkswagen in Duitsland.

Steeds opnieuw krijgt China de schuld. Maar waar is de eigen verantwoordelijkheid? Winsten werden niet geherinvesteerd. Productie werd verplaatst en subsidies verdwenen in de zakken van aandeelhouders. Van neoliberaal extremisme gesproken.

Nu ziet iedereen wat werknemers en vakbonden al lang zeggen. Dit kon perfect voorkomen worden. Fabrieken hadden een nieuwe bestemming kunnen krijgen, werknemers hadden kunnen worden omgeschoold, jobs hadden hier kunnen blijven en we waren concurrerend geweest.

Nu halen we de industrie terug. Geweldig! Maar wie gaat alle slachtoffers van herstructureringen, delokalisatie en sluitingen compenseren? Dit mogen we nooit meer doen.

Productie moet weer in publieke handen komen. We moeten een economisch langetermijnplan opstellen en investeren in de economie en in onze werknemers.
2-0053-0000.englishText:
Mr President, CEOs are in a panic because the European automotive industry is disappearing. But where was that panic when millions of workers were laid off? I am one of them. In 2010, thousands of colleagues and I lost our jobs after Opel Antwerp closed. Since then, things have only gotten worse. Audi Brussels, Van Hool in Lier, and now Volkswagen in Germany.

Time and again, China is blamed. But where is personal responsibility? Profits were not reinvested. Production was relocated, and subsidies vanished into the pockets of shareholders. Talk about neoliberal extremism.

Now everyone is seeing what workers and trade unions have been saying for a long time. This could easily have been prevented. Factories could have been given a new purpose, workers could have been retrained, jobs could have stayed here, and we would have been competitive.

Now we are bringing industry back. Great! But who is going to compensate all the victims of restructuring, relocation, and closures? We must never let this happen again.

Production must be brought back into public hands. We must draw up a long-term economic plan and invest in the economy and in our workers.

2-0054-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica! V samo dveh letih je v evropski avtomobilski industriji izgubilo službo več kot 100 000 ljudi. To je približno 140 ljudi na dan. 140 družin vsak dan, ki se je soočilo z izgubo službe. In v prihodnjih letih jih lahko pričakujemo samo še več. Zakaj?

Ker smo se odločili vsiliti eno samo tehnologijo in ignorirati realnost. Trinajst milijonov osemsto tisoč Evropejcev je odvisnih od avtomobilske industrije. Lani so različne vrste hibridov prekosile čiste električne avtomobile v prodaji za več kot dva proti ena. Ker ljudje si želijo izbire, ne želijo si ideologije.

Medtem Kitajska nadzoruje že več kot 80 odstotkov svetovnih baterij za električna vozila. Tog pristop „samo elektrika“ ne stane le delovnih mest, ampak nas stane naše industrijske suverenosti in oddaja našo prihodnost drugim. Seveda ne bi smeli biti odvisni od fosilnih goriv, ampak ne smemo zamenjati ene odvisnosti z drugo. In nujen ukrep, ki ga potrebujemo, je tehnološka nevtralnost.

Široko moramo odpreti vrata vsem učinkovitim rešitvam in naj odločata konkurenca in inovacije. In ne vem, zakaj se nekateri tako bojite tega – ker samo tako bomo zaščitili kakovostna delovna mesta, ohranili svetovno priznano evropsko inženirstvo in dejansko dosegli hitrejšo dekarbonizacijo.

Ker naši delavci poganjajo Evropo že generacije in tehnološka svoboda v Evropski uniji ne sme biti le fleksibilnost – mora biti standard. In zdaj imate priložnost, da spremenimo napake, ki so bile storjene in dejansko rešimo evropsko avtomobilsko industrijo.
2-0054-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In just two years, more than 100,000 people have lost their jobs in the European automotive industry. That is approximately 140 people a day. 140 families every day facing job losses. And we can only expect more in the coming years.

Why? Because we decided to impose a single technology and ignore reality. Thirteen million eight hundred thousand Europeans depend on the automotive industry. Last year, various types of hybrids outsold pure electric cars by more than two to one. Because people want choice, they do not want ideology.

Meanwhile, China already controls more than 80 percent of the world's electric vehicle batteries. The rigid "electric-only" approach not only costs jobs, but costs us our industrial sovereignty and hands our future over to others. Of course, we should not be dependent on fossil fuels, but we must not replace one dependency with another. And the urgent measure we need is technological neutrality.

We must open the door wide to all efficient solutions and let competition and innovation decide. And I do not know why some are so afraid of this – because this is the only way we will protect quality jobs, preserve world-renowned European engineering, and actually achieve faster decarbonization.

Because our workers have been driving Europe for generations, and technological freedom in the European Union must not be just flexibility – it must be the standard. And now you have the opportunity to reverse the mistakes that have been made and actually save the European automotive industry.

2-0055-0000.sourceText:
Fru formand! Europas bilindustri står ved en skillevej. Vi kan blive ved med at beskytte fortiden, eller vi kan investere i fremtiden. For mig er valget klart: Vi skal gøre reglerne enklere for den europæiske bilindustri, men uden at svække Europas grønne ambitioner. Hvis de europæiske bilproducenter bliver ved med at hænge fast i gårsdagens teknologi, så taber vi ikke bare endnu mere marked til Kina og USA, vi taber også de gode europæiske arbejdspladser.

Derfor er der brug for, at vi får flere elbiler på de europæiske veje, og mange, mange flere af dem skal bygges i Europa. Og ja, det kan godt være, at den europæiske elbil hverken er bedst eller billigst lige nu, men det bliver den aldrig, hvis ikke vi tør investere ægte i den grønne omstilling. Det handler om, at vi skal styrke vores konkurrenceevne, klimaet og de gode job. For at vi når derhen, kræver det politisk mod, og det mod handler om ikke at give op på den grønne pagt.
2-0055-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Europe's automotive industry stands at a crossroads. We can continue to protect the past, or we can invest in the future. For me, the choice is clear: We must simplify the rules for the European automotive industry, but without weakening Europe's green ambitions. If European car manufacturers keep getting stuck in yesterday's technology, we will not only lose even more market share to China and the USA, we will also lose good European jobs.

Therefore, there is a need to get more electric cars on European roads, and many, many more of them must be built in Europe. And yes, it may well be that the European electric car is neither the best nor the cheapest right now, but it will never become that if we do not dare to truly invest in the green transition. This is about strengthening our competitiveness, the climate, and good jobs. For us to get there, it requires political courage, and that courage is about not giving up on the Green Deal.

2-0056-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, kolegyně a kolegové, pokaždé, když některý z evropských výrobců automobilů oznámí omezení výroby nebo propouštění, měli bychom si položit jednoduchou otázku: „Jaký signál vysíláme jednomu z nejvýznamnějších evropských průmyslových odvětví?“ Všichni chceme čistší dopravu. Musíme ale vycházet z reality. Transformace postupuje pomaleji, než se očekávalo, zatímco tlak na výrobce stále roste. Pokud bude naší odpovědností a odpovědí jen další regulace a další povinnosti, automobilový průmysl nezachráníme. Přesuneme výrobu i pracovní místa mimo Evropu. Evropa potřebuje méně byrokracie, jednodušší pravidla a respekt k technologické neutralitě. Dejme našim výrobcům prostor pro konkurenceschopnost a inovace. Chceme-li zachovat kvalitní pracovní místa a výrobu automobilů v Evropě, potřebujeme politiku založenou na realitě, a nikoli ideologii.
2-0056-0000.englishText: Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, every time one of the European car manufacturers announces production cuts or layoffs, we should ask ourselves a simple question: "What signal are we sending to one of Europe's most important industrial sectors?" We all want cleaner transport. But we must start from reality. The transformation is progressing more slowly than expected, while the pressure on manufacturers continues to grow. If our responsibility and response are only further regulation and more obligations, we will not save the automotive industry. We will move production and jobs outside of Europe. Europe needs less bureaucracy, simpler rules, and respect for technological neutrality. Let us give our manufacturers space for competitiveness and innovation. If we want to maintain quality jobs and car manufacturing in Europe, we need a policy based on reality, not ideology.

2-0057-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Wystarczy spojrzeć na dwa duże kraje na świecie – oprócz Unii Europejskiej, gdybyśmy patrzyli na Unię Europejską łącznie: Chiny i Stany Zjednoczone. Za chwilę dołączą do nich Indie i Brazylia. Dlaczego chińskie samochody są tańsze? Dlatego, że koszty produkcji w Europie są większe. Jeżeli chińskie samochody mają nowoczesną technologię, to dlatego, że koszty produkcji pod względem kosztów energii są po prostu mniejsze.

Jeżeli spojrzymy na Stany Zjednoczone, tam również koszty energii są dwa razy mniejsze, koszty benzyny są mniejsze. No ale co robi ta sala? Ta sala w tej chwili debatuje nad tym, co zrobiliście w zeszłej kadencji. Proste pytanie o ETS2. Przecież można się z tego wycofać. Za chwilę koszty benzyny będą jeszcze wyższe. Koszty energii ETS1 są coraz wyższe. Nowoczesne technologie, sztuczna inteligencja potrzebują więcej energii. Więcej energii to większe koszty.

Można by było zadać proste pytanie, ale nie chciałbym być nieuprzejmy wobec Pana Komisarza: ci, którzy to wymyślili, może niektórzy z tych urzędników powinni zostać zweryfikowani, czy nie pracują na przykład dla przemysłu amerykańskiego czy chińskiego, bo niemożliwe jest, żeby tak zamordować europejski przemysł.
2-0057-0000.englishText:
Madam President! One only needs to look at two large countries in the world—aside from the European Union, if we were to view the European Union as a whole: China and the United States. Soon they will be joined by India and Brazil. Why are Chinese cars cheaper? Because production costs in Europe are higher. If Chinese cars feature modern technology, it is simply because production costs in terms of energy are lower.

If we look at the United States, energy costs are also twice as low there, and petrol costs are lower. But what is this chamber doing? This chamber is currently debating what you did in the last parliamentary term. A simple question about ETS2. Surely, one can withdraw from it. Soon, petrol costs will be even higher. The energy costs of ETS1 are getting higher and higher. Modern technologies and artificial intelligence need more energy. More energy means higher costs.

One could ask a simple question, but I would not want to be impolite to the Commissioner: those who came up with this, perhaps some of these officials should be vetted to see if they are working, for example, for the American or Chinese industry, because it is impossible to murder European industry like this.

2-0058-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, ymmärrän, että autoteollisuus on monessa Euroopan maassa keskeinen talouden ala, ja se työllistää noin 13 miljoonaa ihmistä tämän maanosan puitteissa. On selvää, että jos puhumme strategisesta autonomiasta, niin teollisuus on siinä keskeinen asia, niin autoalan kuin muunkin teollisuuden osalta. Samalla tietenkin ne suuret keskustelut, kun tehdään toimia ilmastonmuutoksen vastustamiseksi ja sen torjumiseksi ja samalla koetamme edesauttaa teollisuutemme pärjäämistä, niin näiden ei pitäisi olla mitenkään toisiaan poissulkevia.

Emme saa tehdä sellaista sääntelyä, että tärkeät toimialamme ajautuvat Euroopan ulkopuolelle, koska siellä päästöt ovat varmasti suuremmat. Ilmakehä on kuitenkin yksi yhteinen, joten on tärkeää pitää nämä toimialat Euroopassa, mutta samalla tehdä järkeviä, teknologianeutraaleja toimia ja olla kunnianhimoinen niiden suhteen. Suomessa autoala on kärsinyt, mutta toisaalta tämä sama suomalainen autotehdas on nyt aloittanut panssariautojen ja diesel- ja sähkökäyttöisten linja-autojen valmistuksen, joten ei kannata taistella taantuman harjalla, vaan olla kehityksen kärjessä.
2-0058-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I understand that the automotive industry is a key economic sector in many European countries, employing around 13 million people within this continent. It is clear that when we talk about strategic autonomy, industry is a key issue there, both in terms of the automotive sector and other industries. At the same time, of course, the major debates when we take action to combat and tackle climate change and at the same time try to help our industry succeed, these should not be mutually exclusive in any way.

We must not create regulation such that our important industries drift outside Europe, because emissions there will certainly be higher. However, the atmosphere is a single shared one, so it is important to keep these industries in Europe, while at the same time taking sensible, technology-neutral measures and being ambitious about them. In Finland, the automotive sector has suffered, but on the other hand, this same Finnish car plant has now started manufacturing armored vehicles and diesel- and electric-powered buses, so it is not worth fighting on the crest of a recession, but rather being at the forefront of development.

2-0059-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Erstmals übersteigen Chinas Autoimporte in die Europäische Union die europäischen Exporte in die Volksrepublik. 250 000 Arbeitsplätze sind in der Automobilindustrie bereits verloren gegangen; weitere über 100 000 Arbeitsplätze stehen auf dem Spiel. Arbeitsplätze wandern ins Ausland ab, und Investitionen in Forschung und Entwicklung gehen auch ins Ausland. Die Lage ist wirklich dramatisch, aber die Lage ist kein Naturereignis, sondern auch das Ergebnis politischer Entscheidungen, die wir jetzt dringend korrigieren müssen.

Was ist zu tun? Erstens: Wir müssen die CO2‑Ziele korrigieren und echte Technologieoffenheit zulassen. Die CO2‑Flottengrenzwerte müssen angepasst werden. Abzulehnen sind Quoten zur Elektrifizierung von Flotten; das ist nämlich nichts anderes, als das Verbrennerverbot wieder über die Hintertür einzuführen. Zweitens: Wir müssen den Plug‑in‑Hybrid in Europa halten; der Utility Factor muss eingefroren werden. Und drittens: Wir brauchen bessere Standortbedingungen, und das heißt vor allen Dingen, dass wir die Energiepreise, die Stromkosten senken müssen. Die europäische Industrie zahlt heute rund doppelt so viel wie die amerikanische. Wir müssen Netzentgelte und Abgaben reduzieren, Einnahmen aus dem Emissionshandel zur Entlastung der Industriestrompreise nutzen, Genehmigungen beschleunigen und vor allen Dingen auch Bürokratie abbauen.

Nur auf eine Technologie zu setzen, ist falsch, ist falsch gewesen und wird immer falsch bleiben.
2-0059-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues! For the first time, China's car imports into the European Union exceed European exports to the People's Republic. 250,000 jobs have already been lost in the automotive industry; a further 100,000 plus jobs are at stake. Jobs are migrating abroad, and investments in research and development are also going abroad. The situation is truly dramatic, but the situation is not a natural phenomenon; it is also the result of political decisions that we must now urgently correct.

What needs to be done? Firstly, we must correct the CO2 targets and allow genuine technological openness. The CO2 fleet limits must be adjusted. Quotas for the electrification of fleets are to be rejected; that is nothing other than reintroducing the ban on combustion engines through the back door. Secondly, we must keep the plug-in hybrid in Europe; the utility factor must be frozen. And thirdly, we need better framework conditions for business, and that means above all that we must lower energy prices and electricity costs. European industry currently pays around twice as much as American industry. We must reduce network charges and levies, use revenues from emissions trading to relieve industrial electricity prices, speed up permit procedures and, above all, cut red tape.

Focusing on only one technology is wrong, was wrong and will always remain wrong.

2-0060-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, questo dibattito arriva in un momento cruciale, con il pacchetto automotive in discussione nelle varie commissioni competenti.

E non vi è dubbio che le scelte che verranno fatte nei prossimi mesi saranno decisive per il settore, chiamato a decarbonizzarsi, salvaguardando competitività e posti di lavoro. Penso anche alla componentistica, per una buona parte non riproducibile nella dimensione dell'elettrico.

Promuovere l'innovazione e accompagnare la trasformazione: per rilanciare il principale settore della manifattura europea servono cospicui investimenti, anche pubblici – lo abbiamo detto e lo ripetiamo – anche perché, visibilmente, regole e sanzioni, da sole, sono insufficienti a produrre il cambiamento auspicato, soprattutto in presenza di una concorrenza cinese ampiamente sussidiata dallo Stato.

Ma, in assenza di investimenti adeguati, serve ragionevolezza. Spero quindi che i negoziati dei prossimi mesi mettano al centro la sostanza, tenendo fermi gli obiettivi di decarbonizzazione, da una parte, e, dall'altra, trovando la giusta misura delle flessibilità necessarie a governare il processo di transizione.
2-0060-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, honourable colleagues, this debate comes at a crucial moment, with the automotive package under discussion in the various competent committees.

And there is no doubt that the choices made in the coming months will be decisive for the sector, which is called upon to decarbonise while safeguarding competitiveness and jobs. I am also thinking of component manufacturing, a good part of which cannot be replicated in the electric vehicle dimension.

Promoting innovation and accompanying the transformation: to relaunch the main sector of European manufacturing, substantial investments are needed, including public ones – we have said this and we repeat it – also because, visibly, rules and sanctions alone are insufficient to produce the desired change, especially in the presence of Chinese competition that is heavily subsidised by the State.

But, in the absence of adequate investments, reasonableness is needed. I therefore hope that the negotiations in the coming months will focus on substance, keeping decarbonisation objectives firm on the one hand, and, on the other hand, finding the right measure of the flexibility needed to govern the transition process.

2-0061-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, Monsieur le Vice-Président, l’industrie européenne est en panne. Il y a urgence! La production a chuté de 20 % en cinq ans, et 100 000 emplois ont été détruits en 2024. Pourtant, ici, la droite préfère garder le véhicule thermique, alors que l’Europe brûle.

Pendant ce temps, la Chine accélère. Cette année, sa part de marché a doublé en Europe. Elle vend plus véhicules en Allemagne que les Allemands n’en vendent en Chine. Pour sauver nos emplois, il nous faut de toute urgence des droits de douane de 35 % – y compris sur l’hybride – et des critères de contenu local strict. Lancez la petite voiture made in Europe accessible pour booster la demande!

Chers collègues, le choix est simple: investir dans l’électrique made in Europe pour assurer un avenir serein aux 3 millions et demi de travailleurs du secteur, ou bien regarder dans le rétroviseur – et en 2035, nous aurons 1 million d’emplois en moins et toujours plus de pollution.

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
2-0061-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Mr Vice-President, European industry has broken down. It is urgent! Production has fallen by 20% in five years, and 100,000 jobs were destroyed in 2024. Yet here, the right prefers to keep the internal combustion engine vehicle, while Europe burns.

Meanwhile, China is accelerating. This year, its market share has doubled in Europe. It sells more vehicles in Germany than the Germans sell in China. To save our jobs, we urgently need 35% tariffs – including on hybrids – and strict local content criteria. Launch the small, accessible "made in Europe" car to boost demand!

Dear colleagues, the choice is simple: invest in "made in Europe" electric vehicles to ensure a peaceful future for the 3.5 million workers in the sector, or look in the rearview mirror – and by 2035, we will have 1 million fewer jobs and ever more pollution.

(The speaker takes a blue-card question)

2-0062-0000.sourceText:
Cher collègue, pas plus tard que ce matin, une étude d’un cabinet d’experts est sortie et elle affirme qu’une usine automobile sur trois en Europe est «inutile à cause de nos surcapacités de production». Nous savons tous ici comment cela va finir si vous ne vous réveillez pas: des suppressions d’emplois massives et des fermetures d’usines, notamment en France – et cela a déjà commencé.

Alors, cher collègue, j’ai une question à vous poser: est-ce que vous assumez d’avoir bradé notre industrie automobile au profit de la Chine, en soutenant des normes irréalistes, hors sol, et l’interdiction du thermique en 2035? Et surtout, est-ce qu’un jour vous allez enfin présenter, avec vos collègues, vos excuses à tous les salariés et à nos constructeurs et équipementiers qui se sont retrouvés au chômage, dans la précarité par votre faute?
2-0062-0000.englishText:
Dear colleague, no later than this morning, a study by an expert firm was released stating that one in three car factories in Europe is "useless because of our overproduction capacities." We all know here how this is going to end if you do not wake up: massive job losses and factory closures, particularly in France – and this has already begun.

So, dear colleague, I have a question for you: do you take responsibility for having sold off our automotive industry for the benefit of China by supporting unrealistic, out-of-touch standards and the ban on combustion engines by 2035? And above all, will you finally one day present, along with your colleagues, your apologies to all the employees and to our manufacturers and equipment suppliers who have found themselves unemployed and in precarious conditions through your fault?

2-0063-0000.sourceText: Chère collègue, je vous invite à ouvrir les journaux et à voir que le nombre de véhicules vendus en France, électriques, a doublé en un an. Vous êtes en retard par rapport au marché, vous êtes en retard par rapport aux citoyens européens, et ce que nous faisons avec l’électrification, c’est qu’au contraire nous rattrapons notre retard par rapport à la Chine. Vous, vous regardez dans le rétroviseur, et bientôt, avec votre action, c’est l’ensemble de l’industrie automobile européenne qui connaîtra un krach.
2-0063-0000.englishText: Dear colleague, I invite you to open the newspapers and see that the number of electric vehicles sold in France has doubled in a year. You are lagging behind the market, you are lagging behind European citizens, and what we are doing with electrification is, on the contrary, catching up with China. You are looking in the rearview mirror, and soon, with your actions, it is the entire European automotive industry that will experience a crash.

2-0065-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Storslagna mål som inte tar hänsyn till förutsättningarna att förverkliga dem indikerar inte ledarskap.

Europa har inte råd att ägna sig åt önsketänkande eller fler politiska luftslott. Ändå valde EU att göra just det under förra mandatperioden. Förbränningsmotorförbudet är det tydligaste exemplet. I ivern att driva den gröna omställningen ignorerades basala frågor. Var finns den stabila elproduktionen och laddinfrastrukturen? Blir klimatet bättre av åtgärderna? Svaret är nej. Förbudet minskar inte vårt beroende, det flyttar det: från rysk olja till kinesiska kritiska råmaterial. Det är inte en grön omställning, det är geopolitisk naivitet.

Medan Europa kväver den egna industrin, jobben och investeringsviljan fortsätter världens stora klimatbovar att öka sina utsläpp. Politik måste utgå från verkligheten. Europa behöver teknikneutralitet, innovation och konkurrenskraft, inte fler symboliska förbud.
2-0065-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Grandiose goals that do not take into account the conditions for realizing them do not indicate leadership.

Europe cannot afford to engage in wishful thinking or more political castles in the air. Yet the EU chose to do just that during the last parliamentary term. The combustion engine ban is the clearest example. In the eagerness to drive the green transition, basic questions were ignored. Where is the stable electricity production and charging infrastructure? Do the climate measures actually help? The answer is no. The ban does not reduce our dependence, it shifts it: from Russian oil to Chinese critical raw materials. That is not a green transition, it is geopolitical naivety.

While Europe stifles its own industry, jobs, and willingness to invest, the world's major climate polluters continue to increase their emissions. Politics must be based on reality. Europe needs technological neutrality, innovation, and competitiveness, not more symbolic bans.

2-0066-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, ați început intervenția dumneavoastră spunând că anul trecut ați spus că industria auto este în pericol de moarte. Și așa este. Problema este să întrebăm de ce? Comisia Europeană cred că a plecat la un program, neluând în seamă situația concretă. Un manager privat ține cont de situația globală și iată de ce acum suntem în situația în care, global, noi nu putem să producem ca și China, avem costuri, inputuri mai mari și la energie, evident, și infrastructura ne lipsește, sistemul de încărcare în tot spațiul Uniunii Europene și să ne mai gândim și la clasa de mijloc, domnule comisar: credeți că poate? Mașina nu este un lux, doar cele care merg la curse.

Mașinile sunt acum o necesitate pentru mobilitate și atunci noi trebuie să ne gândim să construim un sistem auto care să nu mai disponibilizeze, ci să aducă în Europa. Și foarte bine că ați venit cu această propunere. Da, aș vrea să se țină cont de Made in Europe în tot lanțul valoric al construcțiilor de mașini și să ne gândim să adaptăm din mers programul pentru sistemul mașinilor electrice.
2-0066-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, you began your speech by saying that last year you said the automotive industry is in mortal danger. And so it is. The question is to ask why? I believe the European Commission set off on a program without taking the concrete situation into account. A private manager takes the global situation into account, and that is why we are now in a situation where, globally, we cannot produce like China, we have higher costs, inputs, evidently in energy too, and we lack infrastructure, the charging system across the entire European Union space, and let us also think about the middle class, Commissioner: do you think it can afford it? The car is not a luxury, except for those that go to races.

Cars are now a necessity for mobility, and then we must think about building an automotive system that no longer lays off workers, but brings them back to Europe. And it is very good that you came up with this proposal. Yes, I would like "Made in Europe" to be taken into account across the entire value chain of car manufacturing and let us think about adapting the program for the electric car system on the fly.

2-0067-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, ομολογήσατε ότι θα γίνουν 600.000 απολύσεις, 100.000 μόνο στον όμιλο Volkswagen. Καημός της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης είναι να στηρίξει τους ομίλους στον οξυμένο ανταγωνισμό με Κίνα και ΗΠΑ σε μια σειρά τομείς —μπαταρίες, ηλεκτροκίνηση—, πάνω απ' όλα όμως με στροφή στην πολεμική οικονομία ως διέξοδο κερδοφορίας μέσα από την παραγωγή οχημάτων, αρμάτων και ειδών διπλής χρήσης. Χαλαρώνετε περαιτέρω τις πράσινες προδιαγραφές για τις επιχειρήσεις, για να ενισχυθεί η κερδοφορία τους και, στον αντίποδα, τα λαϊκά νοικοκυριά φορτώνονται νέα βάρη για παλιά σπίτια, οχήματα, καυστήρες πετρελαίου.

Με το Ταμείο Ανάκαμψης πριμοδοτήθηκε το ξεχαρβάλωμα συλλογικών συμβάσεων, κλιμακώθηκε η ενεργειακή φτώχεια, η ακρίβεια, ο πληθωρισμός. Ο καπιταλιστικός τρόπος παραγωγής που διαφημίζουν η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, οι κυβερνήσεις και τα κόμματά της στην ανάπτυξη και στην κρίση εκτοξεύει την εκμετάλλευση των εργαζομένων για τα κέρδη του κεφαλαίου.

Στηρίζουμε τις μεγαλειώδεις εργατικές κινητοποιήσεις στη Γερμανία, για να μη χαθεί καμία θέση εργασίας, να στηριχτεί το εργατικό εισόδημα με συλλογικές συμβάσεις και ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις στους μισθούς. Συμπέρασμα και ανάγκη: η παραγωγή να οργανωθεί με κριτήριο τις σύγχρονες ανάγκες και όχι τα κέρδη και τον πόλεμο.
2-0067-0000.englishText:
Madam President, you admitted that 600,000 layoffs will take place, with 100,000 in the Volkswagen group alone. The European Union's sorrow is to support conglomerates in fierce competition with China and the USA in a series of sectors—batteries, electromobility—, but above all with a shift towards a war economy as a way out for profitability through the production of vehicles, tanks, and dual-use goods. You are further loosening green standards for businesses to boost their profitability and, conversely, working-class households are loaded with new burdens for old houses, vehicles, oil boilers.

With the Recovery Fund, the dismantling of collective agreements was subsidized, energy poverty, high costs, and inflation escalated. The capitalist mode of production advertised by the European Union, its governments, and its parties in growth and crisis skyrockets the exploitation of workers for the profits of capital.

We support the grand labor mobilizations in Germany, so that no job is lost, and so that workers' income is supported with collective agreements and substantial wage increases. Conclusion and necessity: production must be organized based on modern needs and not profits and war.

2-0068-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Mercedes is decreasing wages by 20 %, Volkswagen is shutting down factories and firing tens of thousands of workers, Stellantis has achieved a net loss of EUR 20 billion last year, and the European Commission estimates that 600 000 jobs in the auto industry are at risk. And the Commissioner is also saying that the automotive sector is in mortal danger.

But only ten years ago, we had in Europe the best auto industry in the world. The Commission now points the finger at China and wants new regulations. But the crisis facing the European car industry is purely of our own making. It is the result of foolish, ideologically driven policymaking at European level.

Restrictive measures have stifled innovation and competition to instead impose a single technology, chosen not by the consumer, but by politicians. We should have never given in to the Dieselgate blackmail either.

We need to re-industrialise Europe. Only a coalition of patriots – ECR, ECN and EPP – can do that. Keeping the cordon sanitaire is industrial suicide.

2-0069-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, el sector de la automoción es vital para Galiza, para mi país, donde hay miles de trabajos directos e indirectos —como sabe usted— en el sector y, además, donde estamos reclamando un plan industrial que no pueda ser un cheque en blanco para darle subvenciones a la industria automovilística mientras se destruye y se precariza el empleo.

Se paga por deslocalizar, como hemos visto en estos años, para perder empleos. No puede ser, señor comisario, que se le dé el mismo tratamiento a los vehículos fabricados en Europa que a los vehículos fabricados fuera. No puede ser que la crisis la sigan pagando los trabajadores. Si hay competencia desleal, Europa tiene que actuar: fabricar en Europa, crear puestos de trabajo con salarios dignos, porque se le han dado muchas ayudas al sector, pero la transición, a pesar de que tenga que ser justa, tiene que ser también para las personas, para las economías locales.

Por eso, le pregunto: ¿más ayudas para quién? ¿Para las multinacionales del sector del automóvil o para crear empleo digno y de calidad?
2-0069-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the automotive sector is vital for Galiza, for my country, where there are thousands of direct and indirect jobs —as you know— in the sector and, furthermore, where we are demanding an industrial plan that cannot be a blank check to give subsidies to the automotive industry while employment is being destroyed and made precarious.

Money is paid to delocalize, as we have seen in recent years, to lose jobs. It cannot be, Commissioner, that vehicles manufactured in Europe are given the same treatment as vehicles manufactured outside. It cannot be that the workers continue to pay for the crisis. If there is unfair competition, Europe must act: manufacture in Europe, create jobs with decent wages, because a lot of aid has been given to the sector, but the transition, even though it must be just, must also be for the people, for the local economies.

Therefore, I ask you: more aid for whom? For the multinationals of the automotive sector or to create decent and quality employment?

2-0070-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Seien wir ehrlich: Die aktuelle Krise ist keine Krise der Profite, sondern eine Krise der Arbeitsplätze. Hunderttausende Arbeitsplätze wurden in den letzten Jahren abgebaut, und Hunderttausende stehen weiterhin auf der Streichliste. Die Kolleginnen und Kollegen bei VW, bei Mercedes, bei Bosch, in der Industrie in Deutschland und europaweit streiken derzeit, kämpfen um ihre Arbeitsplätze und bessere Löhne, und ihnen gehört unsere Solidarität.

Die Wahrheit ist, diese Krise ist kein plötzlicher Schock; es ist eine Krise mit Ansage. Die Transformation wurde verschleppt und der letzte Tropfen für den Profit ausgequetscht. Die einzige Industriepolitik der Kommission bestand darin, die Rüstungsindustrie auszubauen, was aber volkswirtschaftlich Bullshit ist. Ihr Einstieg in den Ausstieg, Ihr Ausstieg aus dem Ausstieg hat wirklich keinem geholfen, das Hin und Her hilft niemandem. Milliardenhilfen sind geflossen, aber keine Konditionen für Arbeitsplatzerhalt wurden diktiert – und genau das ist der Fehler. Die Frage aktuell ist: Auf welcher Seite stehen Sie eigentlich?
2-0070-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Let's be honest: the current crisis is not a crisis of profits, but a crisis of jobs. Hundreds of thousands of jobs have been cut in recent years, and hundreds of thousands more remain on the chopping block. Colleagues at VW, at Mercedes, at Bosch, in industry in Germany and across Europe are currently on strike, fighting for their jobs and better wages, and they have our solidarity.

The truth is, this crisis is no sudden shock; it is a foreseeable crisis. The transition was delayed and the last drop squeezed out for profit. The Commission's only industrial policy consisted of expanding the arms industry, which economically is absolute bullshit. Your entry into the exit, your exit from the exit has truly helped no one; the back and forth helps no one. Billions in aid have flowed, but no conditions for job retention were dictated – and that is precisely the mistake. The question right now is: Whose side are you actually on?

2-0071-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, kolegyně a kolegové, víte, kdy přestal být automobilový průmysl konkurenceschopný? Ve chvíli, kdy nastoupila Ursula von der Leyenová a její „poskoci“ do čela Komise, přesně v ten moment. My jsme tady slyšeli pana komisaře, jak nám řekl: „Zabráníme smrtícímu cyklu, dlužíme to našemu průmyslu.“ A potom nám oznámí, že chystá další legislativu, další regulace, že budeme definovat evropský vůz. Prosím vás, my, než si vydefinujeme, co je evropský vůz, tak tady nebude žádná továrna na automobilový průmysl. To jediné, co bychom v tuhle chvíli měli udělat, pane komisaři, je škrtat, rušit, okamžitě přestat s tou obrovskou byrokracií a podpořit jakýmkoliv způsobem automobilky, například v tom, co slibujete dva roky, co sedíte v Komisi, že snížíte ceny energií. S ničím takovým jste nepřišel, takže jediné, co pomůže automobilovému průmyslu, je, že vy skončíte, navždy.
2-0071-0000.englishText: Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, do you know when the automotive industry stopped being competitive? The moment Ursula von der Leyen and her "lacklings" took over the Commission, precisely at that moment. We heard the Commissioner here telling us: "We will prevent the deadly cycle, we owe it to our industry." And then he announces to us that he is preparing more legislation, more regulations, that we will be defining the European car. Please, before we define what a European car is, there will be no automotive factory left here. The only thing we should do right now, Commissioner, is to cross out, cancel, immediately stop this huge bureaucracy and support car manufacturers in any way, for example in what you have been promising for two years since you have been sitting in the Commission, that you will lower energy prices. You haven't come up with anything like that, so the only thing that will help the automotive industry is for you to resign, forever.

2-0072-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjereniče, danas smo ovdje jer su postavljeni ciljevi za europsku automobilsku industriju bili preambiciozni, previše rigidni i nedovoljno usklađeni sa stvarnim mogućnostima naših proizvođača.

Europska industrija koja zapošljava gotovo 14 milijuna ljudi suočila se s visokim troškovima, gubicima radnih mjesta i premalo tehnološke fleksibilnosti, sve radi inzistiranja radikalne ljevice i zelenih.

Istodobno su kineski proizvođači jačali zahvaljujući državnim subvencijama, niskim troškovima te kontroli nad baterijama i ključnim sirovinama, a u prvih šest mjeseci ove godine dosegnuli su rekordni tržišni udio u Europi od 7,3 posto.

Zato pozdravljam automobilski paket i ambiciozniji nacrt izvješća kolege Salinija. Oni zadržavaju smjer prema klimatskoj neutralnosti, ali i našoj industriji daju više vremena, fleksibilnosti i tehnoloških mogućnosti.

Europa ne smije donositi političke odluke koje dobro zvuče na papiru, a u praksi slabe našu industriju, ulaganja i radna mjesta.
2-0072-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, we are here today because the targets set for the European automotive industry were too ambitious, too rigid, and insufficiently aligned with the actual capabilities of our manufacturers.

The European industry, which employs nearly 14 million people, has faced high costs, job losses, and too little technological flexibility, all due to the insistence of the radical left and the Greens.

At the same time, Chinese manufacturers have been strengthening thanks to state subsidies, low costs, and control over batteries and key raw materials, and in the first six months of this year, they reached a record market share in Europe of 7.3 percent.

That is why I welcome the automotive package and the more ambitious draft report by our colleague Salini. They maintain the direction towards climate neutrality, but also give our industry more time, flexibility, and technological opportunities.

Europe must not make political decisions that sound good on paper, but in practice weaken our industry, investments, and jobs.

2-0073-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, Monsieur le Commissaire, trois priorités pour préserver les emplois de qualité dans l’automobile européenne: premièrement, investir massivement dans les compétences; deuxièmement, relocaliser les segments à forte valeur ajoutée (batteries, logiciels, électronique de puissance, semi-conducteurs, recyclage); troisièmement, renforcer l’attractivité des métiers industriels (conditions de travail, perspectives d’évolution, partenariats entre entreprises, universités et centres de recherche).

L’Union européenne s’est donné des objectifs climatiques ambitieux, mais une question s’impose: a-t-on évalué avec la même rigueur les conséquences de ces décisions sur notre capacité à produire, investir, créer des emplois durables de qualité? La réponse est malheureusement non. La transition écologique et numérique crée de nouvelles occasions, mais exige des investissements importants dans les compétences, l’innovation et l’accompagnement des employés.

Je propose que, à l’avenir, toute initiative législative majeure soit soumise à deux évaluations complémentaires: son impact sur notre compétitivité industrielle et son impact sur l’emploi de qualité dans l’Union européenne.
2-0073-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Commissioner, three priorities to preserve quality jobs in the European automotive industry: firstly, to invest massively in skills; secondly, to relocate high value-added segments (batteries, software, power electronics, semiconductors, recycling); thirdly, to strengthen the attractiveness of industrial professions (working conditions, career prospects, partnerships between companies, universities and research centres).

The European Union has set itself ambitious climate goals, but one question arises: have the consequences of these decisions on our capacity to produce, invest and create sustainable quality jobs been assessed with the same rigour? Unfortunately, the answer is no. The ecological and digital transition creates new opportunities, but requires significant investments in skills, innovation and support for employees.

I propose that, in future, any major legislative initiative should be subject to two complementary assessments: its impact on our industrial competitiveness and its impact on quality employment in the European Union.

2-0074-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica! Morda je prihodnost avtomobilske industrije res električna, nisem pa povsem prepričan, da smo danes pripravljeni na električno prihodnost. Ali so na to pripravljena omrežja, ali je na to pripravljena proizvodnja električne energije? Ali imamo rudnine, potrebne za električne baterije? Odgovor je ne. In zato seveda potrebujemo neko razumno prehodno obdobje, kjer bomo zagotavljali tehnološko nevtralnost.

Evropa je svetovni prvak pri proizvodnji najčistejših motorjev z notranjim izgorevanjem in morali bi biti resnično nori, da bi se temu odpovedali in se popolnoma podredili novi odvisnosti, to je odvisnosti od kitajskih električnih vozil. Zato je edina prava pot tehnološka nevtralnost, da damo priložnost tako klasičnim vozilom kot električnim vozilom.
2-0074-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The future of the automotive industry may indeed be electric, but I am not entirely convinced that we are ready for an electric future today. Are the grids ready for this, is electricity generation ready for this? Do we have the minerals needed for electric batteries? The answer is no. And therefore, of course, we need a reasonable transitional period where we will ensure technological neutrality.

Europe is the world champion in the production of the cleanest internal combustion engines, and we would truly have to be crazy to give this up and completely subject ourselves to a new dependency, namely dependency on Chinese electric vehicles. Therefore, the only right path is technological neutrality, to give a chance to both traditional vehicles and electric vehicles.

2-0075-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, z debaty o autech se nám vytrácí to nejdůležitější – zájem zákazníků, běžných motoristů, kteří potřebují levné a dobré auto. Ne nesmysly, kvůli kterým jsou auta drahá, špatná a plná „kazítek“. Kdyby unijní regulace nebylo, tak moderní, jednoduché auto by mohlo stát 6 000 EUR a kvalitní rodinné auto třeba 10 000 nebo 12 000 EUR. Ve světě to jde. Ale naši lidé platí třikrát tolik nebo jezdí v průměru 16 let starými ojetinami, protože na nové nemají. Pojďme proto seškrtat regulace, protože na papíry to nejezdí, jak se říká mezi motoristy. Nechme lidi kupovat taková auta, která opravdu chtějí, ne jaká jim předepisujete. A firmy, ty ať nevyrábí podle regulací, ale podle přání zákazníka jako před lety, když byl náš automobilový průmysl ještě mladý a úspěšný. A kdo neumí vyrobit dobré a levné auto, tak ať zkrachuje a uvolní místo lepším.
2-0075-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear Commissioner, the most important thing is disappearing from the debate about cars – the interest of customers, ordinary motorists, who need a cheap and good car. Not nonsense that makes cars expensive, bad and full of "planned obsolescence". If it were not for EU regulations, a modern, simple car could cost EUR 6,000 and a quality family car maybe EUR 10,000 or 12,000. It is possible in the world. But our people pay three times as much or drive 16-year-old used cars on average because they cannot afford new ones. Therefore, let us slash regulations, because cars do not run on paperwork, as motorists say. Let people buy the cars they really want, not the ones you prescribe for them. And companies, let them not manufacture according to regulations, but according to customer wishes, like years ago when our automotive industry was still young and successful. And whoever cannot produce a good and cheap car, let them go bankrupt and make room for better ones.

2-0076-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, I think there is nothing more depressing than to see a traditional industry like the automotive industry basically going down the tubes, especially because of unfair competition from China.

So that's up to us to ensure that competition is stopped and that we give a fair advantage to our own industries. But also, I think, we can move forward and be a little more creative.

I agree with EVs. They suit certain people, they don't suit other people, they are growing in sales, but they have to be European. 'Made in Europe' has to be the key.

But also, hybrid cars. I have a hybrid car, plug-in hybrid. It says it will do 100 km. I have never done more than 50 or 55, driving even as slow as possible. So, if the hybrid cars could cover a longer distance under the electric part of it, then I think that would be a win-win for Europe.

And we have to look at these creative measures to ensure that the automotive industry stays in Europe, is made in Europe and bought in Europe.

2-0078-0000.sourceText:
Die Aussprache ist geschlossen.

Die Sitzung wird kurz unterbrochen. Sie wird in wenigen Minuten mit der Erläuterung des Tätigkeitsprogramms des irischen Ratsvorsitzes wieder aufgenommen.
2-0078-0000.englishText:
The debate is closed.

The sitting will be briefly interrupted. It will resume in a few minutes with the presentation of the programme of activities of the Irish Council Presidency.

2-0078-5000.sourceText:
Az európai autóipar súlyos problémákkal küzd. Az Ursula von der Leyen által meghirdetett zöldpolitika és az azt kísérő, a valóságtól elrugaszkodott szabályozások megjelenése óta az európai autógyártás globális piaci részesedése folyamatosan csökken. Ez pedig immár az európai családok mindennapjaiban is megjelent – 2024-ben százezer európai autóipari munkahely szűnt meg. Iparági becslések szerint közvetlenül további négyszázezer, közvetve pedig több mint egymillió, az autóiparból élő, család megélhetése lehet veszélyben.

A tét óriási, ezért azonnal cselekednünk kell. Először, a Bizottság által jelenleg is javasolt szigorú előírások és büntetések helyett rugalmasságra és pozitív ösztönző intézkedésekre van szükség. Újabb adminisztratív terhek helyett ösztönzők kellenek ahhoz, hogy jövőt adjunk az autóiparnak.

Másodszor, az európai autóipar technológiasemlegességet kér. És igaza van. A munkahelyek megőrzése érdekében fel kell szabadítani az iparágat és meg kell adni a polgároknak és a vállalkozásoknak a lehetőséget, hogy a számos rendelkezésre álló technológiájú gépjármű közül a számukra legmegfelelőbbet válasszák ki.

Harmadszor, le kell törni az energiaárakat. Ma egy európai autóipari vállalat globális versenytársaihoz képest négy-ötszörös árat fizet az energiáért. Ez elfogadhatatlan.
