We support it because it reinforces political dialogue with a strategic partner, because it is based on cooperation and benefits health, education, and research, as well as disaster preparedness, because it respects people and natural resources, and because it is based on commitment and human rights, the Paris Agreement, labor rights, trade, equality, and the environment. Because, furthermore, it opens new opportunities for our SMEs and especially protects sectors such as nougat or citrus fruits.

But, above all, we support it because, on the current geopolitical chessboard, an agreement with a country like Mexico is the best compass. Based on mutual respect, on the recognition of our own history, our diversity, and on cooperation.

2-0246-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de Partij voor de Vrijheid kiest voor handel die Nederland sterker maakt en daarom steunen wij dit strategisch partnerschapsakkoord.

Mexico is met 130 miljoen inwoners een van de grootste economieën ter wereld en een belangrijke groeimarkt voor onze ondernemers. De Europese export van goederen en diensten kan met 75 % toenemen en Europese bedrijven besparen jaarlijks tot 100 miljoen EUR aan douanerechten. Dit akkoord verlaagt handelsbarrières, geeft onze bedrijven betere toegang tot Mexicaanse overheidsaanbestedingen en biedt enorme kansen voor de Nederlandse hightech machinebouw en logistiek. Ook onze boeren profiteren ervan, want hoge invoertarieven op onder meer kaas, kip en varkensvlees verdwijnen.

Maar hoewel wij voor het akkoord zijn, zijn we tegen de resolutie van het Parlement. Want opnieuw misbruikt links een handelsakkoord om zijn klimaathysterie, genderagenda en ngo-obsessie door te drukken. Strategische partnerschappen gaan over handel en wederzijds voordeel. "Woke" is geen exportproduct.
2-0246-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the Party for Freedom chooses trade that makes the Netherlands stronger and therefore we support this strategic partnership agreement.

With 130 million inhabitants, Mexico is one of the largest economies in the world and an important growth market for our entrepreneurs. European exports of goods and services can increase by 75% and European companies save up to 100 million EUR annually in customs duties. This agreement lowers trade barriers, gives our companies better access to Mexican public procurement and offers enormous opportunities for Dutch high-tech machine building and logistics. Our farmers will also benefit, because high import tariffs on cheese, chicken and pork, among other things, will disappear.

But although we are in favour of the agreement, we are against the Parliament's resolution. Because once again the left is misusing a trade agreement to push through its climate hysteria, gender agenda and NGO obsession. Strategic partnerships are about trade and mutual benefit. "Woke" is not an export product.

2-0247-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner Šefčovič, finally, we have a trade deal in front of us that does not jeopardise the position of European farmers or our European food security. The trade deal with Mexico offers ample opportunities for farmers and the EU industry: lower tariffs on agricultural products to Mexico, protection of geographical indications and easier access to Mexican products.

Nevertheless, I do have one concern because we cannot import what we cannot produce, meaning Mexico needs to comply with all EU standards if they want to export to the European Union. As the use of antibiotics as growth promoters through veterinary prescription in feed is still common practice in Mexico, I urge the Commission to implement sufficient audits on the ground to make sure there is compliance with our standards.

The Farmer‑Citizens Movement of the Netherlands welcomes this deal as a necessary diversification in a conflicted world where the EU cannot afford to bet on a single horse.

2-0248-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, vivimos en un contexto complejo y lleno de incertidumbres donde sabemos que —además— los aranceles se están utilizando como amenazas continuas.

En este contexto, los acuerdos comerciales con aliados que sean estables y de confianza y que nos den garantías de que se van a respetar valores compartidos y las reglas del juego que establezcamos parece que son más importantes que nunca.

Parece que este año 2026 es un año de nuevas oportunidades para nuevos mercados y para la reducción de dependencias. Se trata de Mercosur, la India, Australia y México, que es de lo que nos toca hablar hoy.

Qué vamos a decir: México es un aliado internacional estratégico para las empresas europeas y para las empresas vascas.

Resaltamos tres cosas que esperamos en el despliegue de este Acuerdo. Primero, que sirva para reducir los niveles de violencia que existen en el país y solucionar las denuncias que existen a ese respecto. Segundo, que se despliegue el comercio respetando derechos de comunidades locales e indígenas de forma íntegra. Y tercero, que seamos capaces, por supuesto, de acompañar a nuestras empresas e industrias a sacar el máximo provecho de este Acuerdo con relaciones que sean beneficiosas para ambas partes de una manera equilibrada.
2-0248-0000.englishText:
Madam President, we live in a complex and uncertain context where we also know that tariffs are being used as continuous threats.

In this context, trade agreements with allies that are stable and reliable and that give us guarantees that shared values and the rules of the game we establish will be respected seem more important than ever.

It seems that this year 2026 is a year of new opportunities for new markets and for the reduction of dependencies. We are talking about Mercosur, India, Australia, and Mexico, which is what we have to discuss today.

What can we say: Mexico is a strategic international ally for European companies and for Basque companies.

We highlight three things that we expect from the implementation of this Agreement. First, that it serves to reduce the levels of violence that exist in the country and resolve the complaints that exist in this regard. Second, that trade be implemented while fully respecting the rights of local and indigenous communities. And third, that we are able, of course, to accompany our companies and industries to make the most of this Agreement with relations that are beneficial for both parties in a balanced way.

2-0249-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I would like to start to congratulate you and the Commission for bringing this agreement forward. I will fully support it and I am actually very impressed by the Commission and the pace with which you now deliver new free trade agreements. It is important to mention also that the trade policy of the European Union is not only about new free trade agreements, it is also about modernising the ones we have.

The modernised agreement with Mexico has been in play for 26 years, I think, and now, the update of it will bring new possibilities for European businesses, new opportunities for European farmers. It will strengthen the cooperation on critical raw materials. It will simplify the rules for SMEs and it will improve the access for public procurement and provide stronger protection for intellectual properties.

So, I call on the Commission to continue to modernise other existing trade agreements. We need to ensure that European companies can benefit from the growth taking place beyond our borders.

2-0250-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, viviamo un tempo di sfide verticali, la forza vale più delle regole, si proclama.

Attori globali puntano alla supremazia su vicini e lontani, agitano ricatti, impongono dazi, alzano muri, muovono guerra.

L'Unione europea sa e può percorrere la via opposta: incontro, negoziato, costruzione e custodia di regole condivise, partenariato vincente, l'unica reale vittoria.

Il rinnovato accordo globale con il Messico giunge in un momento cruciale, va nella giusta direzione, rafforza il dialogo politico con un partner strategico dell'America Latina, apre opportunità concrete per le imprese – specie PMI e agroalimentare – precisa impegni vincolanti sui diritti umani e dei lavoratori e sulle questioni climatiche.

Tutto ciò va realizzato e monitorato in un dialogo aperto con la società civile. Oggi più che mai l'Europa deve dimostrare che un altro modo di stare al mondo è possibile e dà frutti.
2-0250-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, honourable colleagues, we live in a time of vertical challenges; strength is worth more than rules, it is proclaimed.

Global actors aim for supremacy over near and far, wave blackmail, impose tariffs, raise walls, wage war.

The European Union knows and can pursue the opposite path: encounter, negotiation, construction and custody of shared rules, winning partnership, the only real victory.

The renewed global agreement with Mexico comes at a crucial time, goes in the right direction, strengthens political dialogue with a strategic partner in Latin America, opens concrete opportunities for businesses – especially SMEs and agri-food – and specifies binding commitments on human and workers' rights and climate issues.

All this must be implemented and monitored in an open dialogue with civil society. Today more than ever, Europe must prove that another way of being in the world is possible and bears fruit.

2-0251-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, alors que toutes les grandes puissances protègent leurs économies de la concurrence étrangère, la Commission européenne est lancée dans une course sans fin aux traités de libre-échange. Avec quel pays nous n’avons pas encore signé de traité de libre-échange? La liste est courte.

Avec le Mexique, on nous dit qu’on a pris toutes nos garanties, et que ce sera très favorable. Mais je note quand même qu’on a abandonné totalement les contrôles sanitaires et phytosanitaires. Et deuxièmement, on va quand même importer de nombreux produits agricoles – bovins, miel, fruits – qui inquiètent nos agriculteurs. Alors à chaque fois, on nous dit: «Oui, mais ce sont de faibles volumes.»

Oui, mais: faibles volumes + faibles volumes = gros volumes. Parce que, dans le même temps, nous avons des traités de libre-échange avec l’Ukraine, la Malaisie, le Mercosur, l’Australie.

Nos agriculteurs vivent dans un contexte très tendu au niveau de leurs revenus. Ils ne supportent plus ces traités de libre-échange. Il est temps de cesser cette course en avant.
2-0251-0000.englishText:
Madam President, while all the major powers are protecting their economies from foreign competition, the European Commission has embarked on an endless race for free trade agreements. Which country have we not yet signed a free trade agreement with? The short list.

With Mexico, we are told that we have taken every guarantee and that it will be very favorable. But I note all the same that health and phytosanitary controls have been completely abandoned. And secondly, we are still going to import numerous agricultural products—beef, honey, fruit—which are worrying our farmers. So every time, we are told: "Yes, but these are small volumes."

Yes, but: small volumes + small volumes = large volumes. Because, at the same time, we have free trade agreements with Ukraine, Malaysia, Mercosur, Australia.

Our farmers live in a very tense context regarding their incomes. They can no longer bear these free trade agreements. It is time to stop this headlong rush.

2-0252-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, la forza dell'Europa non si misura dal numero degli accordi che firma, ma dalla capacità di costruire partenariati che tutelino i suoi interessi e promuovano valori comuni, tra cui lo Stato di diritto e i diritti fondamentali.

Come vicepresidente della delegazione per le relazioni con il Messico, sono orgogliosa della firma dell'accordo globale modernizzato. È una scelta di politica estera, industriale e strategica, significa diversificare le nostre relazioni economiche, rafforzare le catene del valore, proteggere le nostre indicazioni geografiche e azzerare i dazi per le nostre imprese, in un contesto internazionale sempre più competitivo.

Ma nessun partenariato può essere solido senza un principio irrinunciabile: il rispetto reciproco, rispetto delle regole, degli impegni assunti e delle nostre imprese, e condizioni di concorrenza realmente eque.

Su queste basi la cooperazione diventa un fattore di crescita, sicurezza e prosperità condivisa, perché l'Europa davvero protagonista non è quella che firma più accordi, è quella che sa farli rispettare, che difende i propri interessi e che trasforma ogni partenariato in un vantaggio per i suoi cittadini e per le sue imprese.
2-0252-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, honourable colleagues, the strength of Europe is not measured by the number of agreements it signs, but by its ability to build partnerships that protect its interests and promote common values, including the rule of law and fundamental rights.

As Vice-Chair of the Delegation for relations with Mexico, I am proud of the signing of the modernized global agreement. It is a foreign, industrial and strategic policy choice; it means diversifying our economic relations, strengthening value chains, protecting our geographical indications and eliminating tariffs for our businesses in an increasingly competitive international context.

But no partnership can be solid without an indispensable principle: mutual respect, respect for rules, undertaken commitments and our businesses, and truly fair competitive conditions.

On these bases, cooperation becomes a factor of growth, security and shared prosperity, because a truly leading Europe is not the one that signs the most agreements, but the one that knows how to enforce them, that defends its own interests and that turns every partnership into an advantage for its citizens and its businesses.

2-0253-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, europeos y mexicanos sabemos bien que nuestra prosperidad es mayor cuando es compartida y, en un mundo donde la confianza escasea y la lista de socios fiables cada vez es más corta, México se reafirma con este Acuerdo como un aliado comercial estratégico para España y para Europa.

Este Acuerdo abrirá nuevas oportunidades para nuestros exportadores y nuestras empresas y animará a muchas empresas europeas —ya presentes al otro lado del Atlántico— a seguir invirtiendo, creciendo y creando prosperidad junto con México.

Precisamente por eso, porque creemos que es una relación sólida y de futuro, lamentamos que no se haya incluido un capítulo ambicioso sobre energía. Pedimos por tanto a la Comisión que siga exigiendo al Gobierno de México la necesaria seguridad jurídica para las inversiones de nuestras empresas energéticas. Solo así garantizaremos que este acuerdo sea no solo una oportunidad comercial circunstancial, sino una verdadera alianza estratégica entre Europa y México.
2-0253-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Europeans and Mexicans know well that our prosperity is greater when it is shared and, in a world where trust is scarce and the list of reliable partners is getting shorter, Mexico reaffirms itself with this Agreement as a strategic trade partner for Spain and for Europe.

This Agreement will open up new opportunities for our exporters and our companies and will encourage many European companies—already present on the other side of the Atlantic—to continue investing, growing, and creating prosperity together with Mexico.

Precisely for this reason, because we believe that this is a solid relationship with a future, we regret that an ambitious chapter on energy was not included. We therefore ask the Commission to continue demanding from the Government of Mexico the necessary legal certainty for the investments of our energy companies. Only in this way will we guarantee that this agreement is not merely a circumstantial trade opportunity, but a true strategic alliance between Europe and Mexico.

2-0254-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, creo que esto es justo lo que necesitamos: relaciones honestas, proporcionales, con principios y valores democráticos y tolerantes.

Enhorabuena a los ponentes; más al ponente López que al ponente Larraz, porque he visto que ha «ayuseado» un poquito y no sé si era necesario.

Me parecen especialmente positivos los estándares acordados en materia de protección laboral, sanitaria y medioambiental. Por cierto, hablando de medio ambiente, en el informe se cita el Acuerdo de París, el Convenio sobre la Diversidad Biológica. Muy bien, señores del PP. Ya que han cogido esa racha con México, háganlo también aquí. No vaya a ser que defiendan el Pacto Verde Europeo en los acuerdos y después no lo hagan en la Unión Europea.

Por cierto, en cuanto al sector agroalimentario: creo que va a traer beneficios con relación a la eliminación de los aranceles mexicanos sobre nuestros productos. Para los que venimos de tierra de vino, es una muy buena noticia que se quiten estos aranceles. Por tanto, este es el camino: relaciones proporcionales, tolerantes, democráticas. Este es el camino.
2-0254-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I think this is precisely what we need: honest, proportional relations, based on principles and democratic, tolerant values.

Congratulations to the rapporteurs; more so to rapporteur López than to rapporteur Larraz, because I noticed he "Ayuso-ed" a little bit and I am not sure if that was necessary.

I find the agreed standards on labor, health and environmental protection to be particularly positive. By the way, speaking of the environment, the report mentions the Paris Agreement and the Convention on Biological Diversity. Very good, ladies and gentlemen of the EPP. Since you have caught that streak with Mexico, do it here as well. Heaven forbid you defend the European Green Deal in the agreements and then fail to do so within the European Union.

By the way, regarding the agri-food sector: I believe it will bring benefits in relation to the elimination of Mexican tariffs on our products. For those of us who come from wine-producing lands, the removal of these tariffs is very good news. Therefore, this is the way forward: proportional, tolerant, democratic relations. This is the way forward.

2-0255-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, for Europe to thrive in a multi-polar world, economic and political agreements are essential, especially with reliable and like-minded countries like Mexico. This is why the modernised strategic partnership agreement is so important. It is not only a trade agreement, it is a strategic investment in our common future.

This partnership opens new opportunities for European agri-food exports, improves access for EU companies to public procurement and services in Mexico, and supports small and medium-sized enterprises through simpler rules and procedures.

It enables us also to strengthen Europe's global competitiveness by diversifying supply chains and deepening cooperation with a key partner in Latin America. While we are separated geographically, we are united by shared values and by a clear mutual interest in strengthening our partnership.

2-0256-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, η συμφωνία στρατηγικής εταιρικής σχέσης μεταξύ της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης και του Μεξικού αποτελεί σίγουρα ένα σημαντικό βήμα για μια πιο ισχυρή, δημοκρατική και ανθεκτική συνεργασία σε μια περίοδο πολύ μεγάλων γεωπολιτικών ανακατατάξεων. Δεν αρκεί όμως να μιλάμε μόνο για περισσότερες εμπορικές συναλλαγές. Το εμπόριο πρέπει να συνοδεύεται από ισχυρές εγγυήσεις για τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα, την προστασία του περιβάλλοντος, τα δικαιώματα των εργαζομένων και την καταπολέμηση της διαφθοράς.

Για μας στην Ελλάδα αλλά και στην Ευρώπη, η συμφωνία μπορεί να δημιουργήσει νέες ευκαιρίες για τις εξαγωγές ποιοτικών αγροδιατροφικών προϊόντων και για τις μικρομεσαίες επιχειρήσεις μας. Είναι κρίσιμο όμως να διασφαλιστεί η ουσιαστική προστασία των ευρωπαϊκών γεωγραφικών ενδείξεων και να τηρούνται ισότιμοι κανόνες ανταγωνισμού, ώστε οι Ευρωπαίοι παραγωγοί να μη βρεθούν αντιμέτωποι με αθέμιτες πρακτικές.

Η Ευρώπη χρειάζεται αξιόπιστους εταίρους. Αυτή πρέπει να είναι η πυξίδα της ευρωπαϊκής εμπορικής πολιτικής μας.
2-0256-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the Strategic Partnership Agreement between the European Union and Mexico is certainly an important step towards a stronger, more democratic and resilient cooperation in a period of major geopolitical upheavals. However, it is not enough to talk only about more trade. Trade must be accompanied by strong guarantees for human rights, environmental protection, workers' rights and the fight against corruption.

For us in Greece and in Europe, the agreement can create new opportunities for the export of quality agri-food products and for our small and medium-sized enterprises. However, it is crucial to ensure the effective protection of European geographical indications and the observance of a level playing field, so that European producers do not face unfair practices.

Europe needs reliable partners. This must be the compass of our European trade policy.

2-0257-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, yo también celebro la modernización del Acuerdo con México, un país con el que nos unen profundos vínculos y uno de los dos socios estratégicos de la Unión Europea en América Latina.

Espero que esta modernización refuerce también nuestro diálogo político y nuestra coordinación ante desafíos comunes. Pienso, por ejemplo, en la lucha contra el crimen organizado y el narcotráfico, y en el deterioro del Estado de Derecho.

El Acuerdo es una buena noticia en general, pero lamento que, finalmente, no se haya incluido un capítulo específico sobre energía: habría sido conveniente para dar seguridad jurídica a la inversión europea en este sector de tanta importancia en México. Espero que la revisión a los tres años incluya una regulación de esta materia.

Me preocupa —señor comisario, usted lo sabe— la liberalización completa de las exportaciones mexicanas de conservas de atún a partir del séptimo año. Es un producto muy sensible para determinadas regiones de la Unión y México tiene un gran potencial exportador. La Comisión debe vigilar la evolución del volumen de estas importaciones. El sector conservero europeo está muy preocupado por el efecto acumulativo de estas concesiones a la conserva de atún en los acuerdos comerciales: ahora es México, mañana serán países del sudeste asiático, grandes productores. La Comisión tiene que ser cuidadosa en estas negociaciones.
2-0257-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I also welcome the modernisation of the Agreement with Mexico, a country with which we share deep ties and one of the European Union's two strategic partners in Latin America.

I hope this modernisation will also strengthen our political dialogue and our coordination in the face of common challenges. I am thinking, for example, of the fight against organised crime and drug trafficking, and the deterioration of the rule of law.

The Agreement is generally good news, but I regret that a specific chapter on energy was ultimately not included: it would have been advisable to provide legal certainty for European investment in this sector of such importance in Mexico. I hope that the three-year review includes regulation on this matter.

I am concerned —Commissioner, you know this— about the complete liberalisation of Mexican exports of canned tuna from the seventh year onwards. It is a very sensitive product for certain regions of the Union and Mexico has great export potential. The Commission must monitor the evolution of the volume of these imports. The European canned fish sector is very concerned about the cumulative effect of these concessions to canned tuna in trade agreements: now it is Mexico, tomorrow it will be Southeast Asian countries, major producers. The Commission must be careful in these negotiations.

2-0258-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Wir sprechen heute über ein Abkommen, auf das wir lange und geduldig hingearbeitet haben: unsere neue Partnerschaft mit Mexiko. Fast zehn Jahre Verhandlungen, und seit dem 22. Mai liegt das Ergebnis unterschrieben vor uns. Das ist mehr als ein technisches Abkommen; es ist ein starkes Signal der Partnerschaft. Ich denke dabei an die vielen mittelständischen Unternehmen in Europa, die genau solche Abkommen als ein Signal brauchen – weniger Zölle und praktische Hürden im Unternehmensalltag, weniger Wartezeit an der Grenze und mehr Verlässlichkeit beim Exportieren.

Wir leben in einer Zeit, in der Lieferketten zerbrechen können und Handelspartner nicht mehr selbstverständlich verlässlich sind. Umso wichtiger, dass wir mit Mexiko einen Partner haben, mit dem uns schon seit über 25 Jahren eine gute Zusammenarbeit verbindet. Über 45 000 Unternehmen, die meisten davon klein und mittelständisch, werden von diesem Abkommen profitieren, durch einfachere Zollverfahren, klare Investitionsregeln, geschützte Herkunftsbezeichnungen. Und wir öffnen unsere Märkte, ohne unsere Standards preiszugeben – verbindliche Verpflichtungen bei Arbeitnehmerrechten und Umweltschutz, hohe Anforderungen an Lebensmittelsicherheit.

Aber, auch das ist zu bedenken: Das Vertrauen in Rechtsstaatlichkeit und Institutionen in Mexiko ist ausbaubar. Darauf müssen wir hinweisen. Trotzdem bin ich froh, dass wir über das Abkommen abstimmen, und bitte Sie deswegen um Ihre Zustimmung.
2-0258-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Today we are talking about an agreement that we have worked towards for a long time and with great patience: our new partnership with Mexico. Almost ten years of negotiations, and since May 22nd the signed result has been before us. This is more than a technical agreement; it is a strong signal of partnership. I am thinking of the many small and medium-sized enterprises in Europe that need exactly such agreements as a signal – fewer tariffs and practical hurdles in everyday business, shorter waiting times at the border, and more reliability when exporting.

We live in a time when supply chains can break and trading partners are no longer reliable as a matter of course. This makes it all the more important that we have a partner in Mexico with whom we have shared a good cooperation for over 25 years. Over 45,000 companies, most of them small and medium-sized, will benefit from this agreement through simpler customs procedures, clear investment rules, and protected designations of origin. And we are opening our markets without compromising our standards – binding commitments on labor rights and environmental protection, high requirements for food safety.

However, this must also be considered: Trust in the rule of law and institutions in Mexico can be improved. We must point this out. Nevertheless, I am glad that we are voting on the agreement and therefore ask for your approval.

2-0259-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Auf der Tagesordnung steht jetzt EU‑Mexiko – das klingt wie ein Fußballspiel in Tagen wie diesen, aber das ist es diesmal nicht. Die EU ist ja auch noch mit vielen Mannschaften im Rennen, unter anderem der Mannschaft von Belgien, dem Heimatland unserer europäischen Hauptstadt.

Diesmal geht es um Kooperation, und das ist es, wofür ich immer und immer wieder eintrete. In einer Welt voller Konfrontation, wo viele auch versuchen, ihre Ziele durch mehr und mehr Konfrontation zu erreichen, müssen wir die Kooperation suchen, auch weil das die Lehre aus der europäischen Geschichte ist und auch weil es unserem Wohlstand und dem Wohlstand kommender Generationen umso mehr dienen wird.

Mexiko teilt vieles mit uns: die Werte unserer Zivilisation; Mexiko ist ein verlässlicher Partner, und auf kontinentaler Ebene ist eindeutig Europa der verlässlichste Partner in der heutigen Welt. Daher ist es für beide Seiten gut, dass wir Wohlstand möglich machen, Wachstum möglich machen und das Abkommen mit Mexiko modernisieren.
2-0259-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues! On the agenda now is EU-Mexico – that sounds like a football match in days like these, but it is not this time. After all, the EU is still in the running with many teams, including the team from Belgium, the home country of our European capital.

This time it is about cooperation, and that is what I advocate for time and time again. In a world full of confrontation, where many also try to achieve their goals through more and more confrontation, we must seek cooperation, not least because that is the lesson of European history and also because it will serve our prosperity and the prosperity of future generations all the more.

Mexico shares a lot with us: the values of our civilisation; Mexico is a reliable partner, and on a continental level Europe is clearly the most reliable partner in today's world. Therefore, it is good for both sides that we make prosperity possible, make growth possible and modernise the agreement with Mexico.

2-0261-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, I support free trade with democratic partners. Strengthening our relationship with Mexico makes strategic sense, especially when it comes to critical raw materials and reducing our dependence on China. But this Parliament's report on the EU‑Mexico agreement is such a disgrace to read.

While Mexico struggles with cartel violence, corruption, organised crime and border security, this House chooses to devote almost manic attention to gender ideology, identity politics, and climate activism. Instead of these leftist slogans, I have conservative guidelines for the EU when it negotiates new trade deals: defend our strategic interests, support trade where it benefits Europeans, protect our farmers and leave ideological activism out of our trade policy.

2-0262-0000.sourceText:
Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, vážení kolegové, modernizace globální dohody mezi EU a Mexikem je další ze série liberalizací obchodu mezi EU a druhou stranou. A tak jako předchozí liberalizace je i tato namířena především na škodu našich pracujících. Opravdu nestačí, že si pracovní místa v automobilovém průmyslu likvidujeme zelenou transformací? Musíme se nyní snažit usnadnit přesouvání naší výroby do Mexika, kde mimochodem tak silná environmentální opatření neplatí? Jaký je k tomu důvod? Komu má toto pomoci, kromě několika nejbohatších? Lidem, co pracují v automobilkách tady v Evropě určitě ne, a životnímu prostředí, kvůli kterému si tady tento průmysl likvidujeme, to také jen uškodí.

Ale za skutečnou drzost považuji opět pokus obejít členské státy a jejich parlamenty s umístěním obchodní části dohody do prozatímní dohody, tedy tato část může fakticky platit i přes možný nesouhlas některého demokraticky zvoleného sboru. Pro mantru volného obchodu zde necháte likvidovat místní průmysl, životní prostředí i demokratické zásady a suverenitu členských států. Tato logika by skutečně měla skončit.
2-0262-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, the modernization of the global agreement between the EU and Mexico is another in a series of trade liberalizations between the EU and the other side. And just like previous liberalizations, this one is primarily aimed at the detriment of our workers. Is it really not enough that we are destroying jobs in the automotive industry with the green transition? Do we now have to try to facilitate the relocation of our production to Mexico, where, by the way, such strong environmental measures do not apply? What is the reason for this? Who is this supposed to help, apart from a few of the richest? Certainly not the people working in car factories here in Europe, and it will only harm the environment, for the sake of which we are destroying this industry here.

But I consider it a real audacity to once again attempt to bypass member states and their parliaments by placing the trade part of the agreement into an interim agreement, meaning that this part can effectively apply despite the possible disagreement of any democratically elected body. For the mantra of free trade, you are letting the local industry, the environment, and the democratic principles and sovereignty of the member states be destroyed here. This logic should truly come to an end.

2-0264-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, I would like to thank all honourable Members for their intervention and, very telegraphically, I would like to reassure honourable members that, if it comes to the concerns concerning tuna, honey or SPA standards, we have been really carefully negotiating all these categories. I can assure you that everything will be okay, under control, and this agreement will bring huge benefits to European economic operators and, as I mentioned earlier, especially to the agrifood sector.

On the energy sector, what I would like to say is that we made also big progress in this regard, because we have been able to assess with certainty the domestic energy policy, which was related to the now finalised Mexican constitutional reforms in the economic sphere, and the agreement we reached on energy issues ensures consistency of the modernisation with the Mexican reforms in the energy sector, while ensuring the overall balance of the negotiated outcome is rebalanced and that now we are in a much better situation than before.

On top of it, we got the guarantee that EU investors will be treated on equal footing with investors from other important third countries. Also, you rightly pointed out that we have agreed on a review clause in order to discuss in the medium term the changes, recalibration or removal of some of the energy commitments that have been agreed in in the agreement, and we will definitely use those opportunities.

If you allow me, the last point concerns the issue which was raised by Mr Warborn and this is linked with the pace of our free trade agreement negotiations. We accelerated it because the economic situation in the world and in Europe clearly demands it. We simply need to diversify our trade. We need to diversify the opportunities for our economic operators. We'll simply have to look for new markets beyond the traditional export destinations. And, of course, if you want to be strategically autonomous, we have to have new access to the critical raw minerals, to the sensitive technologies, and therefore we are actually expanding the horizon and possibility for the European economy to thrive.

Let's not forget that almost half of our GDP depends on how well we trade. Despite what is happening right now, we are the biggest trader in the world if we take together goods and services. So I think what we should focus on is how we can consolidate the position in the future. And with the pace of negotiation comes my request.

Madam President, I would like to kindly ask this House and great colleagues from the INTA and other committees to support us in a smooth consent vote, organisation and procedures. Today, we discuss Mexico. Earlier with the Taoiseach, I was putting the accent on our agreements with India and Indonesia, which should get the consent of this House this year, so we can really benefit from these agreements as of 1 January next year. And, of course, we have on the table also the agreement with Australia. So I would just highlight these agreements where we need to coordinate very well between Parliament, the Council and the Commission, so we can really use these opportunities as soon as possible.

2-0265-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en primer lugar, como ponente, lo primero que querría hacer es reconocer la fantástica cooperación entre la Comisión de Asuntos Exteriores y la Comisión de Comercio Internacional, especialmente con Borja Jiménez Larraz, que ha sido su ponente, y con coponentes de Grupos diferentes, pero que han trabajado con visiones con un objetivo común —aun con matices—: el fortalecimiento de las relaciones entre la Unión Europea y México. No solo hemos trabajado con Borja Jiménez Larraz, sino también con todos los ponentes alternativos que han contribuido a una mejor resolución y a hacer un buen trabajo en el Parlamento.

Destacaría tres mensajes políticos. Uno: la diversificación de nuestra economía es una póliza de seguros geopolítica. Con esto estamos dando un paso hacia delante para nuestra diversificación económica. También lo hace México, que apuesta por su diversificación. Además, gracias al buen trabajo y la fantástica cooperación que siempre tienen el comisario Šefčovič y el Parlamento, hoy tenemos en marcha una batería de acuerdos de asociación —algunos de ellos importantes— con la región. Son acuerdos que van a apostar por esta diversificación. Es importante estratégicamente para la Unión Europea.

Dos: se ha hablado sobre los retos y algunos problemas que tiene México. No solo los tiene México, nosotros también tenemos algunos de ellos. Y, además, muchos de ellos no han aparecido ahora o en los últimos años, sino que han estado ahí durante largo tiempo. Lo importante para el Parlamento y para Europa es enviar el mensaje de que el Acuerdo Global Modernizado va a ayudarnos a afrontar conjuntamente los retos comunes y a cooperar para ser más eficaces. Entre los retos, obviamente, se encuentran el crimen organizado, fortalecer la seguridad, la transición ecológica, la transición digital, tener una verdadera prosperidad compartida... Lo que no hacemos es valorar las leyes que decide otro Parlamento, pues es otro Parlamento quien tiene que decidir los resultados de forma plural y diversa en función de las elecciones. Lo digo porque también el pueblo mexicano ha dejado bastante claro cuál es su opinión sobre las decisiones que toman sus autoridades.

En último lugar, todos coincidimos en que México es un socio fiable con el que compartimos valores y, por eso, mañana tendrá en esta Cámara un apoyo muy mayoritario en la votación, como tuvo unanimidad en el Consejo Europeo, con pluralidad de Gobiernos y colores políticos.
2-0265-0000.englishText:
Madam President, first of all, as rapporteur, the first thing I would like to do is acknowledge the fantastic cooperation between the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on International Trade, especially with Borja Jiménez Larraz, who has been its rapporteur, and with co-rapporteurs from different groups, but who have worked with visions towards a common goal—even with nuances—: the strengthening of relations between the European Union and Mexico. We have not only worked with Borja Jiménez Larraz, but also with all the shadow rapporteurs who have contributed to a better resolution and to doing a good job in Parliament.

I would highlight three political messages. One: the diversification of our economy is a geopolitical insurance policy. With this, we are taking a step forward for our economic diversification. Mexico is also doing so, by betting on its diversification. Furthermore, thanks to the good work and fantastic cooperation that Commissioner Šefčovič and Parliament always have, today we have a battery of association agreements under way—some of them important—with the region. These are agreements that will commit to this diversification. It is strategically important for the European Union.

Two: there has been talk about the challenges and some problems that Mexico has. Not only does Mexico have them, we also have some of them. And furthermore, many of them have not appeared now or in recent years, but have been there for a long time. The important thing for Parliament and for Europe is to send the message that the Modernised Global Agreement is going to help us jointly address common challenges and cooperate to be more effective. Among the challenges, obviously, are organised crime, strengthening security, the ecological transition, the digital transition, having true shared prosperity... What we do not do is evaluate the laws decided by another Parliament, since it is another Parliament that has to decide the results in a plural and diverse way based on elections. I say this because the Mexican people have also made quite clear their opinion on the decisions made by their authorities.

Lastly, we all agree that Mexico is a reliable partner with whom we share values and, therefore, tomorrow it will have a very large majority support in this Chamber in the vote, just as it had unanimity in the European Council, with a plurality of governments and political colors.

2-0266-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en primer lugar, yo también querría dar las gracias al comisario por este afán y este objetivo que se ha marcado de diversificar las relaciones comerciales, que creo que es algo que es fundamental, y, por supuesto, por la colaboración con el ponente —con Javi López— durante estos últimos meses.

Este Acuerdo es, en esencia, una apuesta por la apertura, por la cooperación y por el comercio basado en reglas. México y la Unión comparten mucho más que intereses económicos. Compartimos fuertes lazos: historia, tradiciones, cultura, lengua. Este es un Acuerdo que refuerza además nuestra posición global, que mejora nuestra competitividad. Es también un mensaje claro: Europa sigue apostando por el comercio basado en reglas, frente al proteccionismo y al cierre de mercados.

Esta es, además, una oportunidad para consolidar una relación estratégica en Iberoamérica, pero también quiero insistir en que este nuevo nivel de relación exige honestidad y sinceridad —hablarnos claro—. Y ahí hay cuestiones que son mejorables, eso es lo que hemos venido expresando a lo largo de este debate: sin un fuerte Estado de Derecho no hay inversión, sin seguridad jurídica no hay confianza.

México y la Unión Europea comparten historia. Hoy tenemos la oportunidad de construir juntos un futuro, en un mundo en el que cada vez más actores se relacionan por medio de la imposición de la ley del más fuerte, en el que se desprecia la cooperación y el multilateralismo.

Este Acuerdo nace del convencimiento y de la determinación de quienes saben que estamos en el camino correcto. El camino de dos pueblos que se entienden, que dialogan y que saben que la cooperación es la mejor vía para generar prosperidad. Dos pueblos que creen que un orden internacional basado en reglas es la mejor inversión. Y este Acuerdo se sustenta, además, sobre una concepción básica: una Europa abierta es una Europa más libre.
2-0266-0000.englishText:
Madam President, first of all, I would also like to thank the Commissioner for this effort and goal he has set of diversifying trade relations, which I think is fundamental, and, of course, for the collaboration with the rapporteur—Javi López—over these past months.

This Agreement is, in essence, a commitment to openness, cooperation, and rules-based trade. Mexico and the Union share much more than economic interests. We share strong ties: history, traditions, culture, language. This is an Agreement that also reinforces our global position, that improves our competitiveness. It is also a clear message: Europe continues to commit to rules-based trade, in the face of protectionism and market closures.

This is also an opportunity to consolidate a strategic relationship in Ibero-America, but I also want to insist that this new level of relationship demands honesty and sincerity—speaking clearly to one another. And there are issues there that can be improved, that is what we have been expressing throughout this debate: without a strong Rule of Law there is no investment, without legal certainty there is no trust.

Mexico and the European Union share history. Today we have the opportunity to build a future together, in a world in which more and more actors relate to one another through the imposition of the law of the strongest, in which cooperation and multilateralism are despised.

This Agreement stems from the conviction and determination of those who know that we are on the right path. The path of two peoples who understand each other, who dialogue, and who know that cooperation is the best way to generate prosperity. Two peoples who believe that a rules-based international order is the best investment. And this Agreement is also based on a basic conception: an open Europe is a freer Europe.

2-0267-0000.sourceText:
Die gemeinsame Aussprache ist geschlossen.

Die Abstimmung findet morgen, Mittwoch, 8. Juli 2026, statt.
2-0267-0000.englishText:
The joint debate is closed.

The vote will take place tomorrow, Wednesday, 8 July 2026.

2-0267-5000.sourceText: Mexiko ist ein wichtiger Partner. Es liegt in unserem Interesse, die Beziehungen mit Mexiko zu vertiefen - im Sinne unseres Handels, unserer Investitionen und der geopolitischen Diversifizierung, die uns unabhängiger macht und unsere strategische Autonomie stärkt. Es braucht hierfür offene Märkte, verlässliche Partnerschaften und bessere Rahmenbedingungen für unsere Unternehmen. Es braucht auch gegenseitigen Respekt - das aber ist die Schwachstelle dieses Berichts, der sich im Idealfall auf Handelspolitik beschränkt hätte, aber leider die werteimperialistische Hybris und Bigotterie der EU offenlegt: Brüssel sorgt sich um die Demokratie in Mexiko, während auf europäischer Ebene die ESN-Partei verboten werden soll und in den EU-Mitgliedsländern Repressionen gegen patriotische Parteien an der Tagesordnung sind. Wer vom Rest der Welt Demokratiestandards verlangt, gegen die er selbst permanent verstößt, ist unglaubwürdig. Und diese mangelnde Glaubwürdigkeit schwächt uns auf internationaler Ebene. Die Eurokraten sind nicht in der Position, ein stolzes Volk wie das mexikanische moralisch zu belehren und von oben herab zu behandeln. Wir sollten uns in unseren Beziehungen mit Mexiko auf gemeinsame Interessen fokussieren, allen voran auf den gemeinsamen Handel. Arrogante Belehrungen sind dabei zu unterlassen.
2-0267-5000.englishText: Mexico is an important partner. It is in our interest to deepen relations with Mexico - in terms of our trade, our investments and geopolitical diversification, which makes us more independent and strengthens our strategic autonomy. This requires open markets, reliable partnerships and better framework conditions for our companies. It also requires mutual respect - but that is the weak point of this report, which ideally would have been limited to trade policy, but unfortunately reveals the value-imperialist hubris and bigotry of the EU: Brussels is worried about democracy in Mexico, while at the European level the ESN party is to be banned and in EU member states repression against patriotic parties is the order of the day. Anyone who demands democratic standards from the rest of the world that they themselves constantly violate lacks credibility. And this lack of credibility weakens us at the international level. The Eurocrats are not in a position to morally lecture a proud people like the Mexicans and treat them condescendingly. In our relations with Mexico, we should focus on shared interests, above all on mutual trade. Arrogant lectures must be refrained from.

2-0269-0000.sourceText:
Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgt die Aussprache über die Erklärungen des Parlaments zu den Folgen der türkischen Invasion von 1974 für zyprische Frauen und Mädchen, den von den türkischen Streitkräften verübten Verbrechen und den Konsequenzen für die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter (2026/2617(RSP)).

Ich weise die Mitglieder darauf hin, dass es bei dieser Aussprache nur eine Rednerrunde der Fraktionen geben wird. Deshalb werden weder spontane Wortmeldungen noch blaue Karten akzeptiert.
2-0269-0000.englishText:
The next item on the agenda is the debate on Parliament's statements on the consequences of the 1974 Turkish invasion for Cypriot women and girls, the crimes committed by the Turkish armed forces, and the consequences for gender equality (2026/2617(RSP)).

I would like to remind Members that there will only be one round of political group speakers for this debate. Therefore, neither catch-the-eye interventions nor blue cards will be accepted.

2-0270-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι, δεν είναι μόνο το ψήφισμα για την Κύπρο που σας ζητώ να στηρίξετε. Είναι η ιστορία πίσω από το ψήφισμα. Είναι οι γυναίκες, τα κορίτσια, εκείνες που έφυγαν, εκείνες που είναι ακόμα εδώ, εκείνες που συναντήσαμε πριν από έναν χρόνο στην αποστολή μας, εκείνες που μας διηγήθηκαν τα πιο σκοτεινά γεγονότα βίας, απόγνωσης, εξευτελισμού και κακοποίησης· εκείνες που το 1974 ήταν ακόμα ανήλικα κορίτσια, έγκυες γυναίκες, νιόπαντρες κόρες, μητέρες, γιαγιάδες, και βασανίστηκαν, βιάστηκαν, κακοποιήθηκαν από τους Τούρκους εισβολείς.

Οι γυναίκες που συναντήσαμε πέρυσι έσπασαν τη σιωπή τους για πρώτη φορά 51 χρόνια μετά. Πολλές από αυτές μάς είδαν κρυφά από τους άντρες και τα παιδιά τους. Παραδέχτηκαν πως δεν έχουν μιλήσει ποτέ, είτε από φόβο είτε από ντροπή, γιατί ο βιασμός τους δεν τελείωσε τότε. Συνεχίστηκε από το στίγμα, την απομόνωση, την περιθωριοποίηση, την απόρριψη, τη μοναξιά. Οι γυναίκες που συναντήσαμε μίλησαν για όλες εκείνες που θα μείνουν για πάντα καταδικασμένες στη σιωπή. Εμείς, πάλι, δεν μπορούσαμε να πούμε πολλά. Οι λέξεις δεν έβγαιναν. Ήταν οι λυγμοί που κυριαρχούσαν και τα δάκρυα που μας ένωναν εκείνες τις ώρες.

Πριν αποχωρήσουμε από την Κύπρο, δώσαμε μια υπόσχεση: ότι θα κάνουμε τις κραυγές των γυναικών αυτών να ακουστούν παντού και δυνατά· ότι θα δώσουμε όλο μας το είναι για να αναγνωριστούν και εκείνες και όλες, και τότε και τώρα, ως θύματα εγκλημάτων πολέμου. Για να φροντίσει κάποιος επιτέλους, έστω και αργά, αυτές τις ανοιχτές πληγές. Για να αναγνωριστεί ο βιασμός ως όπλο σε περιοχές συγκρούσεων. Για να πληρώσει η Τουρκία αποζημιώσεις για τα θύματα και να στείλουμε δυνατά το μήνυμα πως όλα όσα έκανε δεν μπορούν να ξεχαστούν επειδή ανήκουν στο παρελθόν.

Δώσαμε μια υπόσχεση πως ο πόνος αυτών των γυναικών, το συλλογικό τραύμα των Κυπρίων, δεν θα παραμείνει ούτε βουβό ούτε αόρατο. Δεν είναι λοιπόν το ψήφισμα που σας καλώ να στηρίξετε, αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι. Είναι η ιστορία που έχει ήδη γραφτεί. Είναι η ψυχή, η ανάγκη για δικαίωση των θυμάτων, η υπόσχεση που δώσαμε, οι γυναίκες της Κύπρου που σας ζητώ να στηρίξετε.
2-0270-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, it is not only the resolution on Cyprus that I am asking you to support. It is the story behind the resolution. It is the women, the girls, those who left, those who are still here, those we met a year ago on our mission, those who recounted to us the darkest events of violence, despair, humiliation, and abuse; those who in 1974 were still underage girls, pregnant women, newlywed daughters, mothers, grandmothers, and were tortured, raped, and abused by the Turkish invaders.

The women we met last year broke their silence for the first time 51 years later. Many of them saw us secretly from their husbands and children. They admitted that they had never spoken, either out of fear or out of shame, because their rape did not end then. It continued through the stigma, isolation, marginalization, rejection, and loneliness. The women we met spoke for all those who will remain forever condemned to silence. We, on the other hand, could not say much. The words would not come out. Sobs dominated and tears united us during those hours.

Before leaving Cyprus, we made a promise: that we will make the cries of these women heard everywhere and loudly; that we will give our all so that they and all women, both then and now, are recognized as victims of war crimes. So that someone finally cares, even late, for these open wounds. So that rape is recognized as a weapon in conflict zones. So that Turkey pays reparations for the victims and so that we send a loud message that everything it did cannot be forgotten because it belongs to the past.

We made a promise that the pain of these women, the collective trauma of the Cypriots, will remain neither silent nor invisible. Therefore, it is not just the resolution that I am calling you to support, dear colleagues. It is the history that has already been written. It is the soul, the need for vindication of the victims, the promise we gave, the women of Cyprus whom I ask you to support.

2-0271-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il 1974 fu un anno di violenza senza precedenti per la popolazione di Cipro.

L'invasione turca fece dell'isola un teatro di massacri e orrori contro la popolazione civile, con una ferocia inaudita. Lo stupro fu usato su larga scala come strumento di guerra e a farne le spese furono le donne e le bambine dell'isola.

Le forze turche condussero sistematicamente stupri di gruppo e violenze su donne greco‑cipriote dai 12 ai 70 anni. Le forze parlamentari fasciste di EOKA‑B violentarono e massacrarono la popolazione femminile di interi villaggi turco‑ciprioti.

Come in molti, troppi scenari di guerra, i responsabili sono rimasti impuniti e le vittime, nella maggior parte dei casi, non hanno avuto accesso a cure sanitarie e psicologiche adeguate.

Il 1974 a Cipro non è un evento isolato: si inserisce nel solco storico dell'uso dello stupro come arma di guerra, un abominio che ancora oggi qualcuno cerca di trattare come "casi isolati", "effetti collaterali". Ma non è così. La violenza di genere nei conflitti armati è un orrore sistematico e deliberato, che può e deve essere combattuto percorrendo due strade: assicurare alla giustizia i carnefici e offrire un supporto reale per le vittime.

Anche oggi, dall'Ucraina al Sudan, alla Palestina, le vittime di stupro ci chiedono giustizia e ci chiedono assistenza. Anche oggi, in Europa, abbiamo il dovere di garantire alle vittime di violenza di genere, incluse le donne e le bambine rifugiate, pieno accesso gratuito ai servizi di salute riproduttiva, incluso l'aborto e il trattamento delle malattie veneree. Abbiamo il dovere di portare in tribunale i criminali di guerra perseguibili sotto la giurisdizione universale e i ricercati dalla Corte penale internazionale dell'Aia.

Non è solo per rispetto del diritto: è l'unico modo per rispettare la dignità delle vittime in tutto il mondo, quelle passate e quelle future. Perché l'impunità dello stupro alimenta la cultura dello stupro e, invece, noi chiediamo giustizia per quello che è successo nel 1974 a Cipro, per quello che succede oggi, chiediamo giustizia perché non vogliamo più piangere le vittime di domani.
2-0271-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, 1974 was a year of unprecedented violence for the population of Cyprus.

The Turkish invasion turned the island into a theatre of massacres and horrors against the civilian population, with unheard-of ferocity. Rape was used on a large scale as an instrument of war, and the women and girls of the island paid the price.

Turkish forces systematically carried out gang rapes and violence against Greek-Cypriot women aged 12 to 70. The fascist parliamentary forces of EOKA-B raped and massacred the female population of entire Turkish-Cypriot villages.

As in many, too many war scenarios, those responsible have remained unpunished and the victims, in most cases, have not had access to adequate health and psychological care.

1974 in Cyprus is not an isolated event: it fits into the historical furrow of the use of rape as a weapon of war, an abomination that even today some try to treat as "isolated cases", "collateral effects". But it is not like that. Gender-based violence in armed conflicts is a systematic and deliberate horror, which can and must be fought by pursuing two paths: bringing the executioners to justice and offering real support for the victims.

Even today, from Ukraine to Sudan, to Palestine, victims of rape ask us for justice and ask us for assistance. Even today, in Europe, we have a duty to guarantee victims of gender-based violence, including refugee women and girls, full and free access to reproductive health services, including abortion and the treatment of venereal diseases. We have a duty to bring to court war criminals prosecutable under universal jurisdiction and those wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

It is not only for respect for the law: it is the only way to respect the dignity of victims all over the world, past and future. Because the impunity of rape fuels the culture of rape and, instead, we demand justice for what happened in 1974 in Cyprus, for what happens today, we demand justice because we no longer want to mourn the victims of tomorrow.

2-0272-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, «Οι νεκροί βρομούσαν από ένα μίλι μακριά. Ήταν ανελέητο το τελευταίο καλοκαίρι. Τρυπούσε τους ίσκιους των δέντρων, τις στέγες των σπιτιών. Φριχτό καλοκαίρι για τους ανθρώπους. Μπάσαν τους νεκρούς από την πίσω πόρτα στον Άη Γιάννη· δεν τους χωρούσαν, λέει, τα φέρετρα. Και ο πιτσιρικάς, πήχτρα το αίμα στα ρούχα του, άνοιγε λάκκους, τον χτυπούσε ο ήλιος ανελέητα στους κροτάφους, στη μνήμη βαθιά ως το μέλλον. Τον ήξερες αλλιώτικα τον κυπριώτικο ήλιο, θεία Μαρίνα, την αυγή με τα περιστέρια στους ώμους.» Λεύκιος Ζαφειρίου.

Κι όμως, στις 20 Ιουλίου 2026 συμπληρώνονται 52 ολόκληρα χρόνια που η ψυχή του Ελληνισμού με την αρπαγή της μισής Κύπρου μαύρισε για πάντα. Οικογένειες ξεριζώθηκαν, γυναίκες βιάστηκαν, άνδρες άνανδρα δολοφονήθηκαν από τον Τούρκο εισβολέα κατακτητή. Χιλιάδες οι αγνοούμενοι που πίσω τους έχουν μάνες, γυναίκες, αδελφές και κόρες που ακόμα περιμένουν να τους δοθούν οι σοροί τους. Γυναίκες, μητέρες και κορίτσια βιάστηκαν και βασανίστηκαν από Τούρκους στρατιώτες με κτηνώδη τρόπο.

Και εσείς εδώ αυτούς τους άνανδρους δολοφόνους, που συνεχίζουν έως και σήμερα να απειλούν την Ελλάδα, την Κύπρο μας και το Ισραήλ, θέλετε να τους βάλετε στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, και δεν ντρέπεστε. Για τον Ρώσο εισβολέα ξέρουμε να μιλάμε και να κάνουμε το σωστό· για τον Τούρκο εισβολέα όμως ξέρουμε μόνο να κάνουμε τα στραβά μάτια. Και η Κύπρος μας, η Αμμόχωστος, η Κερύνεια, η Καρπασία, η Μόρφου, ο Καραβάς, το Ριζοκάρπασο; Ακόμα εκεί τα αγιασμένα με αίμα εδάφη μας κάτω από τον Τούρκο εισβολέα. Κι εσείς μόνο σιωπή, μπουκωμένοι από τα βρόμικα χρήματα του κατακτητή. Ντροπή σας!
2-0272-0000.englishText:
Madam President, "The dead smelled a mile away. It was a relentless last summer. It pierced the shadows of the trees, the roofs of the houses. A dreadful summer for the people. They brought the dead in through the back door at St. John's; the coffins couldn't hold them, they say. And the kid, blood choked in his clothes, was digging graves, the sun beating mercilessly on his temples, deep in memory all the way to the future. You knew the Cypriot sun differently, Aunt Marina, at dawn with the doves on your shoulders." Lefkios Zafiriou.

And yet, on July 20, 2026, a full 52 years will have passed since the soul of Hellenism was blackened forever by the seizure of half of Cyprus. Families were uprooted, women were raped, men were cowardly murdered by the Turkish invading conqueror. Thousands of missing persons leave behind mothers, wives, sisters, and daughters who are still waiting for their remains to be given to them. Women, mothers, and girls were raped and tortured by Turkish soldiers in a bestial manner.

And you here, you want to bring these cowardly murderers, who continue to this day to threaten Greece, our Cyprus, and Israel, into the European Union, and you have no shame. About the Russian invader we know how to speak and do the right thing; but about the Turkish invader, however, we only know how to turn a blind eye. And our Cyprus, Famagusta, Kyrenia, Karpasia, Morphou, Karavas, Rizokarpaso? Still there, our lands sanctified with blood under the Turkish invader. And you, only silence, stuffed with the conqueror's dirty money. Shame on you!

2-0273-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, σήμερα επαναφέρουμε στις μνήμες όλων μας ένα έγκλημα πολέμου που έμεινε ξεχασμένο: τους βιασμούς και τη σεξουαλική βία που υπέστησαν οι γυναίκες και τα κορίτσια της Κύπρου κατά την τουρκική εισβολή του '74. Υπενθυμίζουμε σε όλους ότι σε ένα κράτος μέλος της Ένωσης, 52 χρόνια μετά, ο πόνος παραμένει ανεξίτηλος, το δράμα αδικαίωτο, η μνήμη άσβεστη, η κατοχή συνεχιζόμενη.

Ενώ θα έπρεπε να μιλάμε για το αυτονόητο, είμαστε εδώ για να επαναφέρουμε την κοινή λογική. Αποτελεί ντροπή ότι ανώτατοι αξιωματούχοι της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, η κ. Kallas και η κ. Kos, επέλεξαν πριν λίγες μέρες να παρουσιάσουν την Τουρκία ως βασικό στρατηγικό εταίρο, μιλώντας για εμβάθυνση της συνεργασίας. Η στάση τους αυτή είναι προσβολή απέναντι στις γυναίκες που σήμερα δηλώνουμε ότι υπερασπιζόμαστε. Προσβολή απέναντι στις ίδιες τις αξίες της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης. Οι γυναίκες της Κύπρου είναι περήφανες και δεν εκλιπαρούν. Απαιτούν δικαιοσύνη και λογοδοσία. Όχι λήθη και υποκρισία.
2-0273-0000.englishText:
Madam President, today we bring back to everyone's memory a forgotten war crime: the rapes and sexual violence suffered by the women and girls of Cyprus during the Turkish invasion of '74. We remind everyone that in a Member State of the Union, 52 years later, the pain remains indelible, the drama unvindicated, the memory unquenched, the occupation ongoing.

While we should be talking about the obvious, we are here to bring back common sense. It is a shame that high-ranking European Union officials, Ms. Kallas and Ms. Kos, chose a few days ago to present Turkey as a key strategic partner, talking about deepening cooperation. Their stance is an insult to the women we declare today that we are defending. An insult to the values of the European Union itself. The women of Cyprus are proud and do not beg. They demand justice and accountability. Not oblivion and hypocrisy.

2-0274-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, colleagues, the suffering of the women of Cyprus following the Turkish invasion in 1974 and the enduring consequences must not be forgotten. These women were attacked for the simple fact that they were women. They were put for these terrible sufferings as a way to demoralise the population and achieve a military goal. It is despicable.

We have to recognise publicly the harm that the women of Cyprus went through. We have to ask for a better support system that can help women deal with the trauma. And we have to continue advocating for a permanent solution for Cyprus.

Just as importantly, we have to learn from these devastating events because we see that conflict-related sexual violence continues to be a tool used in war in other conflicts, even today. I am afraid to say that its use might even be increasing. And that is because we are turning a blind eye to so many examples across the world.

We cannot normalise sexual violence and allow for impunity. We need the EU to speak out against any form of sexual violence, no matter where it happens and no matter who is committing it.

2-0275-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, everything we know about war, we know with a man's voice. Belarusian Nobel Prize laureate Svetlana Alexievich wrote that about women's often forgotten testimonies and experiences of war. Three decades later, those words remain tragically relevant.

Sexual violence is among the most devastating weapons of war. They can destroy people's lives, but also destroy entire communities. The widespread stigma means that women and girls are often left isolated, untreated and silenced, carrying these traumas for decades. What makes me most furious about this is that we know. We don't only know what happened in Cyprus, but we know that today over half a billion women and girls live in conflict zones where they are not only victims of fighting, but their bodies are actively used as targets.

With increasing wars and conflicts, sexual violence is tragically on the rise, from Congo to Gaza, Ukraine and Sudan. This is the security threat that requires special attention. We know this, we know the devastating consequences and we know what is needed to prevent it and to help survivors. The EU must make the prevention of conflict‑related sexual violence and comprehensive support for survivors a top priority in its external action. We must also break this silence.

2-0276-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, οι έμφυλες συνέπειες του πολέμου —από τις πιο ανατριχιαστικές πτυχές του— συχνά αποκρύβονται. Οι τουρκικές ένοπλες δυνάμεις το 1974 στην Κύπρο, συστηματικά και οργανωμένα, άσκησαν σεξουαλική βία σε βάρος Ελληνοκύπριων γυναικών αλλά και ανδρών κάθε ηλικίας. Ακόμα ένα στυγερό έγκλημα από την Τουρκία που παραμένει ατιμώρητο.

Πρέπει όμως να είμαστε ειλικρινείς. Βαρβαρότητες διαπράχθηκαν και από ελληνοκυπριακές παραστρατιωτικές ομάδες σε βάρος Τουρκοκυπρίων γυναικών. Ο βιασμός δεν έχει χρώμα, φυλή και θρησκεία. Τα τραύματα δύσκολα επουλώνονται. Τώρα που δειλά-δειλά ομολογούνται, ας είναι λυτρωτικά. Η Κύπρος και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση έχουν υποχρέωση να διασφαλίσουν τα δικαιώματα, την αξιοπρέπεια και την ιστορική μνήμη όλων των γυναικών της Κύπρου. Ο κοινός πόνος να γίνει κινητήρια δύναμη για τη δικοινοτική συνεργασία και την ειρήνη στο νησί μας.
2-0276-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the gendered consequences of war—among its most harrowing aspects—are often concealed. The Turkish armed forces in 1974 in Cyprus systematically and in an organized manner committed sexual violence against Greek Cypriot women as well as men of all ages. Yet another heinous crime by Turkey that remains unpunished.

We must, however, be honest. Barbarities were also committed by Greek Cypriot paramilitary groups against Turkish Cypriot women. Rape has no color, race, or religion. Wounds are difficult to heal. Now that they are timidly being confessed, let them be redeeming. Cyprus and the European Union have an obligation to ensure the rights, dignity, and historical memory of all women of Cyprus. Let common pain become a driving force for bicommunal cooperation and peace on our island.

2-0277-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Der Zypernkonflikt ist eines der Themen des heute stattfindenden NATO-Gipfels. Morgen treffen sich dazu der Präsident des Europäischen Rates, die Kommissionspräsidentin und der türkische Staatschef Erdoğan; mit einer Lösung des Zypernkonflikts ist dabei nicht zu rechnen. Während die Türkei die Zweistaatenlösung als Grundlage für weitere Verhandlungen fordert, bevorzugt die EU die Annäherung an ein Konföderationsmodell. Gerade wir Deutschen wissen, wie schwierig es ist, sich Jahrzehnte nach dem Ausbruch eines Konflikts zu versöhnen, wieder miteinander zu sprechen und sich vergeben zu können. Mit unseren polnischen Nachbarn ist uns das zu einem guten Stück gelungen: Mittlerweile kämpfen wir im Europäischen Parlament gemeinsam für ein Europa der souveränen Nationen.

Umso unverständlicher ist es, warum der FEMM-Ausschuss des Europäischen Parlaments ausgerechnet heute mit einer Entschließung zu den Übergriffen der türkischen Streitkräfte auf zypriotische Frauen und Mädchen aus dem Jahr 1974 um die Ecke kommt. Niemand möchte das Leid und die Verbrechen aus jener Zeit relativieren oder gar verharmlosen, doch hier wird erneut der Versuch unternommen, einen andauernden geopolitischen Konflikt mit EU-Richtlinien zu Gender Mainstreaming zu verknüpfen.

Eine Anhörung unter Beteiligung von gendergerechten NGOs, um damalige Zeugenaussagen im institutionellen Rahmen der EU formal anzuerkennen, eine nachträgliche Rechtfertigung von Abtreibungen, um den Schwangerschaftsabbruch in einen völkerrechtlichen Kontext zu heben, eine finanzielle und technische Unterstützung der EU für gendersensible Beratung sind nicht die vordringlichen Probleme zwischen der Türkei und Griechenland.

Erneut überschreitet der FEMM-Ausschuss seine Kompetenzen und möchte, dass dieser Konflikt gendergerecht gelesen wird. Was für eine Anmaßung! Lassen Sie uns stattdessen an einer besseren Zusammenarbeit zwischen diesen beiden NATO-Partnern arbeiten.
2-0277-0000.englishText:
Madam President!
The Cyprus conflict is one of the topics at today's NATO summit. Tomorrow, the President of the European Council, the President of the Commission, and Turkish Head of State Erdoğan will meet to discuss it; a solution to the Cyprus conflict is not to be expected. While Turkey demands the two-state solution as the basis for further negotiations, the EU prefers an approach closer to a confederation model. We Germans in particular know how difficult it is to reconcile decades after the outbreak of a conflict, to speak to one another again, and to be able to forgive. We have succeeded in doing this to a large extent with our Polish neighbours: meanwhile, in the European Parliament, we are fighting together for a Europe of sovereign nations.

All the more incomprehensible is why the FEMM Committee of the European Parliament is coming out, of all days today, with a resolution on the attacks by Turkish armed forces on Cypriot women and girls from 1974. Nobody wants to relativise or even trivialise the suffering and crimes from that time, but here an attempt is once again being made to link an ongoing geopolitical conflict with EU guidelines on gender mainstreaming.

A hearing involving gender-sensitive NGOs to formally recognise witness testimonies from back then within the institutional framework of the EU, a retroactive justification of abortions in order to elevate the termination of pregnancy into an international law context, and EU financial and technical support for gender-sensitive counselling are not the pressing problems between Turkey and Greece.

Once again, the FEMM Committee is exceeding its competences and wants this conflict to be read in a gender-sensitive way. What an presumption! Let us instead work on better cooperation between these two NATO partners.

(PPE), γραπτώς – Αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι, η σημερινή συζήτηση αφορά την ίδια την αξιοπιστία της Ευρώπης απέναντι στα θύματα πολέμου και τη δέσμευσή της να μην επιτρέπει στη σιωπή να συγκαλύπτει εγκλήματα.

Είμαι περήφανος που σήμερα, έστω και πενήντα δύο χρόνια μετά την τουρκική εισβολή του 1974, το Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο έκανε αυτό το ιστορικό βήμα. Για πρώτη φορά αναγνωρίζει ξεκάθαρα ότι οι βιασμοί και οι συστηματικές κακοποιήσεις Ελληνοκύπριων γυναικών από τον τουρκικό στρατό αποτέλεσαν εγκλήματα πολέμου και ότι η σεξουαλική βία χρησιμοποιήθηκε ως όπλο πολέμου.

Πίσω από κάθε μαρτυρία υπάρχει μια γυναίκα που κουβαλούσε επί δεκαετίες ένα βάρος που δεν της ανήκε. Η ντροπή δεν ήταν ποτέ δική τους. Η ευθύνη ανήκει αποκλειστικά στους θύτες και σε όσους επέτρεψαν να επικρατήσει η σιωπή.

Η αναγνώριση αυτή αποτελεί ηθική δικαίωση για τις επιζήσασες, αλλά και ένα ισχυρό μήνυμα ότι η αλήθεια δεν παραγράφεται. Η κατονομασία της Τουρκίας και η απαίτηση για λογοδοσία και αποζημιώσεις αποτελούν ουσιαστικά βήματα προς τη δικαιοσύνη.

Η Ευρώπη οφείλει να υπερασπίζεται τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα με συνέπεια, χωρίς εκπτώσεις και χωρίς δύο μέτρα και δύο σταθμά. Η μνήμη των θυμάτων μάς υποχρεώνει να συνεχίσουμε να αγωνιζόμαστε για αλήθεια, δικαιοσύνη και μια λύση του Κυπριακού που θα εδράζεται πλήρως στο διεθνές δίκαιο, στα ψηφίσματα των Ηνωμένων Εθνών και στο ευρωπαϊκό κεκτημένο.
2-0280-5000.englishText:
(PPE), in writing. – Dear colleagues, today's debate concerns Europe's very credibility toward the victims of war and its commitment not to allow silence to cover up crimes.

I am proud that today, fifty-two years after the Turkish invasion of 1974, the European Parliament has taken this historic step. For the first time, it clearly recognizes that the rapes and systematic abuses of Greek Cypriot women by the Turkish army constituted war crimes and that sexual violence was used as a weapon of war.

Behind every testimony is a woman who carried for decades a burden that did not belong to her. The shame was never theirs. The responsibility belongs exclusively to the perpetrators and to those who allowed silence to prevail.

This recognition constitutes a moral vindication for the survivors, as well as a strong message that truth is not subject to a statute of limitations. Naming Turkey and demanding accountability and reparations are essential steps toward justice.

Europe must defend human rights consistently, without discounts and without double standards. The memory of the victims obliges us to continue to fight for truth, justice, and a solution to the Cyprus problem that will be fully based on international law, United Nations resolutions, and the EU acquis.

2-0290-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, today, the Commission has adopted a new action plan on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. It follows a commitment I made to this House in May, in light of the unprecedented cyber security capabilities of the latest models. Such models can be used not only for defensive, but also for offensive objectives in cyberspace. Their new capabilities are marking a strategic shift for the Union's security. Most importantly, these models fundamentally now change the economics of malicious actors, whether cyber criminals or national states. These advanced AI models can now build cyber exploits in minutes or hours at a fraction of the cost of vulnerability discovery by trained humans. Once weaponised, these vulnerabilities endanger the security of our infrastructure and society, so we must be prepared for these new capabilities being available widely, including to malicious actors, especially as other capabilities, (inaudible), for instance, are also growing.

The Commission's response has been immediate. We engaged with the entire AI and cybersecurity ecosystem, with you, with Member States, with our AI providers, with industry, and with our international partners. The action plan is not starting from scratch, as we know. The EU already has very robust legal and policy foundations. We are now turning them into action: capability and resilience along three priorities.

So first, AI models with high cyber capabilities deployed in Europe must be safe and our European players must have access to use them. The AI Act provides us with the world's most advanced framework to protect us against the risks of AI. And in less than one month, our AI office will also have the enforcement powers to ensure that providers also establish appropriate safeguards against misuse, including in the cyber domain. Assessing models before release is a cornerstone of risk mitigation. Europe must build excellence in this area. We will launch a call to step up Europe's evaluation capacity of AI models, including in cybersecurity, by 2027. The EU agency for cybersecurity, ENISA, will play an important role in making this action plan operational and together with ENISA, the Commission will also develop a European blueprint for structural access to advanced AI models with a focus on cybersecurity. We need common, clear and also transparent conditions for accessing these models, which also serves as a basis for cooperation and alignment with our international partners. And we must also strengthen our know-how on how to deploy these technologies for our cybersecurity. And this is why already by the end of this year, the Commission will also set up a secure platform to test how these models can be used safely for cybersecurity in critical sectors such as finance, energy, health, transport or public administration.

Second, we must protect ourselves against malicious attacks exploiting such models. Our immediate priority is now to identify and fix the most critical vulnerabilities, faster. The first step is the full and effective implementation of our cybersecurity legislation, so the NIS2 Directive, DORA and the Cyber Resilience Act. Not tomorrow, now. And to fix these vulnerabilities where exposure is the highest for our critical infrastructure, this is open source software. So we will launch a critical open source resilience campaign. In parallel, we will also support our critical sectors and our SMEs in understanding and also deploying existing AI tools, including those openly available to enhance their cyber resilience.

Third, we must build Europe's own AI powered cyber capabilities. We cannot rely only on non-European solutions for capabilities that are becoming critical for our security. So Europe has everything it takes to be competitive in this area. We have talent, a solid cybersecurity and AI ecosystem, and with AI factories and in the future also AI gigafactories, we have also the infrastructure. But we must get serious about financing. Frontier AI requires very large-scale investment, as we know. Far beyond what public funding alone can provide. We need to mobilise private capital especially equity. The new European tech equity capacity announced in the tech sovereignty package can be a game-changer here. Some will say that the cost of building European frontier capabilities is too high. In today's world, the cost of not building them will be much higher and it will grow every year. So our action plan now addresses the pressing challenges that frontier AI models present to cybersecurity, and we are building capacities for a stronger Europe in this domain.

2-0291-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, cybersecurity is a matter of national security. Yet even here, Europe remains heavily dependent on US vendors for cloud security, threat intelligence, identity management and endpoint protection. The same is true for AI. We must reduce the risk of supply chain attacks by expanding trusted partners worldwide, while gradually building more of our own tech stack.

Our dependency is not primarily about AI models, it is about the infrastructure they rely on. Europe has strong AI research, but too few companies operating at this frontier. That is why we must speed up EU‑level regulatory sandboxes, market harmonisation, and make sure our public sector chooses European tech first.

Right now, Europe is rightly pushing for computing capacity. However, quantum and giga factories don't help us if we don't have European businesses who use this capacity so that quantum can be commercialised. Investments in data centres and European cloud must go hand in hand with policies that help to create demand here at home. Data centres will not bring high‑tech jobs to Europe.

We also need to be realistic. We unfortunately cannot switch off from the US vendors any time soon. Europe relies so heavily on US cloud, software and hardware solutions that we will shoot ourselves in the foot if we speed up without extended supply chains and domestic solutions. The answer is not more regulation. It is smarter enforcement, strategic public procurement and an industrial policy that strengthens security, supports emerging technologies and reduces critical dependencies.

A shift from digital regulation towards tech sovereignty does not have to happen overnight. It will require a tremendous focus on details and pushing for overall mind change. But the worst we can do now is do nothing.

2-0292-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the more we digitise our lives, the more vulnerable our society is to cyber attacks. Where hackers used to be only human persons, today we are facing bots and artificial intelligence models. These can further expose our vulnerabilities. We saw what Anthropic's Mythos can do and in the future we will see AI-based hacking tools that are much more powerful. This is not a matter to be taken lightly. Situations like these can have devastating repercussions: power outages, disruption to airport operations or worse, in hospitals or other essential services when they are targeted.

Europe must anticipate, prepare and strengthen its defences against AI-powered hacking. Let us use the most advanced models proactively, identify the weaknesses of these attacks, while strengthening our digital defences. But in this digital reality we can no longer rely solely on foreign technology to keep us safe. Let us direct the right resources and European technological talent in the right direction. Let us invest in European capabilities.

2-0293-0000.sourceText:
