The accession process, too, is being subordinated to geopolitical interests in the middle of the war. Solidarity does not mean prolonging a war endlessly. Solidarity means protection for people, social rights and reconstruction in the interest of the people. Europe does not need escalation, but the path to peace.
2-0375-0000.factCheck: Although the speaker claims that the protection of Ukrainian refugees is being subordinated to Ukraine's military needs by turning away men of military age, the European Parliament actually rejected amendments to its resolution on the 2025 Commission report on Ukraine that proposed returning draft-age men, and the EU's Temporary Protection Directive continues to protect all refugees regardless of military status.

2-0376-0000.sourceText:
�� Господин Председател, pъководителите в Киев носят главната отговорност за това Украйна да не е изпълнила нито един от основните критерии за влизане в Европейския съюз. Най-близките приятели и сътрудници на Владимир Зеленски са обвинени, че са създали корупционни схеми за присвояването на огромни суми пари.

Представяте ли си какво ще направят тези хора или други подобни с европейските средства, ако страната им все пак влезе в Европейския съюз? Ако това присъединяване наистина се случи, ще имаме държава - член на Евросъюза, в която няма независими медии, няма свобода на словото, няма и политически плурализъм. Властите в Киев в момента провеждат активна политика по възвеличаването на хора, които активно са участвали в нацистките престъпления през Втората световна война. Личности и организации, отговорни за престъпления срещу човечеството, днес там се честват като герои, а Евросъюзът винаги категорично е осъждал подобни чудовищни деяния. Ето защо държавни ръководители, които се прекланят пред нацистки престъпници, няма как да преговарят за членство в Европейския съюз. А напоследък властите в Киев правят всичко възможно, за да забранят официално и украинската православна църква, просто защото тя не желае да се подчинява на диктата им.

Изобщо днешната власт в Киев е олицетворение на всичко това, срещу което Европейският съюз твърди, че се бори, Тя е корумпирана, унищожава свободата, величае нацизма и принуждава милиони украинци да търсят спасение в чужбина. Ако Брюксел допусне такива управляващи в Европейския съюз, той без съмнение ще спечели Световното първенство по лицемерие.
2-0376-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the leaders in Kyiv bear the main responsibility for Ukraine failing to fulfil a single one of the core criteria for joining the European Union. Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s closest friends and associates have been accused of creating corruption schemes for the embezzlement of huge amounts of money.

Can you imagine what these people or others like them will do with European funds if their country nevertheless enters the European Union? If this accession really happens, we will have a member state of the European Union in which there are no independent media, no freedom of speech, and no political pluralism. The authorities in Kyiv are currently pursuing an active policy of glorifying individuals who actively participated in Nazi crimes during the Second World War. Figures and organisations responsible for crimes against humanity are celebrated as heroes there today, and the European Union has always categorically condemned such monstrous acts. That is why state leaders who bow before Nazi criminals cannot possibly negotiate membership in the European Union. And lately, the authorities in Kyiv are doing everything possible to officially ban the Ukrainian Orthodox Church simply because it does not wish to obey their diktat.

Generally speaking, today’s government in Kyiv is the personification of everything that the European Union claims to fight against. It is corrupt, destroys freedom, glorifies Nazism, and forces millions of Ukrainians to seek refuge abroad. If Brussels admits such rulers into the European Union, it will undoubtedly win the World Championship of Hypocrisy.
2-0376-0000.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine has failed to fulfill a single core criterion for joining the European Union is false; the European Commission confirmed in June 2024 that Ukraine had completed all seven reform steps required to start accession negotiations, which formally began that month, and the first negotiating cluster on 'Fundamentals' was officially opened in June 2026.

2-0377-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, when I was in Kyiv once, the Government asked me: 'Madam Commissioner, what is your priority? What we do here now is being part of the accession process. We have to do the reforms under the Ukrainian plan and we are fighting the war, meaning we are fighting to survive. Can you tell us what is your priority?' Whatever we do in the evaluation, what Ukraine is doing today and how long it will take, please don't forget these are not normal circumstances.

In spite of this, Ukraine is advancing in the accession process. Ukraine is doing the reforms. We cannot expect that everything will be done in one week, in one month, in one year. It will not be done, but it will remain merit-based. I am the guardian of the merit-based process but merit-based does not necessarily mean slow. So I will use your words: let's stay vigilant, focused and united. Only with this we can help Ukraine.

2-0378-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, this motion for EU Parliament resolution is a very good paper. It lists carefully most of the Russia's heinous crimes against Ukraine and Ukrainians. It also delivers a very comprehensive list of actions that EU and EU Member States should take to support Ukraine and punish Russia.

In the end, the ESN Group gives its minority position to the Commission report. Most of the position is used for Putin-supporting nonsense that we are used to await from the ESN. However, there is one point where I must agree – ESN opposes the continued endorsement of open-ended financial military support without clear, objective and measurable conditions. This is true. We need a clear EU strategy on how we will end this war and secure Russia's defeat as soon as possible.

As this Parliament report states: we need a comprehensive, long-term strategic approach to support Ukraine, not just ad hoc assistance – a strategy that tells Russia that it has already lost. This paper tells us the tools, now the Commission and the Council need to make a real comprehensive strategic plan. Slava Ukraini!

2-0379-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, na madrugada da passada quinta-feira, as forças russas lançaram drones e mísseis sobre Kiev, num ataque que o presidente da câmara descreveu como «o mais massivo contra a capital». Alguns de nós tinham acabado de regressar da Ucrânia, de mais uma reunião da Comissão Parlamentar de Associação.

Também por isso, hoje, quero deixar aqui uma nota pessoal. O relatório que discutimos não é só sobre um país que, há mais de uma década, escolheu um futuro europeu. É sobre um processo de adesão de um país que tem territórios ilegalmente ocupados e se defende de uma guerra de agressão, enquanto progride no processo de reformas. Um país que não compreende porque é que os seus aliados não reforçam o apoio de meios de defesa aérea ou porque é que o Conselho não lhe permite a abertura de todos os capítulos temáticos de uma reforma. Um país perante o qual eu, hoje, coraria de vergonha com as palavras de alguns deputados nesta casa, que invocam os pequenos interesses dos seus países e os seus medos.

Apesar da lei marcial, mais de 80 % dos ucranianos defendem que o país deve continuar a reforma judicial e mais de 65 % desejam maior exigência externa nesse sentido, mostra um estudo. Este é um sinal claro de que a via de integração é uma escolha de toda a sociedade. Saibamos estar à altura.
2-0379-0000.englishText:
Mr President, in the early hours of last Thursday, Russian forces launched drones and missiles at Kyiv, in an attack that the mayor described as "the most massive against the capital". Some of us had just returned from Ukraine, from yet another meeting of the Parliamentary Association Committee.

For that reason too, today, I want to leave a personal note here. The report we are discussing is not just about a country that, for over a decade, chose a European future. It is about the accession process of a country that has illegally occupied territories and is defending itself against a war of aggression, whilst progressing in its reform process. A country that does not understand why its allies do not reinforce support with air defence assets or why the Council does not allow it to open all thematic chapters of a reform. A country before which I, today, would blush with shame at the words of some MEPs in this house, who invoke the petty interests of their countries and their fears.

Despite martial law, more than 80% of Ukrainians believe that the country should continue judicial reform and more than 65% desire greater external demands in that regard, a study shows. This is a clear sign that the path of integration is a choice of society as a whole. May we know how to rise to the occasion.

2-0380-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, commissaris, de Nederlandse bevolking wil niet dat Oekraïne toetreedt tot de EU. Dat werd tien jaar geleden al duidelijk. Meer dan 60 % van de Nederlanders sprak zich toen in een referendum uit tegen het EU-associatieverdrag met Oekraïne. De Nederlandse regering negeerde de uitkomst van het referendum en tekende uiteindelijk toch, nadat de EU in een juridisch bindende verklaring had bevestigd dat dit verdrag geen opstap zou zijn naar EU-lidmaatschap. Vandaag handelt de EU in strijd met die bindende verklaring door de toetreding van Oekraïne juist te versnellen.

De EU spreekt zich graag uit over democratie en rechtsstaat, maar trekt zich niets aan van de Nederlandse kiezer of van haar eigen afspraken.

Oekraïne is een door en door corrupt land. De Commissie erkent dan ook zelf dat ingrijpende hervormingen nodig zijn. Toch worden de onderhandelingen voortgezet. Bovendien is Oekraïne een land in oorlog. De wederopbouw van het land zal naar verwachting meer dan 507 miljard EUR kosten. Iedereen weet wie dit uiteindelijk zal moeten betalen: de Europese belastingbetaler. Onze kiezers hebben daar nooit mee ingestemd. We hebben de afgelopen jaren al genoeg miljarden naar Oekraïne gestuurd.

Nederland kan niet blijven opdraaien voor de rekening van anderen. Genoeg is genoeg. Bescherm Europa. Stop de uitbreiding van de EU.
2-0380-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, the Dutch population does not want Ukraine to join the EU. That was already clear ten years ago. More than 60% of the Dutch people spoke out in a referendum at the time against the EU association agreement with Ukraine. The Dutch government ignored the outcome of the referendum and ultimately signed it anyway, after the EU had confirmed in a legally binding declaration that this treaty would not be a stepping stone to EU membership. Today, the EU is acting in breach of that binding declaration by actually accelerating Ukraine's accession.

The EU is keen to talk about democracy and the rule of law, but ignores the Dutch voter and its own agreements.

Ukraine is a thoroughly corrupt country. The Commission itself therefore acknowledges that far-reaching reforms are necessary. Yet the negotiations are continuing. Moreover, Ukraine is a country at war. The reconstruction of the country is expected to cost more than EUR 507 billion. Everyone knows who will ultimately have to pay for this: the European taxpayer. Our voters have never agreed to that. We have already sent enough billions to Ukraine in recent years.

Migration—[Correction based on text: The Netherlands] cannot continue to foot the bill for others. Enough is enough. Protect Europe. Stop the EU's enlargement.
2-0380-0000.factCheck: The claim that the EU is breaching the 2016 legally binding declaration by advancing Ukraine's accession is misleading; that declaration only clarified that the Association Agreement itself did not automatically confer candidate status or commit the EU to doing so, but it did not bar Ukraine from applying for membership or the EU from granting candidate status under standard treaty procedures.

2-0381-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, è nei momenti più difficili che si misura la credibilità dell'Europa, e oggi essere credibili significa sostenere l'Ucraina, ma anche lavorare con determinazione per una pace giusta, duratura e fondata sul rispetto del diritto internazionale.

Sostenere Kiev significa ribadire la sicurezza dell'Europa e dell'Alleanza atlantica, che è una responsabilità comune, da assumere secondo le capacità di ciascuno Stato membro, nel pieno coordinamento con la NATO.

Significa anche rafforzare la pressione sulla Russia, rendendo più efficaci le sanzioni e contrastando ogni forma di elusione, a partire dalle cosiddette flotte ombra, che continuano ad alimentare lo sforzo bellico di Mosca.

Allo stesso tempo, il percorso di adesione dell'Ucraina all'Unione europea rappresenta una prospettiva che sosteniamo, ovviamente, con convinzione. Ma, proprio perché crediamo nel progetto europeo, questo percorso dovrà rispettare integralmente i criteri di adesione, le riforme richieste e i tempi necessari. Accelerazioni dettate dalla contingenza politica, dal cuore piuttosto che dalla mente, non rafforzano l'Unione e rischiano, al contrario, di indebolirne la credibilità.

La libertà non è mai un bene acquisito per sempre: va difesa ogni giorno con responsabilità, coerenza e coraggio ed è questo il compito che oggi spetta all'Unione europea.
2-0381-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable members, it is in the most difficult moments that Europe's credibility is measured, and today being credible means supporting Ukraine, but also working with determination for a just, lasting peace based on respect for international law.

Supporting Kyiv means reaffirming the security of Europe and the Atlantic Alliance, which is a shared responsibility to be assumed according to the capabilities of each Member State, in full coordination with NATO.

It also means strengthening pressure on Russia, making sanctions more effective and countering every form of circumvention, starting with the so-called shadow fleets, which continue to fuel Moscow's war effort.

At the same time, Ukraine's path to accession to the European Union represents a prospect that we support, of course, with conviction. But precisely because we believe in the European project, this path must fully respect the accession criteria, the required reforms, and the necessary timeframe. Accelerations dictated by political contingency, by the heart rather than the mind, do not strengthen the Union and risk, on the contrary, weakening its credibility.

Freedom is never a permanently acquired asset: it must be defended every day with responsibility, consistency, and courage, and this is the task that falls to the European Union today.

2-0382-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, sehr geehrte Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! „Wir wollen nicht Sklaven Putins sein“ – das ist der Satz, den ich in der Ukraine am häufigsten gehört habe. Ja, die Menschen in der Ukraine reden von Freiheit; sie wollen in Freiheit leben wie wir, und natürlich gehören sie deswegen auch in die Europäische Union. Da muss noch viel gemacht werden.

Und wenn hier ausgerechnet von rechts, wo es schon wieder Korruptionsskandale gibt, von Korruption gesprochen wird: Ja, das weiß man auch in der Ukraine, aber es gibt eine starke Zivilgesellschaft; das gefällt ihnen auch nicht. Die Leute sind auf die Straße gegangen, als ihnen ein Gesetz nicht gefallen hat. Wir haben mit den Chefs der Antikorruptionsbehörden gesprochen; sie haben uns das alles erklärt. Das hat gezeigt, was das für ein lebhafter Staat ist und ein demokratischer Staat, der natürlich zu uns passt.

Vor Kurzem war Garri Kasparow in Wien, und ich habe ihn gefragt, warum diese Rechtsextremen immer wie Putin reden. Er hat gesagt, er kann sich gar nicht vorstellen, dass die nicht von dort finanziert werden. Bitte, das sagt Kasparow, ist aber interessant, weil die Desinformation natürlich genauso läuft.

Wir stehen auf der Seite des ukrainischen Volkes, weil das ukrainische Volk auch auf unserer Seite steht. Slawa Ukrajini!

Und eines möchte ich noch; ich weiß, ich darf keine Fotos zeigen, aber jeder kann sich das im Internet anschauen. Wenn Sie diese Bilder gesehen haben, dann hören Sie denen auch nicht mehr zu.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0382-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! "We don't want to be Putin's slaves" – that is the sentence I heard most frequently in Ukraine. Yes, the people in Ukraine talk about freedom; they want to live in freedom like us, and of course that is why they belong in the European Union. A lot still needs to be done there.

And when corruption is talked about here, of all places, by the right, where there are corruption scandals yet again: yes, they know about that in Ukraine too, but there is a strong civil society; they don't like that either. People took to the streets when they didn't like a law. We spoke to the heads of the anti-corruption agencies; they explained it all to us. That showed what a vibrant state it is and a democratic state that of course suits us.

Recently, Garry Kasparov was in Vienna, and I asked him why these right-wing extremists always talk like Putin. He said he can't even imagine that they aren't being financed from there. Please, Kasparov says that, but it's interesting because the disinformation naturally operates in the exact same way.

We stand on the side of the Ukrainian people because the Ukrainian people are also on our side. Slawa Ukrajini!

And one more thing; I know I'm not allowed to show photos, but anyone can look them up on the internet. Once you've seen these pictures, you won't listen to them anymore either.

(The speaker agreed to answer a "blue card" procedure question.)

2-0383-0000.sourceText: (ESN), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ja, lieber Kollege Brandstätter, vielen Dank für Ihren Einsatz für die Demokratie und Freiheit in der Ukraine. Mich würde interessieren: Haben Sie dafür auch gekämpft ein Jahr vor dem Krieg, als Selenskyj die Demokratische, damals die stärkste Partei in den Umfragen, verbieten ließ, als er vier Fernsehsender verboten hat und zehn Radiosender? Was haben Sie damals gemacht?
2-0383-0000.englishText: (ESN), blue-card procedure. – Yes, dear colleague Brandstätter, thank you very much for your commitment to democracy and freedom in Ukraine. I would be interested: Did you also fight for this a year before the war, when Zelenskyy had the Democratic party, which was the strongest party in the polls at the time, banned, when he banned four television channels and ten radio stations? What did you do back then?
2-0383-0000.factCheck: The claim that Volodymyr Zelenskyy banned the leading opposition party and ten radio stations a year before the war is false; while three pro-Russian TV channels were sanctioned and taken off the air in February 2021, the prominent opposition party Opposition Platform — For Life was not suspended or banned until after the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022.

2-0384-0000.sourceText: Das war wann? Ich kann mich nämlich nicht erinnern. Wann soll das gewesen sein?
2-0384-0000.englishText: When was that? I can't remember, you see. When is that supposed to have been?

2-0385-0000.sourceText: Ein Jahr vor Ausbruch des Krieges.
2-0385-0000.englishText: One year before the outbreak of the war.

2-0386-0000.sourceText:
(Renew), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Also, wissen Sie, wenn Sie damit anfangen, dass irgendjemand irgendwo was verboten hätte – wenn ich mir anschaue, was die AfD macht, was ich vor Kurzem wieder gesehen habe. Das sind diejenigen, die sagen, sie sind das freundliche Gesicht des Nationalsozialismus. Bitte hören Sie mit diesen Geschichten auf.

Und egal, was auch immer, es geht um das, was jetzt ist. Putin, zu dem Sie auch gefahren sind, mordet täglich. Ich kann Ihnen das Foto jetzt bringen; das werde ich jetzt machen. Hängen Sie sich das doch zu Hause auf. Gehen Sie auf Ihre Wahlversammlungen damit und sagen Sie den Menschen, was in der Ukraine stattfindet. Dann sind Sie glaubwürdig.
2-0386-0000.englishText:
(Renew), reply to a question under the "blue card" procedure. – Well, you know, if you start by claiming that someone somewhere has banned something – when I look at what the AfD does, what I saw again recently. Those are the ones who say they are the friendly face of National Socialism. Please stop with these stories.

And no matter what, it is about what is happening now. Putin, whom you also visited, is murdering people every day. I can bring you the photo now; I am going to do that now. Hang it up at home. Take it to your election rallies and tell the people what is happening in Ukraine. Then you will be credible.

2-0387-0000.sourceText:
Ich nehme zur Kenntnis, dass Sie meine Frage nicht beantwortet haben, dass Sie nichts für die Opposition in der Ukraine getan haben, dass Sie nichts getan haben …

(Der Präsident entzieht dem Redner das Wort.)
2-0387-0000.englishText:
I note that you did not answer my question, that you have done nothing for the opposition in Ukraine, that you have done nothing ...

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone.)

2-0388-0000.sourceText: Sorry, but you can only have a follow-up if the speaker agrees to continue the dialogue.

2-0389-0000.sourceText: Mr President, it was Monday night while many of us woke up early to catch the flight to Strasbourg that Kyiv was hit again. The Russian missiles and drones killed 28 people, dozens wounded and true horror. So some in Europe are tired of the war, that's fair enough. But what gives Ukrainians the strength to keep fighting even though they are so tired of this horror? I have asked this question to Ukrainians in Ukraine and also those who are in my hometown, in Riga. And the answer is always the same: it's Europe, that one day they will belong here among us. So Ukraine must be part of the European Union and we will walk through the difficult issues. There are many and they are real. But the promise itself cannot be doubted, because the promise is exactly what gives Ukrainians the strength to keep fighting for their country and for all of Europe.

2-0390-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Det här är ett bra betänkande som kommer att få stort stöd i denna kammare i omröstningen. Särskilt positivt är att flera av våra ändringsförslag är med: om arbetsrätt och fackliga rättigheter, om förnybar energi, om hälsovård.

Men det kan fortfarande bli ännu bättre. Skrivningarna om skuggflottan i Östersjön bör skärpas. Nu försöker länderna var och en för sig att stoppa trafiken. Vi behöver samordning. Vi behöver handlingskraft. Vi behöver stoppa denna sanktionsbrytande trafik som finansierar det blodiga kriget.

Herr talman! Den ryska propagandan låter alltmer ihålig. Ukraina inte bara försvarar sig, man slår i dag ut raffinaderier och installationer i Ryssland. Den ryska imperialismen är på väg mot nederlag. Det nederlaget är också vägen till fred. Slava Ukraini.

(Talaren godtog en fråga ("blått kort").)
2-0390-0000.englishText:
Mr President! This is a good report that will receive strong support in this House in the vote. It is particularly positive that several of our amendments are included: on labour law and trade union rights, on renewable energy, on healthcare.

But it can still be even better. The wording on the shadow fleet in the Baltic Sea should be tightened. Countries are now trying one by one to stop the traffic. We need coordination. We need decisiveness. We need to stop this sanctions-busting traffic that finances the bloody war.

Mr President! Russian propaganda is sounding increasingly hollow. Ukraine is not only defending itself, it is today striking refineries and installations in Russia. Russian imperialism is heading towards defeat. That defeat is also the path to peace. Slava Ukraini.

(The speaker agreed to take a "blue card" question.)

2-0391-0000.sourceText: Jag välkomnar engagemanget mot den ryska skuggflottan och instämmer också i att vi måste göra mer gemensamt. Men jag vill fråga dig, Jonas Sjöstedt, om du är beredd att jobba för att Nato, och EU tillsammans med Nato, ska få större muskler, fler resurser för att agera? För vi har ju två utmärkta organisationer i Nato och EU som redan är på plats och behöver agera och göra mer.
2-0391-0000.englishText: I welcome the commitment against the Russian shadow fleet and also agree that we must do more together. But I want to ask you, Jonas Sjöstedt, if you are prepared to work to ensure that NATO, and the EU together with NATO, get more muscle, more resources to act? Because we have two excellent organizations in NATO and the EU that are already in place and need to act and do more.

2-0392-0000.sourceText: Jag tror att det finns två olika strukturer som kan samordna arbetet mot skuggflottan. Det ena är den Europeiska unionen, och då måste kommissionen ta ett initiativ i sådant fall. Det andra är att länderna runt Östersjön gör det tillsammans. Bägge de vägarna ligger öppna som jag ser det. USA kan vi inte riktigt lita på i Nato. Trump har i praktiken svikit Ukraina. Så jag tror att vi får räkna med att göra detta själva i Europa, att stoppa skuggflottan. Då handlar det om väldigt praktiska saker som att samordna kustbevakning, att införa liknande regler och att faktiskt konsekvent ingripa mot de ryska fartygen.
2-0392-0000.englishText: I think there are two different structures that can coordinate the work against the shadow fleet. One is the European Union, and in that case the Commission must take an initiative. The other is for the countries around the Baltic Sea to do it together. Both of those paths are open as I see it. We cannot really rely on the US in NATO. Trump has practically betrayed Ukraine. So I think we must expect to do this ourselves in Europe, to stop the shadow fleet. Then it is a matter of very practical things like coordinating coast guard, introducing similar rules, and actually consistently intervening against the Russian ships.

2-0393-0000.sourceText:
Gerbiamas Pirmininke. Sveiki, aš esu iš tos frakcijos, kurios ne visi nariai palaiko Ukrainą, jie iš partijos "Alternatyva Vokietijai". Jų dauguma yra mūsų frakcijos nariai. Tačiau pas mus frakcijoje yra demokratija. Aš balsuoju asmeniškai, visada palaikydamas Ukrainą. Ir manęs frakcija niekada neįspėjo. Elkis pagal savo sąžinę. Man atrodo, kad jūs, dešinieji, tokių teisių čia neturite Europos Parlamente, nors laikote save demokratais. Jeigu Ukraina ir jūs, kurie šiandien, jeigu Europa būtų vieninga ir suteikus didelę finansinę ir karinę paramą Ukrainai nuo pat pirmų dienų, karas būtų pasibaigęs. Jūs kaltinkite ir save, kad per mažai rėmėte Ukrainą. Europos Sąjunga taiko Ukrainai, kuri kariauja, tokias pačias sąlygas, kad ji būtų narė. Ar jūs neturite gėdos? Jau turėjo būti Europos Sąjungos narė Ukraina. Ar jūs turite nors kiek supratimo, ką kalba komisarė? Jūs mažiau kalbėkite, o daugiau darykit. Ne, Trumpas, ne Putinas kaltas, kad Ukraina ne Europos Sąjungos narė – jūs esate kalti. Jūs turėjote padaryti išimtines sąlygas Ukrainai. Jeigu ji būtų Europos Sąjungos narė, ji būtų ir stipresnė finansiškai, ir taip pat kariniu atžvilgiu. Prisiimkite atsakomybę.

(Kalbėtojas sutiko atsakyti į mėlynosios kortelės klausimą)
2-0393-0000.englishText:
Mr President. Hello, I am from that faction where not all members support Ukraine, they are from the party "Alternative for Germany". The majority of them are members of our faction. However, we have democracy in our faction. I vote personally, always supporting Ukraine. And the faction has never warned me. Act according to your conscience. It seems to me that you, the right-wing, do not have such rights here in the European Parliament, although you consider yourselves democrats. If Ukraine and you, who today—if Europe had been united and provided great financial and military support to Ukraine from the very first days, the war would have ended. You should also blame yourselves for supporting Ukraine too little. The European Union applies the same conditions to Ukraine, which is at war, to be a member. Do you have no shame? Ukraine should have been a member of the European Union already. Do you have any understanding of what the Commissioner is talking about? You should talk less and do more. No, Trump, not Putin is to be blamed that Ukraine is not a member of the European Union—you are to be blamed. You should have made exceptional conditions for Ukraine. If it were a member of the European Union, it would be stronger financially and also militarily. Take responsibility.

(The speaker agreed to answer a blue-card question)

2-0394-0000.sourceText:
Dragi kolega, zar je jednoumlje da se agresija nagrađuje davanjem teritorija? Zar je jednoumlje stotine tisuća poginulih i ubijenih? Zar je jednoumlje deseci odvedene djece u Rusiju? Zar je to jednoumlje? Jeste li ikada vidjeli poginulog na ratištu? Jeste li ikada čuli za Hrvatsku? Jeste li ikada čuli za moju zemlju koja je bila zadnja u Europskoj uniji koja je imala ratnu agresiju?

Ne, to nije jednoumlje, to je poštenje, to je humanost i to je ljudskost. Za to se mi zalažemo u Ukrajini.
2-0394-0000.englishText:
Dear colleague, is it unanimity of thought that aggression is rewarded by giving up territory? Is it unanimity of thought hundreds of thousands dead and killed? Is it unanimity of thought dozens of children taken away to Russia? Is it that unanimity of thought? Have you ever seen someone killed on the battlefield? Have you ever heard of Croatia? Have you ever heard of my country, which was the last in the European Union to experience military aggression?

No, that is not unanimity of thought, that is honesty, that is humanity and that is humaneness. That is what we stand for in Ukraine.

2-0395-0000.sourceText: Aš sutinku, kad nėra vieno būdo, bet aš kalbu apie tai, kad Europos Sąjunga turi būti ryžtingesnė, principingesnė, mažiau kalbėti, o daugiau daryti realių veiksmų Ukrainos atžvilgiu. Štai kame yra dalykas. Jūs rezoliucijų priėmėte tiek, kad mylit Ukrainą. Jau man atrodo, visus Briuselio stogus galima nuklijuoti, bet tai nieko nepadeda. Daugiau darbų.
2-0395-0000.englishText: I agree that there is no single way, but I am talking about the fact that the European Union must be more resolute, more principled, talk less, and take more real action regarding Ukraine. That is what the matter is about. You have adopted so many resolutions about how much you love Ukraine. It seems to me that all the roofs in Brussels could be wallpapered with them, but that doesn't help at all. More deeds.

2-0396-0000.sourceText:
Vážený pán predsedajúci. Už tu konečne musí zaznieť pravda. Ukrajina na čele so Zelenským sa správa ako fašistický štát. Opozičných politikov posielajú do pracovných táborov. Oslavujú banderovcov, ktorí masovo vraždili ľudí v Poľsku aj na Slovensku. Zelenskyj sa priamo vyhrážal bývalému maďarskému premiérovi. Ukrajina spáchala teroristický útok na Nord Stream. Menšiny na Ukrajine sú šikanované a Zelenskyj vládne bez volieb. Navyše, Ukrajina je nekonečne skorumpovaná. Za ukradnuté európske peniaze Zelenského kumpáni stavajú haciendy so zlatými záchodmi. Kľúčová otázka je, prečo pani Leyenová a pani Kallasová futrujete zbraňami a miliardami fašistický režim. Sú len dve možnosti: buď ste aj vy presvedčení nacisti a nenávisť voči Rusku ste povýšili nad všetky európske hodnoty, alebo tam posielate miliardy a oni vám posielajú vratky. My Slováci nechceme vašu vojnu proti Rusku! My Slováci chceme mier!

(Rečník súhlasil, že odpovie na otázku položenú zdvihnutím modrej karty)
2-0396-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr President. The truth finally needs to be said here. Ukraine, led by Zelensky, is behaving like a fascist state. Opposition politicians are being sent to labor camps. They celebrate Banderites, who mass-murdered people in Poland and Slovakia. Zelensky directly threatened the former Hungarian Prime Minister. Ukraine committed a terrorist attack on Nord Stream. Minorities in Ukraine are being bullied and Zelensky rules without elections. Moreover, Ukraine is infinitely corrupt. With stolen European money, Zelensky's cronies are building mansions with golden toilets. The key question is why Ms Leyen and Ms Kallas are feeding weapons and billions to a fascist regime. There are only two possibilities: either you are also convinced Nazis and you have elevated hatred of Russia above all European values, or you are sending billions there and they are sending you kickbacks. We Slovaks do not want your war against Russia! We Slovaks want peace!

(The speaker agreed to answer a question raised by the raising of a blue card)
2-0396-0000.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine is sending opposition politicians to labor camps is false; Ukraine does not operate labor camps, and while certain pro-Russian political parties have been suspended or banned under martial law during the ongoing war, there is no evidence of opposition figures being sent to forced labor facilities.

2-0397-0000.sourceText: Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem pekne. Pán Blaha, toto choďte, prosím, prednášať na MGIMO do Moskvy. Tam Vás určite budú radi počúvať. Kedy sa už konečne presťahujete do Ruska, keď tam je to všetko také skvelé, keď tam tak rád chodíte a tu všetko len kritizujete? Tu sú všetci fašisti. Kedy sa tam už konečne presťahujete je moja otázka a dáte nám konečne pokoj v Európe? A druhá otázka: podpora členstva Ukrajiny v Európskej únii je v našom záujme. Je aj v záujme tých Slovákov, ktorí žijú na hraniciach s Ukrajinou a ktorým vy vašou rétorikou ponúkate viete čo? Iba strach a chudobu.
2-0397-0000.englishText: Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem pekne. Pán Blaha, toto choďte, prosím, prednášať na MGIMO do Moskvy. Tam Vás určite budú radi počúvať. Kedy sa už konečne presťahujete do Ruska, keď tam je to všetko také skvelé, keď tam tak rád chodíte a tu všetko len kritizujete? Tu sú všetci fašisti. Kedy sa tam už konečne presťahujete je moja otázka a dáte nám konečne pokoj v Európe? A druhá otázka: podpora členstva Ukrajiny v Európskej únii je v našom záujme. Je aj v záujme tých Slovákov, ktorí žijú na hraniciach s Ukrajinou a ktorým vy vašou rétorikou ponúkate viete čo? Iba strach a chudobu.

2-0398-0000.sourceText:
Pani Karvašová, a ja sa pýtam, kedy Vy pôjdete bojovať na Ukrajinu, keďže teraz nechávate za seba umierať Ukrajincov? Kedy Vy pôjdete na Ukrajinu? Kedy sa konečne presťahujete a dáte pokoj Slovákom? Nie, Slováci nechcú vojnu proti Rusku, Nechcú eskaláciu. Nechcú, aby tu bola tretia svetová vojna. Nechceme, aby Vaše deti a moje deti jedného dňa umierali kvôli týmto vojnovým štváčom. Áno, Slováci chcú mier,

(predsedajúci odobral rečníkovi slovo)
2-0398-0000.englishText:
Mrs Karvašová, and I ask you, when will you go to fight in Ukraine, since you are now letting Ukrainians die in your place? When will you go to Ukraine? When will you finally move away and leave Slovaks in peace? No, Slovaks do not want a war against Russia. They do not want escalation. They do not want a third world war here. We do not want your children and my children to die one day because of these warmongers. Yes, Slovaks want peace,

(The President withdrew the floor from the speaker)

2-0399-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, thank you to the Commission for the good report on Ukraine and thank you to my colleague Michael Gahler for the opinion paper.

I think that here we have to be clear. The accession of Ukraine as a full member of the European Union is a balance exercise. We have to bring together the demands of geopolitical and strategic order that invite for a fast track for the session and, at the same time, to respect the technical criteria of Copenhagen. We have to advance in parallel in both lines.

At the same time, we have to start thinking about the day after. What will happen once there is a ceasefire and a negotiating process? There will be more than 1 million, or around 1 million, demobilised people coming back home. Some millions of displaced people in exile in Europe coming back home. There will be elections, and there will be a fragmented political landscape with a different scenario.

Europe has to be prepared for this and to start thinking about this now, not tomorrow, but today.

2-0400-0000.sourceText:
�� Panie Przewodniczący! Nacjonalizm zabija. Nacjonalizm zabija, kiedy żołnierze przeprowadzają czystki etniczne w imię swojej ideologii, ignorując prawa człowieka, na których zbudowana jest współczesna Europa. Nacjonalizm zabija, kiedy wiele dekad później cyniczni politycy wykorzystują politykę historyczną do grania na emocjach swoich wyborców, rozbijając w ten sposób europejską jedność wobec śmiertelnego niebezpieczeństwa ze strony Rosji.

Cóż za ironia, że ci sami politycy, którzy najgłośniej mówią o bezpieczeństwie i potrzebie chłodnego kalkulowania, dają się tak łatwo sprowokować i popadają w histerię, podczas gdy na froncie w Ukrainie toczą się losy naszego kontynentu. To nie pierwszy raz, kiedy skrajna prawica udowadnia, że to ona jest największym sprzymierzeńcem Rosji, a zarazem największym niebezpieczeństwem dla Europy. Zauważyliście, że cały czas mówią o Ukrainie, a prawie w ogóle o Rosji? Przypadek?

Apeluję do władz ukraińskich, ale także polskich, aby dołożyły wszelkich starań w celu rozwiązania tego sporu. Dobre relacje pomiędzy naszymi krajami to podstawa dla bezpieczeństwa Europy. W przeciwnym razie w przyszłości będziemy musieli kontynuować tę debatę, ale po rosyjsku.

(Mówca nie zgodził się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki przez Piotr Müller)
2-0400-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Nationalism kills. Nationalism kills when soldiers carry out ethnic cleansing in the name of their ideology, ignoring human rights upon which modern Europe is built. Nationalism kills when, many decades later, cynical politicians use historical politics to play on their voters' emotions, thereby shattering European unity in the face of mortal danger from Russia.

What an irony that the same politicians who speak the loudest about security and the need for cold calculation allow themselves to be so easily provoked and fall into hysteria, while the fate of our continent is being decided on the front line in Ukraine. This is not the first time that the far right proves that it is Russia's greatest ally and, at the same time, the greatest danger to Europe. Have you noticed that they talk about Ukraine all the time, and almost not at all about Russia? Coincidence?

I appeal to the Ukrainian authorities, but also to the Polish authorities, to make every effort to resolve this dispute. Good relations between our countries are the basis for Europe's security. Otherwise, in the future we will have to continue this debate, but in Russian.

(The speaker declined a blue-card question by Piotr Müller)

2-0401-0000.sourceText:
�� Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Od kilku lat obserwujemy proces, w którym Ukraina, nie będąc członkiem Unii Europejskiej, korzysta z praw i przywilejów państwa członkowskiego, nie ponosząc jednocześnie żadnych kosztów. Dodatkowo z europejskiego, wspólnotowego długu finansujemy Ukrainę.

W tym samym czasie obserwujemy niekończącą się serię przestępstw korupcyjnych, które wybuchają w otoczeniu samego prezydenta Zełenskiego. Pieniądze naszych podatników finansują bogactwo ukraińskich oligarchów. To rodzi fundamentalne pytanie o zasady równego traktowania.

Polscy rolnicy, przewoźnicy, przedsiębiorcy, a także zwykli obywatele od lat ponoszą koszty dostosowania do unijnych regulacji, norm środowiskowych i wymogów administracyjnych. Jeżeli jednocześnie otwieramy rynek dla podmiotów funkcjonujących w odmiennych warunkach regulacyjnych, trudno mówić o uczciwej konkurencji.

Jest również kwestia polityki historycznej. Polska ma prawo, ma pełne prawo oczekiwać od władz Ukrainy jednoznacznego potępienia zbrodni popełnionych przez organizacje odpowiedzialne za ludobójstwo na ludności cywilnej oraz prowadzenia polityki pamięci opartej na prawdzie historycznej. Gloryfikowanie banderyzmu na Ukrainie przez obecne władze nie tylko nie pozwala myśleć o konstruktywnej współpracy, ale stawia Ukrainę poza nawiasem cywilizacji europejskiej.

Dalsze faworyzowanie Ukrainy kosztem państw członkowskich, szczególnie Europy Środkowo-Wschodniej, jest niedopuszczalne, a członkostwo Ukrainy w Unii Europejskiej nie jest w polskim interesie.

(Mówczyni nie zgodziła się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki przez Sergey Lagodinsky)
2-0401-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Madam Commissioner! For several years we have been observing a process in which Ukraine, without being a member of the European Union, enjoys the rights and privileges of a member state while bearing no costs at the same time. Additionally, we are financing Ukraine from European, common debt.

At the same time, we are witnessing an endless series of corruption crimes that break out in the immediate circle of President Zelenskyy. Our taxpayers' money is financing the wealth of Ukrainian oligarchs. This raises a fundamental question about the principles of equal treatment.

Polish farmers, hauliers, entrepreneurs, and ordinary citizens have for years borne the costs of adapting to EU regulations, environmental standards, and administrative requirements. If at the same time we open the market to entities operating under different regulatory conditions, it is difficult to speak of fair competition.

There is also the issue of historical policy. Poland has the right, the full right, to expect the Ukrainian authorities to unequivocally condemn the crimes committed by organizations responsible for the genocide of the civilian population and to pursue a policy of remembrance based on historical truth. The glorification of Bandera's ideology in Ukraine by the current authorities not only makes it impossible to think about constructive cooperation, but places Ukraine outside the pale of European civilization.

Further favoring of Ukraine at the expense of member states, especially Central and Eastern Europe, is unacceptable, and Ukraine's membership in the European Union is not in Poland's interest.

(The speaker declined a question signaled by the raising of a blue card by Sergey Lagodinsky)
2-0401-0000.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine enjoys the rights and privileges of an EU member state is false; as a non-member, Ukraine does not have voting rights in EU institutions, representation in the European Parliament, or full access to the single market and structural funds, and its financial assistance is subject to strict monitoring.

2-0402-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! W Unii Europejskiej nie ma miejsca dla czcicieli morderców spod znaku UPA. Nie możemy milczeć, gdy gloryfikowana jest Ukraińska Powstańcza Armia - zbrodnicza organizacja, która odpowiada za brutalne mordy na ponad 100 000 Polaków i wszystkich mniejszościach nieukraińskich na Wołyniu i w ówczesnej Małopolsce Wschodniej. Nie możemy pozwolić, aby w Europie mitologizowano Stefana Banderę i rozsiewano kłamstwa na temat zbrodni wołyńskiej.

Polska od samego początku wspiera Ukrainę w walce z Rosją. Jako naród otworzyliśmy swoje domy dla milionów ukraińskich uchodźców. Nikt w Polsce nie ma wątpliwości, że wróg jest w Moskwie. A to nie jest apel przeciwko narodowi ukraińskiemu, tylko polityce jego władz. Tym bardziej jako Polacy mamy moralne prawo powiedzieć: weto. Z Banderą Ukraina do Unii Europejskiej nie wejdzie.

Ukraina ma z kogo być dumna. To bohaterscy obrońcy Ukrainy, którzy od 2014 roku walczą z Rosją o niepodległość. To nie zbrodniarze, którzy nabijali polskie dzieci na widły. Jeśli Ukraina chce zostać częścią naszej wspólnoty, musi odrzucić kult UPA, a nasz sojusz musi zacząć opierać się na historycznej prawdzie i wzajemnym szacunku. Stop banderyzmowi.

(Mówca zgodził się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki)
2-0402-0000.englishText:
Mr President! There is no place in the European Union for worshippers of murderers under the sign of the UPA. We cannot remain silent when the Ukrainian Insurgent Army - a criminal organization responsible for brutal murders of over 100,000 Poles and all non-Ukrainian minorities in Volhynia and former Eastern Lesser Poland - is glorified. We cannot allow Stepan Bandera to be mythologized and lies about the Volhynian massacre to be spread in Europe.

Poland has been supporting Ukraine in its fight against Russia from the very beginning. As a nation, we opened our homes to millions of Ukrainian refugees. No one in Poland has any doubts that the enemy is in Moscow. And this is not an appeal against the Ukrainian nation, but against the policies of its authorities. All the more as Poles, we have the moral right to say: veto. With Bandera, Ukraine will not enter the European Union.

Ukraine has those it can be proud of. These are the heroic defenders of Ukraine who have been fighting Russia for independence since 2014. These are not criminals who impaled Polish children on pitchforks. If Ukraine wants to become part of our community, it must reject the cult of the UPA, and our alliance must begin to be based on historical truth and mutual respect. Stop Banderism.

(The speaker agreed to a question raised by the raising of a blue card)

2-0403-0000.sourceText: Thanks for accepting the blue card, as opposed to many others. How do you react to what the Kremlin is saying? The Kremlin is saying that your president and you yourself have finally seen the light and everything that the Kremlin has been saying all along – that these are Nazis in Kyiv, that now you have recognised it and you agree with the Kremlin.

2-0404-0000.sourceText: Jestem bardzo zasmucony tym, że Putin cieszy się z decyzji pana prezydenta Zełenskiego, ale w otoczeniu prezydenta Zełenskiego poszukałbym agentów Kremla, którzy podpowiedzieli mu, żeby gloryfikować morderców z UPA, nazywając jedną z jednostek armii ukraińskiej właśnie mianem UPA. To było oczywiste, że to oburzy opinię publiczną, nie tylko w Polsce. Przypomnę, że kult UPA, kult zbrodniarzy z UPA potępia również Izrael i wiele innych nacji, których mniejszości były mordowane w latach 40. przez tę organizację.
2-0404-0000.englishText: I am very saddened that Putin is rejoicing at the decision of Mr President Zelensky, but in President Zelensky's entourage I would look for Kremlin agents who suggested to him to glorify the murderers from the UPA, naming one of the units of the Ukrainian army precisely after the UPA. It was obvious that this would outrage public opinion, not only in Poland. Let me remind you that the cult of the UPA, the cult of the UPA criminals, is also condemned by Israel and many other nations whose minorities were murdered in the 1940s by this organization.

2-0405-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Wir haben heute Damen und Herren hier zu Besuch, die unserer Debatte zuhören, und ich bin sicher, manche glauben, sie hören hier nicht richtig. Wir sind im Herzen Europas, dem größten Friedensprojekt der Welt nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg, und erleben seit über vier Jahren einen vollen Angriff auf die Ukraine – streng genommen seit 2014 mit der Annexion der Krim. Hier sind tatsächlich Kolleginnen und Kollegen auf der linken Seite, wie üblich, die die Schuld der Ukraine geben, dass sie überfallen worden ist, auf der rechten Seite, wo irgendeine Geschichte erzählt wird.

Meine Damen und Herren, dieser Angriff auf die Ukraine – das Ermorden, Zerstören, Vergewaltigen, Verschleppen, Foltern –, wenn wir die Ukraine nicht unterstützen, wird eines Tages dieses vor unserer Haustür stehen. Und wer glaubt, dem ist nicht so, der soll nächstes Mal früher aufstehen. Das ist die Realität. Deswegen werden wir die Ukraine weiter unterstützen – wirtschaftlich, humanitär und ja, auch mit Waffen, damit Russland diesen Krieg nie und nimmer gewinnt. Das ist unsere Aufgabe. Und jeder, der hier eine andere Geschichte erzählt, ist nicht auf der Seite der Freiheit, sondern auf der Seite der Aggressoren.

(Die Rednerin ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0405-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! We have ladies and gentlemen visiting us here today who are listening to our debate, and I am sure some believe they are not hearing right. We are in the heart of Europe, the greatest peace project in the world after the Second World War, and have been experiencing a full attack on Ukraine for over four years – strictly speaking since 2014 with the annexation of Crimea. Here we actually have colleagues on the left side, as usual, who blame Ukraine for being invaded, and on the right side, where some story is being told.

Ladies and gentlemen, this attack on Ukraine – the murder, destruction, rape, abduction, torture – if we do not support Ukraine, one day this will be on our doorstep. And anyone who believes otherwise should get up earlier next time. That is the reality. That is why we will continue to support Ukraine – economically, humanitatively, and yes, also with weapons, so that Russia never, ever wins this war. That is our task. And anyone who tells a different story here is not on the side of freedom, but on the side of the aggressors.

(The speaker agreed to answer a blue-card question.)

2-0406-0000.sourceText:
Pani Poseł! Moja rodzina w 1944 roku mieszkała w Małopolsce Wschodniej. To jest region, który przed II wojną światową należał do Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. I w 44 roku zostali ostrzeżeni, że Ukraińska Powstańcza Armia będzie mordowała Polaków mieszkających w wiosce, w której mieszkali, niedaleko Czortkowa. Mój dziadek i moja babcia uciekli przed mordercami z UPA. Niestety kilkudziesięciu mieszkańców tej niewielkiej wioski zostało zamordowanych. W mojej rodzinie pamięć o zbrodniarzach z UPA jest taką samą pamięcią jak pamięć o niemieckich nazistach.

I w dniu dzisiejszym, kiedy prezydent Zełenski zbrodniarzy z UPA honoruje jako bohaterów Ukrainy w nas Polakach budzi...

(Przewodniczący odebrał mówcy głos)
2-0406-0000.englishText:
Madam Deputy! In 1944 my family lived in Eastern Lesser Poland. This is a region that before the Second World War belonged to the Republic of Poland. And in '44 they were warned that the Ukrainian Insurgent Army would murder Poles living in the village where they lived, near Chortkiv. My grandfather and grandmother fled from the UPA murderers. Unfortunately, several dozen residents of this small village were murdered. In my family, the memory of the UPA perpetrators is the same memory as the memory of the German Nazis.

And today, when President Zelensky honors the UPA perpetrators as heroes of Ukraine, in us Poles it arouses...

(The President deprived the speaker of the floor)

2-0407-0000.sourceText:
n (Renew), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Sie sprechen von einer Zeit, dem Zweiten Weltkrieg, dem grausamsten nach dem Ersten Weltkrieg, dessen, was in Europa geschehen ist; darauf ist die Europäische Union aufgebaut worden. Das sind persönlich tragische Geschichten – ich will Ihnen das gar nicht absprechen; jeder hier hat tragische Geschichten in der Familie, bei Eltern und Großeltern erlebt. Und deswegen ist es unsere Aufgabe, hier in Frieden und für Freiheit zu kämpfen.

Und Ihre Aufgabe ist es, in Polen und der Ukraine einen Weg zu finden, denn Sie gefallen nur einem, und das ist Wladimir Putin. Der wartet nur darauf, dass Sie und die Ukraine sich gegenseitig an den Hals gehen, damit Russland Erfolg hat. Und deswegen: Wir sind hier in Europa, um genau das Gegenteil zu machen …

(Der Präsident entzieht der Rednerin das Wort.)
2-0407-0000.englishText:
n (Renew), answering a question under the "blue card" procedure. – You are speaking of a time, the Second World War, the most cruel after the First World War, of what happened in Europe; on that, the European Union was built. These are personally tragic stories – I do not wish to deny that to you at all; everyone here has experienced tragic stories in the family, with parents and grandparents. And that is why it is our task to fight here in peace and for freedom.

And your task is to find a way in Poland and Ukraine, because you are pleasing only one person, and that is Vladimir Putin. He is just waiting for you and Ukraine to go at each other's throats so that Russia succeeds. And therefore: We are here in Europe to do the exact opposite ...

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone.)

2-0408-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, colleagues, Ms Bryłka was standing here and saying Ukraine is not paying the cost. Ukraine is not paying the cost? Ukraine is doing an extraordinary thing – and this is what this report is about. Ukraine is mastering both: on the one hand...

(Addressing other Members) Can you please stop talking over there? What's going on there?

I would like to have new speaking time here. I'm sorry, but if I'm disrupted, I cannot speak.

2-0409-0000.sourceText:
Ms Demirel, please keep quiet in the room.

(Addressing Mr Lagodinsky) Continue.

2-0410-0000.sourceText:
So the extraordinary thing, as opposed to those people who are living here in peace, is that they are getting bombs on their heads while they are preparing for membership, while they are doing their homework, while they're doing reforms, while they're doing anti-corruption reforms.

Yes, not everything is perfect. But before you make accusations like those against those who are fighting against bombs, fighting for the lives of their children, you should make your homework and you should prepare the facts.

It's very clear that in extraordinary times and with extraordinary victims that we're seeing, we need to be extraordinary and out of the ordinary in our support for Ukraine. The best accession help is the defence help. This is what the NATO meeting is about.

Nothing will justify not helping Ukraine now. We're not talking about the victims from the past. We're talking about the victims from now that are killed by Russia and by the Kremlin. It's not just about the past; it's about protecting them in the present.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

2-0411-0000.sourceText:
Szanowny Panie Pośle! Zaskakuje mnie Pana postawa, bo przypominam sobie stanowisko Niemiec na początku, gdy wybuchła w 2022 roku wojna. I wtedy, pamiętam doskonale, bo byłem na spotkaniu z Olafem Scholzem w Berlinie, jak reagował i jak Niemcy były wtedy absolutnie bierne, jeżeli chodzi o pomoc dla Ukrainy. Dlatego jak słyszę dzisiaj Pana wypowiedź i pouczanie Polski w tym zakresie, to niestety przychodzą mi złe myśli.

Natomiast Pan nie rozumie jednej rzeczy. Prezydent Zełenski dokonał błędnej prowokacji, popełnił błąd, nazwał jednostkę wojskową imieniem UPA, czyli zbrodniarzy wojennych, którzy mordowali Polaków. Jak Pan się odniesie do tego? Dlaczego on to zrobił i czy Pan to potępi?
2-0411-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr Member! I am surprised by your attitude, because I remember Germany's position at the beginning, when the war broke out in 2022. And back then, I remember very well, because I was at a meeting with Olaf Scholz in Berlin, how he reacted and how Germany was absolutely passive at that time regarding aid to Ukraine. Therefore, when I hear your statement today and the lecturing of Poland in this regard, unfortunately, bad thoughts come to my mind.

On the other hand, you do not understand one thing. President Zelenskyy made a wrong provocation, he made a mistake, he named a military unit after the UPA, that is, war criminals who murdered Poles. How will you respond to this? Why did he do it and will you condemn it?

2-0412-0000.sourceText:
Colleague, I don't need lessons from you on how to support Ukraine. I and my party have been supporting Ukraine and Maidan since 2014 and since the occupation in Crimea. We were against Nord Stream 2 as one of the few parties. I was for arms sales long before anyone in Poland was talking about arms sales to Ukraine. So I don't need lessons on that.

What I do understand is the grievances of the Polish people. I do understand that, and I do agree that this is maybe not the most smart thing to do – what President Zelenskyy is doing – and if I were his advisor, I would advise him otherwise. But I am not his advisor.

We are not sitting in Kyiv. We are not getting bombed and we're not getting raped. And that's why I don't think we have a moral right to teach anyone in the middle of a war.

2-0413-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, tänään käsiteltävä kollega Gahlerin Ukraina-raportti lähettää selkeän viestin. Euroopan tuki Ukrainalle on horjumaton, ja sen on pysyttävä sellaisena. Tuki Ukrainan EU-jäsenyyspolulle, uudistusten tukemisen edistäminen sekä pitkäjänteinen taloudellinen, sotilaallinen ja poliittinen tuki sodan keskellä on kriittisen tärkeää.

Ukrainan puolustustaistelu ei koske vain sen omaa tulevaisuutta. Se on myös taistelua Euroopan turvallisuuden, demokratian ja kansainvälisen oikeuden puolesta. Siksi meidän on varmistettava, että Ukrainalla on edellytykset puolustaa itseään tänään ja rakentaa tulevaisuuttaan huomenna.

Samalla on tärkeää, että Ukrainan tie kohti Euroopan unionia perustuu oikeusvaltion vahvistamiseen, korruption torjuntaan ja tarvittavien uudistusten johdonmukaiseen toteuttamiseen. Laajentuminen on ansioihin perustuva prosessi, mutta minulle on selvää, että Ukrainan paikka on Euroopan perheessä. Yhtenäinen ja määrätietoinen Eurooppa on paras vastaus Venäjän hyökkäyssodalle. Slava Ukraini!
2-0413-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the report on Ukraine by our colleague Mr Gahler, which we are discussing today, sends a clear message. Europe's support for Ukraine is unwavering and must remain so. Support for Ukraine's EU accession path, the promotion of support for reforms, and long-term economic, military, and political support in the midst of the war are critically important.

Ukraine's defensive struggle is not only about its own future. It is also a fight for European security, democracy, and international law. Therefore, we must ensure that Ukraine has the prerequisites to defend itself today and to build its future tomorrow.

At the same time, it is important that Ukraine's path towards the European Union is based on the strengthening of the rule of law, the fight against corruption, and the consistent implementation of necessary reforms. Enlargement is a merit-based process, but it is clear to me that Ukraine's place is in the European family. A united and resolute Europe is the best response to Russia's war of aggression. Slava Ukraini!

2-0414-0000.sourceText:
�� Herr Präsident, meine Damen und Herren! Die Ukraine droht immer mehr zum Sargnagel der EU zu werden. Mit der Eröffnung von Beitrittsverhandlungen ist der Weg für weitere Milliarden an die korrupte Ukraine bereitet. EU-Studien zufolge soll ein EU-Beitritt Kyjiws 186 Mrd. EUR kosten. Wer soll das bitte bezahlen? Die Bevölkerung in Europa und insbesondere in Deutschland wird für diesen Wahnsinn zur Kasse gebeten. Während in Berlin Schulen und Straßen verfallen, vergolden sich die ukrainischen Oligarchen ihre Toiletten mit unserem Steuergeld.

Doch das ist nicht das einzige Problem. Die Beistandsklausel in den EU-Verträgen bedeutet, dass bei einem Beitritt der Ukraine die EU umgehend im Krieg mit Russland stände. Wer kann das wollen, außer denen, die sich an den Rüstungsaktien dumm und dämlich verdienen?

Die Menschen in Europa wollen Frieden, keinen Krieg mit Russland. Sie wollen, dass ihr Steuergeld für soziale Sicherheit, Bildung und Gesundheit ausgegeben und nicht dazu verwendet wird, dass sich die ukrainische Elite neue Villen an der Côte d’Azur kaufen kann.

(Die Rednerin lehnt eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ von Lukas Sieper ab.)
2-0414-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen! Ukraine is increasingly threatening to become the nail in the coffin of the EU. With the opening of accession negotiations, the path is paved for billions more to go to corrupt Ukraine. According to EU studies, EU accession for Kyiv is said to cost EUR 186 billion. Who is supposed to pay for this, please? The population in Europe, and in Germany in particular, is being made to foot the bill for this madness. While schools and roads are falling into disrepair in Berlin, Ukrainian oligarchs are gilding their toilets with our taxpayers' money.

Yet that is not the only problem. The mutual assistance clause in the EU treaties means that if Ukraine were to accede, the EU would immediately be at war with Russia. Who can possibly want that, apart from those who make a fortune off defence stocks?

The people in Europe want peace, not a war with Russia. They want their taxpayers' money to be spent on social security, education and health, and not used to enable the Ukrainian elite to buy new villas on the Côte d’Azur.

(The speaker refuses a blue-card question from Lukas Sieper.)
2-0414-0000.factCheck: The claim that the EU's mutual assistance clause would immediately put the EU at war with Russia upon Ukraine's accession is misleading; Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union does not automatically mandate direct military intervention, and Ukraine cannot finalize its EU accession while actively engaged in an ongoing armed conflict.

2-0415-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, a very good report, thanks to all the hard work, but I am very worried about the sharp clash between Ukraine and Poland due to their painful common history.

I will not attempt to assess which side – Ukrainians or Poles – is now contributing more to stoking the fire, but I have one request: to assess the context in which we all live and to take the side of a constructive path. The Polish-Lithuanian example shows that old enemies can sit down at the same table, not to force each other to adopt the other side's view, but to evaluate history honestly. This may be the only way forward in this conflict as well.

Armia Krajowa will never be heroes in the memory of Ukrainians. The UPA will never be heroes in the memory of poles. This must simply be understood and accepted. I think there is no other way than open recognition of history and agreement. However, the sharp war on history that has broken out today is very dangerous and beneficial only to one side: Putin's Russia.

2-0416-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, colleagues, I hope you listened well to the naysayers, the defeatists and the Putin powers, including those sitting in this Chamber. You remember what they said just a few weeks ago: they insisted that Ukraine stood no chance, that Kyiv had no cards, that Russia was unstoppable and Europe should appease the aggressor.

And yet, look at the situation today. Today, Russia's offensive has not just stalled, but there is smoke rising over Moscow. And even the most desperate Russians are no longer willing to sign away their lives for a war that they know has no purpose and no prospect of victory.

Colleagues, against all the odds, Ukrainians have created a new strategic reality on the ground. And why? Because Ukrainians never stop believing in their European future and the strength of this European project.

So let us finally do the same, and create the conditions of peace through strength, by locking in long‑term financial support, by delivering urgently needed air defence and, most importantly, by making Ukraine's path to European membership credible, irreversible and clear. Because only then will Putin understand that Ukraine will never again become a Russian colony, but that it was, is and will forever remain a free European nation.

2-0417-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Én Kárpátalján születtem, magyar családban. Jól ismerem az ott élő magyar közösséget. Tagjai lojális és törvénytisztelő állampolgárai Ukrajnának. Elítélik az orosz agressziót és a háború terheit is viselik. Magyar ajkú katonák szolgálnak a fronton, közülük pedig már több mint százan életüket adták Ukrajna védelméért. Mégis ez a közösség 2017 óta folyamatosan kisebbségi jogai korlátozását szenvedi el. Önök szinte egy évtizeden át tétlenül nézték, ahogy ezeket a jogokat fokozatosan leépítették, és figyelmeztetéseinket közönnyel fogadták. Ma pedig ebben a jelentésben üdvözlik a jogok helyreállításáról szóló megállapodást. De ne tegyenek úgy, mintha ez a kisebbségi jogokról szólna, sokkal inkább arról, hogy pusztán ígéretekért cserébe megnyílhatott az első csatlakozási klaszter Ukrajnával.

Ha valóban fontosak Önöknek a nemzeti kisebbségek, akkor azért dolgozzanak, hogy Ukrajna kisebbségi akcióterve egyértelmű, nyilvános és számonkérhető vállalásokat tartalmazzon a kisebbségi jogok teljes helyreállítására. Hiszen a jelenleg elérhető verzióban ez nincs így. A kisebbségek nem ígéreteket, garanciákat kérnek, valódi jogokat kérnek, amelyek a mindennapokban is érvényesülnek. Hogy senki se mondhassa meg nekik, hogy az anyanyelvüket még az iskolai szünetekben vagy a sporteseményeken sem használhatják. A jelentés kimondja, hogy a bővítésnek szigorúan érdemalapúnak kell lennie. Ezzel a ponttal egyetértek. A koppenhágai kritériumok nem ajánlások, hanem kötelező csatlakozási feltételek, és ezeknek Ukrajnának is maradéktalanul meg kell felelnie.
2-0417-0000.englishText:
Mr President! I was born in Transcarpathia, in a Hungarian family. I know the Hungarian community living there well. Its members are loyal and law-abiding citizens of Ukraine. They condemn Russian aggression and also bear the burdens of the war. Hungarian-speaking soldiers are serving at the front, and more than a hundred of them have already given their lives for the defense of Ukraine. Yet, since 2017, this community has continuously suffered the restriction of its minority rights. For almost a decade, you watched passively as these rights were gradually dismantled, and you met our warnings with indifference. And today, in this report, you welcome the agreement on the restoration of rights. But do not act as if this were about minority rights; it is much more about the fact that the first accession cluster with Ukraine could be opened simply in exchange for promises.
If national minorities are truly important to you, then work to ensure that Ukraine's minority action plan contains clear, public, and accountable commitments for the complete restoration of minority rights. Because in the currently available version, this is not the case. Minorities do not ask for promises, they ask for guarantees, real rights that prevail in everyday life as well. So that no one can tell them that they cannot even use their mother tongue during school breaks or sporting events. The report states that enlargement must be strictly merit-based. I agree with this point. The Copenhagen criteria are not recommendations, but binding accession conditions, and Ukraine must also fully comply with them.

2-0418-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, if we truly want to help Ukraine win the war, first we need to publicly say that more often. It's not only about helping Ukraine defend itself, but about winning the war that was started by Russia.

Second, in order to win the war against Russia, we must strengthen the economic and strategic pressure on Russia. And for that reason, the EU and Member States must work together to close the so-called northern corridor. Even today, four years after Russia attacked Ukraine, millions of tonnes of goods from China and Central Asia are coming to Europe through Russia, so they still make a lot of money because those goods are transiting the Russian territory.

Third, the Russian aggression extends far beyond the battlefield. The Kremlin uses the Moscow Patriarch and the Russian Orthodox Church as instruments of political influence and propaganda – both in Ukraine and abroad. I therefore welcome the Ukrainian legislation allowing Orthodox parishes to freely disaffiliate from the Moscow Patriarch.

I also call on the Ukrainian authorities to register, without delay, a religious association called the Romanian Orthodox Church in Ukraine, ensuring that the Romanian Orthodox communities in Ukraine can freely organise their religious life outside the jurisdiction of the Russian Orthodox Church.

2-0419-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, dimanche soir, une fois encore, une pluie de missiles russes s’est abattue sur Kiev, causant la mort d’au moins 14 civils. Ce n’est pas juste la guerre, ce sont des crimes de guerre. Une fois encore, les chancelleries européennes ont déploré, condamné, regretté, mais elles n’ont pas agi – pas même pour élargir les sanctions contre la Russie. Parce que, à peine Orban parti, le président bulgare devient le nouveau maillon faible européen.

Pourtant, ce qu’il faut faire, nous le savons: c’est protéger le ciel ukrainien des drones et des missiles russes, comme nous avons protégé le ciel des Émirats, du Qatar ou du Koweït des drones et des missiles iraniens. Ce n’est pas «escalatoire», car seuls des engins sans pilote survolent et frappent l’Ukraine. Augmenter les défenses antiaériennes de Kiev, participer à abattre missiles et drones avec nos propres forces ne feront pas de nous des cobelligérants. C’est notre inaction qui risque, à force, de faire de nous des complices.

N’imaginons pas que quiconque à Moscou salue aujourd’hui notre prudence bien mal placée. Le régime de Vladimir Poutine nous a rangés depuis longtemps au rang des adversaires et nous le prouve sans relâche. Si nous agissons enfin pour protéger le ciel ukrainien, la Russie saura qu’elle doit compter avec nous, l’Ukraine saura qu’elle peut compter sur nous, et le monde verra enfin ce que veut dire la puissance européenne.
2-0419-0000.englishText:
Mr President, on Sunday evening, once again, a rain of Russian missiles fell on Kyiv, causing the death of at least 14 civilians. This is not just war, these are war crimes. Once again, European capitals have deplored, condemned, regretted, but they have not acted — not even to broaden the sanctions against Russia. Because, no sooner had Orbán left, the Bulgarian President became the new European weak link.

Yet, what needs to be done, we know: it is to protect Ukrainian skies from Russian drones and missiles, just as we protected the skies of the Emirates, Qatar or Kuwait from Iranian drones and missiles. This is not "escalatory", because only unmanned devices fly over and strike Ukraine. Increasing Kyiv's anti-aircraft defenses, participating in shooting down missiles and drones with our own forces will not make us co-belligerents. It is our inaction that risks, eventually, making us accomplices.

Let us not imagine that anyone in Moscow today welcomes our poorly placed prudence. Vladimir Putin's regime has long ranked us among its adversaries and relentlessly proves it to us. If we finally act to protect Ukrainian skies, Russia will know that it must reckon with us, Ukraine will know that it can count on us, and the world will finally see what European power means.

2-0420-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Jag fick frågan av en journalist tidigare i dag, en polsk journalist. Han frågade om vi verkligen har ett problem med Putins inflytande här i Europaparlamentet och bland medlemsländerna. Efter att ha lyssnat till flera av er i dag är det enkelt att konstatera att vi har ett problem.

Jag kan också konstatera att det är en skam vad många av er ger uttryck för. Vi har Ukraina att tacka för att Ryssland inte har lyckats ta sig längre in i Europa. Ukraina hör hemma i EU. Vi måste fortsätta göra allt vi kan, allt i vår makt, använda hela verktygslådan för att se till att Ukraina blir en del av vår union så snart som möjligt. Slava Ukraini.
2-0420-0000.englishText:
Mr President! I was asked by a journalist earlier today, a Polish journalist. He asked if we really have a problem with Putin's influence here in the European Parliament and among the member states. After listening to several of you today, it is easy to conclude that we have a problem.

I can also state that it is a disgrace what many of you are expressing. We have Ukraine to thank for the fact that Russia has not managed to advance further into Europe. Ukraine belongs in the EU. We must continue to do everything we can, everything in our power, to use the entire toolbox to ensure that Ukraine becomes part of our union as soon as possible. Slava Ukraini.

2-0421-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, ditelo chiaramente: avete deciso di mandarci tutti in bancarotta e in guerra, perché state trasformando il processo di adesione dell'Ucraina in una cieca corsa verso l'armageddon bellico, per la necessità impellente di far entrare nell'Unione europea un paese il cui governo ha elevato a eroi nazionali i collaborazionisti dell'UPA, autori delle stragi in Volinia e Galizia.

In questa relazione emerge, di fatto, come l'Ucraina sia un paese quasi fallito, che ha grossi problemi di corruzione, una corruzione che divora i vertici di settori chiave come l'energia e l'industria militare.

Pensare in questo momento all'ingresso dell'Ucraina nell'Unione europea sarebbe una sciagura, soprattutto per il bilancio europeo: un impatto devastante sull'agricoltura e sui fondi in generale.

Volete i numeri? Vi do qualche numero: per le regioni del Sud Italia, ad esempio, secondo un recente studio, significherebbe dal 40 al 60 % di fondi in meno, insomma, una condanna a morte per i nostri territori.

Invece di spingere per allargamenti insostenibili e soffiare sul vento della guerra da utili idioti della NATO, iniziate a occuparvi dei milioni di famiglie e di lavoratori e lavoratrici europei vessati e umiliati dalle vostre fallimentari politiche neoliberiste.

(L'oratore accetta di rispondere a una domanda "cartellino blu")
2-0421-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, say it clearly: you have decided to drive us all into bankruptcy and war, because you are turning Ukraine's accession process into a blind race towards the armageddon of war, out of the pressing need to bring into the European Union a country whose government has elevated to national heroes the collaborators of the UPA, perpetrators of the massacres in Volhynia and Galicia.

This report actually shows that Ukraine is an almost failed country, which has major corruption problems, a corruption that devouring the top echelons of key sectors such as energy and the military industry.

Thinking at this moment about Ukraine's entry into the European Union would be a disaster, especially for the European budget: a devastating impact on agriculture and on funds in general.
*You want numbers? I'll give you some numbers: for the regions of Southern Italy, for example, according to a recent study, it would mean 40 to 60% less funds, in short, a death sentence for our territories.

Instead of pushing for unsustainable enlargements and fanning the winds of war as useful idiots of NATO, start taking care of the millions of European families and workers harassed and humiliated by your failing neoliberal policies.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

2-0422-0000.sourceText:
(Renew), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Herr Kollege, wissen Sie, wer sich jeden Tag für die einfachen Bürgerinnen und Bürger in Europa einsetzt? Ukrainische Soldaten an der Front.

Aber ich habe eine Frage; Sie haben ja gesagt, wir wollen ein Land aufnehmen, das die UPA da irgendwie verherrlicht. Haben Sie sich mit den Reaktionen der Europäischen Union und der Mitgliedstaaten der Europäischen Union auf diese Entscheidung der Selenskyj-Regierung wirklich auseinandergesetzt? Weil dann verstehe ich nicht, wie Sie zu diesem Punkt kommen. Und zweitens: Glauben Sie, dass die vielen, vielen Nachrichten über Korruptionsermittlungen nicht ein Erfolg der Antikorruptionsarbeit in der Ukraine sind statt ein Anzeichen von Misserfolgen?
2-0422-0000.englishText:
(Renew), Blue Card procedure. – Dear colleague, do you know who stands up for ordinary citizens in Europe every day? Ukrainian soldiers at the front.

But I have a question; you said that we want to admit a country that somehow glorifies the UPA there. Have you really looked into the reactions of the European Union and the member states of the European Union to this decision by the Zelenskyy government? Because then I do not understand how you arrive at this point. And secondly: Do you believe that the many, many reports about corruption investigations are not a success of anti-corruption work in Ukraine instead of a sign of failures?

2-0423-0000.sourceText:
Guardi, Le dico molto brevemente: il problema della corruzione in Ucraina c'è ed è evidente, e oggi, qui, alla fine si parla come se niente fosse di accogliere l'Ucraina.

C'è un problema anche sui fondi, c'è un problema sul bilancio europeo, che è importantissimo e, ripeto, impatta tantissimo sulle regioni, ad esempio, del Sud Italia.

Ma io dico una cosa: in quattro anni, finora, non siamo stati capaci di scegliere un inviato per la pace, ma si continua a soffiare sul fuoco della guerra, che, in realtà, non ha portato a nessun effetto.

A me sembra piuttosto che a qualcuno piace giocare con i soldatini chiuso nella cameretta, però il problema vero è che a morire sono i figli del popolo ucraino...

(Il Presidente toglie la parola all'oratore)
2-0423-0000.englishText:
Look, I am telling you very briefly: the problem of corruption in Ukraine exists and is evident, and today, here, in the end people talk as if nothing were the matter about welcoming Ukraine.

There is also a problem with funds, there is a problem with the European budget, which is extremely important and, I repeat, has a huge impact on the regions of Southern Italy, for example.

But I say one thing: in four years, so far, we have not been able to choose a peace envoy, but people continue to fan the flames of war, which, in reality, has not led to any effect.

It rather seems to me that someone likes playing with toy soldiers locked in their bedroom, but the real problem is that the children of the Ukrainian people are the ones dying...

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone)

2-0424-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, Ukrajina je danas naša glavna tema ovdje u Strasbourgu, kao što je i glavna tema u Ankari na samitu NATO-a i ako sam dobro razumio svog prethodnika, on je ponovno išao s tom argumentacijom lažnom da je logika proširenja EU-a, a i NATO-a, ta koja je izazvala sukob, odnosno rusku agresiju.

Nije. Bio sam čak i u Bukureštu na tom samitu NATO-a. Znam da ključni saveznici nisu htjeli tada primiti Ukrajinu, iako je Ukrajina to željela. Ne, pravi razlog agresije je jedan drugi. Bio je i ostao ruski imperijalizam i stoga, ako ne želimo pobjedu tog imperijalizma, ako ne želimo pobjedu ruskoga svijeta, a mi na jugoistoku Europe ne želimo niti njegove kopije u formi nekog srpskoga svijeta, ako ne želimo to, onda moramo podržati Ukrajinu i moramo Ukrajini omogućiti jednu europsku perspektivu.

Ona se neće odmah ostvariti, potrebne su reforme i u Ukrajini i u Europskoj uniji, ali je ključno da se Ukrajini više ne postavljaju blokade na njenom europskom putu.
2-0424-0000.englishText:
