Mr President, Ukraine is our main topic here in Strasbourg today, just as it is the main topic at the NATO summit in Ankara, and if I understood my predecessor correctly, he once again went with that false argument that the logic of EU and NATO enlargement is what caused the conflict, that is, Russian aggression.

It is not. I was even in Bucharest at that NATO summit. I know that key allies did not want to admit Ukraine at that time, even though Ukraine wanted it. No, the real reason for the aggression is something else. It was and remains Russian imperialism, and therefore, if we do not want the victory of that imperialism, if we do not want the victory of the Russian world, and we in Southeast Europe do not want its copies in the form of some Serbian world either, if we do not want that, then we must support Ukraine and we must provide Ukraine with a European perspective.

It will not be realized immediately, reforms are needed both in Ukraine and in the European Union, but it is crucial that blockades are no longer placed on Ukraine's European path.

2-0425-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, souvent l’Europe désespère tant elle est paralysée par des règles qui l’empêchent d’agir. Mais parfois elle prend des décisions à la hauteur de l’histoire: c’est ce qu’elle vient de faire en décidant d’ouvrir les négociations d’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’Union européenne.

Par cette décision nous répondons à l’appel européen de toute une nation et de ses martyrs, tout autant que nous envoyons un message clair à Poutine: sa guerre d’agression est vouée à l’échec. L’Ukraine a besoin de nous, mais l’Europe a aussi besoin de l’Ukraine: pour assurer la paix et la stabilité de notre continent, pour renforcer économiquement et militairement notre Union face aux nouvelles rivalités géopolitiques et pour poursuivre le projet européen, qui est avant tout un projet de reconstruction et de solidarité entre les peuples.

Malgré la guerre, l’Ukraine a fait preuve d’un engagement déterminé dans le processus vers l’adhésion. Bien sûr, nous devrons prendre très au sérieux les inquiétudes des Européens, et à cet égard le processus d’adhésion devra aussi prévoir toutes les protections et les transitions nécessaires. Mais de l’adhésion de l’Ukraine l’Europe n’a rien à craindre, elle a tout à espérer.
2-0425-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, Europe often despair so much because it is paralysed by rules that prevent it from acting. But sometimes it makes decisions worthy of history: that is what it has just done by deciding to open EU accession negotiations with Ukraine.

Through this decision, we are answering the European call of a whole nation and its martyrs, just as we are sending a clear message to Putin: his war of aggression is doomed to failure. Ukraine needs us, but Europe also needs Ukraine: to ensure the peace and stability of our continent, to strengthen our Union economically and militarily in the face of new geopolitical rivalries, and to pursue the European project, which is above all a project of reconstruction and solidarity between peoples.

Despite the war, Ukraine has shown a determined commitment to the accession process. Of course, we will have to take Europeans' concerns very seriously, and in this regard the accession process will also have to provide all the necessary protections and transitions. But Europe has nothing to fear from Ukraine's accession; it has everything to hope for.

2-0426-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Úgy kezdődnek meg a csatlakozási tárgyalások Ukrajnával, hogy az alapvető kérdéseket sem tisztáztuk, a választókat meg végképp nem kérdezte meg senki. Először is makacsul kerülik azt a kérdést, hogy vajon milyen biztonsági kockázatai vannak annak, hogy egy háborúban álló országról van szó. Azt már megszoktuk, hogy a kisebbségi jogok helyzete nem nagyon érdekel senkit itt. De úgy látszik, az sem zavar sokakat, hogy hét éve nem voltak választások, ami persze a háború következménye, de akkor is egy jogállamiságot érintő tény. Azzal, hogy az úgynevezett geopolitikai megközelítést alkalmazzák az érdem alapú megközelítés helyett, valójában azt is mondják, hogy ebben az esetben nem is számítanak azok a jogállamisági feltételek, amelyeket más esetekben számonkérnek. És ami a legfontosabb, nincs érdemi vita a költségvetési következményekről.

Mindezt úgy, hogy a költségvetési átalakítások, azok már elkezdődtek: csökkentik a kohéziós és az agrártámogatásokat, hogy helyet csináljanak az új alapoknak. És egyáltalán nincs vita arról, hogy ha a bővítés bekövetkezik, akkor melyek lesznek a nettó haszonélvező és a nettó befizető országok. Jó pár tagállam átléphet majd az utóbbi körbe. És ha ezek miatt megjelennek a kritikus hangok, akkor mi erre a válasz? Az, hogy megpróbálják ezeket kiiktatni. Például úgy, hogy szűkíteni akarják az egyhangúsággal hozott döntések körét. Azt értjük, hogy vaskos üzleti érdekek fűződnek ehhez a bővítéshez, de ez az eljárás minden, csak nem demokratikus. Arra kérem Önöket, hogy kérdezzék meg a választóikat is arról, hogy mit gondolnak erről az egészről. Mégiscsak ők állják majd a számlát. Meg merik tenni?

(A felszólaló hajlandó válaszolni egy kékkártyás kérdésre)
2-0426-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Accession negotiations with Ukraine are beginning without even clarifying fundamental questions, and voters have certainly not been asked by anyone. First of all, they stubbornly avoid the question of what security risks are posed by the fact that we are dealing with a country at war. We are already used to the fact that the situation of minority rights does not really interest anyone here. But it seems that many are not bothered either by the fact that there have been no elections for seven years, which is of course a consequence of the war, but it is still a fact affecting the rule of law. By applying the so-called geopolitical approach instead of the merit-based approach, they are actually also saying that in this case, the rule of law conditions that are held accountable in other cases do not even matter. And most importantly, there is no substantive debate on the budgetary consequences.

All this while budgetary transformations have already begun: cohesion and agricultural subsidies are being reduced to make room for new funds. And there is quite simply no debate about which countries will be net beneficiaries and net contributors if enlargement takes place. Quite a few member states could cross over into the latter group. And if critical voices appear because of this, what is our response to this? It is that they try to eliminate them. For example, by wanting to narrow the scope of decisions made by unanimity. We understand that heavy business interests are tied to this enlargement, but this procedure is anything but democratic. I ask you to also ask your voters what they think about this whole thing. After all, they are the ones who will foot the bill. Do you dare to do it?

(The speaker agrees to answer a blue-card question)
2-0426-0000.factCheck: The claim that EU cohesion and agricultural subsidies are already being reduced to fund Ukraine is false; no such cuts have been made under the current 2021–2027 budget, and proposed restructurings for the post-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework remain draft proposals subject to ongoing negotiations.

2-0427-0000.sourceText:
Very interesting views. I wonder what you mean by saying that there's no budgetary discussion about the cost of the war? Because Hungary has clearly stated that it wants to support Ukraine in any possible way.

We in Finland, in Denmark, in many other countries, have put several per cent of our GDP towards supporting Ukraine's existential fight for Europe's security. And you claim that that's a problem. The main payers are the Finnish, Dutch, German taxpayers – Hungary is not touched by it. So what's the big problem with the EU supporting Ukraine?

2-0428-0000.sourceText: Azt hiszem, hogy összekevert két különböző dolgot. Ön arról beszél, hogy eddig mennyi pénzt költöttek a háborús finanszírozásra. Ez az összeg egyébként az Európai Tanács honlapján ellenőrizhető, nyilvános. Amiről én beszéltem, az az, hogy a bővítés költségeiről nincsen érdemi és részletes vita. Tehát miközben egyfajta hitvallásként azt várják el a többségtől, hogy feltétel nélkül támogasson egy csatlakozási eljárást, egyáltalán nincsen szó ebben a vitában sem ennek a költségvetési vonatkozásairól: hogy mibe kerül a bővítés, és hogyan kell majd átalakítani az uniós programokat, a kohéziós forrásokat vagy éppen az agrártámogatásokat ahhoz, hogy a bővítést lehetővé tegyék. Erről nincs vita. Ma sem volt, és ez baj.
2-0428-0000.englishText: I think you have mixed up two different things. You are talking about how much money has been spent on war financing so far. That amount, by the way, can be checked on the website of the European Council and is public. What I was talking about is that there is no substantive and detailed debate on the costs of enlargement. So while, as a kind of creed, you expect the majority to unconditionally support an accession process, there is no mention at all in this debate of its budgetary implications: what enlargement will cost, and how EU programmes, cohesion funds, or agricultural subsidies will need to be restructured in order to make enlargement possible. There is no debate about this. There wasn't one today either, and that is a problem.

2-0429-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Sprawozdanie pana sprawozdawcy, niemieckiego posła Michaela Gahlera, słusznie i stanowczo potępia bestialski charakter agresji Rosji na Ukrainę. Odnotowuję także z satysfakcją, że niemiecki poseł podkreśla, że słuszne są roszczenia reparacyjne Ukrainy wobec Rosji. Ta informacja pada aż trzy razy w sprawozdaniu. To słuszne i sprawiedliwe, panie pośle.

Jednak sprawiedliwość historyczna nie może być selektywna. Jako autor raportu o polskich stratach wojennych, chcę podkreślić, że Polska 80 już lat czeka na reparacje wojenne od Niemiec, panie pośle, za skutki II wojny światowej. To nie kwestia pieniędzy, to kwestia elementarnej sprawiedliwości, uczciwości.

Dlatego dziwi mnie też optymizm pana posła co do postępów Ukrainy w drodze do Unii Europejskiej, skoro prezydent Zełenski uhonorował niedawno pamięć zbrodniczych jednostek UPA, które dokonywały czystek etnicznych w Małopolsce Wschodniej. To kuriozalne działanie, zwłaszcza że Putin wykorzystuje kult banderowców jako pretekst do agresji na Ukrainę. Chcę powiedzieć jasno: Polska nie wyrazi zgody na wejście Ukrainy do Unii Europejskiej z Banderą i z UPA na czele.
2-0429-0000.englishText:
Mr President! The report by the rapporteur, German MEP Michael Gahler, rightly and firmly condemns the bestial nature of Russia's aggression against Ukraine. I also note with satisfaction that the German MEP emphasizes that Ukraine's reparation claims against Russia are just. This information appears as many as three times in the report. This is right and fair, Mr MEP.

However, historical symmetry cannot be selective. As the author of the report on Polish war losses, I would like to emphasize that Poland has been waiting 80 years now for war reparations from Germany, Mr MEP, for the effects of World War II. This is not a matter of money, it is a matter of elementary justice and honesty.

Therefore, I am also surprised by the MEP's optimism regarding Ukraine's progress on its path to the European Union, given that President Zelenskyy recently honored the memory of the criminal UPA units that carried out ethnic cleansing in Eastern Lesser Poland. This is a bizarre action, especially since Putin uses the cult of the Banderites as a pretext for aggression against Ukraine. I want to make it clear: Poland will not consent to Ukraine's accession to the European Union with Bandera and the UPA at the forefront.

2-0430-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Alldeles nyss, medan den här debatten började, kom ett besked: Ryssland släpps in i den olympiska värmen. IOK ger Putin den propagandaseger han drömt om. Det här är ett hån, inte bara mot Ukraina, det är ett hån mot hela Europa, mot vår demokrati. Låt oss tillsammans fördöma detta felaktiga, fruktansvärda besked.

Nu ska jag prata om något helt annat. Lyssna noga. EU hjälper Ukraina att försvara sig, och det är väldigt bra. Men på samma gång försvårar vi just nu för landet att självt finansiera sitt försvar. Ja, ni hörde rätt. Därför måste vi öppna upp för en fri handel igen. Sedan en tid tillbaka har det blåst alldeles för mycket protektionistiska vindar mot Ukraina.

Gör om, gör rätt. Låt handeln med Ukraina vara fri.
2-0430-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Just now, as this debate was beginning, news came: Russia is being let back into the Olympic fold. The IOC is giving Putin the propaganda victory he dreamed of. This is a mockery, not just of Ukraine, it is a mockery of the whole of Europe, of our democracy. Let us together condemn this wrong, terrible message.

Now I will talk about something completely different. Listen carefully. The EU is helping Ukraine to defend itself, and that is very good. But at the same time, we are currently making it harder for the country to finance its own defence. Yes, you heard that right. Therefore, we must open up for free trade again. For some time now, far too many protectionist winds have been blowing against Ukraine.

Do it over, do it right. Let trade with Ukraine be free.

2-0431-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, we often talk about how impressive it is that Ukraine defends itself against Russian aggression, and rightly so. But what is also impressive is Anastasiia. She's a Ukrainian woman who built a life for herself in the EU; she's a real powerhouse. She even started a foundation that connects Ukrainian women from all over Europe – from Bulgaria to the Netherlands.

They exchange on how it is to build a life in the EU and how to contribute to society. And they don't passively sit around: they have jobs, they learn languages, they pay taxes. They have seen their children grow up in the EU, and they made sure that they can proudly call these new places their homes.

But they face one big issue: uncertainty. Next March, the temporary protection status of these people will end, and it is unclear what's going to happen next. They deserve certainty. Granting them a form of long-term residence will give them that certainty. So I ask you: let's do everything we can for victory in Ukraine, but let's also look after the Ukrainians living in the EU, because all of them hopefully will soon be part of our EU family.

2-0432-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Polska uznała niepodległość Ukrainy jako pierwsze państwo na świecie 2 grudnia 1991 roku. Zrobiliśmy to, bo wiedzieliśmy, że nie ma bezpiecznej Polski i Europy bez wolnej Ukrainy.

Ale nie ma też wolnej Ukrainy bez wsparcia Polski i całej Unii. Dlatego mówimy jasno: „tak” dla członkostwa Ukrainy w Unii Europejskiej. Jednak ten proces musi opierać się na wzajemnym szacunku, demokratycznych zasadach i prawdzie historycznej. Podkreślam: prawdzie historycznej. Bez prawdy nie będzie pojednania. Bez pojednania nie będzie trwałej współpracy.

Drodzy Ukraińcy, do Unii Europejskiej nie ma drogi na skróty. Przechodziliśmy tę drogę wcześniej i mówimy Wam to z całą odpowiedzialnością, jaką rolę powinni odgrywać odpowiedzialni politycy. A ci, którzy próbują nam wmówić, że bezpieczeństwo Ukrainy jest sprzeczne z bezpieczeństwem Polski, powielają narrację rodem z Kremla. Ten, kto tego nie rozumie, jest ignorantem albo głupcem. Jedno i drugie pcha nas wprost w ogień Putina.
2-0432-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Commissioner! Poland was the first country in the world to recognize Ukraine's independence on 2 December 1991. We did it because we knew that there is no secure Poland and Europe without a free Ukraine.

But there is also no free Ukraine without the support of Poland and the entire Union. That is why we say clearly: "yes" to Ukraine's membership in the European Union. However, this process must be based on mutual respect, democratic principles, and historical truth. I emphasize: historical truth. Without truth, there will be no reconciliation. Without reconciliation, there will be no lasting cooperation.

Dear Ukrainians, there are no shortcuts to the European Union. We went down this path before, and we tell you this with the full responsibility that responsible politicians should play. And those who try to make us believe that Ukraine's security is contrary to Poland's security are repeating a narrative straight from the Kremlin. Anyone who does not understand this is either ignorant or a fool. Both push us straight into Putin's fire.

2-0433-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, estive há poucos dias em Kiev. Vi um país em guerra que não para: o Parlamento reúne, as instituições reformam-se, a sociedade civil fiscaliza. Mas trago um alerta: cuidado com a gestão de expetativas.

Prometer datas que não cumprimos mina a confiança e é essa confiança que precisamos de reforçar: a dos ucranianos em nós e a dos cidadãos europeus neste processo.

Ora, esta confiança constrói-se com equilíbrio - exigência nas reformas do Estado de direito, combate à corrupção, independência judicial e apoio inequívoco, sem hesitações, sem meias-palavras. Exigir sem apoiar é abandono, apoiar sem exigir é ilusão. A credibilidade da União está neste equilíbrio.

A Ucrânia resiste e, com ela, temos de transformar palavras em ações, ações em reformas, reformas em adesão.
2-0433-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I was in Kyiv a few days ago. I saw a country at war that does not stop: Parliament meets, institutions are reforming, civil society is monitoring. But I bring a warning: beware of managing expectations.

Promising dates that we do not meet undermines trust, and it is this trust that we need to strengthen: that of Ukrainians in us and that of European citizens in this process.

Now, this trust is built with balance - demand in rule of law reforms, the fight against corruption, judicial independence and unequivocal support, without hesitation, without mince words. Demanding without supporting is abandonment, supporting without demanding is an illusion. The Union's credibility lies in this balance.

Ukraine is resisting and, with it, we must turn words into actions, actions into reforms, reforms into accession.

2-0434-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! W czasie II wojny światowej na Wołyniu i w Małopolsce Wschodniej bandy UPA dokonały jednego z najbardziej okrutnych ludobójstw w historii Europy. Niewinni Polacy, cywile, w tym starcy, kobiety i dzieci, byli mordowani w sposób przekraczający ludzką wyobraźnię. Palono ich żywcem w zamkniętych stodołach i kościołach, przecinano ich żywcem piłami, ciężarnym matkom rozcinano brzuchy, wyrywając dzieci, a w ich miejsce zaszywano koty, aby kobiety konały w niewyobrażalnym cierpieniu. Małe dzieci przybijano nożami, gwoździami do drzwi domów, ofiarom wyłupywano oczy, skalpowano głowy i rozrywano ciała siekierami oraz widłami.

Całe polskie wsie, rodziny były mordowane przez ukraińskich sąsiadów. Rabowane i palone były ich domostwa. To była bestialska czystka etniczna. Ze zwierzęcą brutalnością Ukraińcy, którzy w tamtym czasie byli sojusznikami Hitlera, wymordowali ponad 100 tysięcy Polaków. Do dziś państwo ukraińskie nie pozwala ich pochować.

A dzisiaj prezydent Zełenski honoruje oddziały armii ukraińskiej, nadając im imię bohaterów UPA. A przecież to zwykli barbarzyńcy. Ta skandaliczna prowokacja nie może przejść bez potępiającego głosu płynącego z Parlamentu Europejskiego. Precz z kultem morderców, z Banderą, Szuchewyczem i UPA. Z kultem ludobójstwa i czystek etnicznych Ukraina nigdy nie będzie częścią...

(Przewodnicząca odebrała mówcy głos)
2-0434-0000.englishText:
Mr President! During World War II in Volhynia and Eastern Lesser Poland, UPA gangs committed one of the most cruel genocides in European history. Innocent Poles, civilians, including the elderly, women and children, were murdered in a manner exceeding human imagination. They were burned alive in locked barns and churches, sawed in half alive while pregnant mothers' bellies were cut open, tearing out children and sewing cats in their place so that the women would die in unimaginable suffering. Small children were nailed with knives and nails to the doors of houses, victims had their eyes gouged out, heads scalped and bodies torn apart with axes and pitchforks.

Entire Polish villages and families were murdered by Ukrainian neighbours. Their homes were looted and burned. This was a bestial ethnic cleansing. With animal brutality, Ukrainians, who at that time were Hitler's allies, murdered over 100,000 Poles. To this day, the Ukrainian state does not allow them to be buried.

And today, President Zelensky honours units of the Ukrainian army by naming them after UPA heroes. And yet these are ordinary barbarians. This scandalous provocation cannot pass without a condemning voice flowing from the European Parliament. Down with the cult of murderers, with Bandera, Shukhevych and the UPA. With the cult of genocide and ethnic cleansing, Ukraine will never be part of...

(The President withdrew the speaker's right to speak)
2-0434-0000.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine does not allow the Polish victims of the Volhynia massacre to be buried is misleading; although a moratorium on searches was in place from 2017, Ukraine lifted this ban in late 2024, and joint teams have since successfully conducted exhumations and reburials of victims in several locations.

2-0436-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, gerbiami kolegos. Šiandien Europos Sąjungos plėtra nėra tik bendros ekonominės ir politinės erdvės plėtra. Tai taip pat ir kova dėl to, į kieno įtakos sferą pasibaigus narystės procesui pateks ar nepateks kandidatės šalys. Kariaujanti Ukraina vykdo reformas, kurias kitos kandidatės turėjo prabangą vykdyti taikos sąlygomis. Skaitant ataskaitą kartais susidaro įspūdis, kad Ukraina yra stumiama siekti tikslų, dėl kurių pradeda abejoti pati Europos Sąjunga. Sutikite, kad kariaujančioje valstybėje, kurioje agresorius kasdien bombarduoja strateginius objektus ir žudo civilius, labai sunku kalbėti apie žaliąją darbotvarkę ir klimato kaitos mažinimą. Todėl reikia blaivaus situacijos vertinimo. Valstybė, kuri priešinasi agresorei Rusijai ir sugeba priversti jos piliečius pajausti jų pačių šalies sukelto karo kainą, kartu daro ir didžiulį progresą siekdama narystės Europos Sąjungoje. Stebint pastarųjų savaičių ar mėnesių politinius procesus, norisi palinkėti mums visiems šalto proto ir politinio įžvalgumo, kad principingumas netaptų dovana Europos priešams.
2-0436-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear colleagues. Today, European Union enlargement is not just the expansion of a common economic and political space. It is also a struggle over whose sphere of influence candidate countries will or will not fall into after the membership process is completed. War-torn Ukraine is implementing reforms that other candidates had the luxury of carrying out in peacetime. When reading the report, one sometimes gets the impression that Ukraine is being pushed to pursue goals that the European Union itself is beginning to doubt. You will agree that in a country at war, where the aggressor bombs strategic objects and kills civilians every day, it is very difficult to talk about the green agenda and climate change mitigation. Therefore, a sober assessment of the situation is needed. A state that resists the aggressor Russia and manages to make its citizens feel the price of the war caused by their own country is at the same time making huge progress towards European Union membership. Observing the political processes of recent weeks or months, one wishes for all of us to have a cold mind and political insight, so that principledness does not become a gift to Europe's enemies.

2-0437-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Trudne, najboleśniejsze kwestie historyczne, takie jak zbrodnia UPA dokonana na polskich cywilach, istnieją i nie wolno ich ignorować. Bez ich przepracowania nie pójdziemy nigdzie dalej. Odpowiedzialność za wzrost napięcia leży po obu stronach. Zarówno w działaniach prezydenta Zełenskiego, który podsycił narrację nacjonalistyczną, jak i w działaniach prezydenta Nawrockiego.

Położono na szali wielki dorobek zaufania zbudowanego między naszymi narodami, w tym ogromny polski wkład w pomoc Ukrainie. Z ubolewaniem obserwuję, że w chwili historycznej szansy, jaką jest przyszła akcesja Ukrainy do Unii Europejskiej, coraz więcej uwagi poświęcamy podziałom. Przez to nie skupiamy się na największym zagrożeniu, jakim jest Rosja, oraz na pozytywach, jakie może przynieść rozszerzenie Wspólnoty. Wraz z kolegami od dwóch miesięcy pracowaliśmy nad poprawkami do tego sprawozdania, które dotyczyły rozwoju inwestycji w drogi, koleje, energetykę, także w państwach granicznych, takich jak Polska.

Potrzebujemy dziś przede wszystkim odpowiedzialności i wyciszenia emocji. Polska i Ukraina mają wspólny interes: bezpieczeństwo, stabilność i rozwój Europy Środkowo-Wschodniej. To jest realna europejska perspektywa. Razem wygramy albo razem przegramy wszystko.
2-0437-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Difficult, most painful historical issues, such as the crimes committed by the UPA against Polish civilians, exist and must not be ignored. Without working through them, we will not go any further. Responsibility for the rise in tension lies on both sides. Both in the actions of President Zelenskyy, who fueled nationalist rhetoric, and in the actions of President Nawrocki.

A great achievement of trust built between our nations has been put at stake, including Poland's huge contribution to helping Ukraine. I observe with regret that at a moment of historical opportunity, which is Ukraine's future accession to the European Union, we are paying more and more attention to divisions. Because of this, we are not focusing on the greatest threat, which is Russia, and on the positives that the enlargement of the Community can bring. Along with my colleagues, for two months we have been working on amendments to this report, which concerned the development of investments in roads, railways, and energy, including in border states such as Poland.

Today, above all, we need responsibility and the calming of emotions. Poland and Ukraine share a common interest: the security, stability, and development of Central and Eastern Europe. This is a real European perspective. Together we will win, or together we will lose everything.

2-0438-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, arvoisa komission jäsen, kello käy. Venäjä ei siirrä yhtä nappulaa kerralla. Se katsoo koko lautaa, ja juuri nyt se näkee aukon. Amerikan tuki heikkenee. Oma yhteinen puolustuksemme on vasta raakile. Siihen rakoon Venäjä työntää parhaillaan kätensä ja testaa valmiuttamme.

Meillä on yksi liittolainen, joka voi ratkaista pelin: Ukraina. Se ei pyydä turvaa, se antaa sitä. Ukraina osaa jo sen, mitä me vasta tavaamme, ja se on maksanut oppinsa verellä. Sillä on tietoa, taitoa ja rohkeutta, joita ei saa jättää hyödyntämättä.

Siksi Saksan liittokanslerin esitys liitännäisjäsenyydestä on oikea siirto oikealla hetkellä. Se ei ole kevennetty jäsenyys, vaan välivaihe. Se sitoo Ukrainan tiiviimmin osaksi puolustustamme juuri silloin, kun me tarvitsemme sitä eniten. Passiivisuus on siirto, jonka annamme vastustajalle, ja Venäjä lukee jokaisen empimisen heikkoutena.
2-0438-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, time is running out. Russia does not move a single piece at a time. It looks at the entire board, and right now it sees an opening. American support is weakening. Our own joint defence is still in its infancy. Into that gap Russia is currently thrusting its hand and testing our readiness.

We have one ally that can decide the game: Ukraine. It is not asking for security, it is providing it. Ukraine already knows what we are still spelling out, and it has paid for its lesson in blood. It has knowledge, skill and courage that must not be left unutilised.

That is why the German Chancellor's proposal for associated membership is the right move at the right time. It is not watered-down membership, but an intermediate stage. It ties Ukraine more closely into our defence precisely when we need it most. Passivity is a move we hand to the opponent, and Russia reads every hesitation as weakness.

2-0439-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Russia non sta vincendo la guerra in Ucraina, anzi, forte della sua resilienza morale, Kiev ha saputo trasformare la sua inferiorità in strutturale capacità di innovazione.

Per la Russia doveva essere una dimostrazione di potenza. È invece una carneficina da cui deriva l'erosione del prestigio su cui poggia il potere di Putin. È anche il fallimento di chi ha continuato a dare l'Ucraina per spacciata, ha contrastato l'invio di aiuti militari e propugnato una pseudo-pace equivalente a una sottomissione.

La Russia non sta vincendo, ma questa non è una ragione per allentare il sostegno europeo. L'incapacità di ottenere una vittoria sul campo porta Mosca a intensificare i bombardamenti sulle città ucraine e le azioni ibride contro i paesi dell'Unione e della NATO.

La vera posta in palio del vertice di Ankara è dunque la tenuta dell'alleanza e della sua capacità di deterrenza. Il sostegno strutturale all'Ucraina e il consolidamento di un pilastro europeo della difesa sono obiettivi anche nostri, che dobbiamo sostenere con grande determinazione.
2-0439-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, Russia is not winning the war in Ukraine; on the contrary, building on its moral resilience, Kyiv has been able to turn its inferiority into a structural capacity for innovation.

For Russia, it was supposed to be a demonstration of power. Instead, it is a carnage resulting in the erosion of the prestige upon which Putin's power rests. It is also the failure of those who continued to write off Ukraine, opposed the sending of military aid, and advocated a pseudo-peace equivalent to subjugation.

Russia is not winning, but this is no reason to ease European support. The inability to achieve victory on the ground leads Moscow to step up its bombardments of Ukrainian cities and hybrid actions against EU and NATO countries.

What is truly at stake at the Ankara summit is therefore the holding together of the alliance and its deterrence capability. Structural support for Ukraine and the consolidation of a European pillar of defence are also our objectives, which we must support with great determination.

2-0440-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Ponad 360 sposobów mordowania ludności cywilnej. Piłowanie ludzi żywcem, rozpruwanie brzuchów ciężarnych kobiet, nadziewanie dzieci na widły – tak UPA mordowała Polaków, Żydów, Czechów, Ormian i samych Ukraińców. A dziś Zełenski nadaje jednostce wojskowej imię bohaterów UPA, buduje państwowy panteon i ogłasza, że Ukraina sama będzie sobie wybierać bohaterów. Szkoda, że wybiera ich spośród nazistów.

Gdyby Niemcy nazwali jednostkę bohaterami SS i stawiali pomniki Hitlerowi, Himmlerowi, Goebbelsowi czy Eichmannowi, czy zaprosilibyście ich do Unii? Nie! Nazwalibyście ich neonazistami. I słusznie. Nie ma moralnej różnicy między czczeniem SS a czczeniem UPA. Ten sam kult siły, ta sama nienawiść etniczna.

Sprawozdanie o Ukrainie milczy na ten temat. To cisza, która morduje pamięć ofiar ludobójstwa na Wołyniu i Kresach Wschodnich po raz drugi. Marsz Ukrainy do Europy z ludobójcami na sztandarach to hańba. Jako Polacy nigdy nie powinniśmy zgodzić się na wejście Ukrainy do Europy. Precz z banderowskim nazizmem!
2-0440-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Over 360 ways of murdering civilians. Sawing people alive, ripping open the bellies of pregnant women, impaling children on pitchforks – this is how the UPA murdered Poles, Jews, Czechs, Armenians, and Ukrainians themselves. And today, Zelenskyy names a military unit after UPA heroes, builds a state pantheon, and announces that Ukraine will choose its own heroes. It is a pity that it chooses them from among Nazis.

If Germany named a unit after SS heroes and erected monuments to Hitler, Himmler, Goebbels, or Eichmann, would you invite them into the Union? No! You would call them neo-Nazis. And rightly so. There is no moral difference between worshipping the SS and worshipping the UPA. The same cult of force, the same ethnic hatred.

The report on Ukraine is silent on this matter. It is a silence that murders the memory of the victims of the genocide in Volhynia and the Eastern Borderlands for the second time. Ukraine's march to Europe with genocidal killers on its banners is a disgrace. As Poles, we should never agree to Ukraine's entry into Europe. Down with Banderite Nazism!
2-0440-0000.factCheck: The claim that the European Parliament's report on Ukraine is silent on the naming of a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) is false; the resolution adopted on July 8, 2026, explicitly includes a provision criticizing President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's decision as an 'unnecessary and unprovoked escalation' that disregards Polish sensitivities.

2-0441-0000.sourceText:
(początek wystąpienia poza mikrofonem) rosyjskich zbrodni wojennych na Ukrainie. Pytam jednak, co ze zbrodniami ukraińskich nacjonalistów z okresu II wojny światowej? Co z dziećmi, kobietami, starcami wymordowanymi tylko dlatego, że byli Polakami? Wrzuconymi do bezimiennych dołów bez krzyża, nazwiska, szacunku. Ludobójstwo dokonane przez OUN i UPA w imię nacjonalistycznej ideologii wzorowanej na niemieckim nazizmie.

Ponad 100 tysięcy Polaków, ale także Żydów, Czechów, Białorusinów i Ukraińców ratujących swoich sąsiadów. Byli tacy. Symbolami tych zbrodni są Bandera i Szuchewycz, bohaterowie Zełenskiego, a faktycznie bestie odpowiedzialne za te zbrodnie.

Dziś Ukraina głosi, że to formacje walczące z Sowietami. Fakty są jednak bardziej złożone. W latach 1944–53 z rąk ukraińskiego podziemia życie straciło ok. 3000 żołnierzy i funkcjonariuszy sowieckich. 8000 Sowietów, a z drugiej strony ponad 100 000 Polaków. Tak więc tak – dla pomocy Ukrainie, ale zdecydowanie nie – dla członkostwa Ukrainy w Unii Europejskiej bez uznania prawdy historycznej i z Banderą na sztandarach.
2-0441-0000.englishText:
(start of speech off microphone) of Russian war crimes in Ukraine. I ask, however, what about the crimes of Ukrainian nationalists from the period of World War II? What about the children, women, and elderly slaughtered just because they were Poles? Thrown into nameless pits without a cross, a name, respect. Genocide committed by the OUN and UPA in the name of a nationalist ideology modeled on German Nazism.

Over 100,000 Poles, but also Jews, Czechs, Belarusians, and Ukrainians saving their neighbors. There were such people. The symbols of these crimes are Bandera and Shukhevych, Zelenskyy's heroes, and in fact beasts responsible for these crimes.

Today, Ukraine proclaims that these were formations fighting the Soviets. The facts, however, are more complex. In the years 1944–53, about 3,000 Soviet soldiers and officers lost their lives at the hands of the Ukrainian underground. 8,000 Soviets, and on the other hand over 100,000 Poles. So yes – to help Ukraine, but definitely no – to Ukraine's membership in the European Union without recognizing historical truth and with Bandera on the banners.
2-0441-0000.factCheck: Although the speaker claims that the Ukrainian underground killed only 8,000 Soviets between 1944 and 1953, historical records show that the total number of Soviet victims was over 30,000; the figure of approximately 8,300 refers only to military and security forces, while the remaining victims were civilians, mostly Ukrainian peasants.

2-0442-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Menschen Europas! Ich war letzte Woche in einem ausgebombten Haus in Kyjiw. Da musste ich an einen Song denken, und der geht so:

Meine Freunde sind Iraner.

Meine Freunde sind aus Gaza.

Meine Freunde sind Ukrainer, Russen.

Und Amerikaner.

Meine Freunde sagen Politik macht diese Welt kaputt.

Meine Freunde empfinden die Gier nach Macht nur als Schmutz.

Ihre Feinde sind die Trumps, Netanjahus und Khameneis.

Ihre Feinde sind die Hamas, Putins.

Alle mit Raketen.

Ihre Feinde haben mit normalen Menschen Nichts zu tun.

Säen auf die Erde Hass und vergießen darauf Blut.

Meine Freunde schreien.

Free Palestine.

Free Iran.

Meine Freunde hassen Krieg.

Doch sie sind nicht radikal.

Ihre Feinde sind nicht Juden und Muslime oder Christen.

Ihre Feinde sind Diktatoren und Faschisten.

Die uns aufeinander hetzen, guck wir drehen uns im Kreis.

Wie oft in der Geschichte zahlten wir denselben Preis.

Ich hab′ es Leid!

Denn ein Mensch hat Emotionen.

Doch wozu sie fähig sind.

Macht sie eher zu Dämonen!

Slawa Ukrajini!
2-0442-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear people of Europe! Last week I was in a bombed-out house in Kyiv. That made me think of a song, and it goes like this:

My friends are Iranians.

My friends are from Gaza.

My friends are Ukrainians, Russians.

And Americans.

My friends say politics is breaking this world.

My friends perceive the lust for power as nothing but filth.

Their enemies are the Trumps, Netanyahus and Khameneis.

Their enemies are Hamas, Putins.

All with missiles.

Their enemies have nothing to do with normal people.

Sowing hatred upon the earth and shedding blood upon it.

My friends are screaming.

Free Palestine.

Free Iran.

My friends hate war.

Yet they are not radical.

Their enemies are not Jews and Muslims or Christians.

Their enemies are dictators and fascists.

Who set us against each other, look, we are going round in circles.

How often in history have we paid the same price.

I am sick of it!

Because a human being has emotions.

Yet what they are capable of.

Makes them more like demons!

Slava Ukraini!

2-0443-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Ukraine is not only writing its history today, it's writing our shared European future. Ukraine has already reached 84 % implementation of the Association Agreement. Yet some still play games with vetoes instead of building a common Europe.

EU enlargement is not a charity. It is a strategic necessity. A bigger Europe is a stronger Europe. But the process is not just one way. We, the existing Member States, must also keep our word. We cannot demand everything from Ukraine while hiding behind vetoes and excuses ourselves.

Promises we do not keep destroy our credibility. The time has come for courage. The time has come for determination. The time has come to say it clearly: Ukraine belongs to the EU.

2-0444-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Rysslands brutala krig mot Ukraina kräver vårt fortsatta och solidariska stöd. Samtidigt måste vi göra mer för att försvaga Putins krigsmaskin. EU:s länder måste sluta köpa den ryska gasen.

EU måste också sätta stopp för den ryska skuggflottan som kringgår sanktionerna. Den är ett hot både mot säkerheten och miljön i våra hav.

Vi får aldrig, aldrig glömma krigets mest oskyldiga offer: barnen. Tiotusentals ukrainska barn har tvångsdeporterats från sina hem, och vi kräver att Ryssland omedelbart och säkert återför alla kidnappade barn till sina hem.

Slutligen: Ukraina visar en imponerande framtidstro. Trots kriget pågår ett målmedvetet arbete för en grön återuppbyggnad och en uppbyggnad av förnybar energi. Där ska EU vara. Där ska vi stödja dem och välkomna dem i den europeiska gemenskapen. Slava Ukraini.
2-0444-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Russia's brutal war against Ukraine demands our continued and solidary support. At the same time, we must do more to weaken Putin's war machine. EU countries must stop buying Russian gas.

The EU must also put a stop to the Russian shadow fleet that bypasses the sanctions. It is a threat to both safety and the environment in our seas.

We must never, ever forget the war's most innocent victims: the children. Tens of thousands of Ukrainian children have been forcibly deported from their homes, and we demand that Russia immediately and safely return all kidnapped children to their homes.

Finally: Ukraine is showing an impressive belief in the future. Despite the war, purposeful work is underway for a green reconstruction and a build-up of renewable energy. The EU must be there. There we must support them and welcome them into the European community. Slava Ukraini.

2-0445-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! 100 tysięcy pomordowanych Polek i Polaków to nie jest kwestia polsko-ukraińska, w dodatku „historyczna″. Uhonorowanie morderców Polaków nie jest konfliktem polsko-ukraińskim. To prowokacja.

Prowokacja nie tylko wycelowana w Polskę, która przecież zawsze była orędownikiem i wsparciem dla Ukrainy. Ale prowokacja wobec wartości europejskiej, bo to wartości europejskie zapisane w traktatach. Nikt na takich wartościach nie może budować relacji z Unią Europejską. To tak jakbyśmy Niemcom pozwolili na to, by gloryfikowali z powrotem Hitlera i jego zbrodniarzy.

Chcemy zakończenia wojny, bo przecież to warunek podstawowy, żeby wejść do Unii Europejskiej. Chcemy uregulowania granic, bo to kolejny warunek, żeby przystąpić do Unii Europejskiej. Wreszcie chcemy realnych negocjacji. A co proponujemy? Powiedzcie to Europie: punkt 102 – otwarcie granic i wolny handel. Mówicie o tym, że CBAM, czyli podatek graniczny, przestał być ważny. Wyrzućcie go do kosza, bo produkty z całego świata przez Ukrainę dotrą do Europy bez żadnych obostrzeń...

(Przewodnicząca odebrała mówczyni głos)
2-0445-0000.englishText:
Madam President! 100,000 murdered Polish women and men is not a Polish-Ukrainian issue, especially a "historical" one. Honoring the murderers of Poles is not a Polish-Ukrainian conflict. It is a provocation.

A provocation not only aimed at Poland, which after all has always been an advocate and support for Ukraine. But a provocation against European values, because these are European values enshrined in the treaties. No one can build relations with the European Union on such values. It is as if we allowed Germany to glorify Hitler and his criminals back again.

We want the war to end, because after all that is a basic condition to enter the European Union. We want borders to be regulated, because that is another condition to join the European Union. Finally, we want real negotiations. And what are we proposing? Tell Europe this: point 102 – opening borders and free trade. You talk about the fact that CBAM, i.e. the border tax, is no longer important. Throw it in the trash, because products from all over the world will reach Europe through Ukraine without any restrictions...

(The President cut off the speaker's microphone)
2-0445-0000.factCheck: The claim that products from all over the world will reach Europe through Ukraine without restrictions is false; the EU-Ukraine Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA) and temporary trade liberalization measures apply strictly to goods of Ukrainian origin, meaning third-country products transiting through Ukraine remain subject to standard EU customs duties, rules of origin, and regulatory requirements like the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).

2-0446-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, het is gemakkelijk om Oekraïne een toekomst in Europa te beloven. De vraag is: hoe gaan we samen met Oekraïne die belofte ook waarmaken?

Oekraïne is een land in oorlog. Juist daarom vraagt het toetredingsproces om urgentie. Wij hebben Oekraïne nodig voor onze veiligheid. Tegelijkertijd moet het toetredingsproces zorgvuldig verlopen om de stabiliteit van Europa te waarborgen.

Oekraïne is geen doorsnee kandidaat-lidstaat. Het land beschikt over een landbouwgebied dat groter is dan dat van Frankrijk. Dit biedt veel kansen voor de toekomstige bio-economie van Europa. Tegelijkertijd ligt het bruto binnenlands product per inwoner ver onder het Europees gemiddelde.

De toetreding van Oekraïne betekent een modernisering van Europa. Anders blijven onze beloften louter beloften, zonder inhoud.
2-0446-0000.englishText:
Mr President, it is easy to promise Ukraine a future in Europe. The question is: how are we going to make that promise a reality together with Ukraine?

Ukraine is a country at war. Precisely for that reason, the accession process requires urgency. We need Ukraine for our security. At the same time, the accession process must proceed carefully to guarantee the stability of Europe.

Ukraine is not an average candidate member state. The country has an agricultural area larger than that of France. This offers many opportunities for Europe's future bio-economy. At the same time, the gross domestic product per capita is well below the European average.

Ukraine's accession means a modernisation of Europe. Otherwise, our promises will remain mere promises, without substance.

2-0447-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Tebevykstant precedento neturinčiam karo spaudimui, Ukraina sėkmingai stiprina demokratines institucijas, vykdo teismų reformas, siekia kovoti su korupcija ir įrodo, kad geba atsakingai įsisavinti kiekvieną paramos eurą. Tuo tarpu Europos Sąjunga privalo, jau privalėjo atverti likusius derybų klasterius, toliau teikti finansinę paramą ir dar griežtinti sankcijas Rusijai, įskaitant kovą su sankcijų apeidinėjimu. Šiandien ukrainiečiai vėl atakavo kelis sankcionuotus šešėlinius rusų tanklaivius, bet iki sisteminio užkardymo vis dar toli. Rusijos šešėlinis laivynas vis dar perveža du trečdalius Rusijos naftos eksporto. Privalome didinti spaudimą, užtikrindami nuolatinį sistemingą Rusijos ekonomikos, jų bankinės sistemos ardymą, įšaldyto turto konfiskavimą, kad rusai pagaliau nutrauktų agresiją.
2-0447-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues. Amid unprecedented war pressure, Ukraine is successfully strengthening its democratic institutions, carrying out judicial reforms, striving to fight corruption, and proving its ability to responsibly absorb every euro of support. Meanwhile, the European Union must, it should have already opened the remaining negotiation clusters, continue to provide financial support, and further tighten sanctions against Russia, including combating sanctions evasion.
Today, Ukrainians attacked several sanctioned shadow Russian tankers again, but we are still far from systemic prevention. Russia's shadow fleet still transports two-thirds of Russia's oil exports. We must increase pressure by ensuring the continuous, systematic disruption of the Russian economy and their banking system, and the confiscation of frozen assets, so that the Russians finally halt their aggression.

2-0448-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, is ábhar fíorthábhachtach é seo dúinn uile.

Therefore, our support for Ukraine must continue to be unconditional and unwavering. This support must remain unconditional even where this brings economic or political challenges for all of us. Ukraine is defending all of Europe, and we must take every single measure possible to choke the Russian economy and ensure nothing we do in the EU enhances its ability to maintain this war.

I support the strongest possible sanctions against Russia and we must build on this in the 21st package, and also on our energy independence. Yesterday, we saw more deadly missile and drone attacks in Kyiv – another stark reminder of the horrors that the Ukrainian people must live with.

On Ukraine's accession: reforms are needed. Enlargement is and must remain merit-based. But we should applaud Ukraine for the work it is doing to make reform after reform, whilst under constant bombardment from Russia.

As regards peace, I will quote Warren Buffett: 'you can't do good business with a bad person'.

Bí cúramach, buaigh an cogadh agus gheobhaimid cogadh agus síocháin bhuan.
2-0448-0000.englishText:
Madam President, this is a matter of vital importance to all of us.

Therefore, our support for Ukraine must continue to be unconditional and unwavering. This support must remain unconditional even where this brings economic or political challenges for all of us. Ukraine is defending all of Europe, and we must take every single measure possible to choke the Russian economy and ensure nothing we do in the EU enhances its ability to maintain this war.

I support the strongest possible sanctions against Russia and we must build on this in the 21st package, and also on our energy independence. Yesterday, we saw more deadly missile and drone attacks in Kyiv – another stark reminder of the horrors that the Ukrainian people must live with.

On Ukraine's accession: reforms are needed. Enlargement is and must remain merit-based. But we should applaud Ukraine for the work it is doing to make reform after reform, whilst under constant bombardment from Russia.

As regards peace, I will quote Warren Buffett: 'you can't do good business with a bad person'.

Be careful, win the war and we will achieve war and lasting peace.

2-0451-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, twelve years ago, Putin attacked Ukraine. He wanted to stop Ukraine from joining the EU. Since then, hundreds of thousands of people have died. Millions of lives are broken. But Putin has not defeated Ukraine. He has made it stronger. With EU and US support, Ukraine is not just resisting, it is growing stronger – in security, in industry, in technology.

Since the war began, the EU has given Ukraine over EUR 200 billion. Ukraine needs this money to defend itself. But the EU needs Ukraine too – to keep Europe safe. If we are not safe, money means nothing.

The question is not 'Who needs who more?' We need each other, and Ukraine should join the EU as soon as possible.

2-0452-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Ukraina har bevisat att det går att slå mot Rysslands hjärta. Genom precisionsattacker mot raffinaderier, militärbaser och annan strategisk infrastruktur höjs kostnaden för Putins krig.

Europa har en skyldighet att ge Ukraina fler av de långdistansrobotar och vapensystem som gör skillnad. Vår plikt är inte bara att hjälpa Ukraina att överleva, utan att göra Ryssland för svagt för att kunna fortsätta sitt anfallskrig.

Gripen-samarbetet mellan Sverige och Ukraina visar att enskilda länder kan gå före. Nu måste politiska begränsningar av attacker mot legitima militära mål i Ryssland avskaffas. Samtidigt måste vi övergå från att skicka materiel till att bygga en gemensam försvarsindustri med Ukraina, och att göra ukrainska företag till en självklar del av Europas försvarsmarknad.

Ledarskap handlar inte om att inte visa vägen när andra tvekar. Det handlar om att agera kraftfullare för att säkra freden i Europa. Slava Ukraini.
2-0452-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Ukraine has proven that it is possible to strike at the heart of Russia. Through precision attacks against refineries, military bases, and other strategic infrastructure, the cost of Putin's war is being raised.

Europe has an obligation to provide Ukraine with more of the long-range missiles and weapon systems that make a difference. Our duty is not only to help Ukraine survive, but to make Russia too weak to be able to continue its war of aggression.

The Gripen cooperation between Sweden and Ukraine shows that individual countries can take the lead. Now, political restrictions on attacks against legitimate military targets in Russia must be abolished. At the same time, we must transition from sending equipment to building a joint defense industry with Ukraine, and make Ukrainian companies a natural part of Europe's defense market.

Leadership is not about failing to show the way when others hesitate. It is about acting more forcefully to secure peace in Europe. Slava Ukraini.

2-0453-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Przyjmujemy bardzo ważne sprawozdanie dotyczące relacji Unia Europejska–Ukraina. Oceniamy kandydata. Rozpoczął się formalnie proces negocjacji akcesyjnych z Ukrainą. Został po długim okresie odblokowany. Ta decyzja była jednością i tu również ma pełne nasze wsparcie.

Ale Unia to nie tylko wspólny rynek, nie tylko Schengen, nie tylko budżet, to przede wszystkim wartości. I musi to wybrzmieć wprost. W rozmowie o wspólnej przyszłości jedna sprawa pozostała niezałatwiona. Unię Europejską tworzą państwa i społeczeństwa, które potrafiły przezwyciężyć demony przeszłości i stanąć w prawdzie wobec zła. I zawsze fundamentem do pojednania i współpracy była prawda.

Ukraina i jej elity muszą tę sprawę rozwiązać. To nie jest sprawa między Polską a Ukrainą. Tu chodzi o europejskie wartości. Nie ma zgody na odwoływanie się do osób i formacji odpowiedzialnych za zbrodnie ludobójstwa. Ta sprawa musi wybrzmieć również w tym sprawozdaniu.
2-0453-0000.englishText:
Madam President! We are adopting a very important report concerning European Union-Ukraine relations. We are assessing the candidate. The formal process of accession negotiations with Ukraine has begun. It was unblocked after a long period. This decision was united and it also has our full support.

But the Union is not only a single market, not only Schengen, not only a budget, it is above all values. And this must be stated outright. In the discussion about a common future, one matter has remained unresolved. The European Union is formed by states and societies that have managed to overcome the demons of the past and confront evil with truth. And truth has always been the foundation for reconciliation and cooperation.

Ukraine and its elites must resolve this matter. This is not a matter between Poland and Ukraine. This is about European values. There is no consent to invoking individuals and formations responsible for the crimes of genocide. This matter must also be voiced in this report.

2-0455-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, este debate intenso y prolongado sobre Ucrania pone de manifiesto dos evidencias que necesitan ser expresadas.

La primera es que la conexión entre el apoyo a la defensa de Ucrania frente a la agresión de Rusia y las negociaciones de la futura adhesión es tan estrecha que no podrá resolverse si la Unión Europea no madura lo bastante y crece lo bastante para ser sentada en la mesa de la negociación que decida el futuro de Ucrania y establezca una paz digna y honorable para este país vecino que aspira a la adhesión.

La segunda es que esa adhesión no basta sencillamente con resolverla con una cuestión de examen de sus méritos individuales en Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción, sino que hará falta —más pronto que tarde— traer también al debate las reformas institucionales que permitan crear el espacio para acomodar a todos los candidatos a la adhesión y, particularmente, a un país tan enorme, con una agricultura tan significativa y con problemas de Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción tan importantes como los que representa Ucrania.
2-0455-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, this intense and prolonged debate on Ukraine highlights two obvious facts that need to be expressed.

The first is that the connection between support for Ukraine's defense against Russia's aggression and future accession negotiations is so close that it cannot be resolved unless the European Union matures enough and grows enough to be seated at the negotiating table that will decide the future of Ukraine and establish a dignified and honorable peace for this neighboring country that aspires to accession.

The second is that such accession cannot simply be resolved as a matter of examining its individual merits regarding the rule of law and the fight against corruption, but rather it will be necessary—sooner rather than later—to also bring into the debate the institutional reforms that allow creating the space to accommodate all accession candidates and, particularly, a country as huge, with such significant agriculture, and with such important rule of law and anti-corruption problems as those represented by Ukraine.

2-0456-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Oczywistym jest, że Rosja jest ogromnym zagrożeniem dla Europy, również dla Ukrainy, co widzimy w działaniach wojennych, które prowadzi ten kraj przeciwko Ukrainie. Natomiast musimy też zdawać sobie sprawę, gdy dyskutujemy dzisiaj tutaj o sprawozdaniu w sprawie Ukrainy, z tego, że wszelkie ruchy ze strony Ukrainy w kierunku europejskim muszą być poprzedzone prawdą. I jestem niestety zszokowany decyzją, którą podjął prezydent Zełenski, decydując się na taki krok, który poczynił, to znaczy nazwanie jednej z jednostek ukraińskich imieniem UPA, czyli zbrodniarzy wojennych, którzy wymordowali ponad 100 tysięcy Polaków w czasie II wojny światowej.

Bez jasnej deklaracji Parlamentu Europejskiego, że było to ludobójstwo, bez jasnej deklaracji Parlamentu Europejskiego, że nie ma zgody na czczenie takich osób jak Bandera, nie możemy mówić w przyszłości o integracji europejskiej, głębszej z Ukrainą. Musi to dzisiaj wybrzmieć. I dlatego apeluję do moich kolegów ze wszystkich frakcji politycznych, również do kolegów z Polski, aby poparli poprawki, które zgłosiła grupa ECR.
2-0456-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is obvious that Russia is a huge threat to Europe, and also to Ukraine, as we see in the military actions that this country is waging against Ukraine. However, we must also realize, when we discuss the report on Ukraine here today, that any steps taken by Ukraine towards Europe must be preceded by the truth. And I am unfortunately shocked by the decision made by President Zelenskyy, deciding on the step he took, that is, naming one of the Ukrainian units after the UPA, i.e., war criminals who murdered over 100,000 Poles during World War II.

Without a clear declaration by the European Parliament that this was a genocide, without a clear declaration by the European Parliament that there is no consent to honoring such people as Bandera, we cannot talk in the future about European integration, deeper with Ukraine. This must resonate today. And that is why I appeal to my colleagues from all political groups, including my colleagues from Poland, to support the amendments submitted by the ECR group.

2-0457-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, I would like to address the deplorable tensions between Poland and Ukraine of historical memory; and it echoes today as well.

We must not fall into this trap. I would recall the example set by Lithuania and Poland in their Treaty on friendly relations and good neighbourly cooperation. The Treaty openly acknowledged that our two nations could hold different interpretations of their shared history. Yet it also affirmed that an awareness of both the good and bad chapters of our past should strengthen mutual understanding.

More than 30 years later, this formula continues to guide the relationship between Lithuania and Poland. I also believe it offers the approach we need today: the courage to accept that history may be interpreted differently while choosing reconciliation over resentment. We must not allow Russia to divide us.

2-0458-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, colleagues, dear Commissioner, the EU is a unique geopolitical force: the only one that doesn't grow through conquest. We grow because countries freely decide to join. Ukraine chooses the EU for its promise of democracy, freedom and dignity.

But sometimes this can create a wrong perception. Just because countries aspire to join our Union doesn't mean that we are the only side with something to offer. Ukraine does not come to the EU empty-handed. On the contrary, since the start of the war, the script has flipped. Ukraine has shown us extraordinary innovation, courage and above all, resilience. Right now, Ukraine has the strongest army in Europe and is the world leader on drone technology. Guess who we ask for help when drones are flying over Europe?

Especially with Ukraine, people mistake a decision of geopolitical survival for charity work. So let's make it clear: both Ukraine and the EU are stronger together.

2-0459-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, dragi colegi, eu știam că atunci când o țară aderă la Uniunea Europeană, trebuie să îndeplinească niște criterii și să ne gândim logic, fără niciun fel de probleme colaterale: Îndeplinește Ucraina aceste criterii? De pildă, Ucraina respectă drepturile minorităților? Am auzit aici de la toți colegii că nu. Vă pot spune și eu despre minoritatea românească, și este a doua minoritate din Ucraina, după minoritatea rusă, că a pățit tot felul de nenorociri și că preoții noștri au fost acolo bătuți, arestați și acuzați de toate prostiile din lume.

Nu este niciunul astăzi condamnat pentru nimic, pentru că nu era nimic adevărat. Respectă Ucraina libertatea de exprimare? Era un coleg aici care spunea că nu este adevărat că ar fi închis Zelenski niște televiziuni în 2021. Vă spun eu că le-a închis și se numesc Zic, New Swan și un 112. Erau televiziunile opoziției de la acea vreme, Care opoziție mai avea puțin și ajungea pe primul loc. Sigur că da, putem să spunem orice dorim, dar Ucraina (...)

(Președinta a retras cuvântul vorbitorului)
2-0459-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, I knew that when a country joins the European Union, it must meet certain criteria and we must think logically, without any kind of collateral problems: Does Ukraine meet these criteria? For example, does Ukraine respect minority rights? I have heard here from all colleagues that it does not. I can also tell you about the Romanian minority, and it is the second minority in Ukraine, after the Russian minority, that it has suffered all sorts of misfortunes and that our priests there were beaten, arrested and accused of all the nonsense in the world.

Not a single one is convicted today of anything, because none of it was true. Does Ukraine respect freedom of expression? There was a colleague here who said it is not true that Zelenskyy closed some television stations in 2021. I am telling you that he closed them and they are called ZIK, NewsOne, and 112. They were the television stations of the opposition at that time, which opposition was almost coming in first place. Of course, we can say whatever we want, but Ukraine (...)

(The President withdrew the speaker's floor)
2-0459-0000.factCheck: Although the speaker claims that the Romanian minority is the second largest in Ukraine after the Russian minority, official data from the 2001 Ukrainian census shows that Belarusians are the second largest ethnic minority at 0.6%, while Romanians make up 0.3% of the population (or 0.8% if combined with Moldovans, who are officially registered as a separate ethnic group).

2-0460-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear Commissioner, colleagues, the European Union proposed clear possible timelines in the Ukrainian accession to the EU. I can tell you: in June 2026, the opening of all six clusters; until the end of 2026, substantial progress in all negotiating chapters; beginning 2027, start of closing all chapters.

And where are we now? Only one cluster was opened. It's a shame on the Council, and today we see certain Member States in the Council finding new reasons to stop the Ukrainian accession. The Council must stop doing this! It is a rotating veto dressed up as a national interest defence. It is our promise to press the Council, to fulfil obligations and to follow the timelines.

2-0462-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, colleagues, thank you for all the contributions. The message to Ukrainians is clear: the commitment for your country stands firm from a large majority in this House. That is also because Ukraine has already achieved so much on the reform path. There is no comparison to 2014.

I regret that the focus of the debate was partly diverted from the accession-related issues to the designation of a Ukrainian special forces unit as 'Heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army'.

Let me be clear: I think this was a wrong move, a political mistake, as it hurts the feelings of Polish citizens and the descendants of other victims. The fact that these UPA groups were fighting also against Stalin, and in favour of Ukrainian statehood, can by no means balance, neutralise or even justify the atrocities that have been committed.

No person, no organisation, can be selectively judged for what they have done. But what is more important than assessing the tragic past is the shared will to address the common future.

In this regard, I welcome the statement from Prime Minister Tusk from the outset, and also later during the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk, and on other occasions, and the meeting of the Foreign Ministers, Sikorski and Sybiha, showing the will to resolve the existing tensions.

Steps in this regard had already been taken earlier, and I call on all concerned to refrain from further verbal or political escalation. Such verbal radicalism from the extreme right only makes Putin happy and serves no constructive purpose. We cannot change the past, but we have to assess it in full, especially each nation's painful periods, and promise ourselves for the future: never again.

It is good to leave the historic assessment to historians, perhaps not only from the two countries concerned, but add experts from third countries who are sometimes more independent in their findings.

Coming from the country that inflicted the most atrocities on other nations in the 20th century, I am grateful that the European Union's purpose and legacy is that those who are inside will never again inflict such horror on each other.

So it is good to be all together for a better future and stand together against our real enemies, which are not inside, but outside.

2-0463-0000.sourceText:
La discussione è chiusa.

La votazione si svolgerà domani, mercoledì 8 luglio 2026.
2-0463-0000.englishText:
The discussion is closed.

The vote will take place tomorrow, Wednesday, 8 July 2026.

2-0463-2500.sourceText:
Európska integrácia Ukrajiny posilňuje celý náš región a vytvára priestor pre spoločnú prosperitu. Od Kyjeva, cez Košice až po Dublin.

Potrebujeme v našom susedstve stabilnú, bezpečnú a prosperujúcu Ukrajinu, nie zničenú krajinu ovládanú Ruskom. Ak bude prosperovať Ukrajina, budú prosperovať aj naše regióny, ktoré s ňou priamo susedia. Prešovský a Košický kraj môžu ťažiť z nových investícií a obchodných príležitostí a lepšieho dopravného spojenia, ako aj profitovať z cezhraničnej spolupráce.

Podpora Ukrajiny je v našom najlepšom záujme. Je totiž aj podporou budúcnosti Slovenska. A tí, ktorí hovoria opak, škodia nielen Ukrajine, ale aj Slovensku a jeho záujmom.
2-0463-2500.englishText:
European integration of Ukraine strengthens our entire region and creates space for shared prosperity. From Kyiv, through Košice, to Dublin.

We need a stable, secure, and prosperous Ukraine in our neighborhood, not a destroyed country controlled by Russia. If Ukraine prospers, our regions that directly border it will also prosper. The Prešov and Košice regions can benefit from new investments and business opportunities and better transport connections, as well as profit from cross-border cooperation.

Support for Ukraine is in our best interest. It is also support for the future of Slovakia. And those who say otherwise are harming not only Ukraine, but also Slovakia and its interests.

2-0463-5000.sourceText:
Co najmniej dwadzieścia tysięcy, a być może nawet trzydzieści pięć tysięcy ukraińskich dzieci zostało przymusowo wywiezionych do Rosji lub zatrzymanych na terenach okupowanych. Odbierano im kontakt z rodziną, zmieniano dane osobowe, poddawano rusyfikacji i propagandzie wojennej. Niektórym zmieniono tożsamość i oddano do adopcji. To nie są straty wojenne. To zbrodnia, którą Rosja prowadzi systematycznie i celowo.

Za każdą z tych liczb stoi konkretne dziecko. Jego strach. Dom. Rodzina, która czeka i nie wie, czy jeszcze kiedyś zobaczy swoje dziecko.

Europa nie może udawać, że tego nie widzi. Odpowiedzialność zbiorowa nie kończy się na deklaracjach solidarności, zaczyna się od konkretnych działań: dokumentowania, identyfikacji, powrotu i rehabilitacji. Każde dziecko, które nie wróci, jest dowodem na to, że ta odpowiedzialność nie została wypełniona.

Ponad cztery miliony Ukraińców korzysta dziś w Unii Europejskiej z tymczasowej ochrony. Wśród nich są dzieci, które uczą się w naszych szkołach i budują tu swoje życie. Nie zapominamy o nich. Nie zapominamy też o tych, których nie ma, o tych, którzy czekają po drugiej stronie na kogoś, kto ich znajdzie.

Naszym obowiązkiem jest zadbać o ich bezpieczny powrót, zdrowie psychiczne i przyszłość. Każde dziecko na to zasługuje.
2-0463-5000.englishText:
At least twenty thousand, and perhaps even thirty-five thousand Ukrainian children have been forcibly deported to Russia or detained in occupied territories. They were denied contact with their families, their personal data was changed, and they were subjected to Russification and war propaganda. Some had their identities changed and were put up for adoption. These are not war losses. This is a crime that Russia is committing systematically and deliberately.

Behind every one of these numbers stands a specific child. Their fear. Home. A family that waits and does not know if they will ever see their child again.

Europe cannot pretend it does not see this. Collective responsibility does not end with declarations of solidarity; it begins with concrete actions: documentation, identification, return, and rehabilitation. Every child who does not return is proof that this responsibility has not been fulfilled.

Over four million Ukrainians currently benefit from temporary protection in the European Union. Among them are children who are studying in our schools and building their lives here. We do not forget about them. Nor do we forget about those who are not here, about those waiting on the other side for someone to find them.

It is our duty to ensure their safe return, mental health, and future. Every child deserves this.

2-0463-6250.englishText: The opening of the first fundamental cluster of accession negotiations with Ukraine in June 2026 is commendable, although in my opinion it should have happened even earlier. Now, however, I hope that the negotiations will progress quickly. The EU must make an effort for the future security of Ukraine and Europe, and when assessing the readiness of candidate countries, it should also take into account their internal situation, including Russia's attempts to incite anti-EU sentiment. Ukraine has made tremendous efforts in strengthening democratic institutions and defending the separation of powers. Despite the ongoing war, Ukraine has made great progress, including in the areas of judicial reform and the fight against corruption. This work must definitely be continued. A strong rule of law ensures transparency and accountability in the reconstruction of the country and the recovery of the economy, and improves the investment climate and partners' trust. I certainly do not agree with the demand of the US administration to hold elections in Ukraine even before the end of the war. Creating the conditions necessary for free and fair elections takes time and must be done when the state of war has ended. It is important to support Ukraine's new momentum on the battlefield and increase pressure on the Russian war economy. I also commend the G7 leaders' statement on June 2026 regarding Ukraine and the disbursement of the first tranche of 3.2 billion euros of the Ukraine support loan.

2-0463-7500.sourceText:
Ukraine is turning the tide.

Its campaign of “long-range sanctions” against the Moscow regime's targets is proving wildly effective.

Russia, a country like a gas station, is watching its oil refineries burn across its territory.

Russia’s war is increasingly being felt on its own soil.

And that’s how it should be.

Where international partners failed to deliver, Ukraine developed its own capabilities.

At the same time, the country is preparing for EU membership.

The progress made by Ukraine in these most difficult circumstances deserves recognition.

Despite our political differences, one thing must be clear:

Europe must secure Ukraine’s victory.

Ukraine today is defending Europe against a common enemy.
