2-0467-0000.sourceText: L'ordine del giorno reca la relazione di Sven Mikser, a nome della commissione per gli affari esteri, sulla relazione 2025 della Commissione sulla Moldova (2025/2258(INI)) (A10-0164/2026).
2-0467-0000.englishText: The next item is the report by Sven Mikser, on behalf of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, on the Commission's 2025 report on Moldova (2025/2258(INI)) (A10-0164/2026).

2-0468-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner Kos, dear Marta, as tonight's debate precedes the vote on this year's EP report on Moldova, I would like to stress that, while a few of Moldova's fellow travellers among the EU candidate countries may have started the journey earlier and covered more ground by today, Moldova's progress over the past year has definitely been among the most impressive.

Moldova's Government has set for itself an ambitious timeline. In order for it to be met, the pace of reforms must not only be maintained, but further increased in many areas, and the reform effort must continue through all domestic political hiccups.

We, on behalf of the EU, must also live up to our end of the bargain. I welcome the start of formal accession negotiations – the opening of Cluster 1 – and I urge the Council to take a merit-based approach seriously and open the next negotiating clusters without any unnecessary delay.

Colleagues, when assessing Moldova's progress, it is particularly remarkable given the extraordinary geopolitical pressure the country is experiencing. During the parliamentary elections last year, we saw how this pressure manifested itself: the Russians orchestrated an unprecedented campaign of information manipulation and interference in order to destabilise Moldova and derail its European path. Russia weaponised significant resources, spending an estimated equivalent of 2 % of Moldova's GDP on illicit financing, disinformation and other malicious operations. I do believe that EU assistance and advice played an important role in beating back those hideous designs.

Furthermore, we cannot discuss Moldova's current situation without recognising how profoundly the country has been affected by the ongoing Russian war of aggression against Ukraine. Moldova has been hit by the security, economic and social fallout of the war. Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure have had a direct impact on Moldova, threatening energy stability and water security, and triggering an environmental emergency.

It is of the utmost importance that the EU and its Member States provide the necessary financial resources, technical assistance and specialised equipment to support Moldova. We must accelerate investments in critical energy infrastructure, such as the recently completed Vulcănești-Chișinău high-voltage power line, in order to eliminate Moldova's reliance on Russian energy sources and reduce vulnerabilities.

Obviously, besides helping to defend the country against external adversaries, Moldova's European integration must deliver concrete, tangible benefits to its citizens. Institutional reforms are at the core of this process. Moldova has made significant strides in reforming its justice sector and fighting corruption, although I must emphasise that these efforts demand sustained, depoliticised commitment to completely dismantle the entrenched oligarchic structures and interests.

Economically, Moldova is deepening its integration into the EU single market. The recent review of the terms of the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area, alongside Moldova's successful inclusion in the Single Euro Payments Area and the EU's 'roam like at home' initiative, are good examples of how our partnership improves livelihoods and stimulates growth. To sustain the momentum and help Moldova meet its target of concluding negotiations by 2028, robust and predictable financial backing by the EU is indispensable. We welcome the timely disbursement of EUR 270 million in pre-financing under the Reform and Growth Facility, as well as the additional EUR 207.9 million delivered following the successful achievement of key reform milestones.

As we provide this support, we must also continue to champion the vital role of civil society and independent media, ensuring they have the tools and protections to hold institutions accountable. We also reiterate our firm commitment to a peaceful, comprehensive resolution of the Transnistrian situation – a solution that will have to be based on Moldova's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

In conclusion, Moldova's goals are ambitious and its European path is not without challenges. But the Moldovan citizens have repeatedly proven their dedication to our European values. Let us stand firmly by their side, providing the guidance and solidarity needed for a secure, vibrant European future for Moldova and, indeed, for our own continent.

2-0469-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, thank you to the rapporteur, Sven Mikser, for your report on Moldova and for your work for Moldova. You have painted a picture of a nation transforming itself as it advances on its European path. Moldova's delivery on reforms is seen all over Europe.

Over the past years, we have seen a nation that stood up against foreign interference and hybrid attacks, and made its choice for Europe and its path towards membership of our Union. This sovereign choice deserves our full support. We have seen a country that is moving against corruption and organised crime, putting people in jail that once seemed untouchable.

Moldova has also been delivering on enlargement reforms at record speed. In the 2025 enlargement report, the Commission assessed that Moldova made progress across all negotiating chapters. This includes important advances on the fundamentals, energy alignment and digital transformation. Since then, Moldova has continued moving forward. We have also seen impressive numbers in the implementation of the growth plan reforms: with 93 %, Moldova is ahead of all other EU candidates that have growth plans.

These reforms build trust. Moldova's European future is an investment in the security and stability of our continent as a whole. I was in Chișinău last month, discussing the next steps in the accession process and, once again, I could see a strong determination to deliver reforms, despite the immense pressure they continue to face. In line with our recommendations, it has implemented key reforms, supported by the guidance provided by Member States during the front‑loading exercise in December 2025 and March 2026. Therefore, I share your opinion: we should call on the Council to open all the clusters as soon as possible. I hope that we will reach this goal.

At the same time, Moldova should continue delivering reforms – particularly on justice, the fight against corruption and economic governance. These reforms are essential to meet the interim benchmarks needed to start closing chapters. As you have stressed, Moldova joined the Single Euro Payments Area in October last year and also became part of the 'roam like at home' area. At the same time, we are also advancing together on energy integration, trade liberalisation and connectivity.

Much has been achieved, but the work is not finished. I count on your continued support in accompanying Moldova on its European path. Supporting Moldova is an investment in a stronger, safer and more united Europe.

2-0470-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, first of all, I would like to thank Sven Mikser and our colleagues for the excellent and very smooth cooperation. It's really a pleasure to work as a team. I would like to confirm, in the name of EPP Group, the four amendments tabled by the rapporteur we support.

Because of the report, I have three messages to our Moldovan friends.

First of all, the EU should open negotiation clusters with Moldova without any delay. My personal perspective, and also in the name of EPP, I can confirm all the clusters should be open because of the number of reforms and the implementation of the reforms. Moldova is ready to continue these negotiations very effectively. So we should do it. This is our obligation not to postpone it.

The second message is a political one because a bigger and more integrated Europe is also a safer Europe. But we have to take into account that we can learn how to fight effectively against disinformation, against Russian activity. Moldova did it. So we should learn from Kyiv how to be effective in the fight against disinformation. We should take into account that issue also.

The third message is about economic progress. This is a huge success and, I think, also personal success of the leadership, Maia Sandu's leadership and the past party, but of course, important is also the European help. It is not a huge one, but very effective. We can mention EUR 1.2 billion in grants – this is last five years – and another EUR 1.7 billion for private sector also during the last five years. But now, very important is the growth plan for Moldova – close to EUR 2 billion in the coming year and also additional EUR 2.5 billion for the private sector.

The fourth – last – message for the Moldovans, in conclusion, we are waiting for you in common Europe.

2-0471-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, en las elecciones de septiembre, el pueblo moldavo dio una lección y dijo claramente que quiere avanzar junto a la Unión Europea y hacia la Unión Europea. Además, lo hizo en un contexto difícil marcado por injerencias externas, por presiones, por desinformación y por mucha intoxicación.

Por eso, el mensaje que lanzaron los ciudadanos y ciudadanas de Moldavia tiene todavía más valor político. Y nosotros, la Unión Europea, tenemos la obligación de responder con responsabilidad y exigencia. La responsabilidad y la exigencia implican reformas, independencia de la justicia, Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción. Pero también tenemos que responder con una actitud constructiva para que cada avance que dé Moldavia se tenga en cuenta.

Además, nos encontramos en un momento en el que algunos están incluso trabajando desde dentro, desde la Unión Europea, para debilitar la Unión y sus valores. En ese momento, Moldavia nos está recordando firmemente a todos por qué nuestro proyecto —el proyecto de Unión Europea— sigue teniendo sentido, porque todavía hay pueblos que ven en Europa una promesa de libertad, de democracia, de seguridad y de prosperidad como nosotros la vivimos.

Ahora es el momento de ser ambiciosos y abrir todos los clústeres de negociación de una vez, porque Moldavia necesita a la Unión Europea, y Europa también necesita pueblos que sigan creyendo en la Unión Europea.
2-0471-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, in the September elections, the Moldovan people gave a lesson and clearly stated that they want to move forward alongside the European Union and towards the European Union.

Furthermore, they did so in a difficult context marked by external interference, pressure, disinformation, and a great deal of manipulation.

Therefore, the message sent by the citizens of Moldova carries even greater political value. And we, the European Union, have the obligation to respond with responsibility and rigor. Responsibility and rigor imply reforms, judicial independence, the rule of law, and the fight against corruption. But we also have to respond with a constructive attitude so that every step forward taken by Moldova is taken into account.

Moreover, we find ourselves at a time when some are even working from within, from the European Union, to weaken the Union and its values. At that very moment, Moldova is firmly reminding us all why our project—the European Union project—still makes sense, because there are still peoples who see in Europe a promise of freedom, democracy, security, and prosperity as we experience it.

Now is the time to be ambitious and open all negotiation clusters at once, because Moldova needs the European Union, and Europe also needs peoples who continue to believe in the European Union.

2-0472-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, dragi colegi, doamnă comisar, o Europă mai puternică înseamnă o Republică Moldova parte a Uniunii Europene. Integrarea este un proces tehnic și politic. De aceea este important să privim în perspectivă istorică: în 20 de ani, unde vedem Moldova și Uniunea Europeană? Atunci când lăsăm un gol de securitate la granițele noastre, acel gol este umplut de instabilitate, iar Republica Moldova se află astăzi în prima linie a acestei realități.

Sprijinirea Moldovei nu este doar un act de solidaritate, ci și o investiție strategică în securitatea și stabilitatea întregii Uniuni Europene. În ciuda presiunilor externe, a atacurilor hibride și a încercărilor constante de destabilizare, Republica Moldova a ales democrația, statul de drept și valorile occidentale. Această alegere necesită din partea noastră însă un sprijin ferm și consecvent.

O Moldovă în Uniunea Europeană înseamnă frontiera estică mai sigură, o reziliență mai mare împotriva ingerințelor externe și un mesaj clar că Europa își protejează partenerii care aleg libertatea și pacea. Extinderea europeană a fost întotdeauna unul dintre cele mai puternice instrumente ale UE pentru a consolida pacea, prosperitatea și stabilitatea în Europa. Cu fiecare extindere, toate țările UE au devenit mai puternice, mai prospere, iar Europa mai stabilă.

Sprijinind Republica Moldova, consolidăm atât viitorul unui stat vecin, cât și întărim securitatea, unitatea și credibilitatea întregului proiect european. Tocmai de aceea, viitorul Republicii Moldova trebuie să fie în Uniunea Europeană.
2-0472-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, a stronger Europe means a Republic of Moldova as part of the European Union. Integration is both a technical and a political process. That is why it is important to look at it from a historical perspective: in 20 years, where do we see Moldova and the European Union? When we leave a security vacuum at our borders, that vacuum is filled by instability, and the Republic of Moldova is today on the front line of this reality.

Supporting Moldova is not only an act of solidarity, but also a strategic investment in the security and stability of the entire European Union. Despite external pressures, hybrid attacks and constant attempts at destabilization, the Republic of Moldova has chosen democracy, the rule of law and Western values. However, this choice requires firm and consistent support from us.

A Moldova in the European Union means a safer eastern border, greater resilience against external interference and a clear message that Europe protects its partners who choose freedom and peace. European enlargement has always been one of the EU's most powerful instruments to consolidate peace, prosperity and stability in Europe. With each enlargement, all EU countries have become stronger and more prosperous, and Europe more stable.

By supporting the Republic of Moldova, we both consolidate the future of a neighboring state and strengthen the security, unity and credibility of the entire European project. That is precisely why the future of the Republic of Moldova must be in the European Union.

2-0473-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, domnule raportor, raportul pe care îl dezbatem astăzi confirmă o realitate incontestabilă: Republica Moldova avansează accelerat și hotărât spre obiectivul său de a deveni un stat membru al Uniunii Europene.

Vreau să salut reziliența extraordinară a cetățenilor moldoveni, în ciuda amenințărilor hibride, a dezinformării și a interferențelor fără precedent orchestrate de Kremlin. Aceștia și-au apărat democrația și au reconfirmat ireversibilitatea parcursului european al Moldovei.

Progresele tehnice și reformele de la Chișinău sunt remarcabile. Faptul că am deschis recent negocierile pe primul cluster, cel al valorilor fundamentale, este o dovadă a seriozității acestui angajament. Moldova este deja parte a spațiului european de roaming și se integrează în zona unică de plăți. De asemenea, prin planul de creștere de 1,9 miliarde aprobat, susținem tangibil și direct modernizarea școlilor, a spitalelor și a întreprinderilor locale.

Republica Moldova nu mai este doar un beneficiar, ci contribuie deja activ la securitatea continentului nostru. Responsabilitate este să renunțăm la scuze și pretexte formale și să rămânem alături de Chișinău la fiecare pas, deoarece locul firesc al Moldovei este aici, în familia europeană.
2-0473-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, Mr Rapporteur, the report we are debating today confirms an undeniable reality: the Republic of Moldova is advancing rapidly and decisively towards its objective of becoming a member state of the European Union.

I want to salute the extraordinary resilience of Moldovan citizens, despite the hybrid threats, disinformation and unprecedented interference orchestrated by the Kremlin. They have defended their democracy and reconfirmed the irreversibility of Moldova's European path.

The technical progress and reforms in Chișinău are remarkable. The fact that we recently opened negotiations on the first cluster, that of fundamental values, is proof of the seriousness of this commitment. Moldova is already part of the European roaming area and is integrating into the single payment area. Also, through the approved 1.9 billion growth plan, we are tangibly and directly supporting the modernization of schools, hospitals and local enterprises.

The Republic of Moldova is no longer just a beneficiary, but is already actively contributing to the security of our continent. Our responsibility is to give up formal excuses and pretexts and to stand by Chișinău at every step, because Moldova's natural place is here, in the European family.

2-0474-0000.sourceText: Fru formand! Den 28. september 2025 var jeg sammen med andre kolleger herfra valgobservatør ved parlamentsvalget i Moldova. Der var stor nervøsitet op til valget på grund af en massiv russisk påvirkning med misinformation, med bestikkelse med videre. Men heldigvis vandt de proeuropæiske demokratiske partier. Derfor kan Moldova fortsætte sin vej mod et EU-medlemskab, og vi støtter reformer, men der er stadig udfordringer med korruption og med organiseret kriminalitet. Den største udfordring er selvsagt udbryderregionen Transnistrien, men også generelt de fortsatte russiske forsøg på hybridkrig, på misinformation, på destabilisering. Det er mit håb, at Moldova som Europas fattigste land vil fortsætte reformprocessen og gøre sig klar til et EU-medlemskab, så Moldova definitivt bliver en del af Europa. Vi vil gerne hjælpe dem, så meget, vi kan.
2-0474-0000.englishText: Madam President! On 28 September 2025, I, along with other colleagues from here, was an election observer at the parliamentary elections in Moldova. There was great anxiety leading up to the election due to massive Russian influence with misinformation, bribery, and so on. But fortunately, the pro-European democratic parties won. Therefore, Moldova can continue its path towards EU membership, and we support reforms, but there are still challenges with corruption and organized crime. The biggest challenge is, of course, the breakaway region of Transnistria, but also generally the continued Russian attempts at hybrid warfare, misinformation, and destabilization. It is my hope that Moldova, as Europe's poorest country, will continue the reform process and prepare for EU membership, so that Moldova definitively becomes a part of Europe. We want to help them as much as we can.

2-0475-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Jag skulle också vilja tacka föredraganden Sven Mikser för ett bra betänkande. Flera av de punkter som var viktiga för oss i vänstern finns med, som att bekämpa fattigdomen i Moldavien, att fortsätta arbetet mot korruptionen, att stödja investeringar i förnybar energi och för ett verkligt energioberoende och att värna miljön. Som helhet är det ett bra betänkande.

Just nu skakas Moldavien av lite turbulens i inrikespolitiken. Viktiga personer har avgått. Det finns anklagelser om korruption. Det är naturligtvis illa, men det hade varit ännu mer illa om det inte hade kommit fram, om man inte hade dragit fram oegentligheter i ljuset.

På ett sätt är det ett gott tecken att även i det statsbärande partiet avslöjas korruption. Det visar att arbetet mot korruptionen tas på allvar.
2-0475-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I would also like to thank the rapporteur Sven Mikser for a good report. Several of the points that were important to us in the Left are included, such as fighting poverty in Moldova, continuing the work against corruption, supporting investments in renewable energy and for true energy independence, and protecting the environment. As a whole, it is a good report.

Right now, Moldova is being shaken by some turbulence in domestic politics. Important figures have resigned. There are accusations of corruption. That is naturally bad, but it would have been even worse if it had not come to light, if irregularities had not been brought into the light.

In a way, it is a good sign that corruption is being exposed even within the ruling party. It shows that the work against corruption is being taken seriously.

2-0476-0000.sourceText:
�� Г-жо Председател, пред Молдова продължават да стоят сериозни предизвикателства в борбата с корупцията, реформата на съдебната система и укрепването на държавните институции. Именно затова призивите за незабавното отваряне на всички групи преговорни глави и ускоряването на присъединителния процес не са в интерес нито на гражданите на Европейския съюз, нито на гражданите на Молдова.

Европейската интеграция е силен инструмент, който трябва да създава реални икономически ползи за бизнеса, да укрепва конкурентоспособността и да защитава традиционните национални общности като българската. Прибързаното придвижване към членство, преди изпълнението на необходимите реформи, би поставило под риск именно тези дългосрочни ползи. Европейският съюз трябва да прилага собствените си критерии по еднакъв начин към всички държави кандидатки. Само така ще запазим доверието в политиката на разширяване и ще гарантираме, че членството се основава на реални заслуги, а не на политическа целесъобразност.
2-0476-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Moldova continues to face serious challenges in the fight against corruption, judicial reform, and the strengthening of state institutions. Precisely for this reason, calls for the immediate opening of all negotiating chapters and the acceleration of the accession process are in the interest neither of the citizens of the European Union nor of the citizens of Moldova.

European integration is a powerful tool that should create real economic benefits for business, strengthen competitiveness, and protect traditional national communities such as the Bulgarian one. Hasty movement towards membership, before the fulfillment of the necessary reforms, would put these very long-term benefits at risk. The European Union must apply its own criteria in the same way to all candidate countries. Only in this way will we preserve trust in the enlargement policy and guarantee that membership is based on real merits, rather than on political expediency.

2-0477-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, doamnă comisar, în ultimul an, Republica Moldova este statul candidat pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană, care a înregistrat cele mai semnificative progrese pe calea integrării europene. Cetățenii Republicii Moldova încep să simtă beneficiile concrete ale integrării în Uniunea Europeană. Deja împreună, prin efortul autorităților din Republica Moldova și prin efortul instituțiilor europene, reușim să integrăm Republica Moldova în tot mai multe programe europene, astfel încât cetățenii să simtă deja, înainte de data aderării, avantajele integrării europene.

În urmă cu puține săptămâni am reușit să deschidem, și la nivel politic, la cel mai înalt nivel politic, negocierile pe primul cluster al negocierilor de aderare, ca urmare a progreselor bune înregistrate la nivel tehnic.

Prin raportul Parlamentului European, pe care îl vom adopta mâine. Solicităm trei lucruri.

În primul rând, deschiderea negocierilor pe toate clasele de negociere la nivel politic, cât mai curând posibil, nu mai târziu de finalul acestui an. Unu la mână. Doi la mână: continuarea reformelor pe calea integrării europene și, trei la mână, creșterea sprijinului financiar și tehnic din partea Uniunii Europene pentru Republica Moldova, fiindcă Federația Rusă a încercat în ultimii ani să țină Republica Moldova pe loc și a eșuat. Dar Federația Rusă va continua să încerce să răspândească știri false, propagandă, dezinformare în Republica Moldova, încercând să țină Republica Moldova pe loc.

Noi trebuie să fim mai puternici, să fim solidari cu oamenii din Republica Moldova, astfel încât Republica Moldova să continue să avanseze rapid pe calea integrării europene. O Republică Moldovă puternică, stabilă, reformată este bună pentru cetățenii Republicii Moldova, dar este o veste bună și pentru Uniunea Europeană în ansamblu.
2-0477-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, over the past year, the Republic of Moldova is the candidate country for accession to the European Union that has registered the most significant progress on the path of European integration. The citizens of the Republic of Moldova are beginning to feel the concrete benefits of integration into the European Union. Already together, through the effort of the authorities of the Republic of Moldova and through the effort of European institutions, we are succeeding in integrating the Republic of Moldova into more and more European programs, so that citizens can already feel, before the accession date, the advantages of European integration.

A few weeks ago we managed to open, also at the political level, at the highest political level, the negotiations on the first cluster of accession negotiations, as a result of the good progress registered at the technical level.

Through the European Parliament's report, which we will adopt tomorrow, we request three things.

First of all, the opening of negotiations on all negotiating clusters at the political level as soon as possible, no later than the end of this year. One. Secondly, the continuation of reforms on the path of European integration and, thirdly, the increase of financial and technical support from the European Union for the Republic_of_Moldova, because the Russian Federation has tried in recent years to hold the Republic of Moldova back and has failed. But the Russian Federation will continue to try to spread fake news, propaganda, disinformation in the Republic of Moldova, trying to hold the Republic of Moldova back.

We must be stronger, be in solidarity with the people of the Republic_of_Moldova, so that the Republic of Moldova continues to advance rapidly on the path of European integration. A strong, stable, reformed Republic of Moldova is good for the citizens of the Republic of Moldova, but it is also good news for the European Union as a whole.

2-0478-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, doresc în primul rând să îl felicit pe colegul meu social-democrat, Sven Mikser, pentru raportul său. Noi, social-democrații, am sprijinit mereu parcursul european al Republicii Moldova. Pentru că da, locul Republicii Moldova este în familia europeană. În ciuda presiunilor externe, a atacurilor hibride și a tentativelor repetate de destabilizare, cetățenii săi au ales calea europeană.

Autoritățile au datoria să facă toate reformele necesare aderării în vederea respectării termenului ambițios fixat pentru finalizarea negocierilor, finalul anului 2028 și suntem aici pentru a sprijini Republica Moldova, iar pentru atingerea acestui obiectiv consolidarea statului de drept, independența justiției, combaterea corupției și modernizarea administrației trebuie să rămână priorități.

Încurajez actorii politici de la Chișinău să gestioneze eficient actualul context politic și să îl transforme într-un impuls pentru accelerarea reformelor europene prin participarea întregii populații. Tocmai de aceea, Parlamentul European transmite astăzi un mesaj clar: Republica Moldova a făcut progrese remarcabile și merită să continue acest parcurs prin deschiderea tuturor capitolelor de negociere la Uniunea Europeană și dorim această deschidere să se întâmple de îndată, pentru că nu putem avea întârzieri.

De asemenea, Uniunea Europeană trebuie să recompenseze meritul, determinarea și rezultatele concrete obținute de Republica Moldova și, în sensul acesta trebuie să oferim un parcurs accelerat de aderare, un parcurs propriu și, de ce nu, chiar fonduri europene suplimentare. În sensul acesta, Republica Moldova, vă așteptăm aici, în Uniunea Europeană.
2-0478-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, I would first like to congratulate my Social-Democratic colleague, Sven Mikser, on his report. We, the Social Democrats, have always supported the European path of the Republic of Moldova. Because yes, the place of the Republic of Moldova is in the European family. Despite external pressures, hybrid attacks, and repeated attempts at destabilization, its citizens have chosen the European path.

The authorities have a duty to carry out all the reforms necessary for accession in order to meet the ambitious deadline set for the completion of negotiations, the end of 2028, and we are here to support the Republic of Moldova. To achieve this objective, the consolidation of the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary, the fight against corruption, and the modernization of the administration must remain priorities.

I encourage political actors in Chișinău to efficiently manage the current political context and transform it into an impetus for accelerating European reforms through the participation of the entire population. That is why the European Parliament is sending a clear message today: the Republic of Moldova has made remarkable progress and deserves to continue this path through the opening of all EU negotiation chapters, and we want this opening to happen immediately, because we cannot afford delays.

Furthermore, the European Union must reward the merit, determination, and concrete results achieved by the Republic of Moldova, and in this regard, we must offer an accelerated accession path, a merit-based path of its own and, why not, even additional European funds. In this sense, Republic of Moldova, we look forward to welcoming you here, in the European Union.

2-0479-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Otwarcie faktycznych negocjacji akcesyjnych Mołdawii z Unią Europejską to dobry i zasłużony krok na europejskiej drodze tego państwa. Mołdawia ma prawo i wolę wyrwania się z postsowieckiej strefy wpływów, a my chcemy jej w tym pomóc.

Naszym zadaniem jest wsparcie mołdawskich partnerów w budowie silnego, nowoczesnego i demokratycznego państwa. Oznacza to m.in. konsekwentną walkę z korupcją i oligarchią, które są zmorą każdego społeczeństwa postkomunistycznego.

Unia musi również wspierać działania na rzecz integralności terytorialnej Mołdawii. Odzyskanie przez Kiszyniów kontroli nad Naddniestrzem jest sprawą kluczową. Unia ma narzędzie nacisku, gdyż 70% eksportu towarów z Naddniestrza trafia na rynek europejski. Należy stosować twardą politykę sankcyjną i celną – albo lojalność wobec Mołdawii, albo koniec interesów z Europą.

Pani Komisarz, dużym problemem dotyczącym tempa integracji Mołdawii z Unią jest połączenie jej kandydatury z kandydaturą Ukrainy. Ukraina nie radzi sobie dziś ani z korupcją, ani z oligarchizacją, ani z odradzającym się nacjonalizmem. Dlatego trzeba przyjąć zasadę, że każde państwo jest oceniane na podstawie indywidualnych osiągnięć.
2-0479-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Opening actual accession negotiations between Moldova and the European Union is a good and well-deserved step on this country's European path. Moldova has the right and the will to break away from the post-Soviet sphere of influence, and we want to help it do so.

Our task is to support our Moldovan partners in building a strong, modern, and democratic state. This means, among other things, the consistent fight against corruption and oligarchy, which are the bane of every post-communist society.

The Union must also support actions for Moldova's territorial integrity. Chisinau regaining control over Transnistria is a key issue. The Union has a leverage tool, as 70% of goods exports from Transnistria go to the European market. A tough sanctions and customs policy should be applied – either loyalty to Moldova, or an end to business with Europe.

Madam Commissioner, a major problem concerning the pace of Moldova's EU integration is linking its candidacy with that of Ukraine. Today, Ukraine is not coping with corruption, oligarchization, or reviving nationalism. Therefore, the principle must be adopted that each country is assessed on the basis of its individual achievements.

2-0480-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, raportul pe care îl discutăm astăzi nu trebuie privit ca o simplă evaluare a progreselor Republicii Moldova în procesul de integrare. Discuția despre extindere s-a concentrat adesea pe costul aderării. Poate că este momentul să nu mai privim totul doar în termeni ce țin de valoarea investiției, ci sa ne întrebăm care ar fi costul dacă nu am aduce mai rapid Republica Moldova în Uniunea Europeană.

Securitatea Uniunii Europene depinde și de securitatea Republicii Moldova, care luptă de peste 35 de ani să scape de influența malefică a Moscovei, ce menține ilegal trupe militare pe teritoriul său. Cetățenii Republicii Moldova și-au câștigat dreptul de a primi o perspectivă clară de aderare la Uniunea Europeană, iar aceasta trebuie doar accelerată.

Republica Moldova, în pofida presiunii agresive și constante a Rusiei, a reușit să înceapă reformele necesare pentru a fi pregătită de aderare, iar acest drum trebuie încurajat și susținut. De aceea, cred că este important să fim cu toții alături de Chișinău în fiecare clipă.
2-0480-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, the report we are discussing today should not be seen as a simple evaluation of the Republic of Moldova's progress in the integration process. The discussion on enlargement has often focused on the cost of accession. Perhaps it is time to stop looking at everything only in terms of the value of the investment, and instead ask ourselves what the cost would be if we did not bring the Republic of Moldova into the European Union more quickly.

The security of the European Union also depends on the security of the Republic of Moldova, which has been fighting for over 35 years to escape the malign influence of Moscow, which illegally keeps military troops on its territory. The citizens of the Republic of Moldova have earned the right to receive a clear perspective of accession to the European Union, and this must simply be accelerated.

The Republic of Moldova, despite Russia's aggressive and constant pressure, has managed to begin the necessary reforms to be prepared for accession, and this path must be encouraged and supported. Therefore, I believe it is important that we all stand by Chișinău at every moment.

2-0482-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, Moldova este singurul candidat care a atins 28 din 30 de obiective de aderare. Și asta sub atacuri hibride, șantaj energetic, otrăvire a Prutului și multe alte scumpiri generate de război. Și eu cred că e rândul nostru să fim la înălțimea lor și nu rândul moldovenilor să fie la înălțimea noastră. Ei o fac deja de mult timp.

Eu sunt român, știu ce înseamnă să lupți pentru Europa, când alții te conving că nu meriți, că România s-a chinuit să demonstreze că trebuie să fie în Europa și iată că împlinim 20 de ani. Dar pentru oamenii ăștia care se chinuie de la o alegere la alta prin greutăți, să intre în Uniunea Europeană și o fac convingător, cu un guvern dedicat, trebuie să arătăm solidaritate.

Așa că nu vreau să ne oprim deloc, pentru că Moldova vrea, Europa vrea, Moldova poate, Europa poate. Și cred că este un moment unic, o fereastră de oportunitate care nu se deschide mereu. Așa că chiar îmi doresc, doamna Kos, să facem hora aia în care ați dansat și dumneavoastră la Chișinău, cu Uniunea Europeană (...)
2-0482-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Moldova is the only candidate that has achieved 28 out of 30 accession objectives. And this under hybrid attacks, energy blackmail, poisoning of the Prut and many other price increases generated by the war. And I believe it is our turn to rise to their level and not the Moldovans' turn to rise to ours. They have been doing it for a long time.

I am Romanian, I know what it means to fight for Europe, when others convince you that you do not deserve it, that Romania struggled to prove that it must be in Europe and behold, we are turning 20 years. But for these people who struggle from one election to another through hardships, to enter the European Union and they do it convincingly, with a dedicated government, we must show solidarity.

So I do not want us to stop at all, because Moldova wants it, Europe wants it, Moldova can do it, Europe can do it. And I believe it is a unique moment, a window of opportunity that does not open all the time. So I really want us, Ms Kos, to do that ring dance that you also danced in Chișinău, with the European Union (...)

2-0483-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Die Republik Moldau befindet sich auf ihrem europäischen Weg – und das ist auch gut so, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen. Doch dieser Weg bedeutet nicht nur Reform auf dem Papier; er bedeutet auch, europäische Grundwerte in der Praxis umzusetzen.

Noch immer gibt es schwerwiegende Menschenrechtsprobleme. Der Europäische Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte hat wiederholt Verstöße festgestellt, unter anderem wegen unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen, Gewalt und erniedrigender Behandlung. Menschenrechte gelten universell: Eine Strafe darf die Freiheit nehmen, aber niemals die Menschlichkeit.

Diese Verantwortung zeigt sich auch im Umgang mit Tieren. Die Situation von streunenden Hunden in Moldau ist weiterhin besorgniserregend: Berichte über schlechte Haltungsbedingungen, grausame Behandlung und Tötungspraktiken müssen ernst genommen werden.

Der Umgang mit den Schwächsten ist ein Maßstab für die Werte einer Gesellschaft. Deswegen braucht es auch im Tierschutz europäische Standards: Kastrations- und Impfprogramme, bessere Bedingungen in Tierheimen und Unterstützung für lokale Akteure.

Der Schutz der Menschenrechte und der Tierschutz folgen beide derselben Grundidee. Eine Gesellschaft zeigt ihre Stärke daran, wie sie mit den Schwächsten umgeht.
2-0483-0000.englishText:
Mr President! The Republic of Moldova is on its European path – and that is also a good thing, dear colleagues. But this path does not only mean reform on paper; it also means putting European fundamental values into practice.

There are still serious human rights problems. The European Court of Human Rights has repeatedly found violations, including due to inhumane detention conditions, violence, and degrading treatment. Human rights apply universally: a punishment may take away freedom, but never humanity.

This responsibility is also evident in the treatment of animals. The situation of stray dogs in Moldova remains alarming: reports of poor housing conditions, cruel treatment, and killing practices must be taken seriously.

The treatment of the most vulnerable is a yardstick for the values of a society. That is why animal welfare also needs European standards: neutering and vaccination programmes, better conditions in animal shelters, and support for local actors.

The protection of human rights and animal welfare both follow the same basic idea. A society shows its strength by how it treats the most vulnerable.

2-0484-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, dragi colegi, eu nu am să mă înscriu în corul lăudătorilor acestei chestiuni cu aderarea Moldovei și Ucrainei la Uniunea Europeană, pentru că eu știam că întotdeauna aceste țări care sunt candidate trebuie să respecte niște criterii. Și criteriul corupției, care este printre primele, nu este deloc respectat. Așa cum știți, probabil Moldova nu mai are premier. Tocmai și-a dat demisia.

De ce și-a dat demisia? În ce context și-a dat demisia? În contextul în care verișoara Maiei Sandu, pseudo președinta acestei pseudo republici... pentru că, de fapt, nu e a noastră Moldova? E parte din România. Mă frapează faptul că nimeni nu spune treaba asta aici, ca și cum ar fi fost normal un pact Ribbentrop-Molotov, de pildă.

Deci ne-am trezit cu verișoara președintei că are salariu de 6000, peste 6000 de euro. Păi noi ajutăm Moldova, noi ducem acolo miliarde pentru reforme și ei își dau salarii de 6000. Dar nu vi se pare (...)

(Președintele a retras cuvântul vorbitorului)
2-0484-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, I will not join the choir of eulogists on this matter of the accession of Moldova and Ukraine to the European Union, because I knew that these candidate countries must always meet certain criteria. And the corruption criterion, which is among the first, is not being met at all. As you probably know, Moldova no longer has a prime minister. They have just resigned.

Why did they resign? In what context did they resign? In the context where the cousin of Maia Sandu, the pseudo-president of this pseudo-republic... because, in fact, isn't Moldova ours? It is part of Romania. I am struck by the fact that no one says this here, as if a Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact, for example, had been normal.

So we woke up to find that the president's cousin has a salary of 6,000, over 6,000 euros. Well, we are helping Moldova, we are taking billions there for reforms and they are giving themselves salaries of 6,000. But doesn't it seem to you (...)

(The President withdrew the speaker's right to speak)
2-0484-0000.factCheck: The claim that EU reform aid was used to pay a €6,000 monthly salary to President Maia Sandu's cousin is misleading; while Anastasia Taburceanu did receive this controversial salary at the state-owned enterprise MoldATSA, it was funded by the company's own air navigation revenues rather than EU aid.

2-0485-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, Moldova je, kao prvo, neovisna država, htio to netko priznati ili ne. I to neovisna država koja se unatoč snažnom ruskom uplitanju i pritisku odlučila za europsku budućnost.

Kada se neke zemlje zapadnog Balkana žale na navodna dvostruka pravila Europske unije, na zastoj u otvaranju nekih poglavlja ili klastera, onda bih im preporučio da pogledaju sve što je Moldova učinila počevši, naravno, od sankcija protiv ruske agresije.

Ja ću ovdje podsjetiti da je Općinski sud u Kišinjevu ustanovio postojanje kampova, na žalost, u Srbiji u entitetu Republika Srpska u Bosni i Hercegovini u kojima se uvježbavalo ljude koji su kasnije trebali u Moldovi potkopavati proeuropsku orijentaciju te zemlje.

Dakako, Moldova ima još puno posla za obaviti, prvenstveno vezano za borbu protiv korupcije, ali njen je napredak očit i stoga Europski parlament mora joj i dalje davati snažnu potporu.
2-0485-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Moldova is, first of all, an independent state, whether someone wants to recognise it or not. And it is an independent state that, despite strong Russian interference and pressure, has chosen a European future.

When some countries of the Western Balkans complain about the alleged double standards of the European Union, about delays in opening certain chapters or clusters, then I would recommend that they look at everything Moldova has done, starting, of course, from sanctions against Russian aggression.

I will remind you here that the Municipal Court in Chișinău established the existence of camps, unfortunately, in Serbia, in the entity of Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where people were trained who were later supposed to undermine the pro-European orientation of that country in Moldova.

Of course, Moldova still has a lot of work to do, primarily related to the fight against corruption, but its progress is obvious and therefore the European Parliament must continue to give it strong support.

2-0486-0000.sourceText:
Г-н Председател, Молдова заслужава категорична и последователна подкрепа от страна на Европейския парламент. Въпреки войната до нейните граници, въпреки хибридните атаки и постоянния външен натиск, страната показва устойчивост и ангажимент към европейския си път.

Европейската перспектива на Молдова трябва да остане надпартиен национален приоритет, основан на демокрация, социална справедливост, върховенство на закона и реални ползи за гражданите. Когато една страна кандидат изпълнява своите ангажименти, Европейският съюз също трябва да изпълни своите. Затова приветствам напредъка на Молдова и призовавам Съвета да даде зелена светлина за следващата стъпка в подготовката и преговорите за членство.

Но подкрепата за Молдова не означава да си затваряме очите за предизвикателствата. Напротив, европейската интеграция изисква реални резултати в съдебната реформа, в борбата с корупцията, в независимостта на институциите и във възстановяването на общественото доверие, особено след оставката на премиера Монтяну. Следващото правителство трябва бързо да върне стабилността, да запази европейския курс и да покаже на гражданите, че реформите не са само изискване на Брюксел, а път към повече сигурност, по-добър живот и по-силна социална защита.

Искам да подчертая и нещо особено важно. Зачитането на правата на малцинствата е основен критерий за всяка страна кандидат. Това включва и българската общност в Тараклия. Всяка административна реформа трябва да гарантира културното и езиково многообразие на общностите в Молдова и тяхното политическо представителство.
2-0486-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Moldova deserves categorical and consistent support from the European Parliament. Despite the war on its borders, despite hybrid attacks and constant external pressure, the country shows resilience and commitment to its European path.

Moldova's European perspective must remain a non-partisan national priority based on democracy, social justice, the rule of law and real benefits for citizens. When a candidate country fulfils its commitments, the European Union must also fulfil its own. Therefore, I welcome Moldova's progress and call on the Council to give the green light for the next step in preparation and membership negotiations.

But support for Moldova does not mean turning a blind eye to the challenges. On the contrary, European integration requires real results in judicial reform, the fight against corruption, the independence of institutions and the restoration of public trust, especially after the resignation of Prime Minister Munteanu. The next government must quickly restore stability, preserve the European course and show citizens that reforms are not just a requirement of Brussels, but a path to more security, a better life and stronger social protection.

I also want to emphasize something particularly important. Respecting the rights of minorities is a fundamental criterion for any candidate country. This includes the Bulgarian community in Taraclia. Any administrative reform must guarantee the cultural and linguistic diversity of the communities in Moldova and their political representation.

2-0487-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, suntem cu toții de acord că locul Moldovei este în Uniunea Europeană. Sunt frații noștri, ai românilor, vorbesc limba română, sunt creștini ortodocși majoritatea și împărtășesc același trecut și aceleași valori cu România, stat membru UE. Când și cum se va face această aderare? Aici este adevărata cheia a acestei dezbateri.

Prima, cea mai rapidă și firească totodată, ar fi soluția germană, despre care eu și colegii mei din partid am tot vorbit. A doua variantă, aderarea propriu-zisă, trebuie făcută pe un calendar propriu, independent de Ucraina. Moldova are propriul ei drum și propria ei viteză de îndeplinire a condițiilor pentru aderare la UE. Deci nu există niciun motiv să o tratăm la pachet cu Ucraina.

În plus, Ucraina este, din păcate, o țară aflată încă în război cu teritoriul disputat, deci nu putem vorbi de aderare efectivă în acest stadiu. Și ar fi nedrept să susținem și Moldova blocată la pachet cu ea. Orice țară care dorește să adere la UE trebuie să îndeplinească fix aceleași condiții ca și antemergători ei, iar din acest punct de vedere trebuie să spunem clar: Moldova se află cu mulți pași înaintea Ucrainei, deci cu mulți pași mai aproape de Uniunea Europeană.
2-0487-0000.englishText:
Mr President, we all agree that Moldova's place is in the European Union. They are our brothers, the brothers of Romanians, they speak the Romanian language, the majority are Orthodox Christians and they share the same past and the same values with Romania, an EU member state. When and how will this accession take place? Here lies the true key to this debate.

The first, quickest and most natural solution would be the German solution, which my party colleagues and I have talked about. The second option, accession proper, must be done on its own timetable, independent of Ukraine. Moldova has its own path and its own speed for fulfilling the conditions for EU accession. So there is no reason to treat it as a package deal with Ukraine.

In addition, Ukraine is unfortunately still a country at war with disputed territory, so we cannot speak of effective accession at this stage. And it would be unfair to keep Moldova blocked as a package with it. Any country that wants to join the EU must meet the exact same conditions as its predecessors, and from this point of view we must say clearly: Moldova is many steps ahead of Ukraine, and therefore many steps closer to the European Union.

2-0488-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, ainsi donc, les négociations d’adhésion s’ouvrent enfin avec la Moldavie: il était temps! Le peuple moldave l’a dit, redit et le répète encore: il se sent européen, il veut entrer dans l’Union européenne. Il a voté en ce sens à plusieurs reprises, en dépit des pressions insensées que la Russie a fait peser sur lui. Manipulation de l’information, achats de voix, oligarques à la botte de Moscou, gangs criminels, pressions économiques: la petite Moldavie a eu droit à tout et a résisté à tout.

On la regarde parfois avec condescendance: on ferait mieux d’en prendre de la graine. Parce que des manipulations de l’information, des groupes de médias étrangers bienveillants vis-à-vis de Vladimir Poutine et des tentatives d’intimidation, eh bien ça ne se passe pas qu’en Moldavie.

Le peuple moldave veut rejoindre l’Union européenne, et ses autorités savent ce qu’elles ont à faire, les réformes qu’elles ont à mener pour y parvenir. Mais nous, est-ce que nous savons ce que nous voulons? Sommes-nous prêts à accueillir de nouveaux membres dans notre Union? J’ai bien peur que nous n’ayons pas encore pris la mesure du monde qui nous entoure.

L’élargissement de l’Union européenne peut être une chance: celle d’échapper à notre encerclement. Mais sa réussite va dépendre aussi de nous.
2-0488-0000.englishText:
Mr President, so accession negotiations are finally opening with Moldova: it was about time! The Moldovan people have said it, repeated it and are saying it again: they feel European, they want to join the European Union. They have voted to that effect on several occasions, despite the insane pressure that Russia has exerted upon them. Information manipulation, vote buying, oligarchs at Moscow's beck and call, criminal gangs, economic pressure: little Moldova has been subjected to it all and has resisted it all.

Sometimes people look down on it with condescension: we would do well to take a leaf out of their book. Because information manipulation, foreign media groups sympathetic to Vladimir Putin and attempts at intimidation do not only happen in Moldova.

The Moldovan people want to join the European Union, and its authorities know what they have to do, the reforms they must carry out to achieve this. But do we, do we know what we want? Are we ready to welcome new members into our Union? I am very much afraid that we have not yet grasped the scale of the world around us.

Enlargement of the European Union can be an opportunity: that of escaping our encirclement. But its success will also depend on us.

2-0489-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, Russia's brutal war of aggression has shown that there are no grey zones on our continent, no place for grey zones. We must therefore continue supporting all enlargement countries who are demonstrating willingness to progress on the path of EU integration.

Moldova has shown a strong determination in the implementation of reforms, in the face of challenging circumstances, despite disinformation campaigns and hybrid attacks from Russia.

While there are still some changes necessary, of course, we cannot allow Moscow to undermine Moldova's European cause.

Russia's actions remind us that enlargement is not a bureaucratic exercise, but one of the EU's most important geopolitical instruments to strengthen stability, security and prosperity across our continent.

Candidate countries must deliver on reforms. At the same time, the EU has to remain a reliable partner.

2-0490-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă comisar, domnule președinte, stimați colegi, programul ambițios al Republicii Moldova pentru a încheia aderarea la sfârșitul anului 2028 trebuie susținut. Este de salutat, dar nu va putea fi pus în aplicare dacă nu îl susținem toți. Și vreau de la bun început să mulțumesc și doamnei comisar, și colegilor care au susținut acest proiect.

Sunt româncă, sunt moldoveancă, cunosc foarte bine Republica Moldova, cunosc cetățenii de acolo, cetățenii își doresc acest lucru și trebuie să-i încurajăm pentru a avea încredere în proiectul Uniunii Europene, pentru că are nevoie administrația de la Chișinău de susținerea populară.

Sigur că nu văd alt drum și trebuie să fim și realiști: Republica Moldova e la graniță, cât de greu este să reziste la atacurile directe, indirecte, fake news-urile și tot ce se întâmplă acolo cu Rusia. Uniunea Europeană este un proiect la care eu, ca româncă, mi-am dorit să fim cu țara mea acolo. De aceea, doamna comisar, Consiliul, Parlamentul trebuie să înțeleagă că Republica Moldova are locul ei în Uniunea Europeană și trebuie să o susținem.

Și mai vreau să adaug un lucru: cred foarte tare că ceea ce acum se întâmplă în Ucraina ține în loc și Republica Moldova. Trebuie să separăm. România și Bulgaria a pățit același lucru cu Schengen. Haideți să fim corecți, obiectivi - în Ucraina nu se pot respecta termenele și jaloanele - și să dăm drumul Moldovei și, la terminarea anului 2028, Republica Moldova să fie în marea familie.
2-0490-0000.englishText:
Madam Commissioner, Mr President, dear colleagues, the ambitious program of the Republic of Moldova to conclude accession by the end of 2028 must be supported. It is to be welcomed, but it will not be able to be implemented if we do not all support it. And I want from the very beginning to thank both the Madam Commissioner and the colleagues who have supported this project.

I am Romanian, I am Moldovan, I know the Republic of Moldova very well, I know the citizens there, the citizens want this and we must encourage them to have confidence in the European Union project, because the Chisinau administration needs popular support.

Of course, I do not see any other path and we must also be realistic: the Republic of Moldova is at the border, how hard it is to resist direct and indirect attacks, fake news and everything that happens there with Russia. The European Union is a project that I, as a Romanian, wanted us to be there with my country. Therefore, Madam Commissioner, the Council, the Parliament must understand that the Republic of Moldova has its place in the European Union and we must support it.

And I also want to add one thing: I strongly believe that what is now happening in Ukraine is also holding back the Republic of Moldova. We must separate them. Romania and Bulgaria experienced the same thing with Schengen. Let us be fair, objective - deadlines and milestones cannot be met in Ukraine - and let us let Moldova go ahead and, by the end of 2028, the Republic of Moldova should be in the great family.

2-0491-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, mă bucur că Republica Moldova a deschis primul capitol de negociere pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană. De acum, datoria noastră este să nu transformăm acest drum european într-o sală de așteptare fără sfârșit. Republica Moldova trebuie evaluată corect. Este firesc ca România să susțină Republica Moldova în parcursul său de aderare la Uniunea Europeană.

Sprijinirea românilor de peste Prut este o datorie istorică și o necesitate strategică. Cu atât mai mult cu cât aproape jumătate din ei sunt și cetățeni ai României. Integrarea sa în Uniunea Europeană reprezintă mai multă stabilitate și mai multă siguranță la frontiera estică a Uniunii. Însă Republica Moldova trebuie să continue să se desprindă de moștenirea sa sovietică, precum și de reflexele trecutului, iar Bruxelles-ul trebuie să-și dovedească deschiderea pentru un rezultat final concret și neîntârziat.

Dacă românii de peste ambele maluri ale Prutului nu s-au putut reunifica precum berlinezii, atunci Republica Moldova și România trebuie să se reunifice măcar prin apartenența lor la Uniunea Europeană.
2-0491-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, I am glad that the Republic of Moldova has opened its first negotiating chapter for accession to the European Union. From now on, our duty is not to turn this European path into an endless waiting room. The Republic of Moldova must be fairly evaluated. It is natural for Romania to support the Republic of Moldova in its European Union accession path.

Supporting the Romanians across the Prut is a historical duty and a strategic necessity. All the more so since almost half of them are also citizens of Romania. Its integration into the European Union represents more stability and more security at the Union's eastern border. However, the Republic of Moldova must continue to break away from its Soviet heritage, as well as from the reflexes of the past, and Brussels must prove its openness to a concrete and prompt final result.

If the Romanians on both banks of the Prut could not reunite like the Berliners, then the Republic of Moldova and Romania must reunite at least through their membership in the European Union.

2-0492-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Mołdawia daje nadzieję tak potrzebną dziś Unii Europejskiej, bo członkostwo Mołdawii w Unii Europejskiej pokazuje, że te starania europejskie to coś więcej niż zabieganie o fundusze, o instytucje. To walka o wartości. I ta droga europejska Mołdawii pokazuje, że można pokonać ruski mir, że można wygrać z ruskimi służbami. Z tym Goliatem Dawid może wygrać prawdą, konsekwencją i determinacją.

Mołdawia jest dla nas wzorcem, w jaki sposób walczyć z oligarchami, którzy próbują destabilizować nasze społeczeństwa, jak walczyć z kłamstwem, ale też jak walczyć z takimi zjawiskami jak kryptowaluty, które nadal w niektórych państwach Unii Europejskiej używane są do niszczenia demokracji, niszczenia Unii Europejskiej. Bierzmy przykład z Mołdawii – małego, ale wielkiego duchem państwa.
2-0492-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Moldova offers the hope so much needed by the European Union today, because Moldova's membership in the European Union shows that these European efforts are something more than just striving for funds, for institutions. It is a fight for values. And this European path of Moldova shows that the "russkiy mir" can be defeated, that one can win against Russian services. Against this Goliath, David can win with truth, consistency and determination.

Moldova is a model for us of how to fight oligarchs who try to destabilize our societies, how to fight lies, and also how to fight phenomena such as cryptocurrencies, which in some European Union member states are still used to destroy democracy, to destroy the European Union. Let us take an example from Moldova – a small state, but great in spirit.

2-0493-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, thank you for the excellent report, Sven Mikser. I cannot stress enough the importance of opening all negotiation clusters for Moldova and Ukraine. Article 49 of the Treaty of European Union clearly states that unanimity is required only for the opening and closing of accession negotiations. But what is the European Council doing? The endless unanimity silos for each chapter are like sand that the Council is throwing in the gears of enlargement.

The situation now is that the Member States are undermining European security, delaying the enlargement process, sabotaging our strategic interests and preventing effective, comprehensive negotiations on all clusters with Moldova. Let us do our best to fulfil our promise to start closing all chapters at the beginning of 2027, as promised.

Dear friends in Moldova and Ukraine, please continue your reforms with the same spirit as before. Please trust us, and we will do our utmost to have you sitting in this Parliament among us in the nearest future. Let's do it!

2-0494-0000.sourceText: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Moldova šiandien demonstruoja įspūdingą europinį pagreitį: užbaigta dvišalė patikra, visi šeši narystės derybų klasteriai jau potencialiai atverti, o dvidešimt keturi iš dvidešimt šešių reformos žingsnių jau įgyvendinti. Matoma akivaizdi pažanga pamatinių vertybių, vidaus rinkos ir išorės santykių srityse. Moldova toliau bando nuosekliai judėti išteklių, žemės ūkio bei sanglaudos kryptimis. Mums, Europos Sąjungai, tai argumentas veikti drąsiai ir atverti derybas dėl narystės, parodant, kad reformos duoda realų politinį rezultatą. Žinoma, Rusijos karinis buvimas Padniestrėje yra tarptautinės teisės pažeidimas ir tiesioginė grėsmė. Rusai privalo besąlygiškai pasitraukti, o mes privalome padėti Moldovai stiprinti atsparumą energetinę nepriklausomybę ir pasitikėjimą europiniu keliu.
2-0494-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues. Moldova is demonstrating impressive European momentum today: bilateral screening has been completed, all six membership negotiation clusters are now potentially open, and twenty-four out of twenty-six reform steps have already been implemented.
Clear progress is visible in the areas of fundamental values, the internal market, and external relations.
Moldova continues to try to move consistently in the directions of resources, agriculture, and cohesion.
For us, the European Union, this is an argument to act boldly and open membership negotiations, showing that reforms yield a real political outcome.
Of course, the Russian military presence in Transnistria is a violation of international law and a direct threat.
The Russians must withdraw unconditionally, and we must help Moldova strengthen its resilience, energy independence, and confidence in the European path.

2-0495-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, doamnelor și domnilor, astăzi nu decidem doar asupra parcursului european al Republicii Moldova. Decidem și cât de credibilă este Uniunea Europeană atunci când un popor își asumă valorile noastre și are curajul să le apere.

Republica Moldova nu cere favoruri. Vine cu reforme, cu sacrificii și cu alegere democratică reafirmate de cetățenii săi. Vine cu demnitate și cu rezistența remarcabilă în fața presiunii și amenințării ruse. De aceea, Republica Moldova nu este doar un stat candidat. Este dovada că proiectul european inspiră, mobilizează și oferă speranțe. Pentru România acest sprijin este o responsabilitate istorică. Pentru Uniunea Europeană, este o chestiune de credibilitate.

Nu putem cere curaj celor care aleg Europa și apoi să-i părăsim. Reformele trebuie să continue în Moldova, iar noi trebuie să răspundem cu un sprijin ferm și consecvent. Astăzi, votul nostru trebuie să fie direct pentru Moldova, cât și pentru Uniunea Europeană unită.
2-0495-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today we are not only deciding on the European path of the Republic of Moldova. We are also deciding how credible the European Union is when a people embraces our values and has the courage to defend them.

The Republic of Moldova is not asking for favors. It comes with reforms, sacrifices, and a democratic choice reaffirmed by its citizens. It comes with dignity and remarkable resistance in the face of Russian pressure and threats. Therefore, the Republic of Moldova is not just a candidate state. It is proof that the European project inspires, mobilizes, and offers hope. For Romania, this support is a historical responsibility. For the European Union, it is a matter of credibility.

We cannot ask for courage from those who choose Europe and then abandon them. Reforms must continue in Moldova, and we must respond with firm and consistent support. Today, our vote must be directly for Moldova, as well as for a united European Union.

2-0496-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Moldau steht erneut an einem Wendepunkt. Die jüngsten politischen Entwicklungen in Chișinău zeigen, wie sensibel die innenpolitische Lage bleibt und wie entscheidend Stabilität, Reformfähigkeit und ein klarer europäischer Kurs jetzt sind.

Gerade vor diesem Hintergrund halte ich diesen Bericht für besonders wichtig. Er zeigt deutlich: Moldau hat trotz enormen äußeren Drucks bemerkenswerte Fortschritte gemacht im EU‑Beitrittsprozess – bei Reformen im Justiz- und Verwaltungsbereich und bei der wirtschaftlichen Annäherung an die Europäische Union.

Aber wir dürfen nicht naiv sein. Moldau steht unter einem anhaltenden hybriden Angriff – Desinformation, Cyberangriffe, Energie-Erpressung und russische Einflussnahme zielen darauf, den europäischen Kurs des Landes zu brechen.

Unsere Antwort muss klar sein: Wir unterstützen Moldau politisch, finanziell und sicherheitspolitisch. Die Beitrittsverhandlungen müssen auf Leistung beruhen, nicht auf Blockaden. Wer Reformen liefert, muss Fortschritt sehen. Moldaus europäische Zukunft ist nicht nur eine moldauische Frage, sie ist eine Frage der Glaubwürdigkeit und Sicherheit Europas.
2-0496-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! Moldova is once again at a turning point. Recent political developments in Chișinău show how sensitive the domestic political situation remains and how crucial stability, the capacity for reform and a clear European course are now.

It is precisely against this background that I consider this report to be particularly important. It clearly shows that Moldova, despite enormous external pressure, has made remarkable progress in the EU accession process – with reforms in the judiciary and administration and in economic rapprochement with the European Union.

But we must not be naive. Moldova is under a sustained hybrid attack – disinformation, cyberattacks, energy blackmail and Russian influence are aimed at breaking the country's European course.

Our response must be clear: we support Moldova politically, financially and in terms of security policy. Accession negotiations must be based on merit, not on blockages. Whoever delivers reforms must see progress. Moldova's European future is not just a Moldovan question, it is a question of Europe's credibility and security.

2-0497-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Mołdawia jest wyjątkowym krajem kandydatem. I chciałbym bardzo serdecznie podziękować również Pani, Pani Komisarz, że od samego początku stawia Pani na Mołdawię – na kraj, który również według tego przedstawionego sprawozdania ma największe postępy, jeśli chodzi o przygotowania do członkostwa. 2-0497-0000.englishText:

2-0499-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the 2025 report on Moldova sends a clear message: despite an extremely challenging geopolitical and economic environment, Moldova continues to move forward on its European path.

The progress is concrete. Moldova is replacing its Soviet-era standards with European ones. These are not merely technical changes, but tangible steps, improving quality, safety and protection for Moldovan citizens. We also see progress in consumer protection. Moldova has made public services more accessible and effective.

Notably, Moldova has consistently cooperated on foreign policy issues, and aligns with the EU's common foreign and security policy positions. 2-0500-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, no entiendo en absoluto qué hacéis algunos diputados —casi todos españoles— aplaudiendo la ampliación de la Unión Europea antes en el debate anterior de Ucrania y ahora en el de Moldavia.

Que lo hagan los alemanes lo puedo entender, pero nosotros, los españoles, ¿no hemos leído aquí el estudio interno filtrado del propio Consejo de la Unión Europea en 2023, en el que se señala que España va a ser el único país que va a pasar de cobrar a pagar? ¿Saben ustedes lo que significan 3 000 millones de euros de la PAC menos para un agricultor en España, en Rumanía, en Portugal o en Italia?

¿Saben lo que significa meter al país más pobre de Europa, que es Moldavia, con 2,4 millones de habitantes —lo sé porque he estado en Moldavia como voluntario, con refugiados de Moldavia— y con una corrupción sistémica del 12 % del PIB? Hablamos de meter ahora mismo a un territorio que tiene 1 500 soldados rusos dentro, en Transnistria, con un referéndum europeo, por cierto, que sacó un 50,4 %, y gracias al voto de la diáspora, porque uno de cada tres moldavos viven fuera de su país.

2-0500-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I completely fail to understand what some MEPs—almost all of them Spanish—are doing applauding the enlargement of the European Union, earlier in the debate on Ukraine and now in the one on Moldova.

That the Germans do it, I can understand, but we Spaniards, have we not read the leaked internal study by the Council of the European Union itself from 2023, which indicates that Spain is going to be the only country that will go from being a net recipient to a net contributor? Do you know what 3 billion euros less in CAP funding means for a farmer in Spain, in Romania, in Portugal or in Italy?

Do you know what it means to bring in the poorest country in Europe, which is Moldova, with 2.4 million inhabitants—I know because I have been to Moldova as a volunteer, with refugees from Moldova—and with a systemic corruption of 12% of GDP? We are talking about bringing in right now a territory that has 1,500 Russian soldiers inside it, in Transnistria, with a European referendum, by the way, that yielded 50.4%, and thanks to the diaspora's vote, because one in three Moldovans live outside their country.

Anyway, I understand that some do, but for Spanish MEPs to support this seems surreal to me.

2-0502-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable members of the European Parliament, it's really good to see that Moldova has so many supporters here in the European Parliament. Some of them are very passionate. It deserves recognition for that progress and our continued support to move forward on its path to EU membership. We have organised the biggest investment conference to date at the beginning of June in Chişinău and the companies from the Member States are already coming. This is the only way to prosperity. So, they have to do the reforms, the investors will come, and then we can speak about the prosperity.

Regarding the question of when Moldova will be able to become a member of the EU: when all the reforms will be done, meaning Moldova has to deliver, but we have to deliver too. I have heard this today many times. So, it is also our responsibility that this will happen as soon as possible. I used to say that Moldova is the best student in my class. Since the last successful way on the reforms, I am saying that Moldova is the best performer in my class.

2-0503-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, first of all, I would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs. It was really intellectually stimulating and a very constructive effort that produced this report. I think that all the pro-European groups who negotiated the report were brought together by a great sense of unity of purpose, but also a sense of urgency. I would also like to thank Commissioner Kos for her personal dedication and commitment to supporting, in every possible way, Moldova's very legitimate European aspirations. And I would like to thank all the colleagues for an extremely constructive debate here.

I hope that the report that we are going to be voting on tomorrow – and also tonight's debate – help us to send a very clear message to the Moldovan people and the Moldovan Government: a message of support and solidarity, but also a message of what our expectations are as to the next steps to be taken in this reform path.

I also hope that the report and the debates send a very clear message to our colleagues, the political leaders in our Member State capitals, who periodically meet around the Council table: a message that we expect them to live up to our end of the bargain, as I said, and to actually act with the same sense of urgency, because it is absolutely clear that the Russian pressure on Moldova will not dissipate until the successful completion of this process.
