2-0507-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, ovogodišnje izvješće odražava stvarnost u Srbiji u jednom od ključnih razdoblja njezine novije povijesti. Gotovo da nema poglavlja u kojem napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji nije ocijenjen kao ograničen ili nepostojeći.

I naša se misija u Beogradu početkom godine odvijala u neobično teškim okolnostima. Zastupnici su bili izloženi verbalnim napadima predstavnika vlasti i provladinih medija, a visoki dužnosnici Srbije više su puta iznosili neutemeljene tvrdnje da Europska unija i neke njezine države članice potiču ili podržavaju tzv. obojenu revoluciju u Srbiji.

Uglavnom, napredak Srbije u ostvarivanju reformi važnima za napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji značajno se usporio. U nekoliko ključnih područja, a posebno u vladavini prava, došlo je i do nazadovanja.

To se reflektira i preko ograničenog napretka u dijalogu Beograda i Prištine, kontinuiranog manjka usklađivanja sa zajedničkom vanjskom i sigurnosnom politikom, nedostatka istinske političke predanosti reformama, agresivne retorike prema Europskoj uniji, pogoršanja uvjeta za rad slobodnih medija i organizacija civilnog društva. Bilježi se kontinuirani neuspjeh u sveobuhvatnoj provedbi preporuka u izbornoj reformi jer i dalje postoji problem s regulatornim tijelom i s biračkim spiskom.

Dok vlasti u Srbiji i dalje predstavljaju članstvo u Europskoj uniji kao svoj strateški cilj, postupci njenog političkog vodstva često to ne potvrđuju. Zadnje izvješće Europske komisije također ukazuje na kontinuirano demokratsko nazadovanje, nedovoljan napredak u reformama vladavine prava i sve veći jaz između izrečenih europskih težnji Srbije i njezine političke prakse. Nažalost, ne vidimo ni napredak u istrazi o urušavanju nadstrešnice željezničkog kolodvora u Novom Sadu, što je potaknulo masovno nezadovoljstvo građana.

Zbog neispunjenih obveza ili ozbiljnog nedostatka rezultata, osobito u području vladavine prava, izvješće poziva Komisiju da zaustavi buduće isplate u okviru Instrumenta za reforme i rast za zapadni Balkan. Također se zalažem za reprogramiranje postojećih i budućih sredstava Europske unije kako bi se ojačala podrška reformi pravosuđa, naporima u borbi protiv korupcije, neovisnim medijima, organizacijama civilnog društva i neovisnom kulturnom sektoru.

Podsjetio bih kako je politika stabilokracije i gledanja kroz prste autokratima u posljednjih desetak godina stimulirala postojeće loše prilike na dobrom dijelu zapadnog Balkana.

Zato se ne moramo pitati kako bi danas prošao referendum o ulasku Srbije u Europsku uniju, upravo zbog niske podrške članstvu. Ima puno razloga zašto je ta podrška najniža u regiji, budući da se protueuropska retorika koristi godinama. Međutim, svakako je važan element za gubitak povjerenja u Europsku uniju i njezine institucije i toleriranje lažnog proeuropskog narativa vlasti u Beogradu svih proteklih godina.

Zbog toga sam uvjeren da je promašeno inzistiranje na otvaranju pregovaračkog klastera 3, čime bi se obnovili pregovori o pristupanju Srbije Europskoj uniji nakon četiri godine zastoja. Ta je stagnacija imala svoje jasne i opravdane razloge, baš kao što ih pokretanje nema ni danas.

Izvješće reflektira kontinuirano urušavanje demokratskih standarda u Srbiji. Zar treba nagraditi neusklađenost s europskom vanjskom politikom koja je tek na 63 posto, unatoč tome što druge države kandidatkinje nemaju problem potpunog usklađivanja? Uz jačanje veza s Kinom i Rusijom, imamo i slučaj da ministar u vladi ide u posjet Iranu, a nemojmo zaboraviti kako je predsjednica srpskog parlamenta svojedobno otišla i na inauguraciju Nicolasa Madura.

Osim toga, nemoguće je ne reagirati na pokušaje iz Beograda da se ugrozi održavanje samita Europske unije zapadnog Balkana nedavno u Crnoj Gori. Sve to pokazuje da odnosi Europske unije i Srbije ne mogu biti tek tako resetirani.

Izuzetno veliki problem je i stanje medija. Upravo se odvija proces preuzimanja i ono malo preostalih slobodnih medija koji lako mogu biti dovedeni u ovisnost od vlasti koja je dokazala da ne tolerira nikakvu kritiku.

(Predsjedavajući je govorniku oduzeo riječ)
2-0507-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, this year's report reflects the reality in Serbia during one of the most crucial periods of its recent history. There is hardly any chapter in which progress towards European Union membership has not been assessed as limited or non-existent.

Our mission in Belgrade at the beginning of the year also took place in unusually difficult circumstances. MPs were subjected to verbal attacks by government representatives and pro-government media, and high-ranking Serbian officials repeatedly made baseless claims that the European Union and some of its member states were instigating or supporting a so-called colored revolution in Serbia.

Overall, Serbia's progress in implementing reforms important for advancing towards European Union membership has slowed down significantly. In several key areas, particularly in the rule of law, there has even been backsliding.

This is also reflected in the limited progress in the dialogue between Belgrade and Pristina, the continuous lack of alignment with the Common Foreign and Security Policy, the lack of genuine political commitment to reforms, aggressive rhetoric towards the European Union, and the deterioration of working conditions for free media and civil society organizations. A continuous failure is noted in the comprehensive implementation of recommendations on electoral reform, as problems with the regulatory body and the voter registry still persist.

While the authorities in Serbia continue to present European Union membership as their strategic goal, the actions of its political leadership often fail to confirm this. The European Commission's latest report also points to continued democratic backsliding, insufficient progress in rule of law reforms, and a widening gap between Serbia's stated European aspirations and its political practice. Unfortunately, we also see no progress in the investigation into the collapse of the railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which sparked massive citizens' dissatisfaction.

Due to unfulfilled obligations or a serious lack of results, particularly in the area of the rule of law, the report calls on the Commission to halt future disbursements under the Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans. I also advocate for the reprogramming of existing and future European Union funds to strengthen support for judicial reform, anti-corruption efforts, independent media, civil society organizations, and the independent cultural sector.

I would recall that the policy of stabilocracy and turning a blind eye to autocrats over the past decade or so has stimulated the existing poor conditions across a large part of the Western Balkans.

Therefore, we do not need to ask how a referendum on Serbia's entry into the European Union would fare today, precisely because of low support for membership. There are many reasons why this support is the lowest in the region, given that anti-European rhetoric has been used for years. However, an important element in the loss of trust in the European Union and its institutions is certainly the tolerance of the fake pro-European narrative of the authorities in Belgrade over all these past years.

For this reason, I am convinced that the insistence on opening negotiating cluster 3 is misguided, which would resume Serbia's accession negotiations with the European Union after four years of stagnation. That stagnation had its clear and justified reasons, just as resuming them has none today.

The report reflects the continuous erosion of democratic standards in Serbia. Should we reward the lack of alignment with European foreign policy, which is at only 63 percent, despite the fact that other candidate countries have no problem with full alignment? Along with the strengthening of ties with China and Russia, we also have a case of a government minister visiting Iran, and let us not forget how the speaker of the Serbian parliament once even attended the inauguration of Nicolas Maduro.

In addition, it is impossible not to react to attempts from Belgrade to jeopardize the holding of the European Union-Western Balkans summit recently in Montenegro. All of this shows that relations between the European Union and Serbia cannot simply be reset just like that.

The state of the media is also an extremely major problem. The process of taking over what little remains of the free media is currently underway, which can easily be brought into dependence on a government that has proven it does not tolerate any criticism.

(The President cut off the speaker's microphone)

2-0508-0000.sourceText: Under the new approach, I have to be stricter – even with the rapporteurs and Commissioners. That's to be fair.

2-0509-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, dear rapporteur Tonino Picula, thank you for your comprehensive report and for your work on Serbia. The Commission appreciates the opportunity for a separate debate on Serbia.

Serbia is an important partner in the region, with a clear EU-accession perspective. The European Commission therefore continues encouraging Serbia to seize the current opportunity to advance towards membership.

At the EU-Western Balkans Summit, we heard clear commitments from the Serbian leadership that the EU path is their strategic priority. We now need to see Serbia demonstrate its strategic commitments, address the EU's concerns and continue to deliver on the much-needed reforms.

As said many times, reforms on the rule of law, and respect for democratic principles and freedoms, will remain essential for Serbia's progress on its EU path. Two weeks ago, the Serbian Parliament took an important step in the right direction to correct the judicial laws adopted in January. This helps starting rebuilding the trust.

Serbia also made tangible progress in addressing key audit recommendations by revising legislation relevant for the electoral framework. In May, amendments to four election-related laws, among others, on the election of the Members of Parliament and on the election of the president, were adopted.

Two particularly important and substantial laws that concern the financing of political activities and the prevention of corruption are currently under preparation, meaning still to be done.

The recent invitation to OSCE/ODIHR to conduct the usual needs assessment mission is an important step to ensure, in a timely manner, a fully-fledged international election observation mission ahead of the next elections.

We now need to see Serbia advancing further on the electoral reform, in line with ODIHR recommendations, in a transparent and inclusive manner – strengthening media freedom and pluralism; ensuring respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, including freedom of peaceful assembly and academic freedom; and an enabling environment for civil society.

Recent developments on the formation of the so-called REM Council have been encouraging, and we hope that this regulatory body can start its important work soon. This is a long-awaited step.

Alignment with our EU objectives extends beyond internal policies to our common foreign and security policy. Serbia's European past therefore requires clear strategic choices. This also needs to be reflected in a consistent and high alignment with the Union's common foreign and security policy.

A credible European trajectory also means a commitment to regional stability, to normalisation of relations with Kosovo, and to a shared understanding of the security challenges facing our continent. It means tackling disinformation and abstaining from hostile political rhetoric, including against the EU, its institutions and honourable Members of this Parliament.

Serbia's commitment to the EU path and its political will to implement the required reforms also have to be strengthened via communication and concrete actions – including meaningful engagement on EU reforms – with the relevant stakeholders, including civil society organisations, to overcome the current deep divisions in Serbian society.

Dear honourable Members, with other countries advancing in the accession process, we do not want to see Serbia fall behind. This is why, in light of the recent – some positive – developments, the Commission renewed its recommendation to the Council to open Cluster 3 in the accession negotiations with Serbia.

The Commission will also continue to incentivise further reform progress for the benefit of all Serbian citizens and the whole Serbian society.

2-0510-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, colleagues, EU enlargement has regained its political importance. This is something that, in general, has benefited countries, but not in the case of Serbia. President Vučić made clear that Serbia can implement EU‑related reforms and has appointed a very professional negotiating operational team. But he also said that Serbia will not turn its back on Russia. Serbia does not perceive itself as part of the West, but pursues a non‑aligned policy, which is deeply rooted in society: it existed before Vučić and will probably continue after him.

While the EU should acknowledge this decision, Serbia needs to understand that it won't make progress towards EU membership if it keeps friendly relations with the EU's adversaries. Sometimes driven by a transactional logic, some key Member States have attempted to change Belgrade's policy. However, they have so far failed – sometimes increasing the level of frustration on all sides.

At the same time, Parliament's criticism, while honest and principled, has had little impact so far on changing the course of events. So what can be done? A realistic approach should envisage cooperation and partial and gradual integration in those areas of mutual benefit – from border management, trade, finance, energy and transport. A pragmatic but firm approach can bring results. We saw it with the repeal of the mortgage laws, with better cooperation on electoral reform, even with better cooperation with the Croatian National Council.

Of course, this should be continued and expanded to the benefit of both sides, but we should also be honest with each other: Serbia will not align with the EU any time soon. There is no political will for it, neither in the government nor in the opposition. To that situation, our response should not be appeasement or isolation, but rather a realistic engagement: firm on values and pragmatic on promoting our interests, without false promises about progress in the negotiations, but with a clear vision of a working relationship that serves the cause of peace in...

(The President cut off the speaker)

2-0511-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I think it is important to say it again: we all want to see Serbia and especially the Serbian citizens in the European Union.

But there is one problem on this way, and the problem has a name. It's Aleksandar Vučić – because under his presidency, the country is going backwards – going backwards on democracy, on media freedom, on transparency, growing corruption is on the rise, the ministers attending the funeral in Iran. Also, Serbia and Belgrade sometimes is seen as a Moscow proxy. I think these are arguments enough also to discuss seriously to freeze further EU money.

Secondly, I think we have to express very clearly here from the European Parliament 100 % solidarity with the students movement. Every week, ten thousands are going on the street, risking a lot of their life, risking their studies and their future, but fighting for a better, a European future. And they have a simple demand, which is a clear, functioning, modern Serbian State. While they are not waving European flags, I think they expect that the European Union is supporting these students' demands: to have a modern, functional, clean Serbian State.

The last point: Vučić now called for new elections. Nobody knows exactly when. It seems to be another trick of this magician of debate. But we have to say, before it comes to election, we need an electoral law which is fulfilling the need for clear and fair elections. We need that the OSCE or the European Parliament recommendations are implemented, and also we need a clear and fair voter registration process. Otherwise, the elections will result in the same result like the old elections.

2-0512-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Mindnyájan egyetérthetünk abban, hogy Szerbia előtt ma komoly kihívások állnak. Folytatni kell a reformokat, erősíteni kell a társadalmi párbeszédet, és előre kell vinni az európai integrációs folyamatot. Ugyanakkor fontos, hogy a mai vitát a jelenlegi európai politikai környezetben értelmezzük. Az elmúlt hetekben világos üzenetet kaptunk: az Európai Unió stratégiai prioritásként tekint a bővítésre. Montenegró újabb tárgyalási fejezeteket zár le. Ukrajna és Moldova megnyitotta első tárgyalási klaszterét. Tegnap az Európai Bizottság egyértelművé tette, hogy támogatja a harmadik tárgyalási klaszter júliusi megnyitását Szerbia számára, mert megítélése szerint ennek feltételei teljesültek. Ez egy kedvező politikai pillanat, amelyet sem Szerbiának, sem az Európai Uniónak nem szabad elszalasztania.

A hiányosságokat meg kell nevezni, de ugyanolyan fontos elismerni azokat az eredményeket is, amelyek megszülettek. Az elmúlt hónapokban Szerbia 23 kulcsfontosságú törvényt fogadott el, köztük uniós jogharmonizációs, igazságügyi és választási reformokat. A szerb parlament ezen a héten további, az ODIR ajánlásait, valamint a 23/24-es tárgyalási fejezetet érintő jogszabályokat tárgyal. Májusban a kormány elfogadta a kisebbségi cselekvési tervet is. Sajnálatos módon a jelentés hangvétele nem tükrözi ezt a kiegyensúlyozott megközelítést. Szinte kizárólag a hiányosságokra összpontosít, miközben a reformok és az elért eredmények csak elvétve jelennek meg benne.

Ha meg is jelenik benne dicséret, újabb bírálatok relativizálják az elismerést. A hiteles és érdemalapú bővítési politika nem csak a hiányosságok feltárását, hanem a reformok eredményeinek elismerését is megköveteli. Csak így őrizhetjük meg a bővítési politika hitelességét, ami Szerbia, a Nyugat-Balkán és az Európai Unió közös érdekét szolgálja.
2-0512-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! We can all agree that serious challenges lie ahead for Serbia today. Reforms must be continued, social dialogue must be strengthened, and the European integration process must be moved forward. At the same time, it is important that we interpret today's debate within the current European political environment. In recent weeks, we have received a clear message: the European Union views enlargement as a strategic priority. Montenegro is closing further negotiating chapters. Ukraine and Moldova have opened their first negotiating cluster. Yesterday, the European Commission made it clear that it supports the opening of the third negotiating cluster for Serbia in July, because in its assessment, the conditions for this have been met. This is a favorable political moment that neither Serbia nor the European Union should miss.

Shortcomings must be named, but it is equally important to acknowledge the results that have been achieved. In recent months, Serbia has adopted 23 key laws, including EU legal harmonization, judicial, and electoral reforms. This week, the Serbian parliament is debating further legislation concerning the ODIHR recommendations, as well as negotiating chapters 23 and 24. In May, the government also adopted the minority action plan. Unfortunately, the tone of the report does not reflect this balanced approach. It focuses almost exclusively on shortcomings, while reforms and achieved results appear only sparsely.

Even when praise does appear in it, further criticisms relativize the recognition. A credible and merit-based enlargement policy requires not only uncovering shortcomings, but also recognizing the results of reforms. Only in this way can we preserve the credibility of the enlargement policy, which serves the common interest of Serbia, the Western Balkans, and the European Union.

2-0513-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, aderarea Serbiei la Uniunea Europeană trebuie să însemne reforme reale, stat de drept și respect deplin pentru minoritățile naționale. Este necesar ca Serbia să trateze drepturile românilor de pe teritoriul său cu seriozitate, fără atribuirea de identități artificiale precum vlahi. Românii sunt români, oriunde ar fi.

Totodată, trebuie să vedem relații de bună vecinătate prin fapte și aici mă refer la proiectul Porților de Fier III de pe Dunăre, pentru că vorbim despre un fluviu internațional, nu despre proprietatea exclusivă a unui stat. De aceea, orice proiect major care poate afecta regimul apelor, securitatea energetică, echilibrul ecologic sau agricultura trebuie discutat transparent cu vecinii, înainte de a deveni o problemă politică.

Integrarea europeană înseamnă încredere, iar încrederea se construiește prin transparență, cooperare și respect reciproc.
2-0513-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, Serbia's accession to the European Union must mean real reforms, the rule of law and full respect for national minorities. It is necessary for Serbia to treat the rights of Romanians on its territory with seriousness, without assigning artificial identities such as Vlachs. Romanians are Romanians, wherever they may be.

At the same time, we must see good neighbourly relations through deeds, and here I am referring to the Iron Gates III project on the Danube, because we are talking about an international river, not the exclusive property of one state. Therefore, any major project that may affect the water regime, energy security, ecological balance or agriculture must be discussed transparently with neighbours, before it becomes a political issue.

European integration means trust, and trust is built through transparency, cooperation and mutual respect.

2-0514-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, I admire the young Serbian people. They are very brave; they go on the street; they fight for a life in freedom. And then they listen to the Commission, and the Commission says, 'we want to open Cluster 3, we want to continue the process'. No! Right now it's not the moment to continue the process because there is a backlash.

There are no reforms, as I hear now. On the contrary, what does Mr Vučić say? He cannot leave power. He takes Putin as a role model. He says: 'what's fine for Putin is now fine for me, so I want to be again the Prime Minister and not the President'. Here, you see, it's not about democracy; it's not about freedom. But it's our job to say to the Serbian people: 'we are on your side'. The Serbians are Europeans like us; the Serbians should be members of the European Union. But autocracy has no place here.

So I think, yes, Commissioner, you said there should be observation of the elections, but there also should be more than only observation during the elections. We need a long observation. We need contact with the opposition, which is also here, with the students. Serbia: yes! Autocracy: no!

2-0515-0000.sourceText:
Gospod predsednik, spoštovani! Evropski parlament ni sovražnik srbskega naroda. Prav tako Evropski parlament ni ovira Srbije na poti k Evropski uniji. Je pa Evropski parlament neomajni podpornik demokracije ter vseh tistih, ki se zanjo borijo.

Svoboda medijev, svoboda izražanja, vladavina prava, spoštovanje drugače mislečih in boj proti korupciji žal nimajo domovinske pravice v Srbiji.

Ker je najprej oblast odgovorna za zaščito demokracije, Evropski parlament pošilja jasno sporočilo: „Ne, nismo zadovoljni s stanjem demokracije in bomo vztrajno zahtevali izpolnjevanje vseh temeljnih vrednot demokracije v Srbiji“.

Srbija si zasluži poštene in svobodne volitve čim prej. Da bo to mogoče, je treba izpeljati reforme, zato poziv Evropski komisiji: „Prišel je čas dejanj nosilcev oblasti in ne odpuščanja“.
2-0515-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen! The European Parliament is not the enemy of the Serbian people. Nor is the European Parliament an obstacle to Serbia on its path to the European Union. However, the European Parliament is an unwavering supporter of democracy and of all those who fight for it.

Media freedom, freedom of expression, the rule of law, respect for those who think differently and the fight against corruption unfortunately have no right of citizenship in Serbia.

Since those in power are primarily responsible for protecting democracy, the European Parliament is sending a clear message: "No, we are not satisfied with the state of democracy and we will persistently demand the fulfillment of all fundamental democratic values in Serbia".

Serbia deserves fair and free elections as soon as possible. To make this possible, reforms must be carried out, hence the call to the European Commission: "The time has come for action by those in power and not for forgiveness".

2-0516-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Serbien står inför ett verkligt vägskäl. På ena sidan Vučićs auktoritära högerregering som aktivt förtrycker oppositionen – ett styre i grunden präglat av korruption och maktmissbruk. Vi ser hur rättsstaten undergrävs. Vi ser hur medias frihet inskränks.

På den andra sidan finns en av Europas mest dynamiska, intressanta och välorganiserade demokratirörelser. De serbiska studenterna har skapat någonting unikt, en gräsrotsrörelse, demokratisk från grunden, som utmanar makten genom ständiga nytänkande, demokratiska protester. De bär fröet till en bättre framtid för Serbien.

Vår uppgift är väldigt tydlig: Det är att göra allt vi kan för ett rättvist val. När det gäller vallagen, när det gäller registreringen av väljare och inte minst när det gäller genomförandet. Det är vårt ansvar.
2-0516-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Serbia is facing a real crossroads. On one side, Vučić's authoritarian right-wing government, which is actively suppressing the opposition – a rule fundamentally characterized by corruption and abuse of power. We see how the rule of law is being undermined. We see how freedom of the media is being restricted.

On the other side is one of Europe's most dynamic, interesting, and well-organized pro-democracy movements. The Serbian students have created something unique, a grassroots movement, democratic from the ground up, that challenges power through constantly innovative, democratic protests. They carry the seed of a better future for Serbia.

Our task is very clear: It is to do everything we can for a fair election. When it comes to the electoral law, when it comes to the registration of voters, and not least when it comes to the implementation. That is our responsibility.

2-0517-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Gestern hat Lars Klingbeil in Berlin den Bundeshaushalt für 2027 vorgestellt: 200 Milliarden Euro neue Schulden; der deutsche Staat ist nur noch auf Pump finanzierbar. Während Deutschland pleite geht, wollen Sie hier immer mehr Mitglieder in die Europäische Union aufnehmen. Die Konrad‑Adenauer‑Stiftung der CDU schätzt, dass der Beitritt Serbiens 3 Milliarden Euro kosten wird, der gesamte Westbalkan 7 Milliarden Euro im Jahr. Deutsche Steuerzahler werden ein Viertel der Kosten schultern müssen, also etwa 2 Milliarden Euro – das ist ungefähr der Betrag, den die Bundesregierung bei pflegenden Angehörigen einsparen möchte. Mit anderen Worten: Deutsche, die ihre Eltern pflegen, bekommen die Rente gekürzt, damit CDU und SPD ihre Steuergelder auf dem Balkan verjubeln können. Ich wundere mich, dass es überhaupt noch Wähler gibt, die diesen Parteien ihre Stimmen geben.

Seit zwei Jahren gehen die Serben jetzt auf die Straße wegen der Korruption in ihrem Land. Der serbische Präsident hat deshalb seinen Rücktritt erklärt, weil er im Unterschied zu deutschen Politikern bereit ist, Verantwortung für die Fehler seiner Regierung zu übernehmen. Ich finde das vorbildlich; Ursula von der Leyen oder Friedrich Merz sollten sich daran ein Beispiel nehmen und es ihm gleichtun.

Wir wollen eine privilegierte Partnerschaft mit Belgrad. Bevor wir aber mit deutschen Steuergeldern den Balkan sanieren, müssen wir erst einmal Deutschland wieder aufbauen.
2-0517-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Yesterday in Berlin, Lars Klingbeil presented the 2027 federal budget: 200 billion euros in new debt; the German state can now only be financed on credit. While Germany is going bankrupt, you want to admit more and more members into the European Union here. The CDU's Konrad Adenauer Foundation estimates that Serbia's accession will cost 3 billion euros, and the entire Western Balkans 7 billion euros a year. German taxpayers will have to shoulder a quarter of the costs, or about 2 billion euros – which is roughly the amount the federal government wants to save from family caregivers. In other words, Germans who care for their parents will have their pensions cut so that the CDU and SPD can squander their tax money in the Balkans. I am surprised that there are still voters who give their votes to these parties.

For two years now, Serbians have been taking to the streets because of corruption in their country. The Serbian president has therefore announced his resignation because, unlike German politicians, he is willing to take responsibility for his government's mistakes. I find that exemplary; Ursula von der Leyen or Friedrich Merz should take an example from him and do the same.

We want a privileged partnership with Belgrade. But before we rebuild the Balkans with German tax money, we must first rebuild Germany.

2-0518-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Mr Brandstätter, dear Helmut, indeed, the election observation is not enough. That's why, for any new elections, we expect them to take place under conditions which ensure free and fair elections, in accordance with the European and international standards.

So the electoral process requires further tangible improvement and reforms. For this, Serbia should build on the first positive steps taken to address concerns about the integrity of the electoral register and the electoral legislation. But work still needs to be done.

So progress on Serbia's path is in the interest of the EU, and when we speak about supporting Serbia, we speak about supporting Serbian citizens.

2-0519-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, naravno, zahvaljujem svima na doprinosu u večerašnjoj raspravi, a pogotovo kolegama izvjestiteljima iz sjene na odličnoj suradnji.

Vjerujem da su današnju raspravu pratili ne samo građani Europske unije, već, prije svega, i građani Srbije. Vjerujem i da građani Srbije žele slobodne i poštene izbore i priliku da grade bolju europsku budućnost, ali nakon godina demokratskog nazadovanja Europska unija ne smije nagraditi srpsku vlast napretkom na pristupnom putu na temelju kvazi reformi.

Srbija je najveća zemlja na zapadnom Balkanu s najvećim kapacitetom za napredak na putu prema članstvu u Europsku uniju. Međutim, umjesto otvaranja i zatvaranja pregovaračkih poglavlja, srpska vlada samo otvara nove dileme i nove napetosti prema susjedima.

Ne možemo govoriti o napretku u dijalogu s Kosovom ako se ne privedu odgovorni za teroristički napad u Banjskoj. Ne možemo govoriti o iskoraku u vladavini prava ako se pokušava ispravljati nešto što je prvobitno urađeno potpuno pogrešno jer ti Mrdićevi zakoni, zapravo Vučićevi zakoni, nisu ni trebali biti usvojeni.

Mi kao Europski parlament moramo biti čvrsti u svojoj predanosti poštivanju vrijednosti i pravila. Ne možemo odšutjeti nazadovanje u vladavini prava, eroziji demokratskih standarda i destruktivnom utjecaju na stabilnost regije.

Ako vlasti u Srbiji žele napredovati na svom putu prema Europskoj uniji, moraju donijeti jasan strateški izbor, napraviti ključne reforme te se u potpunosti uskladiti s vanjskom sigurnosnom politikom Europske unije i sankcijama Europske unije prema Rusiji.
2-0519-0000.englishText:
Mr President, of course, I thank everyone for their contribution to tonight's debate, and especially the shadow rapporteurs for their excellent cooperation.

I believe that today's debate was followed not only by the citizens of the European Union, but, above all, by the citizens of Serbia. I also believe that the citizens of Serbia want free and fair elections and an opportunity to build a better European future, but after years of democratic backsliding, the European Union must not reward the Serbian authorities with progress on their accession path based on quasi-reforms.

Serbia is the largest country in the Western Balkans with the greatest capacity for progress on the path towards EU membership. However, instead of opening and closing negotiating chapters, the Serbian government is only opening new dilemmas and new tensions towards its neighbours.

We cannot talk about progress in the dialogue with Kosovo if those responsible for the terrorist attack in Banjska are not brought to justice. We cannot talk about a step forward in the rule of law if an attempt is made to correct something that was originally done completely wrong, because those Mrdić laws, or rather Vučić's laws, should not have been adopted in the first place.

We as the European Parliament must be firm in our commitment to respecting values and rules. We cannot stay silent about the backsliding in the rule of law, the erosion of democratic standards and the destructive impact on the stability of the region.

If the authorities in Serbia want to progress on their path towards the European Union, they must make a clear strategic choice, carry out key reforms and fully align with the European Union's common security policy and the European Union's sanctions against Russia.

2-0520-0000.sourceText: Rozprava k tomuto bodu sa týmto skončila a hlasovanie sa uskutoční zajtra.
2-0520-0000.englishText: The debate on this item is now closed and the vote will take place tomorrow.

2-0520-5000.sourceText:
Az Európai Parlament Szerbiáról szóló éves jelentése minden korábbinál kritikusabb és elfogultabb.

A jelentés semmilyen reformtevékenységet és eddigi eredményt nem ismer el és egyoldalú, politikailag motivált megközelítést alkalmaz. Ez a hozzáállás az Unió részéről sajnos egyre jellemzőbb a nyugat-balkáni országok és különösen Szerbia esetében, ez pedig lépten-nyomon gyengíti az Európai Unió hitelességét a térségben.

Ez a tendencia azért is aggasztó, mert Szerbia kulcsország a Nyugat-Balkán stabilitása szempontjából, az Uniónak pedig kiegyensúlyozott, felelős és partneri megközelítésre lenne szüksége. A közös cél a térség stabilitásának megőrzése, amelyhez csak egy hiteles, objektív és az eredményeket is elismerő uniós hozzáállás vezethet.

A most tárgyalt jelentés patrióta felelőseként a szöveget kiegyensúlyozatlannak látom. Kétségtelen, hogy számos területen van még mit teljesítenie az országnak, de értékelni kellene a szerb kormány európai elköteleződését és eddig tett erőfeszítéseit az energiapolitika, a családpolitika, a vízumpolitika és a kisebbségpolitika területén. A szöveg ehelyett a hiányosságok bemutatására koncentrál és súlyosan igazságtalan ideológiai torzításokat tartalmaz. A bővítéspolitikában nincs helye kettős mércének, mégis az aktuálpolitikai érdek egyre hangsúlyosabbá válik a semleges, teljesítményen alapuló elbírálás helyett.

Szerbia európai integrációja hozzájárulhat az illegális migráció megfékezéséhez és az energiaellátás hosszú távú biztosításához. Európa és így Magyarország érdeke is egy stabil, az Unió felé elkötelezett Szerbia.
2-0520-5000.englishText:
The European Parliament's annual report on Serbia is more critical and biased than ever before.

The report fails to recognize any reform activities and past achievements, applying a one-sided, politically motivated approach. Unfortunately, this attitude on the part of the Union is increasingly characteristic of Western Balkan countries, and particularly of Serbia, which constantly undermines the credibility of the European Union in the region.

This trend is also alarming because Serbia is a key country for the stability of the Western Balkans, and the Union would need a balanced, responsible, and partner-like approach. The common goal is to preserve the stability of the region, which can only be achieved through a credible, objective EU approach that also acknowledges results.

As the patriotic shadow rapporteur of the report under discussion, I find the text unbalanced. There is no doubt that the country still has much to deliver in many areas, but the European commitment of the Serbian government and its efforts made so far in the fields of energy policy, family policy, visa policy, and minority policy should be appreciated. Instead, the text focuses on presenting shortcomings and contains severely unjust ideological distortions. There is no room for double standards in enlargement policy, yet current political interests are becoming increasingly prominent instead of a neutral, performance-based assessment.

Serbia's European integration can contribute to curbing illegal migration and ensuring long-term energy supplies. A stable Serbia committed to the Union is in the interest of Europe, and thus of Hungary.

2-0522-0000.sourceText: Ďalším bodom programu sú ústne vysvetlenia hlasovania.
2-0522-0000.englishText: The next item on the agenda is the oral explanations of vote.

2-0524-0000.sourceText: A ako prvé sú tu vysvetlenia hlasovania k správe Andreya Novakova: Práva cestujúcich v leteckej doprave.
2-0524-0000.englishText: And first we have the explanations of vote on Andrey Novakov's report: Air passenger rights.

2-0525-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός που ψηφίστηκε επικαλείται τα δικαιώματα των επιβατών στις αεροπορικές μεταφορές, ενώ ικανοποιεί όλες τις απαιτήσεις των μεγάλων ομίλων του κλάδου που σημειώνουν κέρδη ρεκόρ και έχουν ήδη μπουκώσει από κρατικές και ευρωενωσιακές επιδοτήσεις. Μειώνει περαιτέρω τις υποχρεώσεις των αεροπορικών εταιρειών, ψαλιδίζει τις αποζημιώσεις για τους επιβάτες και ανοίγει τον δρόμο για οριστικό περιορισμό τους, διατηρώντας την έννοια-λάστιχο των έκτακτων περιστάσεων, που δίνει την ικανότητα στους ομίλους να αποφεύγουν αποζημιώσεις κατά το δοκούν και να θησαυρίζουν ακόμα και από τις χειραποσκευές στην καμπίνα, όπως και από τις διαστάσεις της βαλίτσας.

Την ίδια στιγμή, οι εταιρείες, στη βάση της απελευθερωμένης αγοράς, έχουν εκτοξεύσει τις τιμές και εκμηδενίσει τις όποιες υπηρεσίες στους επιβάτες. Κριτήριο δράσης τους είναι το κέρδος, όπως βεβαίως και των κυβερνήσεων και της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, που καταδικάζουν τις υπηρεσίες πολιτικής αεροπορίας να λειτουργούν με απαρχαιωμένες υποδομές και λιγοστό προσωπικό σε καθεστώς εντατικοποίησης, βάζοντας σε κίνδυνο την ασφάλεια των πτήσεων. Δεν υπάρχει άλλος δρόμος: Για να κερδίσει δικαιώματα και ασφάλεια ο λαός, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο.
2-0525-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the regulation that was voted on invokes air passenger rights while satisfying all the demands of major industry conglomerates, which are recording record profits and have already been stuffed with state and European Union subsidies. It further reduces the obligations of airlines, slashes compensation for passengers, and paves the way for its definitive restriction by maintaining the rubber-band concept of extraordinary circumstances, which gives conglomerates the ability to avoid compensation at will and to rake in a fortune even from cabin hand luggage and suitcase dimensions.

At the same time, companies, on the basis of the deregulated market, have skyrocketed prices and decimated any services to passengers. Their criterion for action is profit, as is certainly that of governments and the European Union, which condemn civil aviation services to operate with outdated infrastructure and scarce staff under conditions of intensive labour, endangering flight safety. There is no other way: For the people to gain rights and safety, capital must lose.

2-0526-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, en este pleno de julio del Parlamento Europeo ha tenido lugar la votación definitiva del Reglamento sobre los derechos de los pasajeros aéreos y es una votación que tiene dos rasgos extraordinarios que merecen subrayarse.

El primero es la amplísima mayoría: ha votado favorablemente el arco parlamentario casi entero. Ha recibido votos favorables de todos los grupos parlamentarios. La razón es sencilla: después de trece años de bloqueo, por fin se ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Consejo.

El segundo rasgo extraordinario es que, por fin, se produce un avance en los derechos de la ciudadanía y, particularmente, de los pasajeros y muchas veces los derechos laborales —incluso los derechos fundamentales en la Unión Europea— han venido de la mano de los derechos de los consumidores.

Por fin hay un derecho de compensación frente a los abusos de las compañías aéreas, los retrasos, los sobreprecios y las sobreventas, por fin el derecho reconocido a embarcar la maleta en cabina y por fin facilidades expresas para las personas con dificultades de movilidad, para que puedan ejercer sus derechos en igualdad de condiciones con respecto de todos los demás.
2-0526-0000.englishText:
Mr President, in this July plenary session of the European Parliament, the final vote on the Regulation on air passengers' rights has taken place, and it is a vote with two extraordinary features that deserve to be highlighted.

The first is the very broad majority: almost the entire parliamentary spectrum voted in favour. It received favorable votes from all political groups. The reason is simple: after thirteen years of deadlock, an agreement has finally been reached with the Council.

The second extraordinary feature is that, at last, progress is being made in the rights of citizens and, particularly, of passengers, and very often labor rights—even fundamental rights in the European Union—have come hand in hand with consumer rights.

At last there is a right to compensation against the abuses of airlines, delays, overpricing and overbooking, at last the recognized right to bring cabin luggage on board and at last express facilities for people with mobility difficulties, so that they can exercise their rights on an equal footing with everyone else.

2-0528-0000.sourceText: A teraz nasleduje ústne vysvetlenie hlasovania k správe Gabriele Bischoff: Koordinácia systému sociálneho zabezpečenia.
2-0528-0000.englishText: And now follows the oral explanation of vote on the report by Gabriele Bischoff: Coordination of social security systems.

2-0529-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός υπηρετεί τις ανάγκες του κεφαλαίου για φθηνότερη και πιο ευέλικτη εργατική δύναμη. Στην πράξη, προσαρμόζει το ισχύον πλαίσιο εξατομικευμένης και εμπορευματοποιημένης ασφάλισης πείνας, με γενίκευση των επαγγελματικών ταμείων στις ανάγκες της αγοράς, όπως προανήγγειλε πρόσφατα η κυβέρνηση της Νέας Δημοκρατίας μέσω της Τράπεζας της Ελλάδας. Επιδίωξή του η διασυνοριακή κινητικότητα, δηλαδή η μαζική μετανάστευση από χώρα σε χώρα, κυνηγώντας ένα μεροκάματο.

Στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση της πολεμικής οικονομίας και εμπλοκής, όπου ο ένας στους τρεις εργαζόμενους είναι και επίσημα φτωχός και η ανεργία θερίζει, ο κανονισμός προτείνει πιο αυστηρούς όρους πρόσβασης στο επίδομα ανεργίας και διατήρησής του. Στόχος του κανονισμού είναι το ξήλωμα των εργατικών δικαιωμάτων, τα βάρη κράτους/ εργοδοσίας να μετατραπούν σε απώλειες για τους εργαζόμενους.

Για να κερδίσουν οι εργαζόμενοι, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο, τα κόμματα που το υπηρετούν και οι διεθνείς του συμμαχίες. Να οργανώσουν τώρα την πάλη τους για συλλογικές συμβάσεις εργασίας με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς, με πλήρη ασφαλιστικά δικαιώματα και μείωση του εργάσιμου χρόνου.
2-0529-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the regulation serves the needs of capital for cheaper and more flexible labour force. In practice, it adapts the current framework of individualized and commercialized starvation insurance, with the generalization of occupational funds to the needs of the market, as recently announced by the government of New Democracy through the Bank of Greece. Its aim is cross-border mobility, that is, mass migration from country to country, chasing a daily wage.

In the European Union of the war economy and involvement, where one in three workers is officially poor and unemployment is raging, the regulation proposes stricter conditions for access to and retention of the unemployment benefit. The goal of the regulation is the dismantling of workers' rights, so that state/employer burdens are turned into losses for workers.

For workers to win, capital, the parties that serve it, and its international alliances must lose. They must now organize their struggle for collective labor agreements with decent wages, with full insurance rights, and a reduction in working time.

2-0530-0000.sourceText: Týmto sme ukončili vysvetlenia hlasovania a aj dnešné debaty.
2-0530-0000.englishText: We have hereby concluded the explanations of vote and also today's debates.

2-0534-0000.sourceText: Nasledujúce rokovanie sa uskutoční zajtra v stredu 8. júla 2026 so začiatkom o 9. hodine ráno. Program schôdze je uverejnený, bol uverejnený a je k dispozícii na webovom sídle Európskeho parlamentu.
2-0534-0000.englishText: The following sitting will take place tomorrow, Wednesday, 8 July 2026, starting at 9 a.m. The agenda for the sitting is published, has been published, and is available on the website of the European Parliament.

2-0536-0000.sourceText: Zápisnica z tohto rokovania bude predložená Parlamentu na schválenie zajtra po hlasovaní.
2-0536-0000.englishText: The minutes of this sitting will be submitted to Parliament for approval tomorrow after the voting.
